Tracheal Xe concentration ( C Xe ) and flow were monitored using mass spectrometry and pneumotachometry to estimate specific ventilation (sV˙ms) and end-expiratory lung volume (EELV ms ). DECT-derived xenon concentration and tissue density images (mg/mL) were obtained by material decomposition, yielding sV˙DECT and EELV DECT , respectively.
title: Dynamic Xenon-Enhanced Spectral CT Imaging to Evaluate Regional Lung Function in an In Vivo Rabbit Model.

text: Agreement with mass spectrometry and differences between baseline and post-MCh were assessed. Results : The baseline sV˙DECT and EELV DECT agreed with the mass spectrometry, with mean differences of 0.6 min -1 [-0.2 min -1 , 1.4 min -1 ] and 0.6 mL [-6.7 mL, 7.9 mL], respectively. Following MCh administration, the mean differences increased to -2.9 min -1 [-4.1 min -1 , -1.6 min -1 ] for sV˙ and 1.3 mL [-15.3 mL, 12.8 mL] for EELV. Post-MCh, sV˙DECT decreased from 8.6 ± 1.6 min -1 to 3.7 ± 0.9 min -1 ( p = 0.034) and EELV DECT from 29.3 ± 1.0 mL to 27.0 ± 1.3 mL ( p = 0.036), whereas sV˙ms ( p = 0.308) and EELV ms ( p = 0.653) showed no substantial changes. Regional analysis revealed that sV˙DECT in well-ventilated regions matched tracheal sV˙ms.
title: Dynamic Xenon-Enhanced Spectral CT Imaging to Evaluate Regional Lung Function in an In Vivo Rabbit Model.

text: Conclusions: Dynamic Xe-DECT imaging enabled spatial and quantitative assessments of specific ventilation and tissue densities in an in vivo rabbit model. This technique allowed detection of focal alterations that remained undetected by tracheal measurements.
title: Dynamic Xenon-Enhanced Spectral CT Imaging to Evaluate Regional Lung Function in an In Vivo Rabbit Model.

text: Background Viral exanthems (VEs), including vaccine-preventable infections such as measles and rubella and non-vaccine-preventable infections such as roseola, remain clinically relevant. Declining vaccination rates and recent outbreaks have increased the importance of timely diagnosis and mandatory reporting. In addition, the relative rarity of vaccine-preventable diseases in modern clinical practice may reduce physician familiarity with these infections. Methods This IRB-exempt cross-sectional study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of Florida physicians regarding VE diagnosis and reporting requirements using a 19-question Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap; Vanderbilt University, Nashville, USA) survey. Participants included physicians and residents in family medicine, pediatrics, internal medicine, and infectious disease specialties.
title: Physician Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Viral Exanthem Diagnosis and Mandatory Reporting Requirements in Major Metropolitan Regions of Florida, USA.

text: Statistical analyses included analysis of variance (ANOVA), multivariate ANOVA (MANOVA), Tukey post hoc testing, and linear regression. Results A total of 162 physicians completed the survey, with 146 complete responses included in inferential analyses. Pediatricians demonstrated the highest overall knowledge scores (82.66%), followed by internal medicine (76.39%) and family medicine physicians (73.26%). Overall knowledge differences among specialties were significant (F(2,143) = 3.31, p = 0.039), with pediatricians scoring significantly higher than family medicine physicians. No significant specialty differences were identified when vignette-based diagnostic or mandatory reporting questions were analyzed independently. Most physicians, 148 (91.36%), expressed interest in additional training on VE diagnosis and management.
title: Physician Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Viral Exanthem Diagnosis and Mandatory Reporting Requirements in Major Metropolitan Regions of Florida, USA.

text: Greater physician confidence was significantly associated with higher diagnostic knowledge (β = 10.73, p < 0.001) and reporting knowledge (β = 9.68, p < 0.001). Roseola was the most commonly diagnosed VE in clinical practice, followed by measles and rubella. Conclusion Florida physicians demonstrated moderate-to-high knowledge of VE diagnosis and reporting requirements; however, notable gaps remained, particularly in differentiating rubella from similar exanthems. Interpretation is limited by the non-random respondent sample, uneven speciality representation, and potential nonresponse bias. Pediatricians outperformed family medicine physicians, although deficiencies were observed across specialties.
title: Physician Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Viral Exanthem Diagnosis and Mandatory Reporting Requirements in Major Metropolitan Regions of Florida, USA.

text: These findings identify areas in which additional physician education may be beneficial, particularly regarding the clinical differentiation of viral exanthems and mandatory reporting requirements. As vaccination rates decline and outbreaks increase, improving early recognition and reporting of VE remains important for outbreak prevention and public health preparedness.
title: Physician Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Viral Exanthem Diagnosis and Mandatory Reporting Requirements in Major Metropolitan Regions of Florida, USA.

text: Lung cancer is a leading cause of death in the world and is highly heterogeneous with extensive molecular changes and often resistant to therapy. Despite significant advances in clinical management through surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy, some of these treatments are limited in effectiveness by late diagnosis, systemic toxicity, poor accumulation, molecular heterogeneity, and acquired resistance. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current and emerging therapeutic strategies for lung cancer, with particular emphasis on advanced drug delivery systems and nanomedicine-based approaches. Recent advances in lipid-based nanoparticles, polymeric nanoparticles and micelles, inorganic nanoparticles, and nanocrystals are highlighted for their ability to improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, tumor accumulation, cellular uptake, and controlled drug release.
title: Smart nanomedicine for lung cancer: Overcoming drug resistance and therapeutic barriers through targeted delivery, phototherapy, and theranostics.

text: Active targeting and stimuli-responsive nanocarriers can improve tumor selectivity, intracellular drug delivery, and drug retention, potentially addressing selected resistance-associated mechanisms. Gene-delivery and genome-editing approaches offer additional opportunities to modulate resistance-related pathways, while photodynamic and photothermal therapies provide complementary strategies for localized tumor treatment. However, the extent to which these approaches reverse established drug resistance varies with the targeted mechanism and the experimental model employed. Distinguishing functional resistance reversal from improved drug delivery and general anticancer activity is therefore essential for assessing their translational potential.
title: Smart nanomedicine for lung cancer: Overcoming drug resistance and therapeutic barriers through targeted delivery, phototherapy, and theranostics.

text: Newcastle disease virus (NDV) incurs substantial economic losses within the global poultry industry. The matrix (M) protein of NDV is integral to viral replication. In this study, we examined the interaction between the NDV M protein and annexin A6 (AnxA6) in DF-1 cells. Our findings revealed that AnxA6 associates with the C-terminus of the NDV M protein, predominantly within the cytoplasm. Functional analyses indicated that the knockdown of AnxA6 expression significantly enhanced NDV replication, whereas the overexpression of AnxA6 inhibited viral replication. Taken together, these findings suggest that AnxA6 may function as a negative regulator of NDV replication in this cell culture model, potentially through its interaction with the M protein.
title: Annexin A6 Interacts with Newcastle Disease Virus Matrix Protein and Is Associated with Reduced Viral Replication in DF-1 Cells.

text: This study offers new insights into the intricate relationship between viral proteins and host factors in NDV infection and suggests that AnxA6 may serve as a potential target for further investigation. Further research is necessary to elucidate the detailed mechanisms governing the AnxA6-M protein interaction.
title: Annexin A6 Interacts with Newcastle Disease Virus Matrix Protein and Is Associated with Reduced Viral Replication in DF-1 Cells.

text: Prohibitive costs associated with high-field MRI systems have resulted in reduced access in resource-limited areas with consequential healthcare inequities. This has renewed interest in purposefully designed low-field (LF) systems that, despite inherently lower signal-to-noise ratios, have advantages in terms of cost, portability, and accessibility. This pilot study successfully translated a previously developed LF (0.05 T) MRI canine cadaver brain protocol for in vivo application and compared the acquired images with paired 1.5 T images from 21 different canine patients. The visibility of 15 anatomic features was ordinarily scored (scale 1-3) on transverse T1-weighted post-contrast (21/21 patients) and T2-weighted (17/21 patients) sequences.
title: Canine brain imaging with a new low-field portable (0.05 T) MRI scanner: a pilot <i>in vivo</i> comparison to conventional 1.5 T.

text: Lateral ventricles were easily visualized (89.3%-100% scored 3/3) across all sequence‒system combinations, with T2-weighted sequences also providing good identification of the mesencephalic aqueduct (56.3%-100%), fourth ventricle (77.1%-100%), and thalamus (68.8%-100%). Absolute visual grading characteristics (VGC) analysis confirmed comparable performance of the LF system to the 1.5 T MRI for these features, a particularly relevant finding given the system's originally intended application for pediatric hydrocephalus neuroimaging in resource-limited areas. This study represents the first in vivo usage and evaluation of a 0.05 T MRI in a clinical veterinary context.
title: Canine brain imaging with a new low-field portable (0.05 T) MRI scanner: a pilot <i>in vivo</i> comparison to conventional 1.5 T.

text: Sympathetic hyperactivity following acute brain injury (ABI) impedes recovery, yet effective treatments are lacking. Recently, N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) modified by fat mass and obesity-associated gene (FTO) has been demonstrated to play critical roles in multiple neurological diseases. Here, we found that sympathetic hyperactivity occurred in traumatic brain injury and intracerebral hemorrhage patients and mouse models in vivo. In mouse ABI models, the RNA demethylase FTO was upregulated in hypothalamic neurons. Through m 6 A methylation sequencing, we found that FTO mediated m 6 A demethylation of Trhr mRNA, enhancing its stability by inhibiting YTHDF2-dependent decay. This increased neuronal TRHR expression and sensitivity to TRH, culminating in sympathetic hyperactivity. Conversely, restoring hypothalamic FTO or TRHR levels alleviated this condition.
title: Hypothalamus Participates in Peripheral Sympathetic Hyperactivity After Acute Brain Injury by Regulating <i>Trhr</i> M<sup>6</sup>A Modification.

text: We further mapped and functionally validated a monosynaptic projection from lateral hypothalamic TRHR neurons to the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM), demonstrating that modulating these neurons controls sympathetic tone. Collectively, our findings elucidate a novel FTO-Trhr axis in post-ABI autonomic dysfunction and highlight a promising therapeutic target.
title: Hypothalamus Participates in Peripheral Sympathetic Hyperactivity After Acute Brain Injury by Regulating <i>Trhr</i> M<sup>6</sup>A Modification.

text: The deubiquitinating enzyme, ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L3 (UCHL3), has been implicated as a potential therapeutic target for cancer with a role in regulating the DNA damage response pathways. While the target has been studied using genetic methods there is a lack of reliable chemical probes to selectivity target UCHL3. In this study we report hit identification and optimisation of a new chemical scaffold that irreversibly inhibits UCHL3. The observed structure-activity relationships are corroborated by ligand-bound crystal structures that confirm covalent adduct formation with the catalytic cysteine of the enzyme. Finally, through gel-shift assays using a ubiquitin activity-based probe we demonstrate on-target engagement with UCHL3 in two cell lines.
title: Identification, optimisation, and structural elucidation of chloroacetamide scaffold as covalent inhibitors for ubiquitin C-terminal Hydrolase L3.
journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry

text: The work as a whole presents a comprehensive evaluation of the new scaffold that can be utilised to probe UCHL3 in different biological contexts.
title: Identification, optimisation, and structural elucidation of chloroacetamide scaffold as covalent inhibitors for ubiquitin C-terminal Hydrolase L3.
journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry

text: Suicidal ideation is common among adolescents, yet most who experience it never make a suicide attempt. Identifying which youth go on to engage in suicidal behavior remains one of the most pressing challenges in clinical psychiatry. This systematic review synthesizes the evidence on risk and protective factors that are associated with the transition from suicidal ideation to suicidal behavior in adolescents and young adults. We searched five electronic databases from inception through November 2025, yielding 52 studies meeting eligibility criteria. Included studies assessed suicidal ideation at a defined baseline and measured subsequent suicidal behavior, evaluating at least one predictor of that transition in samples with participants under age 30.
title: Which youth with suicidal ideation will go on to make a suicide attempt? A systematic review.
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics

text: Across case-control, retrospective, and prospective designs, the strongest predictors of transition were characteristics of the ideation itself, particularly the presence of a plan or intent, high duration and intrusiveness, and lack of controllability. Past suicidal behavior and non-suicidal self-injury were also robust predictors. Psychiatric comorbidity, especially mood disorders combined with externalizing disorders, substance use, or post-traumatic stress disorder, meaningfully increased risk, as did maltreatment, peer victimization, and family conflict. Conversely, parent-child connection, social support, and school connectedness were protective. Findings from this review can inform more precise clinical risk assessment and help identify the highest-priority targets for intervention among youth presenting with suicidal ideation.
title: Which youth with suicidal ideation will go on to make a suicide attempt? A systematic review.
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics

text: Background Gastric cancer (GC) is the fourth most common malignancy, affecting one in 11 men (9.1%) and one in 23 women (4.38%). Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) infection and smoking are the primary risk factors for GC. Individuals who have multiple other family members with GC are also at higher risk owing to lifestyle and genetic factors. H. pylori -eradicating medications can reduce the risk of disease. The incidence of GC increases after 50 years of age, particularly among men; however, the reason for the differing incidence rates between the sexes remains unclear. Methods To clarify the reasons for sex differences in GC incidence rates from a molecular pathological perspective, we utilized cancer genome profiling (CGP) and information on BRCA2 expression levels obtained by immunohistochemistry and the number of GC cases in the family.
title: Relationship Between Estrogen-Induced BRCA2 and Development of Gastric Cancer.

text: Results We investigated the incidence of GC in families with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) and found it to be 4.2-fold higher than that in non-HBOC families. In families with versus without HBOC, men accounted for 74.57% and 53.67% of all GC cases, respectively, indicating that men are more likely to develop GC in the former group. Furthermore, estrogen stimulation induced breast cancer type 2 (BRCA2) expression in genetically modified mice as well as in cultured cells, and low-grade atypical cells were observed in the gastric mucosal tissues of female mice that underwent ovarian resection. Additional research experiment revealed that stimulation by the female hormone estrogen induces the expression of BRCA2, which suppresses the development of GC.
title: Relationship Between Estrogen-Induced BRCA2 and Development of Gastric Cancer.

text: Clinical studies have also shown that patients with GC who have high BRCA2 expression exhibit longer survival rates than those in whom BRCA2 expression is low. Conclusions Overall, the data suggest that the higher mortality rate of GC in men than in women may be due to a protective effect of BRCA2.
title: Relationship Between Estrogen-Induced BRCA2 and Development of Gastric Cancer.

text: Purpose of review β-adrenergic receptors (ADRBs) are key mediators of stress responses, which have important roles in cancer growth and dissemination. β-blockers, inhibitors of ADRBs that are well established for treating cardiovascular conditions, have been proposed to be potentially useful, cost-effective, repurposed drugs for treating various cancers, including melanomas. This study aims to critically appraise the evidence for the diverse roles of ADRBs in melanoma cell biology and pathogenesis, through a systematic review of the literature and a meta-analysis of clinical applications of β-blockers in melanoma patients. Recent findings In vivo and in vitro experimental studies have shown β-blockers to have various beneficial effects on melanoma cell proliferation, tumor growth, differentiation, angiogenesis, metabolism, immune evasion, invasion and metastasis.
title: The Pathological Roles of β-adrenergic Receptors in Melanoma and Their Potential as Therapeutic Targets: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

text: However, many of these studies have used high drug concentrations that have questionable specificity for ADRBs and are clinically unattainable. The role of ADRBs in interactions between melanoma cells and tumor-infiltrating nerve and immune cells is being defined. Clinical application of β-blockers in melanoma patients may provide some progression-free survival benefit when taken prior to disease onset, indicating a role for ADRBs in melanoma progression. New approaches to administering β-blockers via synthetic particles are being developed to improve their effectiveness. Our understanding of the importance of ADRBs in the pathogenesis and treatment of cancer has grown rapidly in recent years. ADRBs are at the nexus between the sympathetic nervous system and immune cells in melanomas.
title: The Pathological Roles of β-adrenergic Receptors in Melanoma and Their Potential as Therapeutic Targets: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

text: Determination of the optimal approach to implementing β-blockers to treat melanomas awaits further biological and clinical studies that will clarify their intrinsic effects and their interactions with existing treatments.
title: The Pathological Roles of β-adrenergic Receptors in Melanoma and Their Potential as Therapeutic Targets: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

text: Background Leptospirosis is an important cause of acute kidney injury (AKI) in dogs and commonly induces renal tubular dysfunction. Although electrolyte abnormalities are frequently recognized during the course of leptospirosis, clinically relevant hypomagnesemia associated with neurological manifestations has rarely been reported in dogs. This report describes a dog that developed severe symptomatic hypomagnesemia during recovery from severe leptospirosis-associated AKI treated with continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Case presentation A 9 year old, 12 kg spayed female mixed-breed dog was referred for severe leptospirosis-associated AKI complicated by anuria, hyperbilirubinemia, thrombocytopenia, and pulmonary involvement. Blood and urine polymerase chain reaction assays confirmed Leptospira spp.
title: Clinically relevant hypomagnesemia during recovery from severe leptospirosis-associated acute kidney injury in a dog treated with continuous renal replacement therapy: a case report.

text: Infection Because of persistent anuria and progressive azotemia despite intensive medical management, the dog underwent two continuous renal replacement therapy sessions approximately 15 and 18 h, respectively. Urine production subsequently recovered, and the dog entered a polyuric recovery phase with progressive improvement in azotemia. On day 13 after admission, generalized tremors, hypersalivation, and altered mentation developed concurrently with severe hypomagnesemia (ionized magnesium, 0.24 mmol/L; total magnesium, 1.4 mg/dL). Fractional excretion of magnesium (FEMG) was markedly increased (38.8%), suggesting inappropriate renal magnesium loss despite improving renal function. Intravenous magnesium sulfate administered as a bolus followed by continuous rate infusion resulted in rapid resolution of the neurological signs.
title: Clinically relevant hypomagnesemia during recovery from severe leptospirosis-associated acute kidney injury in a dog treated with continuous renal replacement therapy: a case report.

text: At follow-up evaluations performed 11 and 23 days after the hypomagnesemic episode, fractional excretion of magnesium remained increased at 30.2% and 28.4%, respectively, despite improvement in serum creatinine concentration, supporting persistent impairment of renal tubular magnesium handling during recovery. Conclusions This case demonstrates that clinically significant hypomagnesemia may develop during the polyuric recovery phase of severe leptospirosis-associated AKI in dogs, even after apparent improvement in renal function. Serial measurements of fractional excretion of magnesium supported continued renal magnesium loss during recovery and emphasized the importance of monitoring magnesium concentrations in dogs with leptospirosis, particularly when neurological abnormalities develop.
title: Clinically relevant hypomagnesemia during recovery from severe leptospirosis-associated acute kidney injury in a dog treated with continuous renal replacement therapy: a case report.

text: Woody plants are threatened by fungal and oomycete pathogens that cause root and wood rots, cankers, vascular wilts, dieback, fruit decay, and other diseases. Meanwhile, intensive production systems and repeated fungicide use have raised concerns about resistance, environmental persistence, and non-target effects. Essential oils (EOs) have emerged as promising natural antimicrobial resources, yet their effectiveness depends strongly on chemical composition, pathogen susceptibility, concentration, formulation, and application strategy. This review synthesizes current evidence on EO-based management of pathogens affecting forest trees, fruit trees, woody crops, and wood materials, emphasizing the chemical and biological determinants of antifungal efficacy.
title: Plant essential oils against woody plant fungal pathogens: chemical composition, antifungal mechanisms, and translational challenges.

text: Across diverse pathosystems, EO activity is associated with phenolic monoterpenes, aldehydes, monoterpene hydrocarbons, and oxygenated terpenoids, while chemotypic and geographical variation can substantially influence performance. EOs act through multiple complementary mechanisms, including disruption of fungal cell membranes and walls, ergosterol depletion, interference with sterol and cell-wall biosynthesis, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, morphological damage, inhibition of spore germination, and suppression of pathogen development. Some EOs may additionally stimulate host defense responses, indicating that disease suppression can involve both direct antifungal activity and plant-mediated resistance. Advances in vapor delivery, coatings, nanoemulsions, and wood-preservative applications further enhance their potential.
title: Plant essential oils against woody plant fungal pathogens: chemical composition, antifungal mechanisms, and translational challenges.

text: However, practical deployment remains limited by compositional variability, volatility, phytotoxicity, formulation instability, limited persistence, inconsistent dose responses, and insufficient field validation. Future research should prioritize standardization, mechanism-guided formulation, synergistic combinations, ecotoxicological assessment, techno-economic evaluation, and field- and commercial-scale validation to enable reliable integration of EOs into sustainable woody plant disease management.
title: Plant essential oils against woody plant fungal pathogens: chemical composition, antifungal mechanisms, and translational challenges.

text: Gilvetmab is a caninised monoclonal antibody against canine PD-1. Concurrent or sequential administration of anti-PD-1 antibodies and radiation therapy (RT) improves survival time in various species. Eighteen dogs with mast cell tumours (MCTs) were prospectively treated with 24 Gy of RT over Days 0, 7 and 21 and gilvetmab every 2 weeks beginning on the second fraction of RT (Day 7) for up to 10 doses. Best tumour response was complete in one (6%), partial in eight (44%) and stable disease in nine dogs (50%) for an ORR of 50%. Median time to best response was 7 days after the first fraction of RT. Thirteen dogs (72%) developed progressive disease with a median progression free interval (PFI) of 116 days after the first fraction of RT.
title: Combination of Hypofractionated Radiation Therapy and Gilvetmab for the Treatment of Cutaneous or Subcutaneous Mast Cell Tumours in Dogs.

text: Nine adverse events (AEs) attributed to gilvetmab were recorded in seven dogs (39%) consisting of infusion reactions in four, metabolic changes in three and gastrointestinal signs and pancreatitis in one each. Overall, five dogs (28%) experienced Grade 3 AEs. Radiation AEs were limited to Grade 1 for both acute and late effects in seven dogs (39%). There was a significant difference in PFI and MST for dogs with and without lymph node metastasis with a median PFI of 64 versus 292 days and MST of 103 versus 587 days (p = 0.02 and 0.005, respectively). This sequence, or combination, of therapies did not provide durable tumour control for canine MCT and the AE profile warrants further evaluation.
title: Combination of Hypofractionated Radiation Therapy and Gilvetmab for the Treatment of Cutaneous or Subcutaneous Mast Cell Tumours in Dogs.

text: Ochratoxin A (OTA), a mycotoxin produced by Aspergillus and Penicillium species, is a widespread feed contaminant with nephrotoxic, hepatotoxic, immunotoxic, reproductive, and teratogenic effects. Despite the particular susceptibility of rabbits to OTA, information on ochratoxicosis in this species remains limited. This review summarizes current evidence on OTA occurrence, toxicokinetics, mechanisms of toxicity, clinicopathological effects, immunotoxicity, and preventive strategies in rabbits. Following gastrointestinal absorption, OTA has a high affinity for plasma proteins and preferentially accumulates in the kidneys and liver.
title: Ochratoxin A Toxicity in Rabbits-A Review.

text: Its toxicity is mediated by the inhibition of protein synthesis, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, genotoxicity, apoptosis, and immune dysregulation, ultimately leading to renal and hepatic injury, hematological and biochemical alterations, impaired growth, and reproductive toxicity. OTA-induced immunosuppression may also increase susceptibility to secondary infections, including Pasteurella multocida . Importantly, pathological and biochemical alterations may occur following relatively low-level exposure, while residual OTA levels may persist in tissues after exposure is discontinued. Effective prevention of OTA contamination in feed is therefore crucial for controlling ochratoxicosis.
title: Ochratoxin A Toxicity in Rabbits-A Review.

text: Microbial and enzymatic detoxification, probiotics, and phytogenic additives represent promising approaches for the prevention and mitigation of OTA toxicity; however, further studies in rabbits are needed to establish their efficacy and optimal application and to evaluate the effects of different OTA doses, early biomarkers, and tissue residue kinetics.
title: Ochratoxin A Toxicity in Rabbits-A Review.

text: CLN2 disease is a fatal lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme tripeptidyl peptidase 1 (TPP1), resulting in progressive neurodegeneration and non-neuronal pathology. While enzyme replacement therapy has improved disease management, there remains a critical need for objective molecular biomarkers capable of monitoring disease progression and therapeutic response. The purpose of this study was to utilize a canine model of CLN2 disease to investigate proteomic changes in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and in minimally invasive biofluids tears and plasma to identify candidate disease biomarkers. Untargeted proteomic analysis was conducted using these biofluids from unaffected controls and CLN2-affected dogs at presymptomatic, symptomatic, and advanced disease stages. CSF demonstrated the greatest degree of proteomic alterations over the disease progression.
title: Biofluid Proteomic Biomarker Discovery in a Large Animal Model of CLN2 Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis.

text: Proteins associated with cytoskeletal organization, synaptic signaling, lysosomal biology, mitochondrial metabolism, lipid homeostasis, and inflammatory responses were significantly altered. Tear fluid demonstrated overlapping biological themes with CSF, particularly involving mitochondrial metabolism, lysosomal function, and lipid-associated pathways. In contrast, plasma proteomic alterations were comparatively modest but supported systemic changes associated with extracellular signaling, inflammation, and lipid metabolism. Collectively, these findings demonstrate progressive and coordinated proteomic alterations across multiple biofluids in CLN2 disease that can serve as candidate biomarkers of disease progression.
title: Biofluid Proteomic Biomarker Discovery in a Large Animal Model of CLN2 Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis.

text: Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by persistent synovitis, progressive joint destruction, and significant morbidity. Despite advances in targeted therapies, achieving sustained remission remains challenging, necessitating the exploration of novel, multi-targeted therapeutic strategies. This study investigates the therapeutic potential of a self-emulsifying nanoformulation, quercetin-loaded pumpkin seed oil nanoemulsion (Qu-PSONE), in a complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA)-induced RA rat model, focusing on elucidating its integrated molecular mechanisms.
title: Deciphering the Therapeutic Effect of Quercetin-Loaded Pumpkin Seed Oil Nanoemulsion on Rheumatoid Arthritis in a Rat Model.

text: Methods: Adult male Wistar rats (n = 50) were divided into a normal control group (n = 10) and an RA-induced rat model (n = 40), with the latter being further subdivided into four experimental groups: RA control, free quercetin (Qu), pumpkin seed oil nanoemulsion (PSONE), and Qu-PSONE-treated groups. We performed comprehensive analyses, including physicochemical characterization of the nanoformulations and quantification of synovial protein levels of key mediators (IL-17, TLR-4, NF-κBp65, Nrf2, OPG, RANKL, JAK1, and STAT3) via ELISA. In parallel, synovial gene expression of GSDMD and miRNA-146a was assessed using RT-qPCR. Treatment efficacy was further evaluated through paw thickness measurements, clinical arthritis scoring, radiographic assessment of joint erosion, and histopathological examination, alongside immunohistochemical staining for TNF-α and MMP-9.
title: Deciphering the Therapeutic Effect of Quercetin-Loaded Pumpkin Seed Oil Nanoemulsion on Rheumatoid Arthritis in a Rat Model.

text: Results: Our findings demonstrate that Qu-PSONE exerts a superior nutrigenomic inhibitory effect on the inflammatory cascade and joint deformity associated with CFA-induced adjuvant arthritis. The Qu-PSONE significantly modulated miRNA-146a expression, serving as a sensitive indicator of attenuated synoviocyte activation. This treatment concurrently increased Nrf2 synovial level, suppressed synovial NF-κBp65, TLR-4, and IL-17 levels, which in turn downstream-inhibited the JAK/STAT pathway, balanced RANKL/OPG signaling, and downregulated transcriptional priming of the pyroptotic marker GSDMD . Together, these findings demonstrate that Qu-PSONE effectively breaks the inflammatory cascade in adjuvant arthritis.
title: Deciphering the Therapeutic Effect of Quercetin-Loaded Pumpkin Seed Oil Nanoemulsion on Rheumatoid Arthritis in a Rat Model.

text: These palliative effects of Qu-PSONE were robustly correlated with reduced paw edema, improved arthritis scores, mitigated radiographic joint damage, and diminished synovial infiltration and MMP-9 expression, as confirmed by histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Conclusions: Qu-PSONE halts arthritic progression and curtails joint damage through multitarget suppression of the NF-κBp65/TLR-4/IL-17 inflammatory axis at the synovial level. This response is accompanied by reduced JAK1 and STAT3 protein expression, re-established RANKL/OPG homeostasis to mitigate bone destruction, and attenuated GSDMD transcript levels, with miRNA-146a serving as a responsive biomarker of disease resolution.
title: Deciphering the Therapeutic Effect of Quercetin-Loaded Pumpkin Seed Oil Nanoemulsion on Rheumatoid Arthritis in a Rat Model.

text: England's first pharmacopoeia hid from the untrained knowledge of the medicines physicians prescribed in its Latin text. In the absence of censorship during the interregnum, Nicholas Culpeper (1616-1654) translated it for all to read and appended a commentary pointing out worthless or dangerous remedies to his untrained readers and poor instructions to apothecaries for compounding others. Meanwhile College Fellows were preparing a new updated edition which paid little attention to Culpeper's criticisms and provoked harsher attacks on the College when he translated it in turn. The direction of criticism was reversed when Culpeper's publisher Peter Cole, in anticipation of a new reality in Restoration England, engaged medical editors to rectify and supplement the translation to make it acceptable to the College.
title: Contested Medical Knowledge: The College of Physicians' London <i>Pharmacopoeia</i>, Culpeper's Translations and the Redacted Version of His Publisher Peter Cole.
journal: Social history of medicine : the journal of the Society for the Social History of Medicine

text: This article compares these various texts, highlighting lines of criticism, examples of scurrilous abuse and how the editors defended the official Galenic and chymical remedies of the day.
title: Contested Medical Knowledge: The College of Physicians' London <i>Pharmacopoeia</i>, Culpeper's Translations and the Redacted Version of His Publisher Peter Cole.
journal: Social history of medicine : the journal of the Society for the Social History of Medicine

text: Emerging animal viruses pose persistent threats to livestock breeding and public health, underscoring the need for a deeper understanding of virus-host interactions. Nevertheless, the regulatory roles and conserved mechanisms of host non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) during animal virus infections remain fragmented, and ncRNA-mediated mechanisms for emerging animal viruses are particularly poorly characterized, with no systematic collation or theoretical summarization available. Studies indicate that ncRNAs, including miRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs, have emerged as important regulators of the interplay between animal viruses and their hosts. This review synthesizes evidence from eleven animal viruses covering swine, poultry, ruminant, feline, canine, and mink hosts, with emphasis on virus-induced changes in ncRNA expression and their antiviral or proviral functions.
title: Non-coding RNA-mediated tug-of-war between emerging viruses and host antiviral defense: lessons from animal viruses.

text: Across diverse virus-host systems, three recurring regulatory paradigms are identified: host antiviral defense, viral hijacking, and viral antagonism. Host cells can dynamically reshape their ncRNA expression to regulate host restriction factors, proviral host factors, and other ncRNAs, thereby influencing innate immune signalling, viral replication cycles, autophagy, apoptosis, and metabolic reprogramming. Conversely, animal viruses, including PEDV, PRRSV, PRV, SVA, AIV, ALV-J, NDV, BVDV, FHV-1, CIV, and MEV, have evolved sophisticated strategies to hijack host ncRNA networks or antagonize ncRNA-mediated antiviral immunity, and remodel the intracellular microenvironment to facilitate viral replication. These paradigms provide a unified theoretical system for understanding and predicting ncRNA-mediated regulatory mechanisms in emerging animal viruses.
title: Non-coding RNA-mediated tug-of-war between emerging viruses and host antiviral defense: lessons from animal viruses.

text: They also offer references for dissecting the pathogenic patterns of ASFV, SADS-CoV, and future unknown emerging viruses, as well as, for mining, screening, and identifying potential antiviral drug targets.
title: Non-coding RNA-mediated tug-of-war between emerging viruses and host antiviral defense: lessons from animal viruses.

text: Inter-organ communication is governed by a complex "secretome," yet mapping the journey of these factors from their origin to precise cellular destinations remains a fundamental challenge. Proximity labeling emerges as a powerful tool to dissect the secretome, yet conventional workflows typically rely on single-compartment biotinylation at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), failing to capture proteins that utilize unconventional secretion. Here, we present DuO-SCOUT (Dual-Organelle Secretome Conjugation and Organ-Uptake Tracking), a high-performance platform that simultaneously targets BioID2 to the ER and the trans-Golgi network (TGN). This integrated strategy captures the full secretory maturation relay, increasing protein identification by over 120% compared to traditional ER-anchored methods. We translated this in vivo using an Adipoq-Cre mouse model to map the adipose secretome.
title: Dual-Organelle Secretome Conjugation and Organ-Uptake Tracking (DuO-SCOUT) Enables Deep and Sensitive Mapping of the Secreted Proteins.

text: To bridge the gap between systemic transport and tissue-specific uptake, DuO-SCOUT integrates BSPA (Biotin-Specific Proximity Amplification), a visualization toolkit detecting biotinylated proteins with sub-nanomolar sensitivity. In obese mice, we identified the piriform cortex (PIR) as a previously unrecognized extra-hypothalamic sink for adipose-derived leptin. This is associated with a localized neuroinflammatory signature, including significant induction of Il6. DuO-SCOUT establishes a broadly applicable framework for dissecting the complex molecular logic of systemic organ-organ communication.
title: Dual-Organelle Secretome Conjugation and Organ-Uptake Tracking (DuO-SCOUT) Enables Deep and Sensitive Mapping of the Secreted Proteins.

text: Background and objectives The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic significantly disrupted healthcare systems and altered patterns of healthcare utilization worldwide. In India, where structural inequities in healthcare access persist, the pandemic may have influenced health-seeking behaviour differently across urban and rural populations. Understanding these behavioural shifts is critical for strengthening health system preparedness in future public health emergencies. This study aimed to explore, using a qualitative descriptive design, participants' perceived changes in health-seeking behaviour, healthcare preferences, and decision-making following the COVID-19 pandemic among adults aged 18-85 years living in urban and rural areas of eastern Gujarat, India.
title: Perceived Changes in Health-Seeking Behaviour Following the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study of Urban and Rural Populations in Eastern Gujarat.

text: Methods This descriptive qualitative study was conducted as part of a larger mixed-methods investigation in eastern Gujarat between October 2023 and April 2025. Face-to-face, semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 20 purposively selected participants (10 from urban Vadodara and 10 from rural Sankheda taluka, Chhota Udaipur district). Interviews were conducted in Gujarati or Hindi, audio-recorded, and translated into English. The interview guide was pilot-tested and refined before data collection and was informed by the PASS model and relevant literature. Data were analysed using inductive thematic analysis, with codes organized into categories and themes through iterative review. Results Five major themes emerged. Participants described perceived changes in health-seeking behaviour following the COVID-19 pandemic.
title: Perceived Changes in Health-Seeking Behaviour Following the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study of Urban and Rural Populations in Eastern Gujarat.

text: These included greater preference and trust in formal healthcare, alongside a continued preference for private facilities despite financial constraints. Healthcare decisions remained influenced by affordability, accessibility, perceived quality of care, symptom severity, and family considerations. Self-medication, home remedies, and other traditional systems of medicine continued to be used, particularly for minor illnesses. Telemedicine was viewed positively by some participants but had limited uptake. Participants also described greater attention to hygiene, diet, exercise, and other preventive practices. Conclusions Participants described perceived changes in health-seeking behaviour following the COVID-19 pandemic, including greater trust in formal healthcare and increased attention to preventive practices.
title: Perceived Changes in Health-Seeking Behaviour Following the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study of Urban and Rural Populations in Eastern Gujarat.

text: However, financial constraints, accessibility barriers, perceived delays in public facilities, and continued self-treatment for mild symptoms remained important influences on healthcare decisions. These findings provide contextual insights into healthcare decision-making in the selected study settings.
title: Perceived Changes in Health-Seeking Behaviour Following the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study of Urban and Rural Populations in Eastern Gujarat.

text: Purpose Peripheral inflammation induces anxiety-like and sickness behaviors, yet the underlying epitranscriptomic correlates remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the regional transcriptional alterations of key N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) regulatory enzymes across the limbic system in response to systemic immune challenge. Methods Systemic inflammation was induced in mice via lipopolysaccharide (LPS) administration, followed by the evaluation of behavioral paradigms for anxiety-like and sickness behaviors. We subsequently mapped the mRNA expression profiles of major m 6 A writers, erasers, and readers across critical limbic brain regions and performed correlational analyses between these transcriptional changes and specific behavioral indices. Findings Inflammatory challenge triggered distinct, region-specific alterations in m 6 A regulators.
title: Brain Region-Specific Expression of m6A Regulatory Enzymes in the Inflammation-Induced Mouse Model of Anxiety.

text: Notably, while FTO was downregulated in both the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and hippocampus, its behavioral associations diverged: only NAc FTO correlated with anxiety-like phenotypes, and FTO exhibited opposite correlations with feeding between these two regions. Furthermore, molecular specificity was observed in the basolateral amygdala (BLA); despite the downregulation of both METTL3 and METTL14, only METTL14 significantly correlated with feeding and anxiety-like behaviors. Conclusion The mRNA expression of major m 6 A regulatory enzymes exhibits complex, brain-region-specific patterns that strongly correlate with distinct behavioral outputs during inflammation.
title: Brain Region-Specific Expression of m6A Regulatory Enzymes in the Inflammation-Induced Mouse Model of Anxiety.

text: These observational findings provide a conceptual framework indicating that regional epitranscriptomic machinery is closely associated with behavioral specificity, highlighting promising transcriptional targets for future functional and mechanistic validation in anxiolytic interventions.
title: Brain Region-Specific Expression of m6A Regulatory Enzymes in the Inflammation-Induced Mouse Model of Anxiety.

text: Canine mammary tumors (CMTs) are the most common neoplasms in intact female dogs, yet early detection remains challenging due to the lack of clinically validated, noninvasive biomarkers. This study aimed to develop a noninvasive diagnostic model for CMT detection by integrating serum autoantibody biomarkers with machine learning. Serum samples from 154 dogs with mammary tumors (31 benign, 123 malignant) and 39 healthy controls were analyzed using a custom multiplex immunoassay detecting autoantibodies against AGR2, HAPLN1, IGFBP5, and TYMS, normalized to anti-BSA levels. Median fluorescence intensity (MFI), standardized autoantibody ratios, and their combination, together with clinical variables, were used to train random forest classifiers.
title: Machine learning-assisted detection of canine mammary tumors using serum autoantibody signatures.

text: The model based on standardized autoantibody ratios achieved the best performance, with an AUC of 0.79 (sensitivity 75.3%, specificity 74.4%) for overall CMT detection; 0.78 (92.7%, 61.5%) for malignant CMTs; and 0.77 (82.2%, 71.8%) for early-stagemalignancies. Assuming a CMT prevalence of 0.5 in the hospital-referred population, the positive and negative predictive values ranged from 0.74-0.75 and 0.75-0.91, respectively. This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that a machine learning-assisted multiplex autoantibody assay offers a feasible noninvasive approach for CMT detection. Further validation in larger, independent cohorts is warranted to support clinical translation in veterinary oncology.
title: Machine learning-assisted detection of canine mammary tumors using serum autoantibody signatures.

text: Background rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccine is recommended for prevention of Ebola virus (EBOV) infection and disease (EVD). However, breakthrough EBOV infections have been observed in vaccinees. Currently available diagnostic and research assays cannot reliably distinguish individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus from those previously infected with the virus. This limitation complicates interpretation of vaccine-effectiveness studies, seroepidemiologic investigations, and estimates of infection or attack rates. The ability to differentiate vaccine-induced immune responses from those resulting from natural infection remains an important unmet public health and research need.
title: Early detection of immunoglobulin A against a vaccine backbone protein enables fast, durable, and objective identification of individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus.

text: Methods We developed a multiplex sero-diagnostic assay simultaneously detecting IgA, IgG, and IgM antibodies against vesicular stomatitis Indiana virus nucleoprotein (VSV-N), a vaccine-specific marker absent in natural infection, and EBOV-GP, the vaccine's target antigen. We evaluated longitudinal samples from 30 individuals after vaccination and 30 placebo (saline) recipients, as well as 8 participants from a long-term vaccination follow-up study. Findings We detected increase in all antibodies against both protein antigens in vaccinated individuals. Critically, the assay reveals that anti-VSV-N IgA responses emerge earlier and more robustly than anti-GP responses in vaccinees, establishing anti-N IgA as a definitive, early, and durable biomarker of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccination with high sensitivity and specificity.
title: Early detection of immunoglobulin A against a vaccine backbone protein enables fast, durable, and objective identification of individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus.

text: Interpretation The assay enables rapid, accurate identification of vaccine recipients and supports real-time assessment of vaccine effectiveness during outbreaks. Furthermore, the assay's adaptability to the expanding pipeline of VSV-vectored vaccines positions it as a transformative diagnostic platform for accelerating preparedness for future infectious disease threats and outbreak response strategies. Funding Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the Divisions of Intramural Research (DIR) and Clinical Research (DCR) of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) at the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH).
title: Early detection of immunoglobulin A against a vaccine backbone protein enables fast, durable, and objective identification of individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus.

text: Introduction Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a debilitating multisystem disorder associated with immune dysregulation yet lacks definitive biomarkers or effective therapies. Acute immune perturbations may transiently modulate disease manifestations. Methods We report the case of a female patient in her 60s with severe, long-standing ME/CFS who experienced changes in symptom following administration of recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analyzed pre- and post-vaccination using flow cytometry, with comparison to a female healthy control. Plasma galectin-9 (Gal-9) levels were quantified by ELISA. Results Both RZV doses were associated with rapid, transient remission of symptoms, including improved sleep, cognition, pain, mobility, and respiratory function, followed by relapse.
title: Transient clinical improvement and immune modulation following recombinant Zoster vaccination in a patient with ME/CFS.

text: Immunologically, pre-vaccination profiling revealed elevated monocytes, increased CD71 + erythroid cells, and features of T cell exhaustion marked by Gal-9/PD-1 co-expression and impaired cytokine responses. Post-vaccination, monocyte frequency decreased, Gal-9 + /PD-1 + T cells were reduced, and NK cell degranulation improved, indicating partial restoration of immune function. Conclusion This case demonstrates that immune stimulation via RZV may transiently reverse immune dysfunction and improve clinical symptoms in ME/CFS. These findings support a role for reversible immune exhaustion in disease pathogenesis and highlight potential avenues for biomarker development and therapeutic intervention.
title: Transient clinical improvement and immune modulation following recombinant Zoster vaccination in a patient with ME/CFS.

text: Physiology has long explained organismal stability through homeostasis, allostasis, feedback regulation, and related systems concepts. These frameworks remain essential, but each is most precise at a particular scale or mode of response. This manuscript proposes stratodynamics as a new theory of layered biological response in vertebrate physiology. The framework holds that biological response is organized through seven functional layers: molecular, subcellular, cellular, tissue, organ, systemic, and organismal. The layer names denote the compositional scale of the focal response unit rather than fixed anatomical compartments; layer assignment is functional and response-specific.
title: Stratodynamics: A New Theory of Layered Biological Response.

text: Each layer reduces its own form of mismatch between actual and required state through a scale-appropriate architecture: molecular-state transition, intracellular integration, cellular-state transition, tissue program, organ output, systemic feedback, or organismal anticipation. The layers are coupled upward, downward, and laterally, allowing local events to become systemic responses and allowing organismal state to shape lower-layer readiness. Stratodynamics locates rather than replaces previous theories: homeostasis is preserved as the canonical systemic architecture, allostasis as organismal predictive regulation, and tissue repair, resolution biology, bioelectricity, and thermodynamic self-organization as complementary layer-specific contributors. The framework is presented as a theoretical synthesis and research program for veterinary and medical sciences.
title: Stratodynamics: A New Theory of Layered Biological Response.

text: We described tumor response and survival in dogs with modified Adams stage 4 intranasal tumors treated with once-weekly hypofractionated radiation therapy (RT) combined with the radiosensitizer α-sulfoquinovosyl-acylpropanediol (SQAP), and compared linear and volumetric response assessments. Twenty dogs treated with intensity-modulated RT (8 Gy per fraction, once weekly) and concurrent SQAP were included in this retrospective case series. Tumor response was assessed using RECIST-like linear measurements and volumetric analysis on contrast-enhanced computed tomography. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Of the 20 dogs, 4 were classified as stage 4a and 16 as stage 4b. The best RECIST-like responses were complete response (CR) in 5 dogs, partial response (PR) in 12, and stable disease (SD) in 4. Volumetric responses were CR in 5 dogs, PR in 11, and SD in 5.
title: Clinical Outcomes of Once-Weekly Hypofractionated Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy with Concurrent α-Sulfoquinovosyl-Acylpropanediol for Modified Adams Stage 4 Canine Intranasal Tumors: A Retrospective Case Series.

text: No cases demonstrated progressive disease as the best response. The median OS for all dogs was 342 days (95% confidence interval [CI], 206-419 days). Censoring one non-tumor-related death yielded a median OS of 356 days (95% CI, 231-419 days). Exploratory analysis revealed median OS of 393 and 297 days for stage 4a and 4b dogs, respectively. Volumetric assessment appeared more sensitive for detecting tumor regrowth in selected cases. Dermatologic adverse events were limited to alopecia within the radiation field, and no complete vision loss was observed. Seizure activity was documented in eight dogs. In conclusion, once-weekly hypofractionated intensity-modulated RT combined with concurrent SQAP was associated with clinically meaningful survival outcomes in dogs with advanced intranasal tumors.
title: Clinical Outcomes of Once-Weekly Hypofractionated Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy with Concurrent α-Sulfoquinovosyl-Acylpropanediol for Modified Adams Stage 4 Canine Intranasal Tumors: A Retrospective Case Series.

text: However, because no radiotherapy-alone control group was available, the independent contribution of SQAP to these outcomes could not be determined.
title: Clinical Outcomes of Once-Weekly Hypofractionated Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy with Concurrent α-Sulfoquinovosyl-Acylpropanediol for Modified Adams Stage 4 Canine Intranasal Tumors: A Retrospective Case Series.

text: Chronic renal disease is recognized in geriatric companion mammals, but detailed clinicopathological descriptions in chinchillas remain limited. An 11-year-old neutered female pet chinchilla ( Chinchilla lanigera ) with a six-month history of progressive weight loss and hyporexia developed acute clinical deterioration following approximately 8 h of indoor heat exposure (estimated maximum 29 °C). Anorexia, lethargy, absence of fecal output, and progressive dyspnoea preceded death. Necropsy revealed severe bilateral chronic renal lesions, gastrointestinal gaseous distension, and severe pulmonary congestion. Histopathology documented chronic tubulointerstitial nephropathy with interstitial fibrosis supported by Masson-Goldner trichrome staining and mineral deposits demonstrated by von Kossa staining. Periodic acid-Schiff staining highlighted glomerular and tubular basement membranes.
title: Severe Chronic Tubulointerstitial Nephropathy in a Geriatric Pet Chinchilla (<i>Chinchilla lanigera</i>): A Case Report and Literature Review.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Marked pulmonary vascular congestion was confirmed histologically, whereas pulmonary oedema and established pneumonia were not demonstrated in the examined sections. Together with the progressive terminal dyspnoea, these findings indicated clinically important respiratory abnormalities, although their underlying mechanism and contribution to death remained uncertain. Pure cultures of Klebsiella pneumoniae were recovered from six anatomical sites, with all isolates exhibiting an identical antimicrobial susceptibility profile and a reported multidrug-resistant phenotype. No bacterial-associated inflammatory lesions were identified in the histologically examined tissues, providing no morphological evidence of established disseminated septic disease.
title: Severe Chronic Tubulointerstitial Nephropathy in a Geriatric Pet Chinchilla (<i>Chinchilla lanigera</i>): A Case Report and Literature Review.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Given the uncertain time of death and a possible post-mortem interval of up to approximately 6 h, ante-mortem infection could not be reliably distinguished from perimortem dissemination or post-mortem translocation. Environmental heat exposure may have contributed to acute deterioration in an animal with severe chronic disease, although heat stroke could not be established retrospectively. This case supports a multifactorial interpretation and highlights the potential One Health relevance of antimicrobial resistance in companion animals, without demonstrating transmission.
title: Severe Chronic Tubulointerstitial Nephropathy in a Geriatric Pet Chinchilla (<i>Chinchilla lanigera</i>): A Case Report and Literature Review.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease that affects mainly peripheral joints because of inflammation of the synovial membrane. Current treatments, such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and glucocorticoids, although effective, are associated with high costs and several adverse effects. In this context, natural products have emerged as promising alternatives because of their potential therapeutic effects and lower toxicity. The objective of this review was to identify and evaluate natural substances with potential applications in RA treatment on the basis of studies published between 2015 and 2020. A literature search was conducted in SciELO, PubMed, and Google Scholar using the keywords "rheumatoid arthritis", "treatment", "toxicity", and "natural products".
title: Toxicity of Some Natural Products in the Treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis.

text: Additionally, we applied in silico methods to predict pharmacokinetic and toxicological parameters using ADMET Predictor ® (Simulation Plus) and compared the results with those of commercial drugs such as diclofenac, ibuprofen, and naproxen. Target fishing (reverse docking) was also performed to identify possible molecular targets related to RA. Seven natural compounds were identified, mostly evaluated through in vivo studies. Among them, paeoniflorin, quercetin, resveratrol, and celastrol are in clinical phases and present potential as RA treatments. In silico analysis highlighted curcumin, tetramethylpyrazine, and resveratrol as the most promising candidates, with ADMET profiles comparable or superior to those of current NSAIDs. In conclusion, natural products represent viable alternatives for RA therapy.
title: Toxicity of Some Natural Products in the Treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis.

text: However, further studies are essential to better understand their safety, pharmacokinetics, and drug interactions to ensure their clinical applicability.
title: Toxicity of Some Natural Products in the Treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis.

text: Feline calicivirus (FCV) is a highly heterogeneous pathogen and a major cause of feline upper respiratory tract disease, highlighting the need for continuous surveillance of its genetic diversity and pathogenic characteristics. In this study, we isolated and comprehensively characterized a newly isolated FCV strain, HN/ZZ/2025, from cats at a feline trading market in Zhengzhou, China, and systematically evaluated its molecular features, in vitro replication characteristics, physicochemical properties, and pathogenicity in cats. Phylogenetic analysis classified HN/ZZ/2025 as genotype GI. The isolate replicated efficiently in CRFK, F81, and Fc3Tg cells, reaching peak titers of 10 7.18 , 10 7.50 , and 10 5.89 TCID 50 /0.1 mL, respectively, and exhibited typical calicivirus-like particles with diameters of 35-40 nm.
title: Isolation, Molecular Characterization, and Pathogenicity Evaluation of a Genotype GI Feline Calicivirus Isolate.

text: Complete genome analysis showed that HN/ZZ/2025 shared the highest nucleotide and amino acid sequence identities of 85.7% and 62.8%, respectively, with the closely related Chinese FCV strain CH-JL4, and revealed distinct amino acid variations within the hypervariable E region of the VP1 capsid protein. Experimental infection of cats (n = 3/group) resulted in pyrexia, with rectal temperatures reaching 39.8-40.2 °C, weight loss, oral ulceration, and persistent viral RNA shedding from 1 to 21 days post-infection. Viral RNA and VP1 antigen were detected in the lungs, trachea, kidneys, and spleen, indicating systemic dissemination and broad tissue distribution.
title: Isolation, Molecular Characterization, and Pathogenicity Evaluation of a Genotype GI Feline Calicivirus Isolate.

text: Although no mortality occurred during the observation period, the observed clinical signs, viral dissemination, and histopathological lesions indicate that HN/ZZ/2025 is capable of causing clinically evident disease in experimentally infected cats. These findings provide useful insights into the molecular epidemiology, tissue tropism, and host-virus interactions of circulating FCV strains and establish HN/ZZ/2025 as a useful isolate for future studies of FCV genetic diversity and pathogenesis.
title: Isolation, Molecular Characterization, and Pathogenicity Evaluation of a Genotype GI Feline Calicivirus Isolate.

text: Introduction Cystolithiasis is a common cause of feline lower urinary tract signs (LUTS). Urinary relative supersaturation (RSS) can be used to estimate an animal's risk of crystallogenesis and urolithiasis, with high RSS values representing a potential increased risk of calculogenesis. Objectives were to determine whether an herbal supplement when compared with a placebo would decrease urinary excretion of electrolytes and minerals, increase urine volume, and decrease urine RSS for struvite (RSS S), calcium oxalate monohydrate (RSS COM), and calcium oxalate dihydrate (RSS COD). Methods A randomized cross-over study in which 7 healthy male cats aged 10 months to 5 years received a herbal supplement or placebo for 2 weeks, followed by a five-day washout preceding the crossover treatment period.
title: A placebo-controlled study of an herbal compound used for management of lower urinary tract disease in healthy cats.

text: Voided 24-h urine samples were analyzed for pH and concentrations of sodium, potassium, chloride, calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, ammonia, oxalate, and citrate. RSS COM and RSS COD, and urine volumes were compared between supplement and placebo administration. Results Six cats were included due to incomplete urine collection from one cat. Urine pH and analyte concentrations, 24-h urinary analyte excretions except phosphorus, which was decreased, and RSS COM and RSS COD did not differ between treatments. Struvite RSS was significantly lower in animals treated with the herbal supplement ( p = 0.04). Discussion Significantly lower RSS S with the herbal supplement suggests that it may be useful in preventing struvite crystallogenesis and calculogenesis in cats.
title: A placebo-controlled study of an herbal compound used for management of lower urinary tract disease in healthy cats.

text: This may be important for young to middle-aged cats (ages 1-7 years), who are at greatest risk for struvite crystal-associated lower urinary tract disease.
title: A placebo-controlled study of an herbal compound used for management of lower urinary tract disease in healthy cats.

text: Nutrient availability shapes antibody responses, yet its role in metabolic checkpoints governing germinal center (GC) B-cell differentiation remains incompletely defined. Using heterozygous (HZ) Slc5a6 M60K mice modeling human loss-of-function mutations in the multivitamin transporter SLC5A6, we found that deficient biotin imports impaired mitochondrial metabolism and restricted preGC-to-dark zone progression after vaccination. Single-cell transcriptomics and RNA velocity revealed disrupted GC trajectories, while B-cell receptor repertoire analysis showed impaired class-switch recombination, somatic hypermutation, and vaccine-induced clonal diversity. Spatial multiplexed imaging showed reduced GL7-high GC-associated B-cell regions.
title: Biotin-dependent metabolism controls germinal center fate and vaccine-induced antibody diversification.

text: Flow cytometric analyses revealed reduced frequencies of RBD-specific B cells and RBD-specific GL7 + CD95 + GC B cells in HZ mice, with higher frequencies after biotin supplementation. Pseudovirus assays demonstrated impaired neutralization of Wuhan-Hu-1 and Omicron BA.2. Dietary biotin supplementation restored GC-associated differentiation, antibody diversification, and vaccine-induced humoral responses. These findings identify biotin-dependent mitochondrial metabolism as an important checkpoint linking micronutrient availability to GC B-cell differentiation and vaccine responsiveness.
title: Biotin-dependent metabolism controls germinal center fate and vaccine-induced antibody diversification.

text: Background Conversational AI systems are increasingly being deployed in health care for clinical decision support, but their performance varies substantially across patient communication styles, health literacy levels, and behavioral patterns. Static benchmarks cannot capture multiturn dynamics through which this variation compounds, and no current evaluation framework implements structured AI risk management guidance for conversational health care AI. The result is a structural risk: AI systems may perform well in aggregate while failing disproportionately for the populations they are intended to help.
title: A Patient Simulation Framework for Risk Assessment of Conversational Health Care AI: Development and Evaluation Study.

text: Objective This study aimed to develop and validate a patient simulation framework that aligns with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) Map and Measure functions, providing an empirical basis for identifying and characterizing performance risks in conversational clinical AI across medical, linguistic, and behavioral patient variations. We applied the framework to a conversational decision aid for antidepressant selection in major depressive disorder (the AI decision aid). Methods The simulator integrated three profile dimensions: (1) medical profiles constructed from All of Us electronic health records using risk ratio gating; (2) linguistic profiles modeling a health literacy gradient and condition-specific communication; and (3) behavioral profiles representing cooperative, distracted, and adversarial engagement.
title: A Patient Simulation Framework for Risk Assessment of Conversational Health Care AI: Development and Evaluation Study.

text: We generated 500 simulated conversations and evaluated profile fidelity through human annotation and a large language model (LLM) judge, and then assessed downstream effects on the AI decision aid's concept retrieval and antidepressant recommendations. Results The patient simulator expressed medical concepts with high fidelity (96.6% accuracy across 8210 concepts), with substantial human interannotator agreement (κ=0.73) and LLM-judge agreement against human annotators (κ=0.78). Behavioral profiles were reliably distinguished (κ=0.93; near perfect agreement), and linguistic profiles showed substantial agreement at the lower bound of the substantial range (κ=0.61), which can be considered adequate to support profile-level analysis. The framework revealed monotonic degradation in AI decision aid performance across the health literacy gradient.
title: A Patient Simulation Framework for Risk Assessment of Conversational Health Care AI: Development and Evaluation Study.

text: Rank-1 concept retrieval increased from 47.6% for limited health literacy to 81.9% for proficient health literacy, with corresponding declines in antidepressant recommendation accuracy. Conclusions Patient simulation grounded in the NIST AI RMF exposes measurable performance risks in conversational health care AI that static benchmarks miss, with direct equity implications. Health literacy operates as a structural risk factor, with degraded performance concentrated in patients carrying the greatest burden of psychiatric illness. The framework supports targeted risk-mitigation interventions before deployment. While we evaluated the framework only on antidepressant selection, extending it to other clinical decision-aid tasks remains an assignment for future work.
title: A Patient Simulation Framework for Risk Assessment of Conversational Health Care AI: Development and Evaluation Study.

text: Neurological disorders (ND) pose a major global health challenge, in large part due to the restrictive nature of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which prevents most therapeutic agents from reaching the central nervous system (CNS). Intranasal delivery (IN) offers a non-invasive and patient-friendly route to bypass the BBB via the olfactory and trigeminal pathways, but its success requires advanced nanocarrier systems capable of enhancing drug retention, stability, and controlled release. In this study, a Quality by Design (QbD) framework was applied to systematically develop and optimize 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine (DSPE-PEG 2000 )-functionalized nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) using Donepezil (DPZ) as a model drug.
title: Quality by design (QbD)-guided development of PEGylated nanostructured lipid carriers of donepezil for intranasal delivery.

text: Through sequential risk assessment, Plackett-Burman screening design (PBD), and Central Composite Design (CCD) optimization, the Critical Formulation Variables (CFVs) and Critical Process Parameters (CPPs) influencing particle size (PS) and entrapment efficiency (%EE) were identified. The optimized DSPE-PEG 2000 -NLCs exhibited nanoscale size (133.4 ± 2.91 nm), high %EE (89.5 ± 1.51%), strong mucin binding (84.6 ± 2.68%), and a distinct core-shell morphology. In vitro and ex vivo studies confirmed a biphasic and sustained drug release up to 60 h & 67 h, outperforming uncoated NLCs and conventional formulations. Stability studies demonstrated improved preservation under refrigerated conditions.
title: Quality by design (QbD)-guided development of PEGylated nanostructured lipid carriers of donepezil for intranasal delivery.

text: Beyond DPZ, the QbD-guided strategy presented here provides a generalizable and regulatory-aligned platform for designing IN nanocarriers, paving the way for reproducible, scalable, and translational drug delivery systems targeting a wide range of ND.
title: Quality by design (QbD)-guided development of PEGylated nanostructured lipid carriers of donepezil for intranasal delivery.

text: China's legal system currently lacks a comprehensive animal protection law, and its Criminal Law contains no specific offense for animal cruelty. Consequently, judicial protection for companion animals relies on offenses designed to safeguard human interests, such as intentional destruction of property, theft, and releasing hazardous substances, manifesting a distinct characteristic of indirect protection. This study systematically reviews criminal cases to examine the current state of animal protection provided by Chinese criminal law, identifying the fundamental limitation that such protection is merely incidental or reflective. The research findings indicate that while current frameworks are human-centric, there is significant untapped potential within existing statutes.
title: Protecting Companion Animals Under Chinese Criminal Law: Current Practice and Future Paths.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Specifically, this article advocates for utilizing the crime of illegal use of information networks and other relevant offenses to address the critical regulatory gap concerning the production, sale, and dissemination of animal torture media. This pragmatic solution offers a valuable reference for jurisdictions facing similar legislative voids where specialized animal protection laws are unlikely to be enacted in the short term, promoting a more effective utilization of existing criminal doctrines to safeguard animal welfare.
title: Protecting Companion Animals Under Chinese Criminal Law: Current Practice and Future Paths.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: The hyperphosphorylated Tau (p-Tau) protein plays a central role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) by driving neurofibrillary tangle formation and neuronal dysfunction. While proteolysis targeting chimeras (PROTACs) offer a promising approach for directly eliminating pathogenic proteins, their real-time visualization in living systems remains challenging. Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of a series of near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent Tau-targeting degraders that integrate theranostic imaging with targeted protein degradation. Among them, compound D9 emerges as a dual-functional degrader capable of both high-contrast fluorescence tracking and potent Tau clearance at 10 nM. Mechanistic investigations indicate that D9 induces Tau degradation through activation of the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), as confirmed by inhibitor assays.
title: Near-Infrared Fluorescent PROTAC Enables Theranostic Imaging and Selective Tau Degradation in Alzheimer's Disease.

text: Beyond Tau degradation, D9 also downregulates amyloid precursor protein (APP) and β-amyloid (Aβ) expression, suggesting broader neuroprotective effects. In in vivo studies, D9 significantly promotes p-Tau clearance and alleviates cognitive deficits in 3 ×Tg-AD mice. These findings demonstrate that D9 represents a first-in-class NIR fluorescent PROTAC for theranostic imaging and targeted degradation of Tau, providing a powerful platform for visualizing degradation dynamics and developing next-generation AD therapeutics.
title: Near-Infrared Fluorescent PROTAC Enables Theranostic Imaging and Selective Tau Degradation in Alzheimer's Disease.

text: Marinobufagin (MBG), a cardiotonic steroid from Rhinella toads, exhibits potent antitumor activity. However, their involvement in the mammalian neurotoxicity remains unclear. Therefore, this study evaluated the systemic (neuro)toxicological action of MBG to understand its central effects, particularly those associated with seizure-inducing activity. Initially, physicochemical, pharmacokinetic, and drug-likeness profiles and molecular docking with receptors/channels were investigated by in silico platforms. Next, the pro-convulsive action of MBG was investigated using pharmacological modulators for specific neurotransmission pathways and in vitro inhibitory activity of acetylcholinesterase was quantified. MBG has intestinal absorption and capacity to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB), binds strongly to plasma proteins, and acts as an inhibitory substrate for the CYP3A4 enzyme.
title: Central toxic effects of an antitumoral bufadienolide: In silico targets and in vivo findings.

text: It was classified as a drug-like molecule according to Lipinski's rule and ineligible according to the Lead-like and World Drug Index criteria. Molecular docking emphasized the interaction of MBG with ictogenesis-related targets, confirmed by reduction of in vivo seizures and death of pretreated animals with pharmacological blockers for dopamine D2 and glutamate NMDA receptors and Na v 1.2 channels, mainly. It was shown that affinity of MBG for excitatory targets is essential for neuronal excitability and onset of seizures and that interaction with GABA A receptors is involved in bufadienolide-induced lethality. The findings also suggest that MBG-induced seizures may involve in silico binding to NMDA receptors and interactions with key excitatory (Na v 1.2 channels and NMDA receptor) and inhibitory (GABA A and D2 receptors) neuronal targets, contributing to altered neuronal excitability.
title: Central toxic effects of an antitumoral bufadienolide: In silico targets and in vivo findings.

text: Notably, it is the first report that characterized MBG-induced seizures and proposes it as a promising chemical option to understand ictogenesis and mechanism(s) of new anticonvulsive agents.
title: Central toxic effects of an antitumoral bufadienolide: In silico targets and in vivo findings.

text: Background and aim Long-acting methylprednisolone acetate (MPA) is widely used in canine medicine for its prolonged glucocorticoid activity. However, uncertainty remains regarding its disease-specific efficacy, safety profile, and overall benefit-risk balance across different routes of administration. This critically appraised topic (CAT) aimed to systematically evaluate and synthesize the available evidence on the efficacy, safety, and clinical applications of depot MPA in dogs, with emphasis on clinically meaningful outcomes and evidence-based recommendations for veterinary practice. Materials and methods A structured literature search was performed in PubMed, CAB Abstracts, and Scopus from database inception to May 17, 2026.
title: Evidence for long-acting methylprednisolone acetate in dogs: A critically appraised topic on efficacy, safety, and clinical applications across administration routes.

text: Eligible studies evaluated depot MPA administered through any route in dogs and reported clinical efficacy, safety outcomes, pharmacokinetics, endocrine responses, or clinicopathological changes. Study quality was assessed using design-specific risk-of-bias tools, including Cochrane RoB 2, ROBINS-I, and SYRCLE's risk-of-bias tool. Data were synthesized narratively todue of substantial heterogeneity in study designs, routes of administration, and outcome measures.
