title: Review and analysis of knowledge, tools, and implementation gaps for the control of cryptosporidiosis in livestock.

text: This means that on-farm operations, including biosecurity measures and management of slurry and manure, should be used in combination with pharmaceutical treatment and vaccination. However, the efficacy of such measures needs further investigation.This review is based on the recently updated DISCONTOOLS analysis, which identifies knowledge gaps and advances the development and implementation of new tools for controlling cryptosporidiosis in livestock. While vaccination and treatment have important roles, appropriate farm management, especially good farm hygiene, as well as handling and treatment of manure, remains a vital component for reducing the risk of cryptosporidiosis.
title: Review and analysis of knowledge, tools, and implementation gaps for the control of cryptosporidiosis in livestock.

text: Erythropoiesis-targeted doping remains a major challenge for sports medicine because pharmacological and genetic manipulation of erythropoiesis can improve oxygen transport and endurance performance while increasing the risk of serious cardiovascular complications. Erythropoiesis-targeting strategies extend beyond recombinant erythropoietin (EPO) to include hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitors (HIF-PHIs), modified erythropoietin receptor (EPOR) agonists, transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling inhibitors, cytoprotective EPO derivatives, and gene- or cell-based approaches, and require complementary detection strategies based on direct analytical methods and the Athlete Biological Passport (ABP).
title: Erythropoiesis-Targeted Doping in Sports: From Improved Oxygen Transport to Cardiovascular Risk.
journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

text: Although they may enhance oxygen delivery and endurance performance, excessive stimulation of erythropoiesis may increase blood viscosity, impair vascular function, and elevate the risk of hypertension, thromboembolic complications, and other cardiovascular (CV) events. Erythropoiesis-targeted doping has evolved beyond recombinant EPO into a diverse group of pharmacological and genetic strategies that require increasingly sophisticated detection approaches. A thorough understanding of their molecular mechanisms and cardiovascular consequences is essential for improving anti-doping surveillance and protecting athlete health. This review summarizes current erythropoiesis-targeting agents, their mechanisms of action, detection strategies, cardiovascular risks, and implications for anti-doping practice.
title: Erythropoiesis-Targeted Doping in Sports: From Improved Oxygen Transport to Cardiovascular Risk.
journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

text: Objectives While rates of self-harm are rising in the United Kingdom, people who self-harm can often struggle to access appropriate treatment. This study sought to explore adult stakeholders' perspectives and experiences of the barriers to, and facilitators of, accessing support for self-harm and also how services could be better tailored to meet needs. Design A cross-sectional qualitative study. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted remotely with 19 participants in the United Kingdom, including 10 individuals with lived experience of self-harm and nine mental health professionals that worked with people who self-harm. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to analyse the data. Normalisation Process Theory (NPT) was used as a guiding framework throughout the study.
title: Experiences of accessing psychological therapies for self-harm: A qualitative study of stakeholders' perspectives.

text: Results Both stakeholder groups felt that services did not offer appropriate support; there were system-level challenges and a sense of associated powerlessness. It was important to understand the person behind the behaviour, as a lack of understanding was reported to increase feelings of shame. Services that prioritise person-centred care, expert-by-experience involvement and early intervention were valued. Professionals outlined the positives of brief interventions, while individuals who self-harm held concerns about whether briefer interventions addressed complex difficulties. Conclusions Findings highlight important organisational barriers and potential facilitators that individuals who self-harm may face when accessing psychological interventions. Results prompt the need for inclusive and easily accessible services.
title: Experiences of accessing psychological therapies for self-harm: A qualitative study of stakeholders' perspectives.

text: Kobuviruses are emerging enteric pathogens with broad host ranges, yet their pathogenic potential in wild large felids remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first case of severe enteric and respiratory disease associated with AiV-A infection in a large felid, designated FeKoV0813, in a captive juvenile white lion ( Panthera leo ). The animal presented with acute respiratory distress and severe diarrhea, culminating in death despite supportive care. Comprehensive diagnostic workflows, including necropsy, histopathology, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and absolute quantitative RT-PCR, were employed to determine tissue tropism and viral dissemination. Whole-genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and selection pressure assessment were conducted to characterize the viral evolutionary dynamics and host-specific constraints.
title: Aichivirus a Infection Associated with Severe Enteric and Respiratory Disease in a Captive White Lion (<i>Panthera leo</i>).

text: The 8213-nucleotide genome exhibited typical Kobuvirus organization, clustering within the AiV-A clade alongside carnivore-derived strains from dogs, cats, and foxes. High viral RNA loads were detected primarily in the small intestine (~7.4 log 10 copies/100 ng RNA) and trachea, with dissemination to the kidney and pancreas. Histopathological analysis revealed epithelial lesions, and FISH localized viral RNA to these affected epithelial cells, while transcriptomic profiling revealed higher transcript abundance of CXCL8 and other pro-inflammatory genes in the intestine than in other tissues. Notably, selection pressure analysis indicated strong purifying selection acting on the feline VP1 gene, with no positively selected sites identified, contrasting with signatures of episodic positive selection observed in human and rodent lineages.
title: Aichivirus a Infection Associated with Severe Enteric and Respiratory Disease in a Captive White Lion (<i>Panthera leo</i>).

text: This study provides the first report of severe respiratory and gastrointestinal disease associated with AiV-A infection in large felids, significantly expanding the known host range of kobuviruses. Our findings underscore the need for vigilant surveillance of kobuviruses in captive wildlife and highlight the potential risk of spillover infections from domestic carnivore reservoirs.
title: Aichivirus a Infection Associated with Severe Enteric and Respiratory Disease in a Captive White Lion (<i>Panthera leo</i>).

text: Oxidative stress and intestinal health are critical factors that are closely linked to the production performance and physiological status of laying hens. This work assessed how dietary incorporation of Pieris japonica leaf powder (PJP) shapes egg quality attributes, hepatic antioxidant defence, gut tissue morphology, and cecal microbial community profiles in layers. A total of 360 healthy 56-week-old Hy-Line Brown layers were randomly assigned to four treatments, each containing six replicate pens housing 15 birds apiece. Animals received basal feeds containing 0.00% (control), 0.05%, 0.10%, or 0.20% PJP throughout the 10-week experimental run that including a 2-week adaptation period. Relative to the control group, diets with 0.05% PJP significantly increased eggshell thickness ( p p Collinsella relative abundance ( p < 0.05).
title: Dietary <i>Pieris japonica</i> Leaf Powder Enhances Hepatic Antioxidant Capacity, Modulates Cecal Microbiota, and Improves Eggshell Thickness in Laying Hens.

text: Noticeably, the 0.20% supplementation exerted adverse effects on egg-related indices. Correlation analysis indicated that cecal microbiota was closely associated with hepatic antioxidant indices and eggshell-related indicators. In summary, dietary PJP inclusion may improve the eggshell thickness of eggs from laying hens by enhancing host antioxidant defense, reshaping the composition of cecal microbial communities. It was reported that 0.10% PJP supplementation yielded the most favorable comprehensive responses under the conditions adopted within this trial.
title: Dietary <i>Pieris japonica</i> Leaf Powder Enhances Hepatic Antioxidant Capacity, Modulates Cecal Microbiota, and Improves Eggshell Thickness in Laying Hens.

text: Methaemoglobin (MetHb) is an oxidised form of haemoglobin (Hb) unable to bind oxygen. Raised levels of MetHb reduce the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity, causing potentially severe hypoxaemia and possible death. The condition arises from three main pathologies: mutations in globin genes causing Haemoglobin-M, inherited deficiency of the enzyme cytochrome b5 reductase (CytB5R) responsible for reducing MetHb back into functional Hb, and exposure to some oxidising agents. Well-documented causative agents include dapsone and cocaine-derived anaesthetics, with emerging evidence highlighting an increasing contribution from recreational and non-prescribed exposures. As the concentration of MetHb level increases, the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood decreases. MetHb levels are usually measured by co-oximetry.
title: Methaemoglobinaemia: From pathophysiology to contemporary clinical management.

text: Patients are typically asymptomatic at MetHb concentrations <10% with symptoms developing as levels increase, including cyanosis, confusion, arrhythmias, coma and death. These features will present alongside misleadingly normal partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood and arterial oxygen saturation values on arterial blood gas and will not improve with supplemental oxygen. Management depends on severity, with intravenous methylene blue remaining first-line treatment for symptomatic cases. Alternative therapies include high-dose vitamin C, exchange transfusion and potentially hyperbaric oxygen, although there is little evidence to suggest how these should be used. Due to the potentially confusing acute presentation of the condition, the diagnosis can easily be missed.
title: Methaemoglobinaemia: From pathophysiology to contemporary clinical management.

text: Obesity is a multifactorial condition that profoundly affects female reproductive health through endocrine, metabolic, and inflammatory mechanisms that disrupt the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis. Women with obesity frequently develop menstrual irregularities, anovulation, amenorrhea, infertility, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), impaired endometrial receptivity, and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Central obesity and insulin resistance contribute to hyperinsulinemia, reduced sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) levels, hyperandrogenism, altered gonadotropin secretion, and impaired folliculogenesis, while adipokines such as leptin and chronic inflammation further impair ovarian steroidogenesis and ovulatory function.
title: Therapeutic Potential of Anti-Obesity Drugs in Obesity-Associated Female Reproductive Dysfunction: Translating Mechanistic Evidence into Personalized Clinical Strategies.

text: Obesity-related oxidative stress and lipotoxicity also negatively affect oocyte quality, embryo development, implantation, and assisted reproductive technology outcomes, increasing the risk of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, miscarriage, and preterm birth. This review evaluates the therapeutic potential of pharmacological weight-loss therapies in obesity-associated female reproductive dysfunction. A comprehensive literature review was conducted using various databases, focusing on anti-obesity pharmacotherapy on obesity, infertility and fertility in reproductive-aged women.
title: Therapeutic Potential of Anti-Obesity Drugs in Obesity-Associated Female Reproductive Dysfunction: Translating Mechanistic Evidence into Personalized Clinical Strategies.

text: Evidence suggests that several FDA-approved and off-label anti-obesity agents, including orlistat, liraglutide, semaglutide, phentermine/topiramate, bupropion/naltrexone, metformin, exenatide, and tirzepatide, may improve reproductive outcomes primarily indirectly through weight reduction and metabolic improvement. GLP-1 receptor agonists, particularly liraglutide, semaglutide, and exenatide, appear especially promising, demonstrating beneficial effects on insulin sensitivity, menstrual regularity, ovulation, androgen levels, and pregnancy rates in women with PCOS. Tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist, has shown potent weight-loss and metabolic effects with potential indirect fertility benefits.
title: Therapeutic Potential of Anti-Obesity Drugs in Obesity-Associated Female Reproductive Dysfunction: Translating Mechanistic Evidence into Personalized Clinical Strategies.

text: Metformin improves insulin sensitivity and is widely used in PCOS to regulate androgen levels and restore ovulation, although its effects on pregnancy and live birth rates remain controversial. However, evidence for several agents remains limited, and concerns persist regarding reproductive safety during pregnancy. Overall, anti-obesity pharmacotherapy may represent an important adjunctive strategy for improving reproductive and metabolic health in women with obesity, although larger randomized clinical trials are still required.
title: Therapeutic Potential of Anti-Obesity Drugs in Obesity-Associated Female Reproductive Dysfunction: Translating Mechanistic Evidence into Personalized Clinical Strategies.

text: Background Veterinary epidemiology studies of the Miniature Schnauzer have revealed high prevalence of several breed-associated diseases. However, owner-reported disease data has not been evaluated, particularly with respect to pancreatic diseases, for which this breed is considered predisposed. This study aimed to examine Miniature Schnauzer health from the owner perspective, and explore relationships between reported pancreatitis and other conditions. Methods An online survey open to UK-based owners of Miniature Schnauzers in 2023, including directed disease-specific questions and opportunity for free-text reporting. Analyses were performed using R, including multivariable logistic regression modelling. Results Responses from 4,786 owners were received, of which 2,910 contained sufficient data for analysis.
title: Prevalence of pancreatitis in UK Miniature Schnauzers: insights from an owner survey-based study.

text: The most prevalent diseases reported were categorised as "dermatological", "mass-associated" and "allergic". Pancreatitis was reported in 7.6% of dogs. A reported diagnosis of pancreatitis was also associated with increased odds of a diabetes mellitus diagnosis. Hyperlipidaemia was reported in 1% of all Miniature Schnauzers, increasing to 3.3% of dogs over the age of 9 years. Conclusions This study identifies a high owner-reported prevalence of pancreatitis in UK Miniature Schnauzers, differing from previous veterinary epidemiological studies. The findings highlight the value of incorporating owner-reported data into breed health research and underscores the importance of effective communication between clinician and owner.
title: Prevalence of pancreatitis in UK Miniature Schnauzers: insights from an owner survey-based study.

text: H3 subtype avian influenza virus (AIV) is one of the most widely distributed and frequently detected low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (LPAIVs) in wild birds and poultry worldwide. Wild waterfowl are the natural reservoir of this virus. In recent years, driven by frequent genetic reassortment and continuous evolution, H3 subtype AIV has expanded its host range to include various mammalian species-dogs, cats, horses, seals, pigs (experimental infection), and humans. Among these, the H3N8 subtype shows the broadest cross-species transmissibility, having established sustained transmission lineages in horses and dogs, while also causing sporadic infections in seals and humans. Avian-origin H3N2 canine influenza virus has circulated stably in dog populations across Asia and North America for nearly two decades.
title: H3 Subtype Avian Influenza Virus: Ecology, Cross-Species Evolution, and Public Health Threats.

text: Between 2022 and 2023, China reported three human cases of H3N8 subtype AIV infection, one of which was fatal (Guangdong, March 2023), indicating that this virus poses a potential zoonotic transmission risk. Novel triple-reassortant strains, including genotype G25 of H3N8 and H3N3, first detected in chicken flocks in late 2022, have continued to emerge. Their HA genes originate from H3 subtype viruses of wild bird or chicken origin, whereas their internal gene segments are predominantly acquired from H9N2 subtype AIV, resulting in enhanced mammalian adaptability. This review summarizes the global epidemiology of H3 subtype AIV (covering wild birds, poultry, and live poultry markets), its genetic evolution and reassortment patterns, and the molecular mechanisms underlying cross-species transmission.
title: H3 Subtype Avian Influenza Virus: Ecology, Cross-Species Evolution, and Public Health Threats.

text: This review particularly highlights the regulatory roles of key amino acid mutations-such as PB2-D701N, M1-M192V, and HA-Q226L/G228S-in receptor binding preference, polymerase activity, and pathogenicity. This review also summarizes recent advances in detection techniques (multiplex RT-PCR, quantum dot-based immunochromatographic strips, RT-RAA, and CRISPR-Cas13a) and vaccine development (inactivated, adenovirus-vectored, and mRNA vaccines). Key prevention and control challenges-including covert circulation, surveillance gaps, and limited subtyping diagnostic capacity at primary laboratories-are also discussed. This review proposes that H3 subtype AIV should be recognized as a potential zoonotic threat warranting continued surveillance, although no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission has been documented to date.
title: H3 Subtype Avian Influenza Virus: Ecology, Cross-Species Evolution, and Public Health Threats.

text: Better understanding of cross-species mechanisms, stronger surveillance and early warning, and evidence-based control strategies are needed to inform future risk assessment.
title: H3 Subtype Avian Influenza Virus: Ecology, Cross-Species Evolution, and Public Health Threats.

text: Background Ceratopogonid midges of the genus Forcipomyia (subgenus Lasiohelea) are small hematophagous insects widely distributed across tropical regions. In Australia, developmental stages of Leishmania (Mundinia) macropodum have been observed in Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea), suggesting that biting midges may play a role in Leishmania transmission beyond traditional sand fly vectors. However, in Southeast Asia-where leishmaniasis caused by Mundinia species is an emerging autochthonous disease in humans-fundamental information on Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea) diversity and its association with Leishmania remains limited.
title: Integrative morphological and DNA barcoding analysis of Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea) midges: cryptic diversity and first molecular detection of multiple Leishmania species in a leishmaniasis-endemic focus in Southern Thailand.

text: Methods An integrated morphological-molecular approach was employed to characterize Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea) midges collected using sweep nets from a leishmaniasis-endemic area in Nakhon Si Thammarat Province, Southern Thailand, near the residence of a patient with locally acquired cutaneous leishmaniasis, during January and June 2025. Morphological examination of mandibular dentition, sensory pits, cibarial armature, and spermathecal structure was combined with mitochondrial cox1 barcoding, Bayesian and maximum likelihood phylogenetic analyses, and species delimitation methods (ASAP and mPTP). Because females of the subgenus Lasiohelea possess a single spermatheca, only single-spermatheca females were selected for species identification.
title: Integrative morphological and DNA barcoding analysis of Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea) midges: cryptic diversity and first molecular detection of multiple Leishmania species in a leishmaniasis-endemic focus in Southern Thailand.

text: Specimens identified as Lasiohelea were subsequently screened for Leishmania using 18S rRNA-qPCR and ITS1-PCR, followed by nanopore-based ITS1 metabarcoding for species-level identification. Vertebrate blood meal sources were also characterized using vertebrate cox1 metabarcoding. Results From 264 collected midges, 72 female specimens with a single spermatheca were selected for analysis. Integrated morphological and molecular data identified seven Lasiohelea specimens forming four genetic clusters, comprising F. (L.) parvitas (n = 2) and three lineages closely related to F. (L.) peditata (n = 2), F. (L.) humilavolita (n = 2), and F. (L.) taiwana (n = 1). These were clearly separated from non-Lasiohelea taxa, including F. (Euprojoannisia) fuscimana and two unclassified Ceratopogonidae lineages.
title: Integrative morphological and DNA barcoding analysis of Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea) midges: cryptic diversity and first molecular detection of multiple Leishmania species in a leishmaniasis-endemic focus in Southern Thailand.

text: Phylogenetic and species delimitation analyses revealed cryptic genetic diversity despite morphological similarity. Leishmania DNA was detected in six of seven Lasiohelea specimens. Nanopore ITS1 metabarcoding identified autochthonous species (L. (Mundinia) martiniquensis and L. (M.) orientalis) and additional Leishmania species (L. (Leishmania) amazonensis and L. (L.) major), including mixed-species detections in four specimens. A single engorged specimen contained DNA from red junglefowl (Gallus gallus spadiceus). Conclusions This study provides the first integrated characterization of Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea) diversity and associated Leishmania detection in Southeast Asia.
title: Integrative morphological and DNA barcoding analysis of Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea) midges: cryptic diversity and first molecular detection of multiple Leishmania species in a leishmaniasis-endemic focus in Southern Thailand.

text: The results identified several putatively distinct species within Lasiohelea and provide evidence of natural exposure of these midges to multiple Leishmania species, suggesting a complex parasite-midge association and parasite co-circulation in the local environment. Although vector competence was not assessed, these findings suggest that Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea) may be involved in the circulation of Leishmania parasites and may represent promising candidates for further investigation of vector competence. Future studies focusing on host associations, parasite development, and experimental transmission are needed to clarify their epidemiological significance.
title: Integrative morphological and DNA barcoding analysis of Forcipomyia (Lasiohelea) midges: cryptic diversity and first molecular detection of multiple Leishmania species in a leishmaniasis-endemic focus in Southern Thailand.

text: Background/objectives Intranasal tumors are common malignancies in dogs, characterized by locally aggressive behavior and clinical signs such as epistaxis, nasal discharge, and facial deformity. Radiotherapy (RT) is considered the treatment of choice due to anatomical limitations to surgical resection. This study aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes, toxicity, and prognostic factors in dogs with primary malignant intranasal tumors treated with cobalt-60-based megavoltage radiotherapy. Methods This retrospective study included 40 dogs with histopathologically confirmed primary malignant intranasal tumors treated between September 2018 and February 2025 at a veterinary radiotherapy clinic in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Medical records were reviewed for patient demographics, tumor characteristics, treatment protocols, response, toxicity, and survival outcomes.
title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes in Dogs with Malignant Intranasal Tumors Treated with Radiotherapy: A Retrospective Study of 40 Cases.

text: Tumors were staged using modified Adams criteria based on computed tomography. Definitive-intent protocols ( n = 32) delivered 48-54 Gy in 10-13 fractions administered three to five times weekly, while palliative protocols consisted of either four fractions of 8 Gy delivered once weekly or five fractions of 4 Gy delivered daily. Results Adenocarcinoma was the most common histologic subtype (42.5%), and 82.5% of dogs had stage III-IV disease. The objective response rate was 82.5% (CR: 17.5%; PR: 65.0%), with clinical benefit observed in 92.5% of cases. Acute toxicity was frequent but manageable, primarily affecting skin, oral mucosa, and eyes. Overall median progression-free interval (PFI) and survival time (MST) were 382 days and 430 days, respectively. Stage IV disease was significantly associated with shorter survival when compared to stage I-III (MST 345 vs.
title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes in Dogs with Malignant Intranasal Tumors Treated with Radiotherapy: A Retrospective Study of 40 Cases.

text: 1063 days, respectively; p = 0.016). Treatment response was significantly associated with PFI in univariate analysis ( p Conclusions Radiotherapy provided high response rates and meaningful clinical benefit with acceptable toxicity in dogs with malignant intranasal tumors, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and treatment. Further prospective studies with standardized protocols are warranted.
title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes in Dogs with Malignant Intranasal Tumors Treated with Radiotherapy: A Retrospective Study of 40 Cases.

text: Purpose To describe cases of canine idiopathic periocular granulomatous inflammation. Material and methods Clinical records were reviewed. Animal studied At the time of presentation, the four patients (German Shepherd dog, mixed breed, Magyar Vizsla, Hovawart) were 1.5-5 (mean 3.75) years old. All dogs were female; two were spayed. Lesions were unilateral in 3/4 cases. Dogs presented with ulcerated (1) or non-ulcerated (3) mass lesions affecting the periocular skin (3/4), medial canthal area (2/4), or third eyelid (1/4). Results Incisional biopsies revealed pyogranulomatous inflammation in three and granulomatous inflammation in one case. There was no evidence of microbial infection in the specimens. Patients received anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive dosages of systemic corticosteroids.
title: Idiopathic Granulomatous Inflammation of the Periocular Structures in Four Dogs: Clinical, Histopathological, and Imaging Findings and Therapeutic Outcome.

text: Three dogs also received systemic cyclosporin (5 mg/kg, sid), and one dog received topical cyclosporin (0.1%, bid). One dog underwent surgical debulking of a circumscribed mass within the left lower eyelid prior to immunosuppressive therapy and developed an additional swelling on the left upper eyelid. Remission of clinical signs was achieved in all patients. Dogs were treated for 5 to 11 months (mean 8.7). No recurrence was reported in 4/4 patients during a mean follow-up period of 17.3 months. In 3/4patients, there was no recurrence within an average of 11 months after discontinuation of therapy. One dog was lost to follow-up. Conclusion Idiopathic granulomatous inflammation is a differential diagnosis for periocular mass lesions. Its diagnosis is based on histopathology and the exclusion of other causes of granulomatous inflammation.
title: Idiopathic Granulomatous Inflammation of the Periocular Structures in Four Dogs: Clinical, Histopathological, and Imaging Findings and Therapeutic Outcome.

text: Background Dietary management plays a central role in the diagnosis and treatment of chronic enteropathy (CE) in dogs. Although hydrolyzed-protein diets are commonly used in patients with CE, and dietary fat restriction is recommended in selected gastrointestinal disorders, the combined effect of low fat and hydrolyzed protein has not been specifically evaluated. Hypothesis/objectives Assess clinical response and acceptability of a low-fat, hydrolyzed diet in dogs with CE. Animals Thirty-one client-owned dogs. Methods Prospective clinical study. Dogs were fed a commercial low-fat (2.01 g/100 kcal metabolizable energy) hydrolyzed salmon protein diet and stratified according to previous dietary history. Dogs were evaluated at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months.
title: Use of a novel low-fat hydrolyzed diet in the management of dogs with chronic enteropathy.

text: The primary outcome was clinical response, classified as complete response (CR), partial response (PR), or non-response (NR) based on gastrointestinal signs and the Canine Inflammatory Bowel Disease Activity Index (CIBDAI) score. Dogs with CR or PR were considered responders. Diet acceptability was assessed. Results At T1, 20 of 31 (64.5%) dogs were categorized as CR, 3 of 31 (9.7%) as PR, and 8 of 31 (25.8%) as NR. Twenty-three of 31 (74.2%) dogs had a positive clinical response. The CIBDAI scores decreased significantly from T0 to T1 (P Conclusions and clinical importance This low-fat, hydrolyzed diet had significant short- and mid-term effectiveness and was well tolerated in dogs with CE, reinforcing its potential as a treatment for food-responsive enteropathy.
title: Use of a novel low-fat hydrolyzed diet in the management of dogs with chronic enteropathy.

text: We evaluated the antiviral activity of a library of 36 urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) against human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV). Structure-spectrum analysis revealed virus-specific structural requirements for antiviral efficacy. By combining the key determinants identified for each virus, we rationally designed optimized dual-acting derivatives. Among these, the optimized compound F832/33 emerged as a potent, broad-spectrum antiviral agent with nanomolar activity against both hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar inhibition of cyclophilin (Cyp) peptidyl-prolyl isomerase (PPIase) activity, and no detectable cytotoxicity. Interestingly, no direct correlation was observed between Cyp PPIase inhibition and antiviral potency, suggesting that Cyp engagement rather than enzymatic inhibition per se is required for antiviral activity.
title: Optimization of the antiviral spectrum of cyclophilin inhibitors targeting respiratory viruses.

text: Competition assays with alisporivir confirmed that the antiviral effects of SMCypIs depend on their specific interaction with Cyp. Beyond its dual efficacy, F832/33 displayed strong antiviral activity against additional clinically relevant respiratory pathogens, including parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and both ancestral and Omicron severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 strains, in immortalized cell lines and fully differentiated human nasal epithelial cells, a physiologically relevant model of respiratory infection. Collectively, our results demonstrate that structure-activity relationship-guided optimization can be successfully applied to expand the antiviral spectrum of SMCypIs, positioning F832/33 as a promising host-targeted broad-spectrum antiviral candidate.
title: Optimization of the antiviral spectrum of cyclophilin inhibitors targeting respiratory viruses.

text: Further in vivo studies are warranted to evaluate its therapeutic potential and clarify its precise mechanism of action.
title: Optimization of the antiviral spectrum of cyclophilin inhibitors targeting respiratory viruses.

text: Clinically, TP53 mutation ( TP53 -mut) has long been simplistically dichotomized as mutant versus wildtype, overlooking their structural and functional complexity. The prognostic significance of TP53 ‑mut in IDH ‑wildtype ( IDH ‑wt) gliomas remains controversial. In 237 IDH ‑wt gliomas, we integrated clinical, genomic, and follow‑up data to test whether mutation subtypes refine risk stratification. In this cohort, 73 patients (73/237, 30.8%) harbored TP53 -mut, which was significantly associated with worse overall survival. Subgroup analysis further revealed that patients with mutations in the β‑strand region had a median outcome of only 12.0 months, markedly inferior to those with mutations in the α‑helix (22.5 months), loop (23.9 months), and turn/other regions (23.6 months).
title: <i>TP53</i> Mutation Heterogeneity Refines Prognostic Stratification in <i>IDH</i>-Wildtype Glioma.

text: Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that TP53 -mut was an independent prognostic factor associated with worse outcome (HR = 1.91; 95%CI: 1.29-2.84; p = 0.001). Notably, TP53 ‑mut patients with variant allele frequency (VAF)≥10% showed significantly worse survival than those with VAF p = 0.030), whereas VAF TP53 ‑wt. In addition, p53 immunohistochemistry score≥4 yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.79 for TP53 -mut prediction. Collectively, TP53 -mut in IDH ‑wt gliomas are prognostically heterogeneous. A VAF≥ 10% identified a potential high‑risk subgroup, with β-strand mutations associated with the poorest survival in our cohort. p53 immunohistochemistry offers a cost‑effective surrogate screen.
title: <i>TP53</i> Mutation Heterogeneity Refines Prognostic Stratification in <i>IDH</i>-Wildtype Glioma.

text: Peripheral nerve injuries of the hand are common; however, exteriorization of a nerve fascicle following minor trauma is exceedingly rare. We present the case of an 80-year-old female who sustained a cat scratch to the dorsum of the hand, resulting in extrusion of a threadlike structure later confirmed to be neural tissue. Initial management included conservative wound care and submission of the specimen as a presumed foreign body. Due to limited clinical information, the specimen underwent gross examination only and was nearly discarded. Following direct communication with pathology, frozen section analysis confirmed the presence of a nerve fascicle. This case highlights the importance of anatomical recognition, accurate specimen labeling, and interdisciplinary communication.
title: Cat Anatomist: Exteriorization of a Presumed Digital Nerve Fascicle Following a Cat Scratch Injury.

text: It also demonstrates a unique mechanism of peripheral nerve injury involving traction and exteriorization along the presumed course of a dorsal digital nerve.
title: Cat Anatomist: Exteriorization of a Presumed Digital Nerve Fascicle Following a Cat Scratch Injury.

text: Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) threatens small-ruminant production in Pakistan, particularly where livestock grazing overlaps with wildlife habitats. In this exploratory cross-sectional study (January-June 2024), 1939 sera from goats ( n = 1327) and sheep ( n = 612) in 56 herds, purposively selected near eight protected wildlife areas, were tested for antibodies against PPR virus (PPRV) using a competitive ELISA. Vaccinated and unvaccinated animals were included, and the assay cannot distinguish vaccine-induced from infection-induced antibodies. The overall apparent antibody seroprevalence was 38.5% (747/1939; 95% CI: 36.4-40.7%) (naive 95% CI; it ignores clustering and understates uncertainty, and between-site heterogeneity was very high, I 2 = 94%), ranging from 16.7% in Peshawar to 73.0% at Kirthar National Park, Sindh.
title: Seroprevalence of Peste des Petits Ruminants Virus Antibodies and Associated Factors in Small Ruminants Sampled Around Protected Wildlife Areas in Pakistan.

text: Crude odds of seropositivity were higher in goats than in sheep (44.8% vs. 25.0%; OR = 2.43, 95% CI: 1.97-3.01), in animals older than three years than in those aged > 1-3 years (52.0% vs. 33.8%; OR = 2.13, 95% CI: 1.69-2.67), and in herds with more than 100 animals than in herds with 50-100 animals (43.3% vs. 35.7%; OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.11-1.72). After adjustment for site, goats remained more likely to be seropositive than sheep (OR = 2.19, 95% CI: 1.76-2.74), although the species difference varied between sites (heterogeneity p = 0.005). Herd-level clustering could not be modelled; associations with herd-level factors (herd size, vaccination status) were sensitive to plausible within-herd correlation and are exploratory. Vaccination categories are reported descriptively only. PPRV antibodies were common in small ruminants sampled near the selected protected areas.
title: Seroprevalence of Peste des Petits Ruminants Virus Antibodies and Associated Factors in Small Ruminants Sampled Around Protected Wildlife Areas in Pakistan.

text: However, wildlife were not sampled, distance categories were confounded with site, and results are not nationally representative; transmission at the livestock-wildlife interface was not demonstrated. Targeted surveillance and integrated livestock-wildlife studies are warranted.
title: Seroprevalence of Peste des Petits Ruminants Virus Antibodies and Associated Factors in Small Ruminants Sampled Around Protected Wildlife Areas in Pakistan.

text: Infectious diseases in swine demand affordable, broad-spectrum antiviral strategies, such as recombinant interferons (IFNs). However, commercial yeast expression platforms often present financial barriers through licensing royalties. To provide a cost-effective regional alternative, we evaluated the domestic, thermotolerant yeast Ogataea polymorpha OP39 for producing recombinant porcine IFNs. Recombinant OP39 strains carrying expression cassettes for types I (poIFN-α1), II (poIFN-γ), and III (poIFN-λ3) IFNs were constructed and evaluated for their recombinant protein production performance. Following initial screening, the highest-yielding candidate, poIFN-α1, was selected for bioprocess optimization in shake flasks and a 5 L fermenter. Results showed that OP39 successfully secreted all three IFN types with a relatively low level of hyperglycosylation.
title: <i>Ogataea</i> Yeast Platform for Recombinant Porcine Interferon-Alpha 1 Production: Toward Alternative Biotherapeutics for Swine Health Management.

text: Batch fermentation scale-up of r-poIFN-α1 achieved a final protein concentration of 0.45 ± 0.10 mg/mL. Crucially, the OP39-produced r-poIFN-α1 exhibited antiviral efficacy in vitro against economically important porcine viruses including African Swine Fever Virus, Porcine Epidemic Diarrhea Virus and Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome Virus. Based on the proof-of-concept results in this study, the OP39 platform can be further developed into a viable, full freedom-to-operate system for local or regional biomanufacturing of biologically active veterinary therapeutics to support livestock health management.
title: <i>Ogataea</i> Yeast Platform for Recombinant Porcine Interferon-Alpha 1 Production: Toward Alternative Biotherapeutics for Swine Health Management.

text: Aptamers are single-stranded nucleic acids that bind to target molecules with high affinity, serving as versatile molecular tools for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. Although several aptamers against the envelope (E) protein of tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) have been reported, their recognition of native viral particles remain insufficiently characterized. We identified novel ssDNA aptamers against TBEV through systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX) using a recombinant E protein that preserved the major antigenic properties of viral particles. The four major aptamer candidates showed binding activity not only to TBEV E proteins but also to TBEV-derived subviral particles. Additionally, these aptamers recognized TBEV-infected cells and retained their binding activity under serum conditions mimicking the in vivo environment.
title: Selection and characterization of ssDNA aptamers targeting tick-borne encephalitis virus particles.

text: Some aptamers also exhibited inhibitory effects against TBEV infection in vitro . Furthermore, sequence truncation yielded optimized variants that retained high target affinity, demonstrated enhanced serum stability over 24 h, and neutralized viral infection. These findings provide crucial functional validation of ssDNA aptamers targeting TBEV particles and support their development as antibody-independent platforms for diagnostic, antiviral, and targeted delivery strategies for TBEV and related flaviviruses.
title: Selection and characterization of ssDNA aptamers targeting tick-borne encephalitis virus particles.

text: Background This study aimed to identify clinical and demographic factors associated with prolonged hospitalisation in patients treated for severe odontogenic cervicofacial infections (CFI). Methods This retrospective study analysed 152 patients who were treated in an inpatient setting for CFI at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Army Hospital Hamburg, between January 2022 and December 2023. Patients were stratified based on length of hospital stay (LOS) into two groups: Results Patients with prolonged hospitalisation (≥ 7 days; n = 79) were older and more frequently had recorded pre-existing disease, multi-space infection, submandibular or floor-of-mouth involvement, dyspnoea, elevated inflammatory markers and delayed presentation in unadjusted analyses.
title: Determinants of extended inpatient care in odontogenic cervicofacial infections: a retrospective observational study.

text: In multivariable logistic regression, recorded pre-existing disease (aOR 6.04, 95% CI 1.10-33.18; p = 0.038) and longer time from symptom onset to hospital presentation (aOR 2.86 per day, 95% CI 2.01-4.07; p Conclusions Although several demographic, anatomical and clinical factors were associated with prolonged hospitalisation in unadjusted analyses, recorded pre-existing disease and delayed hospital presentation remained independently associated with prolonged LOS after multivariable adjustment. These findings highlight the potential importance of comorbidity and timely presentation in identifying patients at risk of extended inpatient care, but prospective multicentre validation is warranted.
title: Determinants of extended inpatient care in odontogenic cervicofacial infections: a retrospective observational study.

text: Objective This scoping review identifies and maps the breadth of evidence describing the preparation of preregistration nursing students to provide care to infants, children, young people, and their families in an Australian context. Introduction Nursing graduates in Australia are expected to deliver safe and competent care to children and families across diverse health care settings. However, pediatric nursing education is commonly embedded within integrated lifespan curricula, with limited access to dedicated pediatric units or clinical placements. This lack of structured pediatric preparation has been associated with student anxiety, reduced confidence, challenges in age-appropriate communication, and reluctance to pursue pediatric nursing pathways following graduation, raising concerns about patient safety and workforce sustainability.
title: Exploring undergraduate nursing students' preparation to care for children and their families in Australia: a scoping review.

text: Eligibility criteria This scoping review included published and unpublished literature relevant to undergraduate preregistration nursing students in Australia. Evidence sources published from 2010 onward were eligible and included empirical studies, non-empirical literature, policy documents, professional standards, and gray literature related to the preparation of nursing students to care for children and their families across all health care settings. Methods This review followed the JBI methodology for scoping reviews. A 3-step search strategy was used between December 2023 and February 2024 to identify relevant literature across the CINAHL (EBSCOhost), MEDLINE (Ovid), Scopus, and ERIC (ProQuest) electronic databases, in advanced Google searches, and across websites of Australian professional organizations, government bodies, pediatric hospitals, and universities.
title: Exploring undergraduate nursing students' preparation to care for children and their families in Australia: a scoping review.

text: Two reviewers independently screened citations, extracted data, and synthesized findings. Results were organized according to regulatory requirements and recommendations, educational preparation approaches, and student experiences. Results In total, 10 peer-reviewed publications and 29 gray literature sources met the eligibility criteria. According to these sources, efforts to prepare nursing students to care for children commonly involved integrated curriculum approaches, simulation-based learning, and supported work-integrated learning experiences. High-fidelity simulation and alternative placement models to improve knowledge, confidence, communication skills, and clinical reasoning were identified.
title: Exploring undergraduate nursing students' preparation to care for children and their families in Australia: a scoping review.

text: Immersive experiential learning to create interest in pediatric nursing pathways-particularly among students with limited prior exposure to children, including male students-was investigated. Publicly available information from universities and pediatric hospitals demonstrated variability in preparation requirements and limited transparency regarding pre-placement preparation. Conclusions Despite clear professional and regulatory recommendations, the preparation of preregistration nursing students to care for children and families in Australia is inconsistent. Integrating pediatric education across undergraduate curricula, supported by simulation and alternative experiential learning opportunities, may enhance student confidence, readiness, and workforce participation in pediatric nursing. Review registration OSF https://osf.io/4mtf6/overview.
title: Exploring undergraduate nursing students' preparation to care for children and their families in Australia: a scoping review.

text: Background/Objectives: Antiseizure drugs (ASDs) are the primary therapeutic approach for epilepsy in small animals. Although ASDs are primarily used to modulate central neuronal excitability, they are commonly administered systemically, most often by the oral route, and may therefore influence neuronal populations outside the central nervous system. Nevertheless, their functional effects on peripheral neuronal populations, including enteric and dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, remain incompletely characterized at a comparative pharmacological level. This study aimed to perform a comparative functional neuropharmacological profiling of commonly used ASDs in primary cultured myenteric and DRG neurons.
title: Comparative Neuropharmacological Effects of Antiseizure Drugs on Cultured Myenteric and Dorsal Root Ganglion Neurons.

text: Methods: Changes in neuronal activity were assessed in primary cultured guinea pig myenteric and DRG neurons using voltage-sensitive dye imaging with Di-8-ANEPPS following direct ASD application under standardized in vitro conditions. Results: ASDs exerted distinct drug- and neuron-type-specific effects on peripheral neuronal excitability. Topiramate induced the most pronounced reduction in neuronal excitability in myenteric neurons, whereas phenobarbital and levetiracetam produced only minor changes compared with buffer control. Potassium bromide induced mainly excitatory effects in both enteric and DRG neurons. Overall, most ASDs predominantly increased neuronal excitability in DRG neurons. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate distinct functional response profiles of ASDs in enteric and sensory neuronal populations.
title: Comparative Neuropharmacological Effects of Antiseizure Drugs on Cultured Myenteric and Dorsal Root Ganglion Neurons.

text: This comparative in vitro approach may provide a basis for future studies investigating peripheral neuronal drug effects and may help relate experimental pharmacological profiling to clinically relevant challenges associated with ASD treatment across different disorders.
title: Comparative Neuropharmacological Effects of Antiseizure Drugs on Cultured Myenteric and Dorsal Root Ganglion Neurons.

text: Zoonoses pose substantial global health risks, highlighting the need to better understand animal-to-human transmission. Reptiles are increasingly recognized as hosts of diverse pathogens, including numerous viruses, yet the diversity and prevalence of reptile pathogens, as well as their potential risk to humans, remain poorly understood. Here, we establish and characterize airway organoids derived from Python regius, providing an in vitro model to study reptile airway infection. Through de novo assembly of a Python regius reference genome, we characterize airway organoids at single-cell resolution, which suggests the presence of diverse cell populations including ionocytes, ciliated, secretory, goblet, endocrine, tuft, and basal cells.
title: Modeling reptile virus infection in vitro using Python regius airway organoids.

text: The organoids support productive infection with Ball Python Nidovirus (BPNV) and mount a robust epithelial antiviral response through the induction of interferon-stimulated genes, cytokines, and genes involved in chemical defense. As a proof-of-concept, treating organoids with antiviral drugs during infection reduces BPNV levels, highlighting the model's utility for drug testing. By providing a reductionist system of the serpentes airway, these organoids constitute a physiologically relevant in vitro model to study reptile viruses and host-pathogen interactions in their native host.
title: Modeling reptile virus infection in vitro using Python regius airway organoids.

text: Diabetes impairs multiple stages of the wound-healing process, resulting in chronic, infection-prone wounds that pose a substantial clinical burden. Despite available therapeutic options, effective management remains challenging owing to inadequate treatment efficacy, increasing antimicrobial resistance, and potential adverse side effects. Diabetic wounds exhibit a complex pathological microenvironment characterized by persistent bacterial colonization, hyperglycemia, tissue hypoxia, chronic inflammation, excessive matrix metalloproteinase activity, oxidative stress, and pH dysregulation. Nonetheless, traditional treatment strategies continue to rely largely on passive protection, inadequately addressing the underlying biological mechanisms responsible for impaired healing.
title: Potential of Chitosan-Based Systems Integrating Therapeutic Ions, Mesoporous Silica and SPIONs as Next-Generation Multifunctional Platforms for Diabetic Wound Healing.

text: Chitosan (CS), a naturally occurring cationic polysaccharide with high biocompatibility, antimicrobial activity, hemostatic properties, and a chemically tuneable structure, represents an attractive platform for advanced wound dressings. This review explores the potential of engineered chitosan-based systems for diabetic wound management through the strategic integration of therapeutic ions (Cu 2+ , Zn 2+ , Mg 2+ , Ag + , Mn 2+ ), mesoporous silica nanocarriers, and superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs). Unlike previous reviews that have primarily examined these components individually, the present work provides the first comprehensive analysis of their integration within a single multifunctional chitosan-based platform.
title: Potential of Chitosan-Based Systems Integrating Therapeutic Ions, Mesoporous Silica and SPIONs as Next-Generation Multifunctional Platforms for Diabetic Wound Healing.

text: By systematically evaluating their complementary therapeutic and diagnostic functions, including antimicrobial activity, angiogenic stimulation, oxidative stress modulation, controlled therapeutic delivery, and magnetic field-responsive behavior, this review establishes a unified design framework for the development of next-generation chronic wound dressings. Furthermore, it identifies potential synergistic interactions, key translational challenges, and future research directions required for the development of clinically relevant smart systems. Collectively, this integrated strategy offers a promising approach to overcoming the complex biological barriers that hinder diabetic wound healing.
title: Potential of Chitosan-Based Systems Integrating Therapeutic Ions, Mesoporous Silica and SPIONs as Next-Generation Multifunctional Platforms for Diabetic Wound Healing.

text: Background Carcinoma of the gallbladder (GBC) is an aggressive malignancy of the hepatobiliary system with a poor prognosis due to late presentation and a lack of effective diagnostic tools. Conventional imaging often fails to accurately detect the disease in its early stages. Both abdominal USG and contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) have lower sensitivities for early-stage GBC. This highlights the need for reliable noninvasive biomarkers that may facilitate early diagnosis and improve clinical outcomes. These novel molecular markers may be used alone or in combination with serum tumor markers to enhance their diagnostic utility. This study was performed to identify novel, noninvasive biomarkers for the diagnosis of GBC and determine their accuracy in differentiating carcinoma from other benign pathologies of the gallbladder.
title: Identification of Noninvasive Biomarkers for Gallbladder Carcinoma.

text: Materials and methods This prospective observational case-control study was conducted over a period of one year, from April 2025 to March 2026, in the Department of General Surgery, Motilal Nehru Medical College, Prayagraj. A total of 60 patients were included, comprising 30 histologically confirmed GBC cases and 30 controls with benign gallbladder disease. Detailed clinical evaluations, laboratory investigations, and imaging studies were performed. Blood samples were collected prior to intervention, and biomarkers, including carbohydrate antigen (CA) 19-9, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), and CA-125, were analyzed using ELISA, while microRNA (miRNA)-21 and miRNA-155 were analyzed using quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) techniques.
title: Identification of Noninvasive Biomarkers for Gallbladder Carcinoma.

text: Statistical analysis was performed, and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results Patients with GBC showed significantly higher levels of the tumor markers CA 19-9, CEA, and CA-125 compared to controls (p < 0.001). The molecular biomarkers miRNA-21 and miRNA-155 were also markedly elevated in carcinoma cases and strongly correlated with tumor stage and histological grade. The combination of biomarkers (CA 19-9 and miRNA-21) showed superior diagnostic accuracy (91.7%), with higher sensitivity (93.3%) and specificity (90%) on ROC analysis (area under the curve (AUC) of 0.956). Clinical and radiological findings were consistent with advanced disease in most cases. Conclusion Noninvasive biomarkers, particularly when used in combination, demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy for the early detection of GBC.
title: Identification of Noninvasive Biomarkers for Gallbladder Carcinoma.

text: Integration of biomarker analysis with clinical and radiological evaluation can further improve diagnostic utility and facilitate better clinical management. These findings support the potential role of biomarker-based screening strategies in high-risk populations.
title: Identification of Noninvasive Biomarkers for Gallbladder Carcinoma.

text: Although short-term CAT score variability has been associated with COPD exacerbations, evidence supporting its integration into virtual assistant-based monitoring remains limited. The aim of this study was to assess the short-term variability in CAT scores using a virtual management tool in patients with COPD and to examine its relationship with the prediction of exacerbations. A prospective observational single-center study was conducted in patients aged >35 with COPD and an exacerbator phenotype (≥2 outpatient exacerbations or ≥1 hospitalization in the previous year). Follow-up was performed weekly, including the CAT questionnaire, through calls were conducted by the virtual assistant Tucuvi Health Manager ® during a period of one year. A total of 106 patients were included; 64.2% were male, with a mean (SD) age of 66.8 (7.9) years and a median FEV 1 (%) of 38.8 (30.1-45.0).
title: COPD Assessment Test Variability as a Predictor of Exacerbations in Patients with COPD: A Prospective Study Using Virtual Assistant Monitoring.

text: The mean follow-up was 25 weeks [IQR 20-35], during which 73 (69%) patients experienced ≥1 exacerbation, accounting for 192 episodes (26% of which required hospitalization). A total of 2550 CAT scores were collected. The mean baseline CAT score was 17.9 (7.6), and scores increased significantly during exacerbations compared with non-exacerbation periods and according to exacerbation severity. Each one-point increase in absolute CAT score was associated with an 11.1% increase in the odds of exacerbation (OR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.08-1.13), while a weekly variation of ≥2 points (MCID) was associated with more than sixfold higher odds (OR: 6.30; 95% CI: 4.28-9.27). The optimal cut-off for CAT change in the prediction of exacerbation risk was 3 points with a ROC curve of 0.773. Weekly deterioration in CAT scores was associated with increased exacerbation risk in patients with COPD.
title: COPD Assessment Test Variability as a Predictor of Exacerbations in Patients with COPD: A Prospective Study Using Virtual Assistant Monitoring.

text: Short-term increases in CAT may serve as clinically useful warning signals for exacerbation.
title: COPD Assessment Test Variability as a Predictor of Exacerbations in Patients with COPD: A Prospective Study Using Virtual Assistant Monitoring.

text: Identifying the drivers of chronic stress is crucial for understanding its impact on mental health. Latent toxoplasmosis, a widespread parasitic infection, has been linked to various psychological changes. The Stress-Coping Hypothesis proposes that at least some of these changes are consequences of chronic stress arising from the infection's negative impact on physical health, rather than direct parasitic manipulation. To test this mediational pathway, we surveyed 1768 individuals previously tested for toxoplasmosis or borreliosis, using the Perceived Stress Scale and the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory. As predicted, Toxoplasma-infected individuals reported significantly poorer physical health and higher levels of perceived stress and anxiety.
title: From Infection to Anxiety: A Sequential Model Linking Latent Toxoplasmosis to Psychological Distress via Health and Stress.

text: Crucially, path analysis revealed a clear sequential mechanism: toxoplasmosis was directly associated only with poorer physical health, which in turn predicted higher perceived stress, which subsequently predicted increased anxiety. This specific, stress-mediated pathway was absent in the control group of individuals with borreliosis, providing strong evidence that the psychological effects of this common infection are side effects of illness-induced chronic stress. These findings offer a mechanistic model of how a chronic physical health burden translates into significant psychological distress and highlight the importance of considering latent infections as a contributor to the global burden of stress-related disorders.
title: From Infection to Anxiety: A Sequential Model Linking Latent Toxoplasmosis to Psychological Distress via Health and Stress.

text: Focal junctional tachycardia (FJT) is a regular, narrow QRS complex tachycardia with subtle cycle length irregularity, frequently associated with isorhythmic atrioventricular dissociation (IAVD). Its presentation may be paroxysmal or non-paroxysmal. This rhythm is well recognized in humans and dogs. However, to the best of the authors' knowledge, FJT has not been previously published in cats. This case report describes a 9-year-old neutered male domestic shorthair cat presenting with signs of congestive heart failure, hyperthermia, and a non-paroxysmal FJT. Electrocardiography demonstrated a narrow QRS tachycardia with type I synchronization IAVD, consistent with suspected FJT. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe biatrial enlargement, concentric ventricular hypertrophy and echocardiographic measures suggestive of high probability of pulmonary hypertension.
title: Suspected Focal Junctional Tachycardia with Type I Isorhythmic Atrioventricular Dissociation Associated with Diffuse Lymphocytic Myocarditis of Undetermined Etiology in a Cat.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: There was apparently preserved global systolic function and diastolic dysfunction. These findings were consistent with a non-specific cardiomyopathy phenotype stage C. Pleural fluid cytology initially suggested a lymphoproliferative disorder; however, postmortem histopathological examination confirmed diffuse lymphocytic myocarditis without evidence of neoplasia. Despite intensive supportive and antithrombotic therapy, the cat experienced sudden death. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first description of suspected FJT with type I IAVD in a cat. This case highlights myocarditis as a critical differential diagnosis in cats presenting with a lymphocytic effusion, structural echocardiographic changes, and complex supraventricular arrhythmias. It also discusses the diagnostic challenges and prognostic implications associated with inflammatory myocardial disease in this species.
title: Suspected Focal Junctional Tachycardia with Type I Isorhythmic Atrioventricular Dissociation Associated with Diffuse Lymphocytic Myocarditis of Undetermined Etiology in a Cat.

text: The continuous antigenic drift of zoonotic H7 avian influenza viruses remains a significant global public health threat. While monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting the hemagglutinin (HA) head offer potent neutralization, their efficacy is often undermined by rapid viral escape. In this study, we systematically mapped the antigenic architecture of the H7 HA head domain using a panel of 30 murine mAbs. By integrating epitope mapping with longitudinal evolutionary analysis of over 2,500 isolates, we identified highly conserved, functionally constrained residues, specifically G70, G132, N167, and M173, that remained nearly invariant over decades. Leveraging these insights, we engineered a chimeric bispecific antibody (BsAb-H7) to simultaneously engage two distinct, non-overlapping conserved epitopes.
title: A bispecific antibody targeting conserved hemagglutinin epitopes confers broad protection against H7 avian influenza and accelerates viral clearance via localized respiratory delivery.

text: BsAb-H7 demonstrated broad neutralization breadth across divergent H7N9, H7N7, and H7N3 subtypes in vitro and exhibited a superior in vivo pharmacokinetic profile. In lethal murine challenge models, BsAb-H7 provided robust prophylactic and therapeutic protection against heterologous H7N7 infection. Notably, localized intranasal administration significantly outperformed systemic delivery by accelerating viral clearance and resolving pulmonary immunopathology during delayed intervention windows. These results demonstrate that bispecific targeting of conserved HA epitopes effectively enhances antiviral breadth and limits immune escape, providing a promising strategy for the development of broadly protective therapeutics against rapidly evolving H7 influenza viruses.
title: A bispecific antibody targeting conserved hemagglutinin epitopes confers broad protection against H7 avian influenza and accelerates viral clearance via localized respiratory delivery.

text: Canine chronic inflammatory enteropathy (CIE) frequently requires a sequential therapeutic approach in which treatment is escalated according to clinical response. This prospective, open-label clinical study evaluates selected dietary, antimicrobial, microbiome-directed, and corticosteroid interventions used within a step-up treatment strategy in dogs with CIE under routine clinical conditions. Fifty-six dogs were enrolled. Clinical response was assessed using the Canine Chronic Enteropathy Clinical Activity Index (CCECAI), together with faecal calprotectin, serum folate, and serum cobalamin concentrations. In the dietary stage, both novel-protein and hydrolysed diets significantly reduced CCECAI and faecal calprotectin. Clinical remission, defined as a final CCECAI score ≤ 3, was achieved in 64% and 60% of dogs, respectively.
title: Comparison of Selected Therapies Within the Step-Up Therapeutic Approach in Canine Chronic Inflammatory Enteropathy.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Baseline-adjusted analyses likewise showed no significant between-group differences in CCECAI, faecal calprotectin, or cobalamin. In dogs receiving second-line treatment, both metronidazole and probiotics combined with fibre significantly reduced CCECAI and faecal calprotectin, while baseline-adjusted comparisons demonstrated no significant differences between treatments for the evaluated outcome. In dogs receiving corticosteroid-containing treatment, substantial numerical reductions in CCECAI and faecal calprotectin were observed in both the prednisone-containing and budesonide-containing regimens; however, the very small subgroup sizes and concomitant dietary, probiotic, and fibre interventions precluded definitive conclusions regarding the specific effects or comparative efficacy of the individual corticosteroids.
title: Comparison of Selected Therapies Within the Step-Up Therapeutic Approach in Canine Chronic Inflammatory Enteropathy.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: These findings provide real-world clinical evidence supporting a structured step-up approach to canine CIE and provide a rationale for larger, adequately powered controlled studies to determine whether non-antibiotic microbiome-directed strategies and locally acting corticosteroid-containing therapy can reduce reliance on empirical antimicrobial treatment and systemic corticosteroids, thereby minimising the potential adverse consequences associated with these therapies.
title: Comparison of Selected Therapies Within the Step-Up Therapeutic Approach in Canine Chronic Inflammatory Enteropathy.

text: Introduction Cutaneous and subcutaneous tumors are frequently encountered in canine patients, posing diagnostic challenges in general veterinary practice. Heat-Diffusion Imaging (HDI) is an active dynamic thermography technique that evaluates tissue thermal changes following controlled stimulation. Integration of HDI with artificial intelligence (AI) provides a non-invasive approach for tumor classification. Objective Our objective was to develop and internally validate HDI-based, tumor-specific AI classifiers for differentiating canine mast cell tumors (MCTs) and lipomas from other cutaneous and subcutaneous masses. Methods This study included 669 dogs with 1010 cutaneous and subcutaneous masses. Dynamic thermal data were recorded from each mass using an HDI system. This was followed by cytological or histopathological diagnosis.
title: Tumor-Specific Classification of Canine Cutaneous and Subcutaneous Tumors Using Heat-Diffusion Imaging and Artificial Intelligence.

text: Thermal features were extracted from the recordings and used to develop, train, and internally validate a primary AI-based classifier that distinguishes benign from malignant lesions. A diagnostically confirmed subgroup was used to train and internally validate tumor-specific classifiers for lipomas and mast cell tumors. The diagnostic performance of all classifiers was independently evaluated. Results The primary classifier cohort comprised 952 masses. Of these, 760 masses were assigned to the training cohort and 192 masses to the test cohort. The primary classifier achieved a sensitivity of 92% (95% CI 83.6-96.3) in the test set of 192 masses, and a prevalence-adjusted negative predictive value (NPV) of 98.1% at an assumed malignancy prevalence of 15%.
title: Tumor-Specific Classification of Canine Cutaneous and Subcutaneous Tumors Using Heat-Diffusion Imaging and Artificial Intelligence.

text: Among the 55 masses assessed by the lipoma classifier, sensitivity was 86.4% (95% CI 73.3-93.6) and specificity 100% (95% CI 74.1-100); all 38 masses flagged as lipoma were lipomas. Among the 81 masses assessed by the MCT classifier, sensitivity was 31.8% (95% CI 20.0-46.6) and specificity 94.6% (95% CI 82.3-98.5); all 16 masses flagged as MCT were malignant, and 14/16 were diagnosed as MCTs. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that combining HDI-derived thermal features with AI enables promising, non-invasive differentiation of common canine cutaneous tumor types. The two-tiered diagnostic approach improves upon the primary classifier by providing tumor-specific classification. This strategy may be particularly valuable in general practice settings, where access to immediate cytological or histopathological evaluation can be limited.
title: Tumor-Specific Classification of Canine Cutaneous and Subcutaneous Tumors Using Heat-Diffusion Imaging and Artificial Intelligence.

text: Mammalian species differ in the biochemical composition of their tissues and fluids-subtle but statistically discriminable variation that vibrational spectroscopy can detect and machine learning can decode for applications spanning forensic investigation, conservation monitoring, and physiological assessment. This review critically examines machine learning applications across near-infrared (NIR), mid-infrared (MIR/FTIR), and Raman spectroscopy specifically for mammalian wildlife samples. We examine unsupervised and supervised learning methods, from principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering to partial least squares discriminant analysis, support vector machines, random forests, and deep learning architectures, alongside the preprocessing, validation, and performance assessment strategies essential for reliable deployment in wildlife contexts.
title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Vibrational Spectroscopy for Mammalian Wildlife: A Critical Review of Conservation and Forensic Applications.

text: Each approach is evaluated with theoretical grounding and specific mammalian case studies spanning blood species identification, live animal monitoring, tissue analysis, and fecal dietary profiling. Despite reported classification accuracies frequently exceeding 95%, the field remains fragmented by inconsistent validation practices, limited external testing across species and geographic populations, and a critical shortage of standardized mammalian spectral reference databases, constraints that limit reproducibility and translation from controlled laboratory conditions to operational conservation and forensic practice.
title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Vibrational Spectroscopy for Mammalian Wildlife: A Critical Review of Conservation and Forensic Applications.

text: By bridging these methodological gaps, this review provides wildlife researchers, conservation biologists, and forensic scientists with a critical synthesis and practical framework for implementing machine learning-enhanced spectroscopy in mammalian wildlife conservation and crime investigation.
title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Vibrational Spectroscopy for Mammalian Wildlife: A Critical Review of Conservation and Forensic Applications.

text: Gene and cell therapies have emerged as transformative approaches for treating a wide range of genetic and acquired diseases. Central to their success is the development of safe and effective gene delivery systems, categorized broadly into viral and non-viral vectors. Each system has its own advantages and limitations, requiring careful consideration of the target tissue, disease, and the balance between safety, efficacy, and scalability. Viral vectors, including adeno-associated viruses, retroviruses, lentiviruses, herpes simplex viruses, and adenoviruses, offer high transduction efficiency and specificity but raise concerns about immunogenicity and production challenges.
title: Advances in gene transfer technologies: comparing viral and non-viral vectors for therapeutic applications.

text: Non-viral systems, such as lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) and other synthetic carriers, provide scalable, cost-effective, and potentially safer alternatives but often face hurdles in transduction efficiency and targeted delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current status of these vector systems for in vivo and ex vivo applications. Key comparisons are made across safety, efficacy, scalability, and immune responses, highlighting recent advancements and innovative approaches. We also discuss the outlook for next-generation gene transfer technologies, focusing on improvements in vector design, manufacturing, and application versatility. By addressing these considerations, we aim to inform the development of optimized therapeutic strategies that leverage the unique strengths of each delivery system.
title: Advances in gene transfer technologies: comparing viral and non-viral vectors for therapeutic applications.

text: Bone metastasis can be facilitated by systemic remodeling, yet the tumor-derived signals that influence the bone marrow microenvironment remain incompletely understood. Large oncosomes (LOs) are atypically large (> 1 µm), tumor-derived extracellular vesicles shed by amoeboid cancer cells. Here, we demonstrate that LOs function as systemic mediators of metastatic niche formation by activating innate immune sensing in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs). Systemic administration of LOs to immunocompetent tumor-bearing mice did not affect primary tumor growth but increased metastatic burden. LOs induced a robust, dose-dependent interferon-driven inflammatory program, characterized by interferon-stimulated genes and neutrophil chemokines.
title: Large Oncosomes Induce Pro-Metastatic Stromal-Myeloid Reprogramming.

text: Mechanistically, this response was driven by LO-associated nucleic acids activating convergent cytosolic DNA- and RNA-sensing pathways in recipient stromal cells. LO-conditioned BM-MSCs promoted the accumulation and polarization of neutrophils toward an immunosuppressive, polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cell (PMN-MDSC)-like phenotype. In vivo, genetic suppression of LO shedding in tumor cells reduced PMN-MDSC accumulation in the bone marrow, which was reversed by systemic LO administration. Together, these findings support a model in which LO-associated signals reprogram the bone marrow microenvironment to support metastatic colonization, identifying a previously unrecognized mechanism linking tumor vesiculation to immune remodeling at distant sites.
title: Large Oncosomes Induce Pro-Metastatic Stromal-Myeloid Reprogramming.

text: In common with many other viruses, influenza A viruses (IAVs) activate the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) p38 pathway. This signalling pathway is strongly implicated in the pro-inflammatory cytokine storm that underlies morbidity and mortality in response to highly pathogenic IAV strains. We previously reported that MAPK p38 increased the expression of many inflammatory mediators via the phosphorylation and inactivation of the mRNA-destabilizing protein tristetraprolin (TTP). Hence, mice expressing a non-phosphorylatable form of endogenous TTP protein were strongly protected against inflammatory effects of polymicrobial sepsis or endotoxaemia. Here, we used the same minimally genetically modified mouse strain ( Zfp36aa/aa ) to investigate responses to a viral mimetic in vitro or IAV infection in vivo .
title: Mitogen-activated protein kinase p38-dependent phosphorylation of tristetraprolin enhances inflammatory and impairs antiviral responses to influenza virus.

text: When challenged in vitro with the viral mimetic poly(I:C), Zfp36aa/aa macrophages underexpressed several TTP-regulated inflammatory mediators. When infected with a pathogenic IAV strain, Zfp36aa/aa mice also under-expressed TTP-regulated inflammatory mediators. Strikingly, expression of type I and III IFNs and IFN-regulated antiviral genes was spared or enhanced in Zfp36aa/aa macrophages or mice. Consistent with these observations, Zfp36aa/aa mice cleared the pathogen more rapidly and were partially resistant to virus-induced airway pathology. These findings suggest that modulating TTP phosphorylation may exert anti-inflammatory effects whilst sparing or enhancing antiviral responses in the context of pathogenic IAV infection.
title: Mitogen-activated protein kinase p38-dependent phosphorylation of tristetraprolin enhances inflammatory and impairs antiviral responses to influenza virus.

text: Retrotransposons comprise large fractions of many genomes and numerous transposon control mechanisms have evolved to combat retrotransposon expansion. The budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae contains several active retrotransposon families but maintains a remarkably compact genome, all without many of the transposon control systems used in mammals. Here, we review restriction factor control of the yeast Ty1 family of LTR-retrotransposons. Several decades of study have identified a novel mechanism that provides highly specific restriction of Ty1 using transposon-derived sequences. Recent work combining structural, biophysical, biochemical, and genetic techniques has revealed a detailed mechanism of this restriction and the determinants of specificity. Interestingly, two Ty1 subfamilies each converged on the same restriction mechanism despite following separate evolutionary histories.
title: Restriction Factor Control of Ty1 Family LTR-Retrotransposons in <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i>.

text: The protein p22/p18 is a self-encoded restriction factor that targets Ty1c and is produced from an internally initiated mRNA. Drt2 is a restriction factor that targets Ty1' and is produced from a transposon fragment endogenized by the host genome. Both interfere with the assembly of transposon virus-like particles using a shared dimerization surface, but subtle sequence divergence in this interface directs each restriction factor against its specific Ty1 subfamily. This work presents a framework to identify novel transposon control systems in other organisms.
title: Restriction Factor Control of Ty1 Family LTR-Retrotransposons in <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i>.

text: The simultaneous screening of multicomponent pesticide residues, rather than a single specific compound, remains a critical yet challenging frontier in safety surveillance, largely due to the inherent one-to-one recognition bottleneck in conventional aptamer- or antibody-based biosensors. Herein, we develop a collective CRISPR-Cas12a biosensing platform for effect-based screening of pesticide residues by integrating effect-based enzymatic recognition with PAM-independent CRISPR signal amplification.
