Rather than employing a dedicated aptamer or antibody for each pesticide, the proposed strategy exploits the inhibitory effects of diverse pesticide residues on alkaline phosphatase (ALP) as a common biochemical response.
title: A Collective CRISPR-Cas12a Biosensing Platform for Effect-Based Screening of Pesticide Residues.

text: ALP activity inhibition serves as a common trigger, converting the presence of diverse toxicants into the controlled generation of Cu + as a unified biochemical signal via ALP-mediated ascorbic acid production. To transduce this signal into a robust nucleic acid output, we further engineer a CRISPR-Cas12a system that operates completely independent of PAM sequences through click chemistry-mediated covalent ligation of two hairpin fragments. The complete activator strand activated Cas12a trans-cleavage, thereby circumventing the sequence constraints imposed by PAM recognition. The platform exhibits quantitative responses toward TCE, CPF, and Piri, with limits of detection of 22.1 nM, 19.3 nM, and 12.0 nM, respectively.
title: A Collective CRISPR-Cas12a Biosensing Platform for Effect-Based Screening of Pesticide Residues.

text: Furthermore, it successfully reports pesticide contamination in a complex real sample matrix, which provides a simple and flexible strategy for preliminary pesticide screening. Importantly, the platform is not intended to convert the collective fluorescence response into the total concentration of diverse pesticide residues; rather, the output reflects the integrated perturbation of the ALP-mediated biochemical pathway under the defined assay conditions. Overall, this work establishes an effect-based collective sensing paradigm that shifts pesticide screening from compound-specific molecular recognition toward integrated biochemical response, providing a flexible strategy for rapid screening and early warning of multicomponent pesticide contamination.
title: A Collective CRISPR-Cas12a Biosensing Platform for Effect-Based Screening of Pesticide Residues.

text: We report a case of severe post-tuberculosis lung disease (PTLD) in a 60-year-old Ugandan man with a six-year history of suboptimally treated pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB), who presented with a three-week history of productive cough, yellow foul-smelling sputum occasionally streaked with blood, dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, fatigue and progressive exercise intolerance. Imaging revealed extensive structural lung damage characterized by bronchiectasis, multiple bullae, and fibrotic changes, more pronounced in the left lung. Laboratory evaluation showed leukocytosis with neutrophilic predominance, and sputum culture grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Streptococcus pneumoniae . A diagnosis of post-tuberculosis structural lung disease complicated by acute infective exacerbation of bronchiectasis was made.
title: Severe Post-Tuberculosis Bronchiectasis With Bullous Lung Disease Complicated by Acute Infective Exacerbation: A Case Report From Uganda.

text: Treatment with intravenous empirical antibiotics followed by culture-directed therapy, along with supportive care, led to clinical improvement and reduction in respiratory symptoms. This case highlights the severe structural sequelae of suboptimally treated PTB and the importance of early recognition and appropriate management of infective exacerbations, particularly in resource-limited settings.
title: Severe Post-Tuberculosis Bronchiectasis With Bullous Lung Disease Complicated by Acute Infective Exacerbation: A Case Report From Uganda.

text: Current preclinical studies evaluating cGAS inhibition as a novel anti-inflammatory strategy rely predominantly on young murine models, leaving the impact of aging largely unexplored. At baseline, aged (56-week-old) female mice, in both WT and cGAS -/- mice, demonstrated more pronounced oxidative stress (malondialdehyde) and diminished antioxidant capacity (glutathione) relative to young (8-week-old) controls. Upon the induction of liver ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), the most severe hepatic damage was provoked exclusively in aged cGAS -/- mice. This exacerbated injury was confirmed by elevated liver enzymes, higher histological scores, widespread apoptosis (activated caspase-3), enhanced macrophage accumulation (F4/80 + cells), and increased serum cell-free DNA as a tissue damage marker.
title: Prominent Hepatic Injury in 56-Week-Old Female Mice with Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate-Adenosine Monophosphate Synthase (cGAS) Deficient.

text: Additionally, aged cGAS -/- mice exhibited a significant surge in serum IL-6 and gut barrier dysfunction (FITC-dextran assay) at 6 h post-injury. Mechanistically, while cGAS -/- macrophages showed blunted inflammatory signaling upon lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation, co-incubation with D-galactose, which induces intracellular peroxide accumulation, restored their pro-inflammatory responses to WT levels. Concurrently, starvation protocols revealed that cGAS -/- hepatocytes were more vulnerable to mitochondrial oxidative stress (MitoSOX) than WT cells. Ultimately, aging critically modifies the cGAS -deficient phenotype, warranting the careful re-evaluation of cGAS therapeutic models in aged populations.
title: Prominent Hepatic Injury in 56-Week-Old Female Mice with Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate-Adenosine Monophosphate Synthase (cGAS) Deficient.

text: Background Campylorrhinus lateralis ('wry nose') is a rare congenital maxillofacial deformity of foals resulting in compromise of the airway and severe class 4 malocclusion. Various surgical techniques to correct the deformity have been described, but contemporary data on single-stage transection and fixation, including use of a rib graft, and long-term functional and cosmetic outcomes remain underreported. Objectives To describe the transection-and-fixation technique and perioperative management used to correct wry nose in horses, and to report postoperative complications and long-term outcomes of horses undergoing this treatment. Study design Retrospective case series. Methods Wry nose of four horses was corrected by using a single-stage transection-and-fixation technique. Pre-operative assessment included physical, oral, and radiographic examinations, and when available, CT imaging.
title: Single-stage orthognathic correction of campylorrhinus lateralis in foals using transection and fixation: Surgical description and outcome of four horses.

text: The surgical procedure involved temporary tracheostomy and laryngotomy, resection of the nasal septum, osteotomy and fixation of the nasal bones, and orthognathic transection and fixation of the premaxillae and maxillae, with bone grafting and alar fold resection performed when indicated. The outcome of horses with complete records and ≥12 months follow-up is reported using descriptive statistics. Results All four horses were presented with respiratory difficulty. The transected premaxillae were stabilised with pins and wires, and the transected nasal bones were stabilised with plates/screws; only one horse received a rib graft. All horses developed a plate-associated infection, and one horse developed an oronasal fistula. At the time of follow-up, all grazed and masticated normally, maintained good body condition, and owners were satisfied with the functional and cosmetic outcome.
title: Single-stage orthognathic correction of campylorrhinus lateralis in foals using transection and fixation: Surgical description and outcome of four horses.

text: Main limitations Small sample size, retrospective design. Conclusions Correcting wry nose of four foals using a single-stage transection-and-fixation procedure achieved satisfactory long-term outcomes. Respiratory function of all horses improved, and all horses grazed and masticated normally. Three horses were able to perform their intended athletic endeavour. All owners reported satisfaction with the functional and cosmetic outcome.
title: Single-stage orthognathic correction of campylorrhinus lateralis in foals using transection and fixation: Surgical description and outcome of four horses.

text: Angiolipomas are uncommon benign mesenchymal neoplasms composed of mature adipocytes and proliferating vascular channels. In dogs, infiltrative angiolipomas are rarely reported and have primarily been described as localized soft-tissue masses. An 11-year-old, 10.8 kg, castrated male Japanese Spitz was referred for evaluation of regenerative anemia, mild thrombocytopenia, recurrent syncopal episodes, and a 5-year history of a slowly enlarging ventral thoracic mass. Preoperative hematological evaluation demonstrated anemia with a hematocrit of 25.4% and an increased absolute reticulocyte count of 122.7 K/µL, supporting a regenerative erythropoietic response. The platelet count was mildly decreased at 109 × 10 3 /µL.
title: Resolution of Regenerative Anemia, Thrombocytopenia, and Syncope After Cytoreduction of an Infiltrative Angiolipoma in a Dog: A Case Report.

text: D-dimer concentration was increased (737.61 ng/mL; reference interval, 0-250 ng/mL), whereas prothrombin time (9.5 s; reference interval, 5-15 s) and activated partial thromboplastin time (15.6 s; reference interval, 15-45 s) were within their reference intervals. Referral history indicated that previous infectious and immune-mediated evaluations had not identified a definitive cause, although the original external testing records were unavailable for verification. Computed tomography revealed a heterogeneous subcutaneous mass with mixed fat- and soft-tissue-attenuating components, suspected infiltration of the superficial pectoral muscle, and focal rather than diffuse contrast enhancement. Surgical cytoreduction, including partial myectomy, was performed because complete excision was not considered feasible owing to deep muscular infiltration.
title: Resolution of Regenerative Anemia, Thrombocytopenia, and Syncope After Cytoreduction of an Infiltrative Angiolipoma in a Dog: A Case Report.

text: Histopathological examination confirmed an infiltrative angiolipoma characterized by mature adipocytes, numerous vascular channels, skeletal muscle infiltration, and frequent intravascular fibrin thrombi. Following surgery, the hematological abnormalities progressively improved without blood transfusion or long-term immunosuppressive therapy. The platelet count increased from 109 × 10 3 /µL preoperatively to 153 × 10 3 /µL by postoperative day 16 and 202 × 10 3 /µL by postoperative day 56. During the same period, the hematocrit increased from 25.4% to 45.0%, and the absolute reticulocyte count subsequently returned to the reference interval. The syncopal episodes ceased after surgery and did not recur during the available 12-month follow-up. Fibrinogen concentration and peripheral blood smear evaluation were unavailable, and serial postoperative coagulation testing was not performed.
title: Resolution of Regenerative Anemia, Thrombocytopenia, and Syncope After Cytoreduction of an Infiltrative Angiolipoma in a Dog: A Case Report.

text: Accordingly, the temporal association between tumor cytoreduction and hematological improvement raises the possibility of a tumor-associated process, but neither the underlying mechanism nor a causal relationship could be established.
title: Resolution of Regenerative Anemia, Thrombocytopenia, and Syncope After Cytoreduction of an Infiltrative Angiolipoma in a Dog: A Case Report.

text: Introduction Risk factors such as the type and amount of fresh and dried grapes (collectively called Vitis vinifera fruit [VVF]) ingested in cases of VVF toxicosis are understudied. Therefore, this study aimed to characterise and identify risk factors for VVF ingestion in dogs recorded by the Veterinary Poisons Information Service (VPIS). The VPIS is a UK-based service for poison-related queries from owners and veterinary professionals. Methods VPIS database cases of VVF ingestion were cleaned, filtered and coded. Descriptive analysis and risk factor analysis by multivariable logistic regression were performed. The defined primary outcome was clinical signs. Defined secondary outcomes were clinical signs associated with potential renal damage. It was hypothesised that dried VVF would be more toxic than fresh VVF.
title: A descriptive cohort study of <i>Vitis vinifera</i> fruit (grape/raisin/sultana/currant) ingestion in dogs, reported by the Veterinary Poisons Information Service between 1994 and 2023.

text: Results A total of 3150 cases of fresh or dried VVF ingestion were reported to the VPIS; 744 received follow-up. Of veterinary professionals' reported cases with follow-up, 4.6% died. Owner-reported cases had no mortalities. Risk factors significantly associated with possible kidney damage-related clinical sign development included type of VVF (fresh vs. dry), the amount ingested and age of the dog. Limitations The dataset lacked consistent follow-up and temporal data, for example, time from ingestion to VPIS contact, meaning not all risk factors could be explored, and hypotheses generated need further testing. Conclusions In the VPIS dataset of followed-up cases, VVF ingestion was commonly associated with a positive prognosis. There is a suggestion that some risk factors (e.g., VVF type, amount) lead to possible kidney damage.
title: A descriptive cohort study of <i>Vitis vinifera</i> fruit (grape/raisin/sultana/currant) ingestion in dogs, reported by the Veterinary Poisons Information Service between 1994 and 2023.

text: Transmissible gastroenteritis (TGE) and pseudorabies (PR) remain important viral diseases causing massive economic losses and posing a continuous burden on the global swine industry. The continuous emergence of variant strains of transmissible gastroenteritis virus (TGEV) and pseudorabies virus (PRV) has gradually weakened the protective efficacy of traditional vaccines, highlighting the urgent need for next-generation preventive vaccine candidates. Here, we constructed a recombinant pseudorabies virus named rPRV-AD expressing the major neutralizing epitopes A and D of the TGEV spike protein via homologous recombination combined with CRISPR/Cas9-gene editing technology and then evaluated its biological characteristics in vitro and immunogenicity in piglets.
title: Construction and Immunogenicity of a Recombinant Pseudorabies Virus Expressing the Major Neutralizing Epitopes A and D of Transmissible Gastroenteritis Virus Spike Protein.

text: The results showed that this recombinant virus exhibited similar replication kinetics and biological properties to the parental strain. Immunization of 2-week-old piglets with rPRV-AD caused no obvious adverse effects and induced specific antibody and neutralizing antibody responses against both TGEV and PRV. Following virulent TGEV challenge, compared with the DMEM control group, rPRV-AD immunization alleviated clinical signs of piglets and significantly reduced viral load in intestine and feces, although its protective efficacy was lower than that of the commercial TGEV vaccine. Moreover, rPRV-AD provided effective clinical protection against challenge with the virulent PRV NY strain.
title: Construction and Immunogenicity of a Recombinant Pseudorabies Virus Expressing the Major Neutralizing Epitopes A and D of Transmissible Gastroenteritis Virus Spike Protein.

text: In summary, these findings suggest that rPRV-AD represents a vaccine candidate that provides partial protection and warrants further optimization, and yet shows short-term protective efficacy against both PRV and TGEV in pigs.
title: Construction and Immunogenicity of a Recombinant Pseudorabies Virus Expressing the Major Neutralizing Epitopes A and D of Transmissible Gastroenteritis Virus Spike Protein.

text: Influenza A virus remains a global health threat due to its high mutation rate and its resistance to existing neuraminidase and polymerase inhibitors. The polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2) subunit is a promising target for novel therapeutics due to its critical role in inhibiting viral transcription and replication. Here, we reported the preclinical characterization of HEC116094, a novel PB2 inhibitor, against influenza A virus. HEC116094 exhibited potent in vitro activities against multiple laboratory strains (IC 50 : 0.012-0.069 nM) and the highly pathogenic avian influenza strains H5N1 and H7N9 (IC 50 : 0.071-0.122 nM). These activities are more potent than VX-787 (Pimodivir) and oseltamivir. Our studies demonstrated that HEC116094 treatment could reduce the extent of weight loss and maintain a 100% survival rate in BALB/c mice, even when initiated 72 h post-infection.
title: Preclinical characterization of HEC116094, an oral inhibitor of the influenza A virus polymerase PB2 subunit.

text: In addition, HEC116094 exerted potent in vitro synergy and in vivo therapeutic benefits when combined with oseltamivir. Furthermore, HEC116094 displayed minimal kinase inhibition and excellent PK characteristics. Superior preclinical activity demonstrated that HEC116094 was a more potent PB2 inhibitor against influenza A virus than VX-787 in this study. Currently, HEC116094 is under evaluation in Phase I clinical studies.
title: Preclinical characterization of HEC116094, an oral inhibitor of the influenza A virus polymerase PB2 subunit.

text: Background Tracheal collapse is a common canine respiratory disease characterized by dorsoventral cartilage flattening, airway lumen narrowing and subsequent mucosal inflammation. Objectives To investigate the efficacy of EAB-277, a marine lipid extract combining Perna canaliculus (30 mg) and Euphausia superba (20 mg) as an adjunctive therapy in the management of tracheal collapse in dogs. Methods Forty-one dogs with confirmed tracheal collapse were randomly assigned to receive standard conventional medications plus either EAB-277 (n = 21) or a placebo (n = 20). The EAB-277 treatment protocol included a loading dose for the initial 14 days. Clinical signs and quality of life were assessed together with fluoroscopy, radiography, haematology and serum biochemistry on Days 0, 14, 28 and 56. Results Dogs receiving EAB-277 showed a significant improvement in exercise tolerance by Day 14.
title: Adjunctive Therapy With a Perna canaliculus and Euphausia superba Extract (EAB-277<sup>TM</sup>) for Clinical Signs of Tracheal Collapse in Dogs: A Prospective, Randomized and Placebo-Controlled Exploratory Trial.

text: Concurrently, fluoroscopic analysis demonstrated significant reductions in the percentage change in tracheal luminal diameter across the cervical, thoracic inlet and intrathoracic regions by Day 14. Both groups showed significant improvements in cough scores throughout the study, with no statistical difference between the groups. Conclusions Although conventional medical therapy effectively manages the clinical signs of tracheal collapse, particularly cough, this study demonstrates that EAB-277 provides additional benefits by significantly improving exercise tolerance and reducing dynamic tracheal collapse at the cervical, thoracic inlet and intra-thoracic regions, which might have the potential to enhance airway health.
title: Adjunctive Therapy With a Perna canaliculus and Euphausia superba Extract (EAB-277<sup>TM</sup>) for Clinical Signs of Tracheal Collapse in Dogs: A Prospective, Randomized and Placebo-Controlled Exploratory Trial.

text: We describe the diagnostic pathway, clinical follow-up and resolution of generalized avian tuberculosis in a Basset Hound dog. Lethargy, anorexia, weight loss and shifting lameness were observed. Cytological examination of specimens collected from prescapular, retromandibular and popliteal lymph nodes revealed the presence of acid-fast bacilli, subsequently identified as Mycobacterium avium subsp. hominissuis by microbiological and molecular tests. MIC determination was performed to guide therapy, which was subsequently based on clarithromycin (5 mg/kg orally every 12 h) and moxifloxacin (10 mg/kg orally every 24 h). Early and rapid diagnosis, combined with prompt initiation of appropriate antibiotic treatment, resulted in complete recovery of the affected dog.
title: An Effective Diagnostic Approach for Successful Recovery from <i>Mycobacterium avium</i> Systemic Infection in a Basset Hound Dog.

text: Emergency Departments (EDs) see a high prevalence of people who smoke, many of whom present with acute smoking-related conditions (e.g., myocardial infarction, stroke, pneumonia, and asthma/COPD exacerbations). The immediacy of illness creates a strong "teachable moment," increasing receptiveness to risk communication and behavior change. Evidence indicates that pairing brief counseling with point-of-care therapeutic support and structured follow-up improves abstinence, although effects vary with local infrastructure, product availability, and staffing models. Despite this promise, scale-up is often constrained by economic barriers, limited staffing and training, and weak integration of cessation workflows into routine ED practice.
title: Smoking cessation in emergency departments: a reality check.

text: The aim of this article is to provide a reality check on ED-based smoking cessation by synthesizing evidence on effectiveness, feasibility, cost-effectiveness, and safety across health-system contexts, and by outlining pragmatic delivery models and research priorities. Embedding low-friction, clinically governed cessation bundles within EDs has the potential to convert acute presentations into durable quit attempts and reduce smoking-related harm at scale, though this population-level impact remains a hypothesis to be tested. Future work should prioritize pragmatic and implementation trials with biochemically verified outcomes, integration metrics, equity impacts, and cost-utility analyses to guide sustainable adoption across diverse settings.
title: Smoking cessation in emergency departments: a reality check.

text: Clostridium perfringens type A causes neonatal clostridial enteritis, hemorrhagic enteritis, and sudden death syndrome in cattle. This study examined a fatal outbreak at a fattening farm housing 58 adult yaks in Southwest China, with an incidence of 22.41% (13/58) and a 100% case fatality rate. Histopathology of deceased yaks showed widespread multi-organ hemorrhage and severe hemorrhagic enteritis. A specific PCR assay amplified the alpha-toxin gene of Clostridium perfringens , while no other pathogens were detected. Clostridium perfringens was isolated from small intestinal contents using TSC agar, designated strain CQ1, and identified as type A through toxinotyping. Whole-genome sequencing revealed that strain CQ1 carries the core alpha-toxin gene along with key accessory virulence determinants ( pfoA , colA , and cloSI ).
title: Isolation, Genomic Evolution, and Pathogenicity of <i>Clostridium perfringens</i> Type A Causing Hemorrhagic Enteritis in Adult Yaks in Southwest China.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Phylogenomic analysis based on core single-nucleotide polymorphisms revealed that strain CQ1 is clustered into a distinct, independent evolutionary lineage with an existing historical yak isolate and a canine-origin isolate. Intraperitoneal challenge in mice confirmed its extreme lethality, causing 100% mortality within 36 h with severe intestinal necrosis. These findings provide fundamental genetic resources for understanding the virulence mechanisms and genetic background of this pathogen and offer critical insights for preventing and controlling clostridial diseases in high-altitude yak farming.
title: Isolation, Genomic Evolution, and Pathogenicity of <i>Clostridium perfringens</i> Type A Causing Hemorrhagic Enteritis in Adult Yaks in Southwest China.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: There are few molecular catalysts where active repair has been demonstrated, and one prominent example is a tetrapyridophenazine-bridged heterodinuclear Ru-Pt hydrogen-evolving photocatalyst, where hydrogenation of the pyrazine ring in the bridging ligand has been shown to lead to an end of photocatalytic activity. Subsequent in situ repair by persulfate enabled catalyst reactivation, but so far at the cost of decreasing catalytic activity over several repair cycles. We now show that tailored polyampholytic graft copolymers enable electrostatic immobilization of the photocatalyst in a unimolecular soft matter matrix, thereby prolonging (photo)catalytic activity due to slower photocatalyst degradation kinetics.
title: Embedding a Dinuclear Ru─Pt Photocatalyst Into Polyampholytic Graft Copolymer Matrix Enables Prolonged Hydrogen Evolution While Allowing Catalyst Repair.

text: We attribute this to a decreased propensity for hydrogenation of the pyrazine ring and, with that, slower degradation of the bridge and improved long-term HER activity, as evidenced by a holistic spectroscopic characterization of the molecular and electronic structure of the photocatalyst. At the same time, the graft copolymer matrix does not hinder oxidative repair of the photocatalyst, thus enabling multiple repair cycles without noticeable loss of catalytic activity. We therefore regard this as a novel blueprint for a synergistic molecule-in-matrix combination for sustainable light-driven catalysis.
title: Embedding a Dinuclear Ru─Pt Photocatalyst Into Polyampholytic Graft Copolymer Matrix Enables Prolonged Hydrogen Evolution While Allowing Catalyst Repair.

text: Acute kidney injury (AKI) frequently progresses to chronic kidney disease (CKD), ultimately leading to end-stage renal failure. Cytokine receptor-like factor 1 (CRLF1) is a secreted protein with low or undetectable expression in normal physiology, but it is transcriptionally and translationally upregulated under pathological conditions. In this study, we found CRLF1 to be upregulated in the kidneys of patients with ATN and CKD, positively correlated with renal interstitial fibrosis, and negatively correlated with renal function. In vivo functional inhibition studies demonstrated that CRLF1 suppression significantly improved renal function, mitigated pathological damage, and delayed fibrosis progression in mouse models of IRI or UUO. Further in vitro studies revealed that CRLF1 promotes fibrosis and inflammation in renal tubular epithelial cells (TECs).
title: Renal Tubular Epithelial CRLF1 Interacts With ITGB1 to Accelerate Fibrosis During the Transition From AKI to CKD.

text: Mechanistically, we employed chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) to validate SMAD3 binding to the CRLF1 promoter and its transcriptional regulation, while elevated CRLF1 interacts with the VWFA domain of integrin β1 (ITGB1). Furthermore, transcriptomic sequencing revealed that CRLF1 activates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, promoting tubular epithelial cell fibrosis progression via ITGB1. These findings underscore the critical role of CRLF1 in renal fibrosis progression and suggest its potential as a therapeutic target for inhibiting the progression from AKI to CKD.
title: Renal Tubular Epithelial CRLF1 Interacts With ITGB1 to Accelerate Fibrosis During the Transition From AKI to CKD.

text: Swine influenza A virus (swIAV) is an endemic respiratory pathogen of pigs with zoonotic relevance. We analysed retrospective serological data from routine diagnostic submissions (January 2023-May 2026) to a single laboratory, comprising 2003 sera from 66 reports on 44 commercial farrow-to-finish farms in seven regions of mainland Greece, tested with a nucleoprotein ELISA that cannot distinguish vaccine-, maternally, or infection-derived antibodies. Overall seroprevalence was 46.4% (929/2003; farm-clustered 95% CI 39.1-53.8%); at least one seropositive animal was found in 51 of 61 farm-years and in 36 of 44 farms. Seroprevalence differed by production stage ( p p = 0.014 and p = 0.39) and persisted after adjustment for year and stage, but it rests on few farms per region and is considered exploratory.
title: Seroprevalence of Swine Influenza A Virus (swIAV) in Commercial Pig Farms in Greece (2023-2026): Age, Regional and Temporal Patterns.

text: As a convenience sample of diagnostic submissions, these data provide descriptive rather than nationally representative estimates and support the addition of molecular, subtype-level surveillance.
title: Seroprevalence of Swine Influenza A Virus (swIAV) in Commercial Pig Farms in Greece (2023-2026): Age, Regional and Temporal Patterns.

text: Background Hemophagocytic syndrome (HPS)/hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome characterized by immune dysregulation, cytokine overproduction, hemophagocytosis, cytopenias, and multiorgan dysfunction. Although diagnostic criteria are established in human medicine, standardized criteria and validated biomarkers are lacking in dogs and cats. Objective To review the pathogenesis, clinical and clinicopathologic features, diagnosis, and differential diagnoses of HPS/HLH, with emphasis on dogs and cats, and to propose a framework for establishing standardized diagnostic criteria for canine HPS. Methods Human and veterinary literature on HLH, HPS, and macrophage activation syndrome was reviewed, including diagnostic criteria, biomarkers, bone marrow morphology, immunohistochemistry, flow cytometry, and molecular diagnostics.
title: In the Midst of a Cytokine Storm-The Hemophagocytic Syndrome (Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis/Macrophage Activation Syndrome).

text: Representative canine cases of secondary HPS and hemophagocytic histiocytic sarcoma were evaluated to illustrate diagnostic challenges. Results HPS results from dysregulated activation of cytotoxic lymphocytes and macrophages, with interferon-γ playing a central role in sustaining hyperinflammation. In dogs and cats, HPS is most commonly associated with infections, neoplasia, and immune-mediated disease. Clinical and laboratory findings are nonspecific, and although hemophagocytosis supports the diagnosis, it is neither required nor sufficient to establish HPS. Distinguishing reactive HPS from histiocytic neoplasia and other non-neoplastic causes of hemophagocytic activity-including drug-associated changes, post-transfusion hemophagocytosis, and PIMA-associated histiocytic activity-requires integration of cytomorphology, tissue distribution, immunophenotyping, and molecular diagnostics.
title: In the Midst of a Cytokine Storm-The Hemophagocytic Syndrome (Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis/Macrophage Activation Syndrome).

text: Human HLH-2004 criteria and the H-score provide useful diagnostic frameworks, but neither has been validated for veterinary species. Conclusions HPS is a challenging and potentially fatal syndrome in dogs and cats, which requires comprehensive clinicopathologic evaluation. Prospective studies are needed to establish species-specific diagnostic criteria and validate quantitative morphologic, immunophenotypic, molecular, and biomarker-based approaches to distinguish HPS from infectious, immune-mediated, and neoplastic disorders in which phagocytic activity is prominent.
title: In the Midst of a Cytokine Storm-The Hemophagocytic Syndrome (Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis/Macrophage Activation Syndrome).

text: Rewilding is increasingly promoted as a conservation strategy for restoring biodiversity and ecosystem processes. Yet rewilding efforts could involve species (re-)introductions that have implications for infectious disease dynamics. Despite the importance of such socio-ecological dynamics at the human-livestock-wildlife interface, the role of rewilding in disease prevalence remains poorly understood. We conducted semi-structured key informant interviews and focus group discussions with 24 stakeholders in the Northern Drakensberg Nature Reserve, South Africa, to examine how ecological dynamics, livestock management practices, governance conditions, and stakeholder perceptions shape disease transmission risks in a rewilding landscape. We analyzed the data using inductive thematic analysis guided by the One Health framework.
title: Socio-ecological dynamics of disease transmission in rewilding landscapes: A case study of the Northern Drakensberg Nature Reserve, South Africa.

text: Ecological and governance factors revealed that scavenger species, particularly vultures, jackals, and free-roaming dogs, shaped carcass persistence and pathogen exposure pathways, while the absence of coordinated governance across private landowners, conservation authorities, park managers, and community members created major gaps in disease surveillance and response. Disease risks were rarely considered in wildlife introduction decisions. Conservation authorities often assumed that pre-introduction health screening was sufficient, with limited attention given to post-release ecological dynamics. Disease awareness varied considerably across stakeholder groups and was influenced more by livelihood practices, concerns over grazing competition, and human safety than by epidemiological understanding.
title: Socio-ecological dynamics of disease transmission in rewilding landscapes: A case study of the Northern Drakensberg Nature Reserve, South Africa.

text: Historical exclusion from conservation decision-making further reinforced distrust, undermining disease reporting and compliance with interventions. These findings demonstrate that disease risks in rewilding landscapes emerge through interacting ecological, behavioural, and institutional processes rather than wildlife dynamics alone. Integrating diverse stakeholder perspectives into rewilding governance will be critical for operationalizing One Health approaches and anticipating unintended health consequences.
title: Socio-ecological dynamics of disease transmission in rewilding landscapes: A case study of the Northern Drakensberg Nature Reserve, South Africa.

text: Self-destructing attenuated adjuvant Salmonella (SDAAS) strains are next-generation attenuated S . Typhimurium strains designed to be used as live adjuvants. They possess diverse means to prevent persistence in vivo , survival if excreted, and to enhance the induction of innate immunity. In this study, we investigated whether SDAAS strains can be safely delivered to chicken embryos by in ovo inoculation without compromising hatchability or hatchling health. We then evaluated their growth in different media, sensitivity to complement-mediated killing, motility, serum agglutination, flagellar and LPS profiling, their ability to attach to and invade Int-407 cells, and the activation of different pattern recognition receptors displayed by HEK-Blue cells.
title: Self-destructing attenuated adjuvant <i>Salmonella</i> strains: design, construction, characterization, and evaluation of safety and efficacy following <i>in ovo</i> inoculation of chicken embryos.

text: We also determined whether these strains could induce protective immune responses in chicks following homologous challenge at day of hatch with a virulent S . Typhimurium strain by reducing intestinal colonization and organ invasion. Our findings demonstrate that SDAAS strains can be safely administered in ovo in a dose-dependent manner. Family A strains exhibit strict requirements for 2,6-diaminopimelic acid and D-alanine, while Family B strains demonstrate absolute dependence on L-arabinose for growth in liquid and solid media. Adjuvant strains demonstrate increased activation of murine receptors NOD1, NOD2, TLR4, TLR5, TLR8, and TLR9 in HEK-Blue cells compared to the parent strain χ3761, despite having lower rates of cell adhesion to and invasion of Int-407 cells. Lastly, we observed that in ovo administration of SDAAS strains reduced titers of S .
title: Self-destructing attenuated adjuvant <i>Salmonella</i> strains: design, construction, characterization, and evaluation of safety and efficacy following <i>in ovo</i> inoculation of chicken embryos.

text: Typhimurium recovered from birds as they became older, suggesting a time-dependent enhancement of protective immunity induced by SDAAS strains.
title: Self-destructing attenuated adjuvant <i>Salmonella</i> strains: design, construction, characterization, and evaluation of safety and efficacy following <i>in ovo</i> inoculation of chicken embryos.

text: Urolithin A (Uro A) is a natural bioactive compound biosynthesized by the gut microbiota after the ingestion of foods that are rich in ellagic acid and ellagitannins, such as strawberries, pomegranate, raspberries and walnuts. Uro A is studied in preclinical and clinical studies for its numerous biological activities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anticancer, cardioprotective and neuroprotective properties, while also possessing a therapeutic potential against metabolic syndrome and mitochondrial-enhancing effects. This narrative review briefly outlines the biosynthesis of Uro A and current evidence on its biological properties and its potential role in mitigating diseases, on the basis of literature searches performed on Google Scholar, Scopus, and PubMed/MEDLINE. In addition, recent clinical trials based on the supplementation with Uro A are summarized herein.
title: Urolithin A: Biosynthesis at a Glance and Biological Properties Supported by Recent Preclinical and Clinical Evidence.

text: Determining the cause and manner of death when human remains are recovered from isolated outdoor environments presents significant forensic challenges, particularly when post-mortem animal scavenging has altered the body. Rodents frequently target soft tissues, producing distinct taphonomic artifacts that can closely mimic sharp-force trauma, ante-mortem assault, or foul play. This case highlights the findings from a cachectic, unidentified adult male discovered in an abandoned forest shelter during winter (ambient temperatures between 5 °C and 16 °C), where rodent nests and rodent droppings were found. External examination revealed extensive soft-tissue destruction across the right side of the face, including the cheek, periorbital tissue, lower eyelid, nose, ear pinna, and underlying muscles and vessels.
title: Post-mortem Rodent Scavenging Artifacts in a Cachectic Deceased Discovered in a Forest Shelter: A Case Report.

text: The wound exhibited pale, irregular margins marked by fine nibbling and 1-2 mm notches characteristic of rodent incisors, alongside minor passive blood pooling from post-mortem vessel disruption. The estimated post-mortem interval was 24-48 hours before post-mortem examination. Diagnosis was established on classic gross macroscopic criteria, including pale wound bases and characteristic incisor striae, supported by the complete absence of vital reaction. The cause of death was determined to be severe hypothermia secondary to extreme exogenous starvation and cachexia. Accurately diagnosing rodent scavenging relies on identifying paired tooth grooves, pale wound margins, absence of vital reaction, and ecological scene context to distinguish post-mortem scavenging artifacts from true mechanical trauma.
title: Post-mortem Rodent Scavenging Artifacts in a Cachectic Deceased Discovered in a Forest Shelter: A Case Report.

text: Background In dogs, primary epilepsy syndrome (PES) requires lifelong pharmacological management. Curcuminoids possess anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties with potential neuroprotective effects. This pilot study preliminarily evaluated the clinical efficacy and molecular mechanisms of curcuminoid supplementation in canine PES. Methods In this prospective, open-label pilot study, eight dogs with PES on stable AED therapy received adjunctive oral curcuminoid supplementation (10-20 mg/kg/day) for 60 days. Clinical response, serum GSH/GSSG ratio (DTNB-glutathione reductase recycling assay), serum cytokine concentrations (ELISA), and global serum proteomic profiles (nano-LC-MS/MS) were assessed. Results Clinical response, defined as a reduction in seizure frequency (3/8) or decreased severity (1/8) was observed in 4 of 8 dogs (50%).
title: Curcuminoid supplementation alters proteomic profiles and clinical outcomes in canine primary epilepsy: A pilot study.

text: Curcuminoid supplementation significantly increased the GSH/GSSG ratio ( P = 0.046) and induced distinct proteomic changes: downregulation of mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway components (Ras-related GTP-binding protein C and regulatory-associated protein of mTOR) and Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) signaling and upregulation of one-carbon metabolism (methylenetetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase) and serine/glycine/threonine metabolism (phosphoserine aminotransferase 1) enzymes. Conclusion Curcuminoid supplementation was safe, well tolerated, and demonstrated a clinical response rate of 50% in dogs with PES. These findings provide preliminary molecular evidence of enhanced antioxidant capacity, mTOR/TLR2 modulation, and metabolic reprogramming.
title: Curcuminoid supplementation alters proteomic profiles and clinical outcomes in canine primary epilepsy: A pilot study.

text: As pilot observations, definitive neuroprotective conclusions require confirmation in larger controlled trials with direct neurological endpoints. Nonetheless, these data provide a molecular rationale for curcuminoids as adjunctive therapy in canine epilepsy.
title: Curcuminoid supplementation alters proteomic profiles and clinical outcomes in canine primary epilepsy: A pilot study.

text: Water-soluble poly-(vinyl alcohol) (PVOH) offers high tensile strength and an excellent oxygen barrier, but its dense hydrogen-bond network places its melting point close to its decomposition temperature, making it difficult to melt-process. Poly-(butylene adipate- co -terephthalate) (PBAT) is melt-processable and ductile but has low strength and dimensional stability that restrict its use. To combine their strengths, PBAT/PVOH blends (10-40 wt % PBAT) were melt-compounded with a 20 wt % ternary plasticizer of dipentaerythritol, ε-caprolactone, and water in equal parts, benchmarked against a water-only control at 40 wt % PBAT.
title: Structure-Processing-Property Relationships in PVOH/PBAT Blends Plasticized with Dipentaerythritol, ε‑Caprolactone, and Water.

text: Across FTIR, XRD, DSC, steady-shear and oscillatory rheology, DMA, tensile, SEM, AFM, TGA, and gas-barrier measurements, the ternary plasticizer governs the structure-property relationship by redistributing the PVOH hydrogen-bond network rather than breaking it; it broadens and shifts the O-H stretching envelope, suppresses PVOH crystallinity and recrystallization, depresses the glass transition by 17-27 °C, and broadens the relaxation spectrum, with no cross-linking or covalent grafting. Composition sets the phase topologydispersed PBAT domains at 20-30 wt % and a cocontinuous structure at 40 wt %while the plasticizer controls interfacial adhesion, converting the weakly bonded, void-laden interfaces of the water-only control into well-adhered ones.
title: Structure-Processing-Property Relationships in PVOH/PBAT Blends Plasticized with Dipentaerythritol, ε‑Caprolactone, and Water.

text: Among the series, the 20 wt % blend (PBAT-20) gives the best stiffness-toughness balance (modulus ≈ 0.23 GPa, ultimate tensile strength ≈ 20 MPa) together with an oxygen transmission rate of ≈6.4 cm 3 m -2 day -1 for a 400 μm film, equivalent to ≈102 cm 3 m -2 day -1 when normalized to a 25 μm thickness. The water-vapor transmission rate of the same film remains high (6.06 g m -2 day -1 ), so the films reported here are suited to oxygen-sensitive but moisture-tolerant applications rather than to moisture-critical ones. These findings position ternary hydrogen-bond engineering as a reaction-free, melt-processing route to property-tunable PBAT/PVOH films for biodegradable flexible packaging.
title: Structure-Processing-Property Relationships in PVOH/PBAT Blends Plasticized with Dipentaerythritol, ε‑Caprolactone, and Water.

text: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) can precipitate anemia in critically ill patients, but temporal hematologic trends and anemia management strategies in cats remain poorly characterized. Medical records of three client-owned cats treated with CRRT for severe acute kidney injury with evidence of pre-existing chronic kidney disease at a single referral center were retrospectively reviewed. Hematologic variables (hematocrit, hemoglobin concentration, absolute reticulocyte count) and renal parameters (blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, phosphorus) were evaluated before, during, and after CRRT, along with the timing of CRRT sessions, whole blood transfusions, erythropoiesis-stimulating agent administration, and adjunctive molidustat use.
title: Hematologic and Renal Trends in Cats Undergoing Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Retrospective Case Series with Molidustat Use.

text: All three cats demonstrated a progressive decline in hematocrit during the CRRT period despite repeated whole blood transfusions, with only transient post-transfusion improvement. Blood urea nitrogen and creatinine concentrations decreased promptly following CRRT initiation but showed variable rebound patterns during follow-up. Absolute reticulocyte counts increased after CRRT discontinuation in two cats, indicating preserved or recovering erythropoietic activity, while one cat with concurrent inflammatory and infectious disease showed a minimal response. Progressive anemia occurred consistently despite transfusion support, highlighting the multifactorial nature of anemia during feline CRRT. These descriptive findings provide clinically relevant insight into anemia progression during feline CRRT and may inform the design of future prospective studies.
title: Hematologic and Renal Trends in Cats Undergoing Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Retrospective Case Series with Molidustat Use.

text: Heat stress is a critical environmental factor that compromises reproductive performance in dairy cattle, primarily through deleterious effects on ovarian follicular cells. Granulosa cells (GCs), which provide essential nutritional and hormonal support for oocyte maturation, are particularly vulnerable to hyperthermic insult. However, the early molecular and subcellular events that precede overt cellular dysfunction remain inadequately characterized. This study aimed to investigate the temporal dynamics of mitochondrial morphological alterations and transcriptomic reprogramming in bovine GCs subjected to acute in vitro heat stress. Bovine GCs were exposed to 43 °C for 10, 20, 30, or 40 min, with untreated cells serving as controls. Heat shock protein expression (HSP90 and HSPA1A) was evaluated by qRT-PCR.
title: Acute Heat Stress Remodels Mitochondrial Ultrastructure and Time-Dependent Transcriptomic Landscapes in Bovine Granulosa Cells.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Intracellular calcium concentration was measured using the Fluo-3 AM fluorescent probe. Mitochondrial ultrastructure was examined via transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Global transcriptional changes were profiled by RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) at 20 and 40 min post-treatment, followed by bioinformatics analysis. Nine selected differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were validated by qRT-PCR. HSP90 and HSPA1A expression was significantly upregulated at 30 and 40 min of heat exposure ( p 2+ concentration exhibited a biphasic pattern-markedly elevated at 20 min but significantly reduced at 40 min. TEM revealed progressive mitochondrial swelling and cristae disruption at both time points, with more severe damage at 40 min. RNA-seq identified 185 DEGs at 20 min and 831 DEGs at 40 min, with 285 genes commonly dysregulated across both time points.
title: Acute Heat Stress Remodels Mitochondrial Ultrastructure and Time-Dependent Transcriptomic Landscapes in Bovine Granulosa Cells.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Functional enrichment analysis demonstrated that the 20-min response was dominated by heat shock protein-related pathways, whereas the 40-min response expanded to encompass apoptosis, inflammation, steroidogenesis, and ciliogenesis pathways. qRT-PCR validation confirmed the reliability of the RNA-seq data. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for understanding heat stress-induced ovarian dysfunction and may inform strategies to preserve fertility in dairy cattle during thermal challenge.
title: Acute Heat Stress Remodels Mitochondrial Ultrastructure and Time-Dependent Transcriptomic Landscapes in Bovine Granulosa Cells.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: The innate immune system is rapidly activated following antigen exposure and plays a critical role in shaping the ensuing adaptive immune responses. In this study, we performed bulk RNA sequencing and proteomic profiling in a cohort of 25 rhesus macaques following Ad26.COV2.S immunization to characterize early innate correlates of vaccine immunogenicity and protection. Our results show that innate immune activation occurred as early as day 1 post-vaccination and demonstrated a systemic enrichment of antiviral interferon pathways, cytokine signaling, and activation of innate immune cell signatures. These early transcriptomic signatures correlated positively with humoral and cellular immune responses at 6 weeks following vaccination and correlated inversely with viral loads following SARS-CoV-2 challenge.
title: Early innate immune signatures correlate with Ad26.COV2.S vaccine immunogenicity and protective efficacy.

text: Similar correlates of immunogenicity were observed in a cohort of 25 adult healthy participants vaccinated with Ad26.COV2.S. Taken together, these findings highlight the importance of early activation of the innate immune responses following Ad26.COV2.S vaccination in shaping the protective adaptive immune response.IMPORTANCEEarly innate immune responses may shape vaccine immunogenicity and protection. We evaluated responses to Ad26.COV2.S vaccination in rhesus macaques and humans and found that day 1 innate immune signatures correlated with subsequent adaptive responses. These findings suggest that early post-vaccination immune programming influences immunogenicity and protective efficacy months later.
title: Early innate immune signatures correlate with Ad26.COV2.S vaccine immunogenicity and protective efficacy.

text: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) play key roles in regulating gene expression across all domains of life. However, relatively few RBPs have been discovered and characterized in Borrelia ( Borreliella ) burgdorferi , the causative agent of Lyme disease. We utilized gradient profiling to identify putative RBPs that co-sediment with small RNAs (sRNAs) and nascent mRNAs. The previously hypothetical proteins BB0749, BB0713 and BB0796, as well as the chemotaxis-related protein CheY2 and the flagella-associated protein FlgV demonstrated RNA unwinding (structural remodeling), RNA annealing, and strand displacement activity. Moreover, in vivo co-IP assays demonstrated BB0749 binds RNA in B. burgdorferi .
title: Identification of proteins exhibiting <i>in vitro</i> RNA chaperone activity through gradient profiling in the Lyme disease spirochete, <i>Borrelia burgdorferi</i>.

text: Since the first review on imaging of intranasal drug delivery (INDD) was published in 2020, interest in the topic has increased, necessitating an update, which is the basis of the current review. INDD is a promising alternative for treating central nervous system (CNS) diseases. In vivo imaging is also important for therapy assessment, both clinically and preclinically. This review details studies that further our understanding of INDD and the fate of these therapies in the CNS using in vivo imaging. We performed a literature search using the keywords "Intranasal delivery" and "Imaging" from 2020 to 2025 and summarized these findings in the current updated review. This review is not comprehensive but provides examples of recent publications that explore the various treatments under development for nose-to-brain (N2B) therapeutic delivery through imaging.
title: Imaging of intranasal drug delivery to the brain: updated review 2.0.

text: Imaging will include magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), gamma scintigraphy, and computed tomography (CT) for both humans and animals. Additional specialty topics pursued experimentally in animals include in vivo optical imaging techniques, including bioluminescence and fluorescence imaging. Finally, we discuss image-guided therapeutic techniques such as focused ultrasound and conclude with future directions. In this review, we introduce each imaging modality, describe its utilization, and outline its strengths and weaknesses, specifically in the context of N2B therapeutics.
title: Imaging of intranasal drug delivery to the brain: updated review 2.0.

text: Background The glucocorticoid receptor gene ( NR3C1 ) regulates hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis feedback. Evidence of its epigenetic and transcriptional alterations in suicide remains limited and inconsistent, particularly in underrepresented populations. Methods We measured regional methylation within the assayed NR3C1 exon 1F promoter region and total NR3C1 mRNA expression in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (BA9) from 13 suicide cases and 13 non-psychiatric controls from northern Mexico. Groups were frequency-matched by age, sex, and post-mortem interval. Methylation was assessed by methylation-sensitive restriction enzyme (MSRE) qPCR and expression by RT-qPCR. Group differences were tested using two-sided exact Mann-Whitney U tests; effect sizes were probability of superiority (PS) and Cliff's δ. Correlation and male-only analyses were exploratory. All p -values were nominal.
title: <i>NR3C1</i> Exon 1F Promoter Methylation and mRNA Expression in the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex of Individuals Who Died by Suicide: A Post-Mortem Case-Control Study from Northern Mexico.

text: Results Cases showed higher total NR3C1 mRNA expression (U = 45, p = 0.04412; PS = 0.734; δ = 0.467) and regional exon 1F methylation (U = 29, p = 0.00349; PS = 0.828; δ = 0.657). The measures showed a non-significant positive correlation (ρ = 0.27, p = 0.179). In males, methylation remained higher in cases ( p = 0.0147), whereas expression remained directionally higher but non-significant ( p = 0.165). Conclusions Individuals who died by suicide showed higher regional exon 1F methylation and NR3C1 mRNA expression in BA9. The measures were not significantly correlated and should be interpreted as separate group-level differences, not evidence of direct methylation-expression coupling. The expression finding is preliminary.
title: <i>NR3C1</i> Exon 1F Promoter Methylation and mRNA Expression in the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex of Individuals Who Died by Suicide: A Post-Mortem Case-Control Study from Northern Mexico.

text: Given the small sample, limited clinical information, and comparison with non-psychiatric controls, the differences cannot be attributed specifically to suicide and require replication.
title: <i>NR3C1</i> Exon 1F Promoter Methylation and mRNA Expression in the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex of Individuals Who Died by Suicide: A Post-Mortem Case-Control Study from Northern Mexico.

text: Background Dirofilaria immitis is a vector-borne filarioid nematode distributed worldwide and endemic across most of North America. In dogs, it is considered the most clinically significant parasite and a known cause of acquired cardiomyopathy. Clinically, canine heartworm disease can manifest acutely as caval syndrome and chronically as heart failure, often resulting in death. Different types of diagnostic tests, such as antigen-detection and microfilariae-detection tests (MFDTs), including modified Knott's test and molecular assays, may be used to diagnose D. immitis infection. Although some molecular tools, such as real-time PCR (qPCR), exhibit high accuracy, cross-reactivity with other Dirofilaria species found in companion animals remains a concern.
title: Improved specificity of a probe-based real-time PCR for the detection of Dirofilaria immitis in canine blood.

text: Following our laboratory's previously published protocol, cross-reactivity was found with Dirofilaria striata isolated from a subcutaneous nodule of a cat from Texas. The objectives of this study were to: (i) evaluate the performance of three newly designed probe-based qPCR assays for detecting D. immitis and (ii) assess overall detection with the newly designed protocols compared with the previously published protocol and other diagnostic tests. Methods We designed three new probes using accessioned D. immitis cytochrome c subunit 1 sequences from various countries worldwide to increase reliability. These new probes were then tested with genomic DNA extracted from D. immitis and D. striata. Following this, we further assessed the performance of these newly designed probes and previously developed probe using 136 archival shelter dog samples previously found to be positive for D.
title: Improved specificity of a probe-based real-time PCR for the detection of Dirofilaria immitis in canine blood.

text: immitis by at least one diagnostic test. Results Out of the three probes tested, two (probe 2 and probe 3) specifically detected D. immitis and showed no cross-reactivity with D. striata. Probe 3 showed the highest prevalence of D. immitis among all qPCR assays (68.4%; n = 93/136 samples), followed by the original probe (66.9%; n = 91/136), with probe 2 (59.6%; n = 81/136) showing the lowest. Our analysis of agreement between probes using Cohen's kappa (κ) statistic indicated almost perfect agreement between probe 3 and the previously published probe (κ = 0.86). The shelter dog samples were also evaluated using other heartworm diagnostic methods, including the modified Knott's test, which was positive for 61.0% (n = 83/136) of the positive samples, and the previously published qPCR, which was positive for 66.9% (n = 91/136) of the samples.
title: Improved specificity of a probe-based real-time PCR for the detection of Dirofilaria immitis in canine blood.

text: All samples were also tested in parallel with a commercially available antigen detection test (DiroCHEK®; Zoetis Inc., Parsippany, NJ, USA), yielding 80.1% positivity pre-heat treatment (n = 109/136) and 94.9% post-heat treatment (n = 129/136). Probe 3 paired with post-heat treatment achieved the highest positivity of the molecular diagnostic tests (97.1%; n = 132/136). Conclusions This optimized probe-based qPCR assay (probe 3) provides an accurate and reliable method to detect D. immitis microfilariae in dogs and other carnivore hosts.
title: Improved specificity of a probe-based real-time PCR for the detection of Dirofilaria immitis in canine blood.

text: The aim of this research was to determine the effect of different anesthesia protocols on the pharmacokinetics of tolfenamic acid in cats undergoing ovariohysterectomy. The research involved 12 cats that underwent ovariohysterectomy. The cats were randomly divided into two equal groups: one ( n = 6) receiving xylazine-ketamine and the other ( n = 6) receiving propofol-isoflurane anesthesia. Tolfenamic acid was administered subcutaneously at a dose of 4 mg/kg 30 min prior to ovariohysterectomy in both groups. The plasma samples were analyzed for tolfenamic acid using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-UV.
title: Comparative Pharmacokinetics of Subcutaneous Tolfenamic Acid Under Two Different Anesthetic Protocols in Cats Undergoing Ovariohysterectomy.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: The terminal elimination half-life (t 1/2λz ), area under the curve (AUC 0-last ), maximum plasma concentration (C max ), and time to reach peak plasma concentration (T max ) values after xylazine-ketamine anesthesia were determined to be 3.30 h, 42.17 h*µg/mL, 6.34 µg/mL, and 2 h, respectively. Tolfenamic acid in the propofol-isoflurane anesthetic group showed shorter t 1/2λz and T max than the xylazine-ketamine group but a greater C max . However, AUC 0-last was similar in both anesthesia groups. These results showed that the pharmacokinetics of tolfenamic acid may vary depending on the anesthesia protocol used in ovariohysterectomy. However, there is a need to evaluate the efficacy of tolfenamic acid in cats under both anesthesia regimens.
title: Comparative Pharmacokinetics of Subcutaneous Tolfenamic Acid Under Two Different Anesthetic Protocols in Cats Undergoing Ovariohysterectomy.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Severe inflammatory lung disease, including acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), is life-threatening with diverse causes and few targeted therapies. Inborn errors of immunity (IEIs) underlie a subset of cases. We describe a novel IEI caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in PTPN6, encoding the immunoregulatory phosphatase SHP1. Seven children from five families developed early-onset anemia and severe inflammatory lung disease, at times presenting as ARDS. The causative variants were shown to destabilize SHP1 and abolish its phosphatase activity. These findings expand the genetic landscape of inflammatory lung disease and suggest SHP1 activation as a potential therapeutic strategy for immune-mediated pulmonary pathology.
title: Biallelic loss-of-function PTPN6 variants lead to inflammatory lung disease and hemolytic anemia.

text: Rationale Imaging tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) may reflect prognosis, therapeutic response and radiotheranostic potential. We report the discovery and development of a synthetic human Fab as the first immunoPET tracer targeting human CD68 (huCD68), the gold standard histopathological biomarker of pan-macrophages. Methods Phage display was used to identify novel huCD68-specific Fabs. The lead Fab for immunoPET development was chosen based on expression yield and stability. Fab was conjugated to p-SCN-Bn-DFO and radiolabeled with 89 Zr, yielding [ 89 Zr]Zr-DFO-Fab. Stability and specific binding of the tracer to THP-1 macrophages were assessed in vitro.
title: A FABulous approach to image human macrophages.
journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

text: The specificity of the tracer in vivo was characterized by PET imaging of two different animal models: 1) BALB/c mice bearing huCD68 antigen- or irrelevant protein-plugs, and 2) tumor xenografted NSG mice intratumorally injected with either THP-1 macrophages or THP-1 undifferentiated cells. Finally, tumors were subjected to immunofluorescence (IF) staining of huCD68 and correlated with PET standardized uptake values (SUV). Results Four novel huCD68-specific Fabs were identified. Fab8 was chosen as the lead based on high expression yield, purity, and stability. In vivo, [ 89 Zr]Zr-DFO-Fab8 uptake was significantly higher in huCD68 antigen-plugs than in irrelevant protein-plugs at 1- and 4-h post-injection (p.i.). Tracer uptake in THP-1 macrophage tumors was also significantly higher than in THP-1 undifferentiated tumors at 1- and 6-h p.i..
title: A FABulous approach to image human macrophages.
journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

text: IF of tumors confirmed higher density of huCD68 in those implanted with THP-1 macrophages than those with THP-1 undifferentiated cells. CD68 expression highly correlated with immunoPET SUV. Conclusion [ 89 Zr]Zr-DFO-Fab8 binds specifically to huCD68, supporting the feasibility of direct PET-to-histopathogical correlation of total TAM burden.
title: A FABulous approach to image human macrophages.
journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

text: Ovine coenurosis, caused by the larval stage of Taenia multiceps ( Coenurus cerebralis ), is a parasitic disease that affects the central nervous system of livestock. While diagnosis traditionally relies on clinical signs, imaging, and postmortem examination, electroencephalography (EEG) remains underutilized despite its potential to detect brain abnormalities. This case report describes EEG and quantitative EEG (qEEG) findings in a 2-year-old sheep presenting with clinical signs suggestive of a chronic focal encephalopathy (ataxia, head tilt and circling) associated with lethargy and progressive weight loss.
title: Electroencephalographic Aspects in a Sheep with Coenurosis.

text: Computed tomography (CT) confirmed a single, discretely bilobate intra-axial cystic lesion within the left cerebral hemisphere, with a severe mass effect, marked deformation and displacement of the ventricular system, compression of the thalamic structures, and contralateral deviation of the median line. A solitary parasitic cyst with no lesion in the right hemisphere was subsequently confirmed at necropsy and on histopathology. Under ketamine-diazepam sedation, both EEG recordings showed a continuous, delta-dominant background consistent with the anesthetic protocol. Epoch-wise asymmetry indices with bootstrap confidence intervals distinguished an unstable component (which reversed in hemispheric sign between recordings) from a reproducible one confined to the occipital derivations, where the asymmetry lay over the right hemisphere in both recordings in every band except delta.
title: Electroencephalographic Aspects in a Sheep with Coenurosis.

text: This reproducible preponderance was contralateral to the cyst, over a hemisphere in which no structural lesion was demonstrable either on imaging or at necropsy, and absolute powers indicated that it arose principally from attenuation of the signal recorded over the diseased hemisphere. These findings provide the first electrophysiological characterization of ovine coenurosis and show that in the presence of a severe mass effect, the side of the surface qEEG abnormality may not indicate the side of the lesion (an electrophysiological false localizing sign described in human patients but not previously in a ruminant). EEG therefore reflects the functional brain disturbance caused by Coenurus cerebralis but should be regarded as a complement to, rather than a substitute for, cross-sectional imaging in neurolocalization.
title: Electroencephalographic Aspects in a Sheep with Coenurosis.

text: In men, cystic fibrosis (CF) leads to infertility in over 95% of cases, due to early and progressive atresia of the vas deferens, resulting in obstructive azoospermia. The advent of highly effective modulator therapy has enabled more men with CF to consider parenthood, raising important questions regarding the impact of these treatments on male fertility. Animal models provide major insights into the mechanism of CF-related reproductive tract abnormalities, yet high interspecies variability complicates model selection. Mouse models display heterogeneous phenotype: knock-in or partial knockout models usually remain fertile, whereas complete knockouts may develop vas deferens atresia with aging.
title: Male reproductive phenotype in cystic fibrosis: comparison of existing animal models.

text: Among currently studied models, CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR)-knockout rats more closely reproduce the human phenotype, showing bilateral absence of the vas deferens and epididymal hypoplasia, although they exhibit more pronounced hypospermatogenesis than observed in men. In larger animal models, including ferrets, pigs, sheep and rabbits, absence of the vas deferens duct and epididymis is frequently observed, often with normal testicular histology; however, most studies in these species have mainly focused on neonatal stages, leaving long-term reproductive outcomes uncharacterized. No single model fully replicates human male reproductive pathology in CF. Combining rodent and large-animal models is probably essential to elucidate the mechanisms of vas deferens absence and to assess the long-term effects of CFTR modulators on male spermatogenesis and reproductive outcomes.
title: Male reproductive phenotype in cystic fibrosis: comparison of existing animal models.

text: Diosmin is a citrus-derived flavone glycoside with anti-inflammatory activity in preclinical models. This study aimed to investigate the effects of diosmin on PTSD-like behaviors, astrocyte morphology, and the expression of STAT1 and CXCL9 in a single prolonged stress and shock (SPS&S) mouse model, and to assess whether Stat1 knockdown could mimic diosmin's effects in primary astrocytes. Male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to the control, SPS&S, and SPS&S + diosmin groups and underwent 14 days of treatment. Behavioral assessments included open-field and elevated plus-maze tests, alongside cue- and context-associated fear tests, complemented by GFAP-based morphometry, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, serum cytokine assays, hippocampal RNA sequencing, and quantitative reverse-transcription PCR (qRT-PCR).
title: Diosmin Attenuates PTSD-like Behaviors and Hippocampal Astrocyte Alterations with Reduced STAT1 and CXCL9 Expression in an SPS&S Mouse Model.

text: The results indicated that diosmin significantly enhanced exploratory behavior and reduced fear responses compared to SPS&S alone, alongside notable alterations in hippocampal astrocyte morphology and a shift in cytokine profiles, with decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines and increased anti-inflammatory markers. RNA sequencing revealed 297 differentially expressed genes, particularly highlighting the roles of Stat1 and Cxcl9, both of which were significantly downregulated upon diosmin treatment. Furthermore, diosmin modulated astrocyte responses to inflammatory stimuli in primary cultures. These findings suggest that diosmin exerts protective effects against PTSD-like symptoms by regulating astrocytic function and immune-related pathways, with STAT1 signaling serving as a key but non-exclusive downstream mechanism underlying its therapeutic actions.
title: Diosmin Attenuates PTSD-like Behaviors and Hippocampal Astrocyte Alterations with Reduced STAT1 and CXCL9 Expression in an SPS&S Mouse Model.

text: Future studies should further elucidate the full spectrum of associated pathways to advance the development of targeted interventions for PTSD.
title: Diosmin Attenuates PTSD-like Behaviors and Hippocampal Astrocyte Alterations with Reduced STAT1 and CXCL9 Expression in an SPS&S Mouse Model.

text: Bovine coronavirus (BCoV) is an important pathogen that exhibits dual tropism for the respiratory and intestinal tracts, causing winter dysentery in adult cattle, diarrhea and respiratory infections in calves, thus imposing considerable economic losses on the global cattle industry. Our previous studies demonstrated that BCoV gains entry into susceptible HRT-18 cells through membrane fusion and clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME). However, the precise mechanisms by which BCoV enters host cells remain incompletely elucidated, particularly in primary bovine intestinal epithelial cells (PBIECs). Importantly, as primary cells derived from the natural host, PBIECs more closely recapitulate the in vivo infection microenvironment than HRT-18 cell lines.
title: Bovine coronavirus enters PBIECs via membrane fusion and clathrin-, caveolin-mediated endocytosis, macropinocytosis.

text: In the present study, chemical inhibitors, RNA interference, and fluorescently labeled BCoV particles were used to define distinct entry pathways. Our data demonstrated that BCoV enters PBIECs via membrane fusion and three distinct endocytic pathways, including CME, caveolin-mediated endocytosis (CavME), and macropinocytosis. Dynamin, microtubules, cathepsins, and an acidic environment are essential for mediating endocytic entry, whereas cholesterol and TMPRSS2 are dispensable for this process. Furthermore, targeted interference with Rab5, Rab7, and Rab11 suppressed BCoV entry into PBIECs. Consistently, co-localization of fluorescently labeled BCoV with Rab5, Rab7, and Rab11 was observed by confocal microscopy, indicating that these Rab GTPases are involved in BCoV entry into PBIECs.
title: Bovine coronavirus enters PBIECs via membrane fusion and clathrin-, caveolin-mediated endocytosis, macropinocytosis.

text: These findings elucidate the entry mechanisms of BCoV and provide novel perspectives to enhance a more comprehensive understanding of the BCoV life cycle.
title: Bovine coronavirus enters PBIECs via membrane fusion and clathrin-, caveolin-mediated endocytosis, macropinocytosis.

text: Leptospirosis is a zoonotic disease that can cause severe acute kidney injury (AKI) in dogs. A three-year-old intact male Border Collie, unvaccinated against leptospirosis, with a history of exposure to urban stagnant water presented with acute vomiting, diarrhea, and moderate dehydration. Initial evaluation revealed extreme azotemia (blood urea nitrogen, 175.8 mg/dL; creatinine, 11.10 mg/dL) and hyperphosphatemia (13.6 mg/dL), consistent with International Renal Interest Society (IRIS) AKI Grade V; urine output remained within the non-oliguric range (2.15-3.0 mL/kg/h) throughout the catheterized period (Day 0-4). Clinical and imaging findings supported acute intrinsic renal injury over chronic kidney disease.
title: Non-Oliguric IRIS Grade V Acute Kidney Injury Associated with Suspected Leptospirosis in an Urban Dog Unvaccinated Against Leptospirosis from the Republic of Korea: A Case Report.

text: A multiplex real-time PCR targeting the Leptospira LipL32 gene was positive in urine (Ct 31.10), providing molecular evidence supporting active infection or shedding of pathogenic Leptospira spp., without identifying the infecting serovar. Empirical antimicrobial therapy targeting suspected leptospirosis, together with intravenous fluid therapy, was initiated on clinical suspicion prior to the PCR result. Renal and inflammatory biomarkers improved progressively over 22 days without extracorporeal kidney support; the patient's non-oliguric status, hemodynamic stability, and objective clinical improvement supported this management approach.
title: Non-Oliguric IRIS Grade V Acute Kidney Injury Associated with Suspected Leptospirosis in an Urban Dog Unvaccinated Against Leptospirosis from the Republic of Korea: A Case Report.

text: This report documents, in detail, the clinicopathological recovery trajectory of a dog with non-oliguric IRIS Grade V AKI associated with suspected leptospirosis, information that may assist clinicians in recognizing and managing similarly severe presentations without assuming that dialysis is always required.
title: Non-Oliguric IRIS Grade V Acute Kidney Injury Associated with Suspected Leptospirosis in an Urban Dog Unvaccinated Against Leptospirosis from the Republic of Korea: A Case Report.

text: Background Canine monocytic ehrlichiosis is an important tick-borne disease in tropical settings, but local epidemiological evidence from Côte d'Ivoire remains limited. This study estimated the apparent seroprevalence of Ehrlichia canis antibodies and evaluated associated host, management and preventive factors among dogs sampled in Cocody, Abidjan. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted from 1 November 2025 to 31 January 2026. A convenience sample of 150 dogs underwent clinical examination, rapid antibody testing and complete blood count assessment; owners completed a structured questionnaire. Univariable analyses and parsimonious multivariable logistic regression were performed. Model discrimination, calibration, prediction error, bootstrap optimism and decision-curve net benefit were evaluated.
title: Seroprevalence of Ehrlichia canis antibodies and associated factors among dogs in Cocody, Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire.

text: Results Seventy-one dogs were seropositive, giving an apparent seroprevalence of 47.3% (95% CI: 39.3-55.3%). In the adjusted model (n = 149), tick presence was associated with higher odds of seropositivity (AOR = 3.94; 95% CI: 1.44-10.75; p = 0.007), whereas regular veterinary care was associated with lower odds (AOR = 0.20; 95% CI: 0.08-0.51; p Conclusions Substantial serological exposure was observed among sampled dogs. Tick control, supervised roaming and sustained veterinary care appear to be priority preventive actions. Because sampling was non-probabilistic and serology does not confirm active infection, population-level and causal interpretations should remain cautious. Nearly half of the dogs tested in this study in Cocody, Abidjan, carried antibodies against the bacterium that causes canine ehrlichiosis, a tick-borne illness.
title: Seroprevalence of Ehrlichia canis antibodies and associated factors among dogs in Cocody, Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire.

text: Dogs with ticks, dogs allowed to roam freely, and dogs without regular veterinary check-ups were most likely to test positive, while dogs receiving regular veterinary care and combined preventive measures (tick treatment, restricted roaming and informed owners) were markedly less likely to do so. Because the test used detects past or present exposure rather than active infection, these findings show how common exposure is in this population rather than how many dogs are currently sick; they point to tick control, supervised roaming and regular veterinary care as practical ways for owners to protect their dogs.
title: Seroprevalence of Ehrlichia canis antibodies and associated factors among dogs in Cocody, Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire.

text: The honeybee gut microbiota plays a key role in shaping host health and susceptibility to disease. Yet, the nutrient environment it experiences within the gut remains poorly characterized. In particular, little is known about the spatial distribution of nutrients across the microbial community, as resolving such fine gradients in vivo has been technically challenging. Here, we engineer the native honeybee symbiont Snodgrassella alvi as a living biosensor to quantify the bioavailability of the dietary sugar arabinose within the gut. By expanding the genetic toolkit for S. alvi through chromosomal integration of high-burden genes and a suite of low-strength promoters, we achieve stable multi-gene expression without compromising host colonization.
title: An engineered bacterial symbiont maps micron-scale sugar gradients in the honeybee gut.

text: The resulting biosensor generates a specific, dose-dependent fluorescent response to arabinose in the living host, enabling visualization of sugar gradients across gut-associated bacterial biofilms at micron-scale resolution. Upon co-colonization with distinct Gilliamella species that differ in arabinose metabolism, the biosensor reported differential in vivo arabinose consumption, directly validating species-specific metabolic specialization within the host. Feeding bees with pollen further uncovered pronounced radial heterogeneity in the distribution of pollen-derived arabinose. These findings demonstrate how diet composition and microbial specialization generate fine-scale microenvironments within the gut. More broadly, this work establishes S.
title: An engineered bacterial symbiont maps micron-scale sugar gradients in the honeybee gut.

text: alvi as a genetically tractable platform for in situ biosensing, opening new avenues for dissecting metabolic interactions and nutrient distribution within living hosts.
title: An engineered bacterial symbiont maps micron-scale sugar gradients in the honeybee gut.

text: Due to limitations in the use of antibiotics as feed additives to promote growth, the development of safe, effective, and environmentally friendly antibiotic alternatives is a critical and urgent research priority in animal nutrition and veterinary medicine.
