Instead, it clusters with fur seal feces-associated circular DNA virus, a lineage that has been proposed for reassignment to the genus Macochavirus .
title: From PCV1 to "PCV5": Genetic Diversity, Evolutionary Dynamics, and Host Adaptation of Porcine Circoviruses.

text: In this review we set the genomes of PCV1 to PCV5 side by side, together with the domain organization of their Rep and Cap proteins and their phylogenetic relationships, and we then turn to evolutionary rates, genetic diversity, host adaptation, and cross-species transmission, read against host immune pressure, intensive swine production, and the global live-pig trade. Our reading of the evidence is that these viruses do not share one ancestor. PCV1 and PCV2 descend from a single lineage long adapted to the genus Sus scrofa ; PCV3 reflects an independent spillover event; the origin of PCV4 is still unresolved; and PCV5 clusters with a fur seal feces-associated circular Rep-encoding single-stranded (CRESS) DNA virus, a phylogenetic affinity consistent with-but at this stage only a testable hypothesis of-an origin at the marine-terrestrial interface.
title: From PCV1 to "PCV5": Genetic Diversity, Evolutionary Dynamics, and Host Adaptation of Porcine Circoviruses.

text: If that is correct, the PCVs are a series of independent spillovers that happened to converge on the same host species, and we argue on that basis for proactive surveillance at the human-livestock-wildlife-environment interface.
title: From PCV1 to "PCV5": Genetic Diversity, Evolutionary Dynamics, and Host Adaptation of Porcine Circoviruses.

text: Background Preterm infants are vulnerable to brain injury because of immature white matter, vascular regulation, and neuroprotective mechanisms. White matter injury (WMI), formerly known as periventricular leukomalacia, is a major cause of cerebral palsy and neurocognitive impairment, while perinatal stroke is an important cerebrovascular cause of adverse outcomes. White matter injury: WMI is linked to hypoxia-ischemia, inflammation or infection, oxidative stress, and impaired oligodendrocyte maturation. It may be cystic or diffuse non-cystic, which is now the most common phenotype. Cystic lesions are strongly associated with motor impairment and spastic cerebral palsy, whereas diffuse injury is increasingly related to cognitive, behavioral, and language deficits.
title: Perinatal Brain Injuries in Preterm Infants.

text: Diagnosis relies on cranial ultrasonography and MRI; prevention focuses on optimized perinatal care, infection control, respiratory stabilization, and neuroprotection. Perinatal stroke: Stroke in preterm infants may occur antenatally or neonatally and includes periventricular hemorrhagic infarction, perinatal arterial ischemic stroke, and cerebral sinovenous thrombosis. Periventricular hemorrhagic infarction is the most common subtype and is often associated with germinal matrix hemorrhage-intraventricular hemorrhage. Risk factors are multifactorial, including fetal, neonatal, placental, thrombotic, infectious, and hemodynamic contributors. Clinical signs may be subtle, making neuroimaging central to classification and prognosis. Conclusion Despite advances in neonatal care, WMI and perinatal stroke remain major causes of long-term neurological morbidity in preterm infants.
title: Perinatal Brain Injuries in Preterm Infants.

text: Early recognition, systematic neuroimaging, risk stratification, and multidisciplinary follow-up are essential. Future research should identify reliable biomarkers and targeted neuroprotective therapies.
title: Perinatal Brain Injuries in Preterm Infants.

text: Veterinary drug delivery must balance efficacy, ease of administration, and animal welfare. Traditional methods, such as oral and injectable routes, pose challenges due to species-specific variations, stress during administration, and the need for repeated dosing. Emerging transdermal systems, particularly microneedle patches, offer a minimally invasive alternative that enhances drug absorption while reducing handling stress toward animals and improving compliance. Microneedle technology enables controlled and sustained drug release, making it particularly effective for pain management, vaccine delivery, and hormone therapies. By facilitating the transdermal administration of analgesics, microneedles deliver long-lasting pain relief with fewer interventions, improving the treatment of acute and chronic conditions in veterinary medicine.
title: Advances in veterinary drug and vaccine delivery: from conventional delivery methods to innovative transdermal approaches.

text: The use of biodegradable materials further enhances safety, eliminates the need for patch removal, and minimizes environmental impact. However, challenges such as species-specific skin permeability, formulation stability, and regulatory approval must be addressed for widespread adoption. This review examines the evolution of veterinary drug delivery, emphasizing microneedle-based technologies and their potential to improve pain management and therapeutic outcomes. By overcoming existing limitations, these systems could transform treatment approaches, simplify administration, and enhance overall animal care. Continued research and development will be essential for optimizing these technologies and expanding their applications in both clinical and agricultural settings.
title: Advances in veterinary drug and vaccine delivery: from conventional delivery methods to innovative transdermal approaches.

text: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) remains constrained by physical barriers, including strict oxygen dependence, acute hypoxia exacerbation, and limited light penetration depth. While conventional photodynamic therapy (PDT) is strictly oxygen-dependent and limited by light scattering, Near-Infrared Photoimmunotherapy (NIR-PIT) overcomes microenvironmental hypoxia through targeted, oxygen-independent biophysical membrane rupture. However, tissue optical attenuation at 690 nm remains a fundamental physical boundary that necessitates interstitial fiber placement for deep lesions.
title: Photoimmunotherapy Meets Systemic Immunotherapy: Molecular Mechanisms, Microenvironmental Remodeling, and Combinatorial Paradigms in Solid Tumors.

text: Concurrently, recent advances in bioengineered nano-photoimmunotherapy (nano-PIT) and organelle-targeted photodynamic/photothermal platforms deliberately execute alternative inflammatory non-apoptotic pathways, such as pyroptosis, cuproptosis, and ferroptosis, and provoke cytosolic leakage of mitochondrial DNA that engages the cGAS-STING innate immune axis. Concurrently, NIR-PIT comprehensively remodels the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) by selectively depleting regulatory T cells (Tregs), myeloid-derived suppressor (MDSCs) cells, and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), thereby deconstructing desmoplastic stroma, lowering interstitial fluid pressure (IFP), and driving the Super-Enhanced Permeability and Retention (SUPR) effect.
title: Photoimmunotherapy Meets Systemic Immunotherapy: Molecular Mechanisms, Microenvironmental Remodeling, and Combinatorial Paradigms in Solid Tumors.

text: Photically released mitochondrial DNA further engages the cytosolic cGAS-STING pathway, stimulating type I interferon signaling and dendritic cell cross-presentation. In selected preclinical models, this biophysical collapse promotes immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tumor microenvironment remodeling. When combined with systemic immunotherapies, NIR-PIT has demonstrated the potential to prime antitumor immunity and elicit abscopal responses in responsive syngeneic models; however, this immune conversion is not universal and is heavily constrained by tumor mutational burden, baseline antigen presentation fidelity, and diverse immunosuppressive networks. Translating these paradigms into clinical practice requires advancing 3D microphysiological models, implantable light technologies, and multi-component dosimetry frameworks.
title: Photoimmunotherapy Meets Systemic Immunotherapy: Molecular Mechanisms, Microenvironmental Remodeling, and Combinatorial Paradigms in Solid Tumors.

text: CRISPR-Cas genome editing represents one of the most transformative advances in modern molecular biology, enabling programmable site-specific genetic modification that has revolutionized functional genomics and precision therapeutic development. Beyond canonical Cas9 nucleases, the CRISPR toolkit has diversified into precision base editors, prime editors, CRISPR-associated transposases, and Cas12/Cas13 RNA-targeting effectors, each with distinct mechanistic properties. Clinically, ex vivo CRISPR therapies for hemoglobinopathies have secured regulatory approval, while base editing, prime editing, and in vivo Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR)-T candidates are advancing through trials for a broad spectrum of hematologic, oncologic, and rare genetic disorders.
title: CRISPR Technology: From Bench to Bedside Applications.

text: However, existing reviews largely address technical innovation or clinical translation in isolation, lacking a holistic, up-to-date synthesis of the full bench-to-bedside trajectory of CRISPR technology. This review systematically dissects the molecular mechanisms, advantages, and limitations of core CRISPR editing platforms; summarizes pivotal clinical data across hemoglobinopathies, CAR-T immunotherapy, muscular dystrophy, cystic fibrosis, cardiometabolic diseases and rare monogenic diseases; evaluates delivery systems including lipid nanoparticles and viral vectors; and discusses key translational barriers such as off-target genotoxicity and immunogenicity alongside emerging optimization strategies. This work provides a holistic bench-to-bedside framework for CRISPR research, offering critical insights to advance next-generation precision genetic medicine.
title: CRISPR Technology: From Bench to Bedside Applications.

text: Next-generation probiotics (NGPs) are promoted as precision tools for animal health, yet the term is often applied to uncommon taxa before causality, safety and target-species efficacy are established. This critical narrative review reframes animal NGPs as a development pathway rather than a taxonomic category. A structured PubMed search was last run on 14 September 2026 with a publication date cutoff of 1 September 2026 and was supplemented by citation tracing and targeted searches of authoritative sources. From the screened literature, 45 representative and conceptually informative sources were purposively selected for the final narrative synthesis; the review was not intended to provide systematic or exhaustive coverage. The detailed synthesis focused on terrestrial farm and companion animals, whereas equine, rabbit and aquaculture studies were treated as boundary evidence.
title: From Microbiome Associations to Deployable Precision Probiotics in Animals: A Critical Narrative Review and Proposed Causal Evidence Framework for Next-Generation Probiotic Development.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: We evaluate how strain-resolved metagenomics, culturomics, metatranscriptomics, metaproteomics, metabolomics, host transcriptomics, machine learning, metabolic modeling and perturbation systems can move discovery beyond association. Studies across animal sectors show many biomarkers but limited causal validation, strain tracking, formulation data, multisite trials and ecological safety assessment. We propose an author-developed conceptual framework comprising a cumulative evidence ladder, from reproducible associations to field-ready deployment, and the ANIMAL-NGP reporting checklist (Animal endotype, Native ecological fit, Identity and genomic safety, Mechanism, Administration and manufacturing, and Longitudinal validation). These tools are intended to align claims with evidence and require prospective application and external validation.
title: From Microbiome Associations to Deployable Precision Probiotics in Animals: A Critical Narrative Review and Proposed Causal Evidence Framework for Next-Generation Probiotic Development.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Multi-omics should therefore function as an evidence-navigation system, not as a substitute for causality.
title: From Microbiome Associations to Deployable Precision Probiotics in Animals: A Critical Narrative Review and Proposed Causal Evidence Framework for Next-Generation Probiotic Development.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: The diagnostic value of the Aβ1-42/Aβ1-40 ratio in peripheral blood as a biomarker for Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains a subject of considerable interest. However, this ratio in plasma exosomes is still underestimated. To investigate the potential clinical performances, this study has established a chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) for the specific detection of Aβ1-42 and Aβ1-40 in plasma exosomes using single-chain variable fragments (scFv). Plasma samples from 20 AD patients and 20 non-AD individuals were detected by the established scFv-based CLIA, with the traditional monoclonal antibody (mAb)-based CLIA as the reference method. The results demonstrated that the plasma exosome Aβ1-42/Aβ1-40 ratio in AD patients (0.70 ± 0.35) was significantly lower than that in the non-AD control group (1.82 ± 0.79, p < 0.001).
title: Single-Chain Variable Fragments Targeting Plasma Exosome Amyloid-β Peptide Subtypes for Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease.

text: In comparison with the mAb-based assay, the scFv-based CLIA exhibited superior analytical performance, with a lower limit of detection (1 pg/mL vs. 50 pg/mL) and higher specificity (cross-reactivity rate < 5%). When the Aβ1-42/Aβ1-40 ratio of 1.075 was set as the cutoff value, the scFv-based assay achieved a diagnostic sensitivity of 90.0%, which was numerically higher than that of the mAb-based assay (85.0%), with comparable specificity (90.0% vs. 90.0%). Generally, this study has developed a highly sensitive and specific scFv-based method for the detection of plasma exosome Aβ subtypes, which supports that the plasma exosome Aβ1-42/Aβ1-40 ratio is a potential non-invasive biomarker for differentiating clinically diagnosed AD from non-AD controls in this pilot cohort.
title: Single-Chain Variable Fragments Targeting Plasma Exosome Amyloid-β Peptide Subtypes for Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease.

text: Background Wolbachia are obligatory bacterial endosymbionts of Dirofilaria immitis heartworms, necessary for worm development, reproductive capability, and viability. We quantitatively examined microfilariae and Wolbachia in doxycycline-treated, heartworm-positive dogs. Methods Microfilaremic heartworm-positive dogs were identified in municipalities within the target areas of Rio de Janeiro and enrolled in this study. Dog owners agreed to allow blood draws from their dogs on day 0 and days 60 and 90 (± 5 days), and to administer doxycycline 10 mg/kg BID for 28 days, with weekly phone follow-up to help ensure compliance. Modified Knott's tests were performed on each experimental day; a portion of each sample was retained and frozen at - 20 °C, and the remaining quantities were submitted for digital PCR (dPCR) of microfilarial and Wolbachia burdens.
title: Persistence of Wolbachia DNA in Dirofilaria immitis-infected canines after doxycycline-only treatment in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil.

text: None of the dogs enrolled in the study received any macrocyclic lactone during the study. Results Thirty-one microfilaremic dogs completed the study, with 27 remaining microfilaremic throughout. Wolbachia were cleared from 25 of the dogs by day 90, demonstrating that the doxycycline dose was fully effective in those cases. Interestingly, 6 dogs remained dPCR positive on the quantitative assessment, and the proportions of Wolbachia/D. immitis on days 60 and 90 were significantly (p Conclusions This study demonstrates that Wolbachia DNA may persist in some dogs for 90 days after doxycycline-only therapy. These data may reflect the lack of macrocyclic lactone use or higher adult burdens in some dogs; however, it is not possible to confidently conclude these factors entirely underpin our observations.
title: Persistence of Wolbachia DNA in Dirofilaria immitis-infected canines after doxycycline-only treatment in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil.

text: We suggest that further studies should investigate whether this is related to lack of efficacy of doxycycline in certain Wolbachia subpopulations or to other factors.
title: Persistence of Wolbachia DNA in Dirofilaria immitis-infected canines after doxycycline-only treatment in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil.

text: This retrospective study describes the relative frequency of common diseases in pet Guinea pigs ( Cavia porcellus , GP) presented to a specialist exotic-animal clinic (Exo-Pet Veterinary Center, Budapest, Hungary). Data from 600 GPs across 1768 visits were reviewed; 51.3% were male and 48.7% female. Malocclusion of the molars was the most common problem (27.5%), followed by urinary tract diseases (18.67%), reproductive tract diseases (16.2%), ectoparasites (16.5%), neoplasms (tumors), and tumor-like lesions (15.8%). We fitted multivariable logistic-regression models with coat type, age, and sex as predictors. Almost one-third of the intact females (32.40%) had ovarian cysts. Age was associated with the recorded incidence of several diseases, although diagnostic opportunity was generally greater in older animals.
title: Diseases of Pet Guinea Pigs (<i>Cavia porcellus</i>) Presented to a Specialist Exotic-Animal Clinic: A Retrospective Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: The incidence of infectious diseases (e.g., fungal disease) declined with age. Owners should be made aware of ectoparasites and fungal infections to prevent potential zoonotic disease. The odds of ovarian cysts, neoplasms (tumors) and tumor-like lesions, gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary and urinary disease increased with age; these associations remained after adjustment for the number of veterinary visits. Males are more likely to develop malocclusion of the molars and incisors. Regular, detailed dental examinations of GPs are important for both prevention and early diagnosis.
title: Diseases of Pet Guinea Pigs (<i>Cavia porcellus</i>) Presented to a Specialist Exotic-Animal Clinic: A Retrospective Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Oxygen inhaled through respiration is consumed in the mitochondria, mainly for oxidative phosphorylation to produce energy. Too little or too much oxygen can be extremely harmful to humans. Insufficient oxygen supply to tissues and organs can result in either dysfunctions or necrosis. However, when the oxygen supply is over supplied, the body is unable to consume the excessive oxygen, which puts the cells in a state of hyperoxia, leading to the production of a large number of reactive oxygen species, which can further cause oxidative damage to the cell membranes and organelles, leading to oxygen toxicity. Although the body has several oxygen-sensing mechanisms to prevent organs and cells from being exposed to hypoxia- or hyperoxia-induced oxidative stress, the relevant capacity and duration of action are relatively limited.
title: Oxygen physiology and mechanisms of oxygen toxicity: a narrative review.

text: Thus, continuous and real-time individualized monitoring and guidance is particularly important in oxygen therapy, especially in the elderly, in order to correct hypoxemia and tissue hypoxia while avoiding or reducing oxygen toxicity caused by hyperoxia. This review aims to briefly summarize the physiology of oxygen and to update the latest progress regarding the mechanism of oxygen toxicity, providing theoretical insights on oxygen therapy practice.
title: Oxygen physiology and mechanisms of oxygen toxicity: a narrative review.

text: The gut microbiota‒host metabolism axis is a critical determinant of metabolic health, yet its functional activity remains difficult to monitor in vivo . The gut microbiota ferments undigested food components such as dietary fibers and proteins, yielding various important metabolites and gases that impact human metabolism. This review synthesizes current evidence on intestinal gases, primarily hydrogen (H 2 ), methane (CH 4 ) and hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S), as non-invasive markers of the trade-off between saccharolytic and proteolytic fermentation. Within the current review, we evaluate the concentrations of important gut metabolites and gases and techniques to measure intestinal gases, including stable isotope breath tests, volatile organic compound (VOC) profiling, and respiration chambers.
title: Intestinal gases as markers to study the diet-gut microbiota-host metabolism axis in humans and their relationship to metabolic health.

text: Crucially, we highlight that these gases may function not only as metabolic byproducts and biomarkers of microbial activity but as active signaling molecules influencing gastrointestinal transit, satiety, and systemic inflammation. This review concludes that real-time gas monitoring provides a unique opportunity to study real-time gut microbial fermentation. We propose a framework for phenotyping individual or subgroup-based fermentation patterns to guide personalized nutritional interventions for obesity and type 2 diabetes.
title: Intestinal gases as markers to study the diet-gut microbiota-host metabolism axis in humans and their relationship to metabolic health.

text: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) initiates infection in mucosal epithelial cells, forming characteristic lesions before establishing lifelong latency in sensory neurons. The innate immune response to HSV is critically mediated by the Toll-like receptor (TLR) family. Expressed in a cell‑type‑specific manner, TLRs recognize viral components, leading to the production of interferons and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Different cell populations, by virtue of their unique TLR expression profiles and signaling contexts, mount specialized and non-redundant responses to the same viral pathogen. We systematically synthesize current research to elucidate the roles of specific TLRs in major cellular targets of HSV, including mucosal epithelial cells, fibroblasts, plasmacytoid dendritic cells, macrophages, peripheral neurons, and resident central nervous system cells.
title: The cell-type-specific roles of Toll-like receptors in herpes simplex virus infection and pathogenesis.

text: By examining how TLR-mediated sensing and signaling diverge across this cellular landscape, this article provides an integrated framework for understanding the coordinated, multi-layered immune defense against HSV and highlights the implications for pathogenesis and therapeutic strategies.
title: The cell-type-specific roles of Toll-like receptors in herpes simplex virus infection and pathogenesis.

text: Traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) is believed to increase the risk of autoimmune diseases, including the autoimmune demyelinating disease multiple sclerosis (MS), in humans. The adaptive immune response against one of the key MS autoantigens, myelin basic protein (MBP), is elevated in mice and persists in patients with SCI even 10 years after the initial injury. Here, we show that β1i-enriched immunoproteasomes and PA28β subunits are elevated as early as 12 h post-SCI in DA rats, and all proteasome catalytic immunosubunits are highly abundant in the injured spinal cord of DA and SD rats 7-14 days post-SCI; these changes may therefore represent a primary event of the adaptive myelin-reactive immune response.
title: Mogamulizumab Suppresses Induction of Myelin-Reactive Antibodies After Experimental Spinal Cord Injury.

text: Mogamulizumab bound a recombinant rat CCR4 N-terminal extracellular fragment, albeit less strongly than the corresponding human fragment, and treatment was associated with weaker CCR4-associated immunoreactivity in peripheral blood leukocyte lysates. Plasma samples from rats with SCI treated with mogamulizumab were characterized by lower levels of antibodies to MBP compared with those from the non-treated group, and by day 60 of the experiment, this discrepancy reached statistical significance. Compared with non-treated animals, rats treated with mogamulizumab showed a significantly decreased glial scar size and total area of cyst-like cavities.
title: Mogamulizumab Suppresses Induction of Myelin-Reactive Antibodies After Experimental Spinal Cord Injury.

text: Thus, mogamulizumab therapy not only improves the morphological features of the glial scar but also suppresses the autoimmune response against myelin, and may offer a complementary immunological strategy for spinal cord protection following injury.
title: Mogamulizumab Suppresses Induction of Myelin-Reactive Antibodies After Experimental Spinal Cord Injury.

text: The rapid evolution and emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants have posed significant public health challenges due to enhanced transmissibility and diverse clinical outcomes. While the effects of these variants in humans have been extensively investigated, their impact on domestic animals remains insufficiently understood. Given the close interaction between humans and dogs, along with documented cases of human-to-animal transmission and the potential role of companion animals as reservoirs for viral evolution, understanding the molecular dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 infection in dogs is of considerable importance. However, in vivo infection studies in non-laboratory animal species are highly resource intensive, time-consuming, require ABSL3 facilities, and involve ethical constraints, limiting their widespread application.
title: Variant-Specific Temporal Transcriptomic Responses of Ex Vivo Dog Lung Explants to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron Infection.

text: In this context, ex vivo culture systems provide a practical and physiologically relevant alternative. Therefore, in the present study, we employed an ex vivo lung explant culture model derived from domestic dogs to investigate host responses to the SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants. Comprehensive transcriptomic profiling across multiple time points post-infection revealed significant alterations in genes associated with cell adhesion, structural components, extracellular matrix (ECM) organization and regulation, immune responses, mitochondrial activity, oxidative phosphorylation, and ribosomal function. Both variants induced marked downregulation of ECM-associated and T-cell-related genes, suggesting disruption of tissue integrity and suppression of adaptive immune responses.
title: Variant-Specific Temporal Transcriptomic Responses of Ex Vivo Dog Lung Explants to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron Infection.

text: The Delta variant was characterized by early and sustained suppression of immune-associated signaling pathways, particularly T-cell receptor signaling, whereas the Omicron variant induced stronger activation of genes associated with mitochondrial activity, oxidative phosphorylation, and translational responses. At later stages of infection, especially at 24 h post-infection (hpi), canine lung explants exhibited increased expression of genes related to tissue repair, epithelial maintenance, mitochondrial function, and ribosomal activity, suggesting activation of compensatory responses aimed at maintaining cellular stability under viral stress.
title: Variant-Specific Temporal Transcriptomic Responses of Ex Vivo Dog Lung Explants to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron Infection.

text: Notably, several hub genes were identified, including CD2 , CD3D , CD3E , CD27 , PTPRC , ZAP70 , SYK , and LCP2 in Delta infection, and FLT3LG , MRPL2 , MRPL4 , MRPS11 , MRPS12 , RPS13 , and RPS5 in Omicron infection, which are involved in critical pathways associated with immune signaling, mitochondrial function, metabolic regulation, and protein synthesis. Furthermore, the observed mitochondrial and ribosomal responses may indicate that therapeutic strategies aimed at supporting mitochondrial function and modulating excessive inflammation could potentially help reduce lung damage during severe infection.
title: Variant-Specific Temporal Transcriptomic Responses of Ex Vivo Dog Lung Explants to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron Infection.

text: Overall, this study provides important insights into the transcriptomic response of dog lung explants following exposure to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants and also highlights the utility of ex vivo canine lung explant cultures as a valuable platform for studying host-pathogen interactions.
title: Variant-Specific Temporal Transcriptomic Responses of Ex Vivo Dog Lung Explants to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron Infection.

text: With global pollinator populations in decline and colony collapse disorder threatening honey bee colony loss, understanding the biology and management of alternative pollinators has become increasingly urgent. Although commercially managed species-particularly honeybees and a few bumblebee species-have been studied extensively, the vast majority of bee species (~80%) are solitary. As such, solitary bees provide a more appropriate foundation for informing conservation and management strategies than their social and eusocial counterparts. In particular, the native North American Blue Orchard Bee Osmia lignaria Say (Megachilidae) has received increasing attention as a viable pollinator for a wide range of crops.
title: Using the Solitary Pollinator <i>Osmia lignaria</i> to Bridge Agricultural Practice and Ecological Theory.

text: However, solitary bee species such as Osmia remain underutilized as model systems for linking behavioral ecology to pollination function, despite their growing use in agricultural systems. In this synthesis, we review current knowledge on Osmia lignaria 's developmental plasticity, nesting behavior, foraging strategies, pollination services, and major stressors. We place special emphasis on how environmental conditions and management practices influence its performance as a crop pollinator and as a model organism for ecological research. We also identify key knowledge gaps to help guide future ecological research and inform more sustainable pollination strategies in both agricultural and natural systems.
title: Using the Solitary Pollinator <i>Osmia lignaria</i> to Bridge Agricultural Practice and Ecological Theory.

text: Background AI-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSSs) can help primary care clinicians provide higher quality care amid rising case complexity and resource constraints. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness and safety in primary care practice is lacking. Objective We synthesized evidence on the effectiveness and safety of AI-CDSSs compared with usual care or non-AI-based systems in primary care settings. Methods We conducted a systematic review following the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and reported the results according to PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines.
title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation.

text: We included experimental and quasi-experimental studies evaluating AI-CDSSs used by health care professionals in primary care settings, compared with usual care or non-AI-based decision support systems, and that reported clinician-, patient-, or system-level outcomes, or safety. An information specialist designed the search strategies and systematically reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and CENTRAL from inception to June 27, 2025. Reviewers independently performed the selection and extraction processes. Data extraction was informed by the DECIDE-AI and CONSORT-AI (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials-AI) reporting guidelines and the APPRAISE-AI tool. We independently assessed the risk of bias using Risk of Bias-2 or Risk of Bias in Non-Randomized Studies of Interventions.
title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation.

text: Owing to substantial heterogeneity, we conducted a synthesis without meta-analysis and explored heterogeneity using an adapted Non-Adoption, Abandonment, Scale-Up, Spread, and Sustainability-informed implementation-context classification. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251119225). Results We identified 4074 records through database searches and 12 additional records through citation searching and trial registration checking. We included 14 records on 11 distinct studies, including 4 experimental and 7 quasi-experimental studies. The risk of bias was high in all experimental studies and serious to critical in quasi-experimental studies. AI-CDSSs showed more consistent positive effects on workflow-related outcomes in structured and protocolized decision contexts, particularly for screening, referral, and alert optimization tasks.
title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation.

text: Patient-level effects were limited and inconsistent, particularly in more complex contexts involving heterogeneous conditions or preference-sensitive decisions. System-level outcomes were heterogeneous, with isolated improvements in service delivery and utilization outcomes. Safety evaluation was rare and poorly specified. Only 2 studies prespecified safety outcomes, and the reported safety information mainly involved technical malfunctions or self-reported side effects. No study reported clinician interaction measures such as agreement with, override of, or reliance on AI outputs. Interpretation of the findings is limited by substantial heterogeneity, short follow-up periods, predominantly high or critical risk of bias, and evidence derived exclusively from high-income countries.
title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation.

text: Conclusions AI-CDSSs in primary care may provide more consistent benefits for workflow-related and process-level outcomes in structured and protocolized decision contexts, while evidence on safety remains insufficient to support confident routine implementation. This systematic review reveals an important gap between the rapid development of AI-CDSSs and the lack of robust, comparable evidence to support their reliable use in primary care.
title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation.

text: Bacterial angular leaf spot, caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. mangiferaeindicae (Xcm), is an important disease that constrains mango production. Resistance-associated molecular markers can improve the efficiency of resistant germplasm screening and accelerate mango breeding; however, such markers remain limited for bacterial angular leaf spot. In this study, transcriptome and whole-genome resequencing data from the highly resistant cultivar 'Renong No. 1' and the highly susceptible cultivar 'Keitt' were reanalyzed to identify nonsynonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in candidate resistance-related genes. Among 86 candidate SNPs converted into Kompetitive Allele-Specific PCR (KASP) assays, 37 generated clear and stable genotype clusters in 25 mango accessions with known resistance phenotypes.
title: Development and Preliminary Verification of Specific KASP Markers for Mango Resistance to Bacterial Angular Leaf Spot.

text: SNP26 showed high consistency with the resistance phenotypes of these accessions and was subsequently used to genotype 322 mango germplasm accessions, which were separated into two genotype groups containing 34 and 288 accessions, respectively. Based on the SNP26 genotyping results, 72 accessions were selected for indoor fruit-puncture inoculation and classified into five resistance levels according to lesion development. SNP26 was located at position 1,299,510 on chromosome 15 within the coding region of HSP83A . The alleles were G in 'Keitt' and A in 'Renong No. 1', resulting in a leucine-to-valine substitution. Sanger sequencing confirmed the polymorphism at this locus. Following Xcm inoculation, HSP83A showed contrasting expression patterns between the two cultivars.
title: Development and Preliminary Verification of Specific KASP Markers for Mango Resistance to Bacterial Angular Leaf Spot.

text: Conserved domain and phylogenetic analyses indicated that HSP83A belongs to the HSP90/HtpG family and is closely related to homologous proteins in other plant species. These findings suggest that SNP26 is a promising resistance-associated marker for the preliminary identification of mango germplasm resistant to bacterial angular leaf spot and may facilitate marker-assisted selection in mango breeding.
title: Development and Preliminary Verification of Specific KASP Markers for Mango Resistance to Bacterial Angular Leaf Spot.

text: The occurrence of viral zoonotic spillover (the transmission of viruses from animals to humans) has attracted worldwide attention due to mounting concerns regarding viral threats such as avian influenza, Hendra, monkeypox, Nipah and bat coronaviruses. It is evident that these events deviate significantly from natural occurrences, being the conflation of ecological, environmental and social factors that are profoundly altering the boundaries between the animal and human domains. Consequently, in order to comprehend both the contemporary and prospective drivers of zoonotic viral spillover, a coordinated, comprehensive global One Health response is essential. The purpose of the present review is to analyze prevailing pathways of transmission between animal reservoirs and human populations.
title: Drivers of Viral Spillover: An Examination of How Pathogens Spread.

text: This examination involves the analysis of historical cases, including those of SARS and Ebola, as well as recent occurrences, such as the global pandemic of SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19). A secondary objective of this review is to comprehend the fundamental mechanisms of cross-species transmission. The development of effective strategies to mitigate the emergence of zoonotic viruses and prevent future pandemics is contingent on a robust understanding of these mechanisms. This analysis is key to identifying pandemic pathogens and preventing the spread of zoonotic viruses. In conclusion, the review provides a thorough evaluation of current global strategies to prevent the spread of zoonotic viruses, highlighting gaps in our understanding and areas for further research.
title: Drivers of Viral Spillover: An Examination of How Pathogens Spread.

text: Blood transfusion is an important supportive therapy in critically ill dogs, but transfusion reactions (TRs) remain a clinically relevant complication. This retrospective study evaluated whether pre-transfusion systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) was associated with transfusion-associated adverse events in dogs. Medical records of dogs receiving red-cell-containing blood products at a veterinary referral hospital in the Republic of Korea between December 2023 and May 2026 were reviewed. Among 146 transfusion episodes from 100 dogs, 142 episodes with evaluable primary outcomes were included in the primary outcome analysis. Transfusion-associated adverse events were identified more frequently in the SIRS group than in the No SIRS group (32.7% vs. 11.4%; p = 0.007).
title: Association Between Pre-Transfusion Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome and Transfusion-Associated Adverse Events in Dogs: A Retrospective Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: In univariable logistic regression, SIRS was associated with increased odds of the primary outcome (OR, 3.78; 95% CI, 1.36-10.51; p = 0.011). In a patient-clustered multivariable generalized estimating equation (GEE) analysis, the adjusted OR remained elevated at 3.57, although the association did not reach statistical significance (95% CI, 0.98-12.98; p = 0.053). Each additional fulfilled SIRS criterion was associated with increased odds of the primary outcome (OR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.10-2.41; p = 0.014). However, the association was attenuated and was not statistically significant in sensitivity analyses using stricter outcome definitions based on imputability and independent re-adjudication.
title: Association Between Pre-Transfusion Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome and Transfusion-Associated Adverse Events in Dogs: A Retrospective Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: These findings suggest an association between pre-transfusion SIRS and clinically suspected transfusion-associated adverse events under the broad retrospective primary outcome definition, but the results were sensitive to the level of diagnostic certainty required for outcome classification. The findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies using standardized reaction definitions and blinded outcome assessment.
title: Association Between Pre-Transfusion Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome and Transfusion-Associated Adverse Events in Dogs: A Retrospective Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Small ruminant lentiviruses (SRVLs), including ovine maedi-visna virus and caprine arthritis-encephalitis virus, are considered genetically a single pathogen that causes a progressive multisystemic inflammatory disease. Continuous interspecies transmission in areas where these species come into contact, along with dual infection in individual animals, results in recombination between variants. The main routes of infection are ingestion of infected colostrum and/or milk and inhalation of respiratory secretions. SRLVs primarily target monocytes/macrophages and dendritic cells. Following infection, chronic lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrates are observed in the main target organs: lungs, brain, joints, and mammary gland.
title: Current Perspectives on the Immunopathogenesis and Pathology of Small Ruminant Lentivirus Infections.

text: Infection with the virus causes lifelong infection in its host, characterized by slow progression until overt disease, which is observed in approximately one-third of the infected animals, occurs. The affected system appears to depend on SRLV strain tropism, the species affected, and the genetic background of each breed or animal. This review examines the immunopathogenesis and pathology of small ruminant lentiviruses.
title: Current Perspectives on the Immunopathogenesis and Pathology of Small Ruminant Lentivirus Infections.

text: The frequent resistance of breast cancer to radiotherapy and systemic therapies has resulted in suboptimal outcomes with traditional treatment regimens. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop more effective methods of treating breast cancer. This study concentrated on measuring the effectiveness of a combination of anti-cancer agent, ionomycin and radiotherapy on breast cancer cells. The combination of ionomycin and radiotherapy resulted in inhibition of the proliferation of breast cancer cells in vitro experiments, which was indicated by cell counting kit-8 and colony formation experiments. Ionomycin and radiotherapy caused Ca 2+ overload in mitochondrial cancer cells, opening the mitochondrial permeability transition pore, inducing reactive oxygen species generation, and increasing DNA double-strand breaks.
title: Ionomycin enhances radiosensitivity in breast cancer through reactive oxygen species generation and mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening.

text: The reduction in cell viability induced by ionomycin combined with radiotherapy was significantly reversed by N-acetyl-L-cysteine (a reactive oxygen species scavenger) and cyclosporine A (mitochondrial permeability transition pore channel inhibitor). The combination therapy extended the opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore in breast cancer cells, causing mitochondrial dysfunction. The prolonged opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore has been observed to raise the levels of cytochrome c and the levels of cleaved caspase-3 protein, which eventually resulted in an escalation in the rate of apoptosis. The treatment also decreased the migration and invasion of the breast cancer cells in this combination treatment.
title: Ionomycin enhances radiosensitivity in breast cancer through reactive oxygen species generation and mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening.

text: This research indicates that ionomycin may function as an effective radiosensitizer, therefore enhancing the efficacy of radiotherapy in the treatment of breast cancer.
title: Ionomycin enhances radiosensitivity in breast cancer through reactive oxygen species generation and mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening.

text: Biological invasions often generate complex ecological paradoxes, particularly when invasive species act as ecosystem engineers that simultaneously compete with and benefit native communities. Understanding these dual dynamics is critical for managing urban biodiversity. Here, we investigated the interactions between invasive monk parakeets (Myiopsitta monachus) and native avifauna to assess the balance between behavioral competition and structural commensalism. We assessed competition through (1) agonistic interactions and (2) correlations between parakeet abundance and that of native species. Commensalism was evaluated by analyzing tenant species in parakeet nests and the drivers of their occurrence.
title: Balancing conflict and coexistence: Interactions between invasive monk parakeets and native urban birds.
journal: Ecological applications : a publication of the Ecological Society of America

text: Agonistic interactions manifested through highly species-specific conflicts: Density-dependent aggression with rock pigeons (Columba livia) was strictly reciprocal, while parakeets directed targeted intimidation toward Eurasian magpies (Pica pica). Conversely, direct agonistic encounters involving either Eurasian tree sparrows (Passer montanus) or house sparrows (Passer domesticus) were negligible. However, spatially, Passer spp. abundance correlated negatively with the number of parakeet nest chambers (a proxy for parakeet abundance), whereas common blackbirds (Turdus merula) showed a positive correlation. Furthermore, parakeets provided a massive structural subsidy. We recorded 11 native species breeding in 48% of surveyed parakeet nests (N = 252). Tree sparrows and stock doves (Columba oenas) dominated this tenant community, accounting for 86% of native breeding pairs.
title: Balancing conflict and coexistence: Interactions between invasive monk parakeets and native urban birds.
journal: Ecological applications : a publication of the Ecological Society of America

text: Native breeding abundance-including tree sparrows, stock doves, and rock pigeons-as well as total species richness scaled positively with nest chamber density. Yet, active parakeet presence limited nest use for stock doves but did not deter tree sparrows or rock pigeons from successful co-nesting. Our findings reveal a dual ecological dynamic: Parakeets show a negative spatial correlation with declining urban sparrows, yet simultaneously act as ecosystem engineers by providing valuable breeding habitats for local biodiversity. However, without data on tenant reproductive success and pathogen transmission, these novel subsidies risk functioning as ecological traps. Consequently, while indiscriminate nest removal could inadvertently harm native tenants, current evidence does not confirm the long-term safety of this commensalism.
title: Balancing conflict and coexistence: Interactions between invasive monk parakeets and native urban birds.
journal: Ecological applications : a publication of the Ecological Society of America

text: Effective management must transcend simple eradication, adopting a holistic framework that weighs the loss of nesting resources against the competitive and sanitary risks of retaining these invasive populations.
title: Balancing conflict and coexistence: Interactions between invasive monk parakeets and native urban birds.
journal: Ecological applications : a publication of the Ecological Society of America

text: Deslorelin (C 64 H 83 N 17 O 12 ) is a peptide GnRH agonist drug with monoisotopic mass 1281.64 Da applied as a drug-releasing implant in veterinary medicine for promoting ovulation and male/female contraception. Despite relative safety, it is suspected of reproductive toxicity and potential harm to unborn or breast-fed children. The compound was designed for high potency and prolonged half-life making it difficult to measure quantitatively in serum. A deslorelin LC-MS/MS method relies on detecting unmetabolized undegraded intact peptide, a crucial consideration since certain metabolites are thought to have activity. We propose a method for analyzing deslorelin indirectly by cleaving a unique portion of the carboxy terminus containing the modified proline ProNHEt (N-ethyl-2-pyrrolidine carboxamide), which can be removed by Clostridiopeptidase specific for arginine bonds.
title: Proposed Method for Mass Spectrometric Measurement of the Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonist Deslorelin.

text: ProNHEt can be extracted from digested serum, reacted to an N-t-butyldimethylsilyl derivative and analyzed by GC-MS/MS. Settings were optimized for detectability to <1 ppb, and derivatization gave maximum yields by adjustment of solvent, reaction time, temperature and additives. MALDI-TOF applied to deslorelin revealed binding by copper. The proposed method can be used to measure deslorelin in serum samples from various zoo and small animals. Detection of deslorelin by examination of released ProNHEt is proposed to have applicability to other GnRH superagonists such as triptorelin and deslorelin breakdown products that exhibit the ProNHEt structure.
title: Proposed Method for Mass Spectrometric Measurement of the Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonist Deslorelin.

text: Growth hormone has the potential to modulate inflammatory responses, alleviate intestinal injury, and preserve intestinal health. However, its limited availability from natural sources restricts further research and practical applications. Therefore, we optimized the coding sequence for porcine growth hormone (pGH) and constructed recombinant Lactococcus lactis ( L. lactis ) expressing pGH. The effect of L. lactis (pNZ8148-pGH) against intestinal damage was evaluated in mice with DSS-induced colitis. Orally administered L. lactis (pNZ8148-pGH) attenuated the symptoms of DSS-induced colitis, including weight loss, colon shortening, and elevated colonic damage scores (CDS), and improved colonic tissue morphology. Compared with the DSS group, L.
title: Expression of Growth Hormone in <i>Lactococcus lactis</i> and Its Effect on Intestinal Barrier Damage in Mice with DSS-Induced Colitis.

text: lactis (pNZ8148-pGH) significantly reduced serum diamine oxidase (DAO) activity, colonic myeloperoxidase activity, and serum D-lactate and endotoxin levels while increasing colonic occludin and claudin-1 levels. Colonic tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-2 (IL-2), and interleukin-6 levels decreased significantly, whereas the interleukin-10 (IL-10) level increased after L. lactis (pNZ8148-pGH) administration. Furthermore, L. lactis (pNZ8148-pGH) significantly increased the numbers of colonic Ki67- and PCNA-positive cells and their positive indices. In addition, compared with the DSS group, L. lactis (pNZ8148) significantly decreased CDS, serum DAO activity, and colonic IL-2 level while increasing colonic occludin and IL-10 levels. In conclusion, oral administration of L.
title: Expression of Growth Hormone in <i>Lactococcus lactis</i> and Its Effect on Intestinal Barrier Damage in Mice with DSS-Induced Colitis.

text: lactis (pNZ8148-pGH) maintained intestinal barrier integrity, suppressed inflammation, promoted mucosal repair, and alleviated DSS-induced colitis.
title: Expression of Growth Hormone in <i>Lactococcus lactis</i> and Its Effect on Intestinal Barrier Damage in Mice with DSS-Induced Colitis.

text: Background The 2016-2019 sylvatic yellow fever epidemic in Brazil spread into the peri-urban areas of São Paulo State, raising concerns about the potential resurgence of urban yellow fever transmission in the Americas. In Alberto Löfgren State Park (PEAL), Serra da Cantareira, one of the world's largest urban forests, southern brown howler monkeys became locally extinct in early January 2018 following a short-lived outbreak. Methods To investigate mosquito feeding patterns during and after the yellow fever outbreak, we collected 5,001 female mosquitoes between December 2017 and March 2020, and screened 143 blood-engorged specimens using Nanopore sequencing.
title: Identification of vertebrate hosts of mosquito blood meals following the 2017-2018 yellow fever outbreak in São Paulo State.

text: Results Vertebrate hosts were identified as the source of blood meals in 74.8% (107/143) of samples, revealing that mosquitoes fed predominantly on mammals (83.2%, 89/107), but also on birds (10.3%, 11/107), and on multiple hosts (6.5%, 7/107). Humans accounted for 76.6% (82/107) of identified blood meals. Other hosts included non-human primate, dog, opossum, mouse and passerine birds. Among Haemagogus leucocelaenus, the primary yellow fever virus (YFV) vector at PEAL, 94.6% (35/37) of blood meals were human-derived, while 5.4% (2/37) contained non-human primate blood. Additionally, two engorged Haemagogus capricornii (100%, 2/2), another YFV vector, fed on humans. Untargeted sequencing recovered a complete YFV genome from an Hg. leucocelaenus specimen with human blood, providing direct evidence of active viral circulation within PEAL.
title: Identification of vertebrate hosts of mosquito blood meals following the 2017-2018 yellow fever outbreak in São Paulo State.

text: Conclusions Sylvatic YFV vectors captured in urban forest fragments of the Serra da Cantareira exhibited marked anthropophilic feeding behaviour. Our findings underscore the risk of mosquito-mediated spillover into densely populated São Paulo, emphasising the urgent need for sustained vaccination together with entomological and virological surveillance to track and respond to yellow fever outbreaks in peri-urban settings.
title: Identification of vertebrate hosts of mosquito blood meals following the 2017-2018 yellow fever outbreak in São Paulo State.

text: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is a gasotransmitter molecule that regulates essential plant biological processes. In the context of climate change and increasing flooding events, its role in plant responses to oxygen (O2) deficiency has gained significant attention. Accumulating evidence indicates that H2S exerts beneficial effects under hypoxia by modulating antioxidant defenses, mitochondrial function, and hormonal signaling, mainly through its ability to refine protein activity via the post-translational modification (PTM) of persulfidation. Here, we discuss how this PTM is linked to the gasotransmitter molecule nitric oxide (NO) and reactive oxygen species (ROS), and how they can act synergistically or antagonistically, influencing the cell redox state and survival.
title: The role of H2S and its derivatives in plant responses to low O2.

text: Additionally, we examine how H2S turnover is intrinsically linked to O2 availability, acting as a conserved mediator of low O2 responses in different domains of life. By integrating biochemical insights with molecular signaling, we underscore the potential of H2S in enhancing crop resilience to low O2-related stresses, such as submergence and waterlogging.
title: The role of H2S and its derivatives in plant responses to low O2.

text: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD) are both neurodegenerative diseases characterized by aggregates composed of 4-repeat (4R) tau protein. They have distinct neuropathological features and classic clinical symptoms; however, the signs and symptoms overlap across the two syndromes. Accumulating evidence suggests that dysregulated immune response is a major contributing factor to neurodegeneration but its role in 4R-tauopathies remains undetermined. The aim is to explore the involvement of neuroinflammation from a vascular perspective in 4R-tauopathies. Autopsies from four controls, three PSP, and three CBD cases were assessed. Samples were obtained from the superior/middle frontal gyrus (S/M-FG) and basal ganglia (BG).
title: The characteristics of perivascular proinflammation in 4-repeat tauopathies.

text: Immunofluorescence staining included neuroinflammatory markers: glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1 (Iba1), cluster of differentiation 68 (CD68); vascular markers: collagen type IV (ColIV), monocarboxylate transporter-1 (MCT1), and α-smooth muscle actin (αSMA). Maximally projected confocal z-stack images of vasculature were used as a mask to quantify total perivascular GFAP+/Iba1+/CD68+ labeling. GFAP immunoreactivity ratio between MCT1 and αSMA double labeled arteries and veins was quantified to further differentiate venular and arteriolar involvement into proinflammatory activation. Both PSP and CBD had widespread perivascular proinflammatory changes, although greater in CBD. The activated GFAP+ astrocytes and microglia/macrophages in CBD were distributed extensively in S/M-FG and BG, with S/M-FG WM more affected.
title: The characteristics of perivascular proinflammation in 4-repeat tauopathies.

text: In PSP, abundant neuroinflammation was found in BG. The involvement of vasculature type was distinct among the two 4R-tauopathies, while CBD showed comparable proinflammatory changes in arterioles and venules, PSP exhibited predominant proinflammation in venules. The regional pattern of perivascular proinflammation differed between PSP and CBD, corresponding to the characteristic affected brain regions. CBD had more severe perivascular proinflammation that involved both arterioles and venules, while venules were more affected in PSP. Perivascular proinflammation may be a critical pathophysiological process in 4R-tauopathies.
title: The characteristics of perivascular proinflammation in 4-repeat tauopathies.

text: Clinical relevance The retina is a unique and accessible window to the central nervous system and its vasculature. Ocular fundus examination is crucial for identifying diagnostic red flags indicative of life- and sight-threatening conditions, such as papilledema and central retinal artery occlusion. In the emergency department (ED), prompt recognition of these conditions is essential to reduce the risk of vision loss and serious complications. Methods This review summarizes advances in ocular fundus examination, imaging, and artificial intelligence (AI) for emergency care. Results The direct ophthalmoscope, a traditional tool for ocular fundus examination by nonophthalmology providers in the ED, is rarely utilized due to technical limitations and lack of user skill and confidence.
title: The Underutilized Ocular Fundus in Emergency Departments: Current Progress and Future Prospect of Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for Patient Care.

text: Recent advancements in retinal imaging technologies have introduced ocular fundus cameras with OCT as valuable alternatives. The advent of nonmydriatic and portable imaging devices has significantly expanded accessibility, enabling remote image interpretation and facilitating teleophthalmology consultations. Moreover, AI, especially deep-learning technology, has demonstrated considerable potential for automated ocular image interpretation. The latest developments in large language models show promise in providing aids in diagnosis and management. Conclusions Further research is needed to validate the reliability of AI-powered ocular fundus assessment and to explore how these emerging technologies can be effectively integrated into ED practice to enhance ocular fundus examination and improve patient care.
title: The Underutilized Ocular Fundus in Emergency Departments: Current Progress and Future Prospect of Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for Patient Care.

text: Following the successes of the messenger RNA (mRNA) lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines against COVID-19, mRNA-LNPs are being explored for varied multidose applications including cancer immunotherapies and protein replacement therapies. LNPs rely on poly(ethylene glycol)-lipid (PEG-lipid) coatings for stability, but increasing anti-PEG antibody prevalence threatens repeat-dose efficacy and increases pseudoallergic risk, creating an urgent need for alternatives. Here, we introduce poly(acrylamido) lipids (PAM-lipids), a family of polymer lipids that effectively replace PEG-lipids in mRNA-LNP formulations. Systematic variation of monomer chemistry, molar mass, and end group reveals critical structure-activity relationships determining LNP size, polydispersity, and transfection efficiency.
title: Poly(acrylamido) PEG-Alternative Lipids Rescue mRNA Efficacy during Repeated Dosing and Enhance Immune Cell Delivery.

text: Varying PAM monomer chemistry allows minimization of antipolymer antibody cross-reactivity, with multiple PAM-lipids demonstrating no anti-PEG antibody binding. Several PAM-LNPs exhibit superior mRNA transfection efficacy to PEGylated clinical benchmarks in vitro and in vivo across multiple cell types, organs, routes of administration, and mRNA cargos. In particular, lead PAM-LNPs enhance mRNA delivery to dendritic cells (up to 120-fold in vitro and 3-fold in vivo) and macrophages (4-fold in vivo), with 2.5-fold superior lymph node expression, driven in part by increased cellular association and lymphoid targeting. Crucially, PAM-LNPs evade circulating anti-PEG antibodies to rescue lost mRNA efficacy after repeated dosing, resulting in 300% mRNA expression relative to that of PEG-LNPs.
title: Poly(acrylamido) PEG-Alternative Lipids Rescue mRNA Efficacy during Repeated Dosing and Enhance Immune Cell Delivery.

text: These findings demonstrate PAM-lipids as a chemically varied, immunologically compatible family of PEG alternatives for mRNA-LNP therapeutics.
title: Poly(acrylamido) PEG-Alternative Lipids Rescue mRNA Efficacy during Repeated Dosing and Enhance Immune Cell Delivery.

text: Manuka honey contains bioactive phenolic and flavonoid chemicals with antibacterial and anti-inflammatory effects. The chemical profile and therapeutic efficiency of Manuka honey against Helicobacter pylori infection were investigated utilizing in-vitro and in-vivo models. The phenolic and flavonoid contents were profiled using HPLC. The antibacterial property of Manuka honey extract was determined using inhibitory zones, MIC, MBC, and time-kill tests. An H. pylori rat model was utilized to investigate changes in weight, bacterial burden, histological modifications, NF-κB expression, inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-4), oxidative stress indicators (CAT, SOD, MDA, NO), and biochemical parameters such as kidney and liver functioning.
title: Manuka honey as a multifunctional therapeutic against Helicobacter pylori: from chemical profiling to in vitro potency and in vivo gastroprotective efficacy.

text: HPLC examination identified seven phenolic chemicals, the most prevalent of which were coumaric, cinnamic, and chlorogenic acids, as well as seven flavonoids, dominated by chrysin, rutin, and kaempferol. Manuka honey demonstrated strong anti-H. pylori activity (inhibition zone 15.1 mm), equivalent to conventional medications with MIC 31.25 µg/mL and MBC 62.5 µg/mL. Time-kill curves revealed no significant differences from normal therapy. Manuka honey treated infected rats by restoring body weight, reducing stomach bacterial load, improving histology, and downregulating NF-κB expression. The treated rats showed decreased TNF-α, increased IL-4, improved antioxidant enzyme levels, lower oxidative stress indicators, and normalized liver and kidney functioning. Manuka honey has substantial anti-H.
title: Manuka honey as a multifunctional therapeutic against Helicobacter pylori: from chemical profiling to in vitro potency and in vivo gastroprotective efficacy.

text: pylori capacity, substantial anti-inflammatory properties, oxidative stress regulation, and protection of gastric tissue, hepatic, and renal functions, indicating its therapeutic usefulness as a natural complementary to H. pylori infection.
title: Manuka honey as a multifunctional therapeutic against Helicobacter pylori: from chemical profiling to in vitro potency and in vivo gastroprotective efficacy.

text: Camera traps generate imagery faster than people can review it, and artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to analyse it. This systematic review asks to what extent AI applied to camera-trap imagery has moved from benchmark performance to ecologically usable monitoring. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus was searched on 6 August 2026 for 2020-2026. Peer-reviewed English-language journal articles applying automated inference to imagery from unattended cameras observing free-ranging animals were included; captive or web-sourced imagery, non-image methods, reviews and conference papers were excluded. Of 637 records, 231 were read in full and 201 were included. Studies were appraised against six quality criteria, findings were synthesised as descriptive counts across five research questions, and performance was tabulated on each study's own metric, without meta-analysis.
title: Eyes in the Wild and Minds in the Loop: A Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence for Camera-Trap Wildlife Monitoring.

text: Output grew by about 29% per year. Detection and species classification each appear in 62% of studies, behaviour recognition in 5%, and study regions invert global biodiversity gradients. Only 62% of studies evaluate beyond their training data, a share unchanged since 2020; the measured generalisation penalty ranges from six to nearly seventy points. Only 35% report field deployment; costs appear only in deployment-oriented studies. The gap between benchmark performance and ecological practice remains the field's central challenge.
title: Eyes in the Wild and Minds in the Loop: A Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence for Camera-Trap Wildlife Monitoring.

text: Leiomyosarcoma (LMS), a malignant neoplasm of smooth muscle cell origin, is relatively rare in birds. This study presents the occurrence of this tumour in a 2-year-old male budgerigar. The bird was brought to the Ashian Veterinary Hospital with complaints of swelling in the medial area of the left leg. Clinical examination and radiological imaging confirmed the presence of soft tissue swelling in the medial region of the left leg. Empirical antibiotic and anti-inflammatory therapy were used to distinguish infectious inflammation from the tumour mass. After 12 days, a clinical diagnosis of suspected neoplasm was made due to a lack of improvement and increasing mass size. Given the deterioration of the bird's general condition, euthanasia was recommended and performed. At necropsy, all viscera were biopsied for histopathological evaluation.
title: Metastatic Leiomyosarcoma Involving Bone and Kidney in an Adult Budgerigar (Melopsittacus undulatus).

text: Microscopic examinations confirmed the initial diagnosis of LMS. To confirm the diagnosis, immunohistochemical staining was performed using antibodies to alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), vimentin and desmin. The results of α-SMA and desmin staining definitively confirmed the presence of an LMS neoplasm with metastasis to the bone and kidneys; however, vimentin staining was negative.
title: Metastatic Leiomyosarcoma Involving Bone and Kidney in an Adult Budgerigar (Melopsittacus undulatus).

text: The discovery of molecular glue degraders (MGDs) is undergoing a paradigm shift from serendipitous discovery toward empirical design. However, efficiently prioritizing active leads from synthetic libraries while simultaneously confirming their E3 dependency remains a formidable challenge. In this study, we introduce the glue perturbation screening (GPS) platform, a conceptual and technical advance that integrates high-throughput, low-cost Digital RNA with pertUrbation of Genes 2 (DRUG-seq2) with isogenic cereblon (CRBN) wild-type/knockout (WT/KO) models. The significance of our work lies in the development of a multi-dimensional readout that digitizes compound activity and mechanism in a single step.
title: A scalable, high-throughput glue perturbation screening platform for molecular glue discovery.

text: By mapping transcriptomic perturbations onto a coordinate system of differential expression and gene set enrichment, we establish a tiered prioritization strategy: distinguishing high-potency glues from non-specific toxic molecules and recognizing latent biological activities in sub-threshold compounds that guide further structural optimization. This platform provides a scalable, mechanism-aware roadmap for the rational discovery of next-generation degraders, offering a powerful tool to accelerate the targeting of "undruggable" proteins.
title: A scalable, high-throughput glue perturbation screening platform for molecular glue discovery.

text: Background Antiviral therapy for cats with feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) has traditionally been administered for 84 days, although the optimal duration of molnupiravir treatment remains unknown. Hypothesis/objectives To evaluate the efficacy of a 42-day course of molnupiravir, orally (PO), for naturally occurring FIP in cats. Animals Nineteen client-owned cats with newly diagnosed FIP. Methods Prospective pilot study. Cats received molnupiravir, PO, q12h for 42 days at a median dosage of 11.5 mg/kg (IQR, 10.2-12.5 mg/kg). Cats with ocular or neurological involvement were excluded. Clinical assessments were performed during treatment and for 6 months after treatment cessation. Results Nineteen cats were enrolled. Two cats failed to complete treatment because of death or persistent clinical signs.
title: Outcomes of a 42-day course of molnupiravir in cats with feline infectious peritonitis: a prospective descriptive study.

text: Fourteen of 19 cats (74%; 95% CI, 49-91) achieved sustained remission on an intention-to-treat basis. Each non-completer failed on day 5 or 10, respectively, within a window common to 42- and 84-day protocols, and therefore do not inform the question of treatment duration; among the 17 cats reaching day 42, 14 (82%; 95% CI, 57-96) remained in remission for at least 6 months. Three cats relapsed after treatment cessation; all responded to retreatment with molnupiravir at the same dosage extended to 84 days. Conclusions and clinical importance This prospective study suggests that a shortened course of molnupiravir is feasible in selected cats with non-ocular, non-neurological FIP.
title: Outcomes of a 42-day course of molnupiravir in cats with feline infectious peritonitis: a prospective descriptive study.
