text: Background Survivors of primary brain tumors (SPBT) frequently struggle to return to work. This study investigated work status and outcomes after tele-based vocational cognitive rehabilitation (t-VCR) in SPBT. Methods We retrospectively reviewed adults (≤65 years) with SPBT at an academic medical center who completed objective cognitive and patient-reported outcome measures between 5/2018 and 5/2022. Participants were grouped by employment status and compared on demographic and clinical characteristics. Work outcomes were analyzed in a subgroup who underwent t-VCR during standard clinical care. t-VCR treatment response was defined as return to work, increase to full-time work, or graduation from a workplace improvement plan versus baseline. Analyses used t-tests, chi-square, and McNemar tests, with content analysis identifying key interventions in responders.
title: Proof of concept using vocational tele-cognitive rehabilitation to improve work status in primary brain tumor.

text: Results Of 77 participants, 35 were working and 42 were unemployed upon referral. Unemployment was associated with worsened verbal learning and memory ( P Conclusion Worsened verbal learning and memory were associated with unemployment, highlighting the impact these cognitive symptoms can have on occupational functioning. Work status improved in the context of t-VCR and warrants further study. Among participants who demonstrated improvement, t-VCR was delivered as a multimodal, individualized intervention that addressed cognitive, emotional, fatigue, and practical workplace-related challenges.
title: Proof of concept using vocational tele-cognitive rehabilitation to improve work status in primary brain tumor.

text: Fear memory reconsolidation provides a temporal window for modifying established fear memories, yet the underlying cellular and neural circuit mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Using in vivo fiber photometry and chemogenetic approaches in freely moving mice, we show that propofol modulates fear memory reconsolidation by inhibiting D2 receptor-expressing neurons in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). These neurons exhibit heightened activity during fear memory reconsolidation and project prominently to the basolateral amygdala (BLA). Notably, local pharmacological activation of D2 receptors in the mPFC recapitulates the fear-attenuating effect of propofol when administered during the reconsolidation window.
title: Propofol Modulates Fear Memory Reconsolidation by Inhibiting D2 Receptor-Expressing Neurons in the Medial Prefrontal Cortex.

text: Circuit-level investigations further show that propofol suppresses the reconsolidation-associated enhancement of the mPFC D2 -BLA synaptic transmission, and chemogenetic activation of this projection counteracts the effect of propofol on fear memory reconsolidation. Moreover, selective knockdown of D2 receptors in BLA-projecting mPFC neurons diminishes the effect of propofol, supporting a critical role for D2 receptor signaling within this projection-defined circuit. Together, these findings identify the mPFC D2 -BLA circuit as a key neural substrate through which propofol modulates fear memory reconsolidation and highlight prefrontal D2 receptor signaling as a potential target for reconsolidation-based interventions aimed at maladaptive fear memories.
title: Propofol Modulates Fear Memory Reconsolidation by Inhibiting D2 Receptor-Expressing Neurons in the Medial Prefrontal Cortex.

text: In this study, 269 fecal specimens were sampled from domestic cats displaying symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals in Daklak and Gialai provinces in Central Vietnam during July 2023 to July 2025. The polymerase chain reaction method was applied to determine the feline parvovirus DNA in the obtained samples. Positive samples were randomly chosen for full-length VP2 gene sequencing using the Sanger method. The feline parvovirus DNA was detected in 25 (9.29%) of 269 samples. The viral DNA-positive rate was 17.65% (15/85) from cats aged below 6 months, significantly higher than that from 6-12- and >12-month-old cats. Seven complete VP2 sequences were successfully obtained from the identified strains, exhibiting a high degree of nucleotide identity (98.23-100%).
title: Molecular Detection and VP2 Characterization of Feline and Canine Parvoviruses in Domestic Cats in Central Vietnam.

text: Comparison to that of other sequences retrieved from GenBank indicated that seven current Vietnamese sequences displayed the highest nucleotide identity was from 99.08 to 99.94 with that of viral strains from China, Italy, and Spain. Phylogenetic analysis constructed using the complete VP2 gene sequences indicated that six Vietnamese sequences obtained belonged to feline panleukopenia virus (FPV) lineage and divided into several clusters, which were closely related to viruses from China, Italy, and Spain. The remaining one sequence was defined as canine parvovirus (CPV) which was genetically related to previous Vietnamese CPV-2c and Chinese strains. Twenty-six negative selection sites were detected in the VP2 protein of the current Vietnamese FPV/CPV strains in this study.
title: Molecular Detection and VP2 Characterization of Feline and Canine Parvoviruses in Domestic Cats in Central Vietnam.

text: Purpose of review Supervised-exercise therapy (SET) is a cornerstone intervention for management of peripheral artery disease (PAD) and is associated with improvement in ambulatory functional status. Despite strong evidence supporting the benefits of SET, accessibility and adherence remains a challenge, underling its full clinical potential. Home-based exercise therapy (HBET) has emerged as more accessible alternative to SET. This paper reviews the benefits of exercise in PAD, explores the role of home-based exercise therapy in the management of PAD, and describes the essential components of HBET in contemporary clinical practice. Recent findings HBET programs have demonstrated similar improvements in ambulatory function, including walking distance and pain-free walking distance, as established SET regimens.
title: The Role of Home-Based Exercise in the Management of Peripheral Artery Disease.
journal: Current treatment options in cardiovascular medicine

text: Recent clinical trials and meta-analysis have established HBET as a reasonable alternative to SET, as reflected in the latest multi-societal clinical guidelines. Summary Functional and quality of life improvements with HBET parallel those with SET and outperform routine exercise education. Successful HBET should include both monitoring and behavioral intervention components to improve adherence and long-term symptomatic improvements. Providers should tailor HBET to the individual patient's needs and limitations. Ongoing research aims to understand the optimal platform to deliver HBET programs to a wide range of patients with symptomatic PAD.
title: The Role of Home-Based Exercise in the Management of Peripheral Artery Disease.
journal: Current treatment options in cardiovascular medicine

text: Bordetella hinzii is a rare, opportunistic Gram-negative bacterium traditionally associated with poultry but increasingly identified as a human pathogen in immunocompromised individuals. We report the first Indian case of B. hinzii causing antenatal sepsis in a 27-year-old pregnant woman with homozygous sickle cell anaemia and β-thalassemia minor, leading to intrauterine fetal demise at 24 weeks of gestation. The patient presented with breathlessness, edema, and absent fetal movements. Laboratory results showed severe anaemia, leucocytosis, and raised inflammatory markers. Blood cultures yielded B. hinzii , confirmed by the VITEK 2 system (bioMérieux, Marcy-l'Étoile, France). The isolate was susceptible to meropenem, piperacillin/tazobactam, cefepime, ceftazidime, and co-trimoxazole, but resistant to aminoglycosides and ceftriaxone.
title: Bordetella hinzii Antenatal Sepsis in a Pregnant Woman With Sickle Cell Disease and Intrauterine Fetal Demise: A rare and first case report from India.

text: The patient improved with empirical therapy, though fetal loss had occurred. This case highlights the emerging clinical significance of B. hinzii in high-risk pregnancies and the need for advanced microbiological tools and antimicrobial therapy in managing rare opportunistic infections.
title: Bordetella hinzii Antenatal Sepsis in a Pregnant Woman With Sickle Cell Disease and Intrauterine Fetal Demise: A rare and first case report from India.

text: Kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) features an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We investigated the role of transcription factor POU2F2 in KIRC oncogenesis and macrophage polarization. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics showed that POU2F2 is upregulated in KIRC and associated with metastasis and poor prognosis. POU2F2 knockdown inhibited KIRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. POU2F2 expression correlated with macrophage infiltration and JAK-STAT signaling. Co-culture assays showed that POU2F2 silencing reduced macrophage recruitment and shifted M2 polarization toward an anti-tumor M1 phenotype. Overall, POU2F2 acts as an oncogenic driver and prognostic biomarker in KIRC, promoting an immunosuppressive TME and representing a potential therapeutic target.
title: POU2F2 as a dual oncogenic and immunomodulatory driver in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma.

text: Pathological lymphovenous communications are poorly characterized in veterinary medicine, and their computed tomographic features and clinical significance remain unknown. This retrospective case series aimed to describe contrast-enhanced computed tomography findings of suspected spontaneous lymphovenous communications in three cats. All cats had dilated, tortuous vessels arising from portal venous tributaries and extending to the cisterna chyli, originating from the splenic vein in two cats and the cranial mesenteric vein in one. The cisterna chyli and thoracic duct were consistently dilated and contrast-enhancing, and reduced portal vein calibre cranial to the communications was present in all cats. Concurrent findings included pleural or peritoneal effusion and subcutaneous edema, with chylous pleural effusion confirmed in two cats.
title: Computed Tomography Findings in Three Cases of Suspected Lymphovenous Communications in Cats.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: The recurrent anatomical distribution and associated portal and lymphatic abnormalities suggest that these communications may represent the enlargement and functional recruitment of pre-existing lymphovenous pathways in response to acquired portal and/or lymphatic hemodynamic disturbances, although a congenital origin cannot be excluded. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography may allow the recognition and anatomical characterization of suspected pathological lymphovenous communications in cats and should be considered when anomalous portal vessels are associated with concurrent cisterna chyli and thoracic duct abnormalities.
title: Computed Tomography Findings in Three Cases of Suspected Lymphovenous Communications in Cats.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Rotaviruses (RVs) are important pathogens which induce gastroenteritis in different kinds of animals, including mammals and birds. Rotaviruses are divided into nine species (RVA-RVD and RVF-RVJ), and RVA-RVC and RVH can infect both humans and pigs. It is vital to understand the genetic diversity and evolution of porcine rotavirus (PoRV) for effective prevention and control of this disease. In this study, 5320 intestinal tissue samples and fecal swabs were collected from different pig farms in Guangxi Province, southern China, from 2022 to 2025. These samples were tested for PoRV species A (PoRVA), PoRVB, PoRVC, and PoRVH using the multiplex RT-qPCR. The positive samples of PoRVA were further selected to amplify and analyze the VP4, VP6, and VP7 gene sequences. The phylogenetic trees were constructed based on the PoRVA VP4, VP6, and VP7 gene sequences.
title: Genetic Diversity and Evolution of Porcine Rotavirus Species A in Guangxi Province, Southern China, Between 2022 and 2025.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Bayesian time-dynamic analysis and recombination analysis were performed for the PoRVA VP4 gene. The results indicated that the PoRVA, PoRVB, PoRVC, and PoRVH positivity rates were 16.92% (900/5320), 0.51% (27/5320), 12.71% (676/5320), and 6.22% (331/5320), respectively. Fifty-two VP4, VP6, and VP7 gene sequences were obtained from the 52 selected PoRVA-positive clinical samples. The nucleotide and amino acid identity analysis of the obtained PoRVA VP4, VP6, and VP7 genes indicated that the genetic diversity of the VP4 gene was higher than that of the VP6 and VP7 genes. The phylogenetic trees based on the VP4, VP6, and VP7 genes revealed that the predominant strains of PoRVA in Guangxi Province were the G9P[13]I5 genotype.
title: Genetic Diversity and Evolution of Porcine Rotavirus Species A in Guangxi Province, Southern China, Between 2022 and 2025.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Bayesian analysis indicated that the population size of PoRVA kept steady with no significant expansion from its discovery in the 1970s to approximately 2016, then exhibited gradual growth. Sequence analysis of the PoRVA VP4 gene revealed substitutions and recombination in the PoRVA strains, and one strain was derived from recombination of a porcine-originating strain and a human-originating strain. This study provided useful information on the molecular characteristics and genetic diversity of PoRVA and supplied important clues for in-depth research on the cross-species transmission of PoRVA.
title: Genetic Diversity and Evolution of Porcine Rotavirus Species A in Guangxi Province, Southern China, Between 2022 and 2025.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Background : Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a highly metastatic epithelial malignancy with limited therapeutic options for advanced disease. Timosaponin AIII (TSAIII), a natural steroidal saponin, exhibits antitumor activity; however, its effects on NPC progression and the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Method : Cell viability, proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and invasion were evaluated using cell growth, colony formation, Annexin V/PI, and Transwell assays. Human chemokine array and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) analyses identified midkine (MDK) as a potential molecular target of TSAIII and its clinical relevance in NPC. Western blotting, qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, and chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assays were used to investigate the underlying signaling mechanisms. Antimetastatic activity was further evaluated in C.B17-SCID mice.
title: Disruption of p-AKT/ERβ-Mediated Midkine Signaling Promotes the Antimetastatic Effects of Timosaponin AIII in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Cells.

text: Results : TSAIII suppressed NPC cell migration and invasion with minimal cytotoxicity, accompanied by reduced the expression of p-AKT (Ser473), estrogen receptor β(ERβ) nuclear localization, and MDK expression. Wortmannin enhanced these effects, while TSAIII attenuated latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1)-induced signaling. In vivo, TSAIII significantly reduced lung metastasis without apparent toxicity. Conclusions : TSAIII suppresses NPC metastasis by targeting the LMP1/p-AKT/ERβ/MDK signaling axis, supporting its potential as an antimetastatic therapeutic candidate for NPC.
title: Disruption of p-AKT/ERβ-Mediated Midkine Signaling Promotes the Antimetastatic Effects of Timosaponin AIII in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Cells.

text: Vision is considered the most important of the five primary senses in birds, particularly in raptors, and the relatively large size of the avian eye reflects its importance. This study provides a morphological and histomorphometric characterisation of the eye and retina of the Common Kestrel ( Falco tinnunculus ), a diurnal raptor with bifoveate retinal organisation. Two adult Common Kestrels, obtained through a wildlife rehabilitation programme, were examined. Eye morphology was characterised using the ratio between corneal diameter and transverse eye diameter, while retinal morphology and layer thickness were evaluated using conventional histological procedures, and opsin expression was examined in both foveae. The eyes showed a globose morphology with a strongly protruding cornea and anterior segment, within the range reported for diurnal birds of prey.
title: Eye Morphology, Foveal Structure and Photoreceptor Composition in Both Foveae of Common Kestrel (<i>Falco tinnunculus</i> Linnaeus, 1758).

text: Marked regional variation in retinal morphology was observed, with the central retina displaying the greatest overall thickness (254.4 ± 27.04 µm), compared with 108.6 ± 15.58 µm in the peripheral retina. Two distinct foveae were identified: a deep convexiclivate fovea within the area centralis and a temporal fovea with a deep pit and steep walls. Both foveae showed displacement of the inner retinal layers and reduced thickness at the foveal pit. The central and temporal foveae exhibited depths of 217.66 µm and 106.38 µm, respectively. S- and L/M-opsin immunoreactivity was detected in both foveae, and the absence of rhodopsin immunoreactivity in the central foveal pit suggests that high-acuity vision in both foveae is predominantly mediated by cones.
title: Eye Morphology, Foveal Structure and Photoreceptor Composition in Both Foveae of Common Kestrel (<i>Falco tinnunculus</i> Linnaeus, 1758).

text: Background Cobalamin dysvitaminosis occurs with congenital portosystemic shunt (cPSS). Limited data exist on the effects of cPSS-type, cPSS-closure, and association with hyperammonemia. Hypothesis/objectives Cobalamin and folate status differ between healthy and cPSS-dogs, before and after cPSS-closure, between complete and incomplete cPSS-closure, and cPSS-types. Cobalamin dysvitaminosis is associated with hyperammonemia, which ameliorates after cPSS-closure. Animals Eighty-three dogs. Methods Concentrations of cobalamin, transcobalamin (TCB), metabolites (homocysteine [HCy], serum [sMMA], urinary [uMMA:crea] methylmalonic acid), folate, and blood ammonia were prospectively compared between 44 cPSS-dogs and 39 age and body weight matched controls.
title: Abnormalities in cobalamin status in dogs with congenital portosystemic shunt before and after shunt closure.

text: Compared were 32 out of 44 intrahepatic (cIPSS) and 12 out of 44 extrahepatic (cEPSS) cPSS-dogs, before (PSS-0) and 12 weeks (PSS-12) after cPSS-closure, and complete versus incomplete cPSS-closure. Results Hypocobalaminemia occurred in 2 out of 44 PSS-0-dogs (cIPSS) and hypercobalaminemia in 8 out of 44 PSS-0-dogs (5/12 cEPSS, 3/32 cIPSS). Of 34 normocobalaminemic PSS-0-dogs, in 47% available HCy samples concentrations were below the reference interval, whereas sMMA and uMMA:crea were higher in 61% and 27%. PSS-0-dogs had lower HCy, higher sMMA and uMMA:crea, and lower folate concentrations than controls (each P Conclusions and clinical importance Dysvitaminosis is common in cPSS-dogs persisting in some cPSS-dogs after cPSS-closure. Abstract (german)
title: Abnormalities in cobalamin status in dogs with congenital portosystemic shunt before and after shunt closure.

text: A 2-year-old male entire Cocker Spaniel was referred for investigation of progressive right hindlimb lameness and polyuria and polydipsia. Investigations conducted by the primary care veterinary surgeon revealed erythrocytosis (haematocrit of 78%, reference interval: 37%-55%) and urine concentration consistent with polyuria and polydipsia (specific gravity 1.014). Upon referral, physical examination revealed a dark red oral mucosa and right hindlimb lameness, characterised by intermittent non-weight bearing of the limb when standing. Neurological examination only revealed a mild short-strided gait, and orthopaedic examination was unremarkable. Secondary causes of erythrocytosis were excluded by normal arterial blood gas, low erythropoietin levels and normal thoracic and abdominal imaging, resulting in a diagnosis of primary erythrocytosis (PE).
title: Primary Erythrocytosis (Polycythaemia) in a Neutered Male Dog Presenting With Right Hindlimb Lameness.

text: Focal ultrasonography identified a right external iliac venous thrombus, suspected to be the cause of the right hindlimb lameness and presumed to be associated with the PE. Initial management involved repeated phlebotomies, followed by long-term treatment with hydroxyurea (31 mg/kg twice weekly) and rivaroxaban (2 mg/kg once daily). At the 5-month recheck, the dog was asymptomatic, with resolution of the iliac thrombus and a normal haematocrit. This case highlights an unusual presentation of PE in a dog, not previously described in the veterinary literature, and re-examines the discussion on the optimal management of this rare condition, with a focus on the necessity of antithrombotic therapy.
title: Primary Erythrocytosis (Polycythaemia) in a Neutered Male Dog Presenting With Right Hindlimb Lameness.

text: Island endemic terrestrial vertebrates, shaped by long-term isolation and ecological specialization, are particularly vulnerable to extinction pressure in the Anthropocene. However, cross-taxon extinction patterns and their drivers remain poorly understood. Here, we compiled a global dataset of 31,865 terrestrial vertebrates, including more than 7500 island endemic species, to evaluate the patterns and drivers of extinction risk in island endemics, in comparison with continent endemics and dual-range species. We found that island endemics face significantly higher extinction risk than non-island endemics, with 3.1% extinct and 34% currently threatened since 1500 CE. Extinction risk among island endemics is unevenly distributed and taxonomically structured, tightly linked to invasive species, overexploitation, and climate change.
title: Global patterns and drivers of extinction risk in island endemic terrestrial vertebrates.

text: Compared with continent endemics and dual-range species, their elevated risk is closely associated with small range size and habitat specialization, while biological traits, climate, and anthropogenic pressures also exert taxon-specific effects. These findings explain the unique vulnerability of island endemic vertebrates and inform conservation priorities across island ecosystems.
title: Global patterns and drivers of extinction risk in island endemic terrestrial vertebrates.

text: Solid lesions of the mandibular-sublingual salivary gland complex are rare in dogs. We report the case of an 11-year-old, 5 kg, intact female Maltese dog that presented with a non-painful, 2-3 cm left cervical swelling, soft at the surface and firm in depth. Fine-needle aspiration yielded clear, sero-mucous fluid. Radiographs revealed a well-defined, ovoid radiopaque structure measuring 3.1 × 2.9 cm in the cranial cervical region. Mandibular and monostomatic sublingual sialoadenectomy via a ventral approach revealed a large, heart-shaped, solid conglomerate within the glandular complex. Histopathological examination confirmed glandular atrophy, fibrosis and sialoadenitis. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectrometry of the submitted fragments indicated a substantial organic, protein- and lipid-rich component, with additional bands suggesting a possible minor mineral component.
title: A Salivary Conglomerate with a Substantial Organic Component Mimicking a Mineral Sialolith in the Mandibular-Sublingual Gland Complex of a Dog.

text: The dog healed completely, with no recurrence detected at the 2-week examination. Limitations include the absence of cross-sectional imaging and elemental analysis and the limited clinical follow-up. This case shows that protein-rich solid conglomerates should be included in the differential diagnosis of cervical swellings in dogs, that radiopacity alone does not establish mineral composition, and that complete surgical excision was associated with a favourable short-term outcome.
title: A Salivary Conglomerate with a Substantial Organic Component Mimicking a Mineral Sialolith in the Mandibular-Sublingual Gland Complex of a Dog.

text: Viruses within the Bandavirus genus ( Phenuiviridae family), phylogenetically divided into SFTSV and Bhanja groups, pose public health risks through cross-species transmission. Despite their significance, a systematic comparison of their infectivity, pathogenicity, and antigenicity is lacking. This study evaluates these key properties for five representative species: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), Guertu virus (GTV), and Heartland virus (HRTV) from the SFTSV group; and Bhanja virus (BHAV) and Lone Star virus (LSV) from the Bhanja group. The five bandaviruses demonstrated efficient replication kinetics across a panel of human and mammalian cell lines, suggesting a broad cellular tropism. Wild-type C57BL/6 mice developed transient viremia (2-10 dpi) without overt disease, followed by neutralizing antibody production.
title: Divergent virulence and serological profiles reveal pathogenic evolution within the <i>Bandavirus</i> genus.

text: Cross-neutralization was robust within each phylogenetic group but restricted between groups, supporting two separate serogroups. In contrast, IFNAR -/- C57BL/6 mice exhibited significant hematological abnormalities and uniformly lethal infection, with the 50% lethal dose-based virulence ranking as SFTSV > LSV > GTV >BHAV >HRTV. Pathological analysis revealed that SFTSV caused severe multi-organ damage, with predominant spleen tropism; GTV and HRTV induced similar but milder spleen-tropic lesions; and LSV and BHAV caused multi-organ injuries primarily affecting the liver and spleen. Our findings demonstrate that the variation in virulence among Bandavirus species is closely linked to their antigenic divergence and evolutionary lineages. The established infection models provide valuable platforms for investigating virus-host interactions and pathogenesis.
title: Divergent virulence and serological profiles reveal pathogenic evolution within the <i>Bandavirus</i> genus.

text: These insights facilitate the development of vaccines and antiviral therapies, and improve public health preparedness against emerging tick-borne pathogens.
title: Divergent virulence and serological profiles reveal pathogenic evolution within the <i>Bandavirus</i> genus.

text: Background No simple, blood-based biomarker to estimate tumor size in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism (PDH) has been evaluated. Hypothesis/objectives Determine whether the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)/cortisol ratio differentiates pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with PDH and correlates with pituitary size. Animals Seventy privately-owned dogs with PDH (microadenomas, n = 30; macroadenomas, n = 40). Methods Retrospective multicenter observational study. Endogenous ACTH and cortisol concentrations obtained at the same time point before treatment were used to calculate the ACTH/cortisol ratio. Pituitary tumor size was classified using the pituitary-to-brain (P/B) ratio. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and multivariable logistic regression.
title: Utility of the ACTH/cortisol ratio for differentiating pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism.

text: Results Dogs with macroadenomas had significantly higher ACTH/cortisol ratios than dogs with microadenomas (median, 9.12; IQR, 6.46-14.28 vs median, 4.90; IQR, 3.08-8.10; P 5.69 yielded 85% sensitivity and 60% specificity (positive likelihood ratio 2.13), whereas a higher ratio >11.74 achieved 90% specificity and 35% sensitivity (positive likelihood ratio 3.50). The ACTH/cortisol ratio showed moderate positive correlation with pituitary size (Spearman's ρ = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.26-0.64; P Conclusions and clinical importance The ACTH/cortisol ratio is associated with pituitary tumor size in dogs with PDH and may support clinical risk stratification, particularly when advanced imaging is unavailable.
title: Utility of the ACTH/cortisol ratio for differentiating pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism.

text: The intestinal epithelium forms a tight barrier against the harsh luminal environment. Absorptive enterocytes have a polygonal, columnar morphology, while mucus-producing goblet cells exhibit a rounded apical shape and a voluminous cell body, raising the question of how epithelial integrity is preserved in tissues with such morphological heterogeneity. Here, we show that, under homeostatic conditions in vivo, goblet cells mechanically induce tight-junction fractures between neighboring enterocytes. This effect is exacerbated by goblet cell hypertrophy and is associated with increased gut permeability.
title: Goblet cells mechanically breach the epithelial barrier in gut homeostasis.

text: Using in vivo and organoid models, combined with pharmacological, genetic and mechanical perturbations and theoretical modeling, we demonstrate that these fractures arise from a force imbalance at cell interfaces: goblet cells exert pressure on adjacent enterocytes, whose junctional rupture depends on tissue rheology controlled by myosin II. Our findings uncover a mechanical role for goblet cells in epithelial cohesion and barrier regulation, revealing how cellular heterogeneity shapes tissue integrity.
title: Goblet cells mechanically breach the epithelial barrier in gut homeostasis.

text: African swine fever virus (ASFV) causes an incurable swine disease with nearly 100% mortality, posing a catastrophic threat to global pig production. The soft tick Ornithodoros lahorensis acts as a critical biological vector that sustains persistent ASFV replication and mediates long-distance viral transmission, yet the molecular mechanisms governing ASFV-tick interplay remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomics and metabolomics to systematically dissect molecular changes in O. lahorensis across three infection stages: Uninfected control, early infection (7 days post-infection, dpi), and late persistent infection (21 dpi). Multi-omics integration revealed that ASFV extensively remodels tick host metabolism, predominantly activating purine/pyrimidine metabolism, lipid biosynthesis, and energy metabolism.
title: Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Profiling Identifies a Core Gene-Metabolite Axis Driving African Swine Fever Virus Replication in the Soft Tick Ornithodoros lahorensis.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

text: We further characterized a conserved regulatory module consisting of 12 core genes and 8 signature metabolites that collectively support ASFV genome replication and virion assembly. Three hub metabolic genes (TK1, ATP5F1B, and IMPDH) were selected for functional validation via siRNA silencing in ticks; individual gene silencing suppressed ASFV loads by 89.2%, 91.5%, and 87.8%, respectively (p < 0.001***). This work represents the first comprehensive multi-omics investigation of ASFV infection in O. lahorensis. We identified tick-specific molecular targets to block vector-mediated ASFV spread and established a standardized multi-omics analytical pipeline for tick-virus interaction research. Our findings elucidate the mechanistic basis of long-term ASFV persistence in soft ticks and deliver novel actionable clues for developing vector-targeted ASF intervention strategies.
title: Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Profiling Identifies a Core Gene-Metabolite Axis Driving African Swine Fever Virus Replication in the Soft Tick Ornithodoros lahorensis.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

text: Autophagy-related protein 13 (ATG13) is a critical component of the autophagy initiation complex and plays a pivotal role in regulating the initiation of autophagy. However, the precise mechanism by which ATG13 modulates influenza A virus (IAV) replication remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that ATG13 specifically interacts with the viral polymerase basic protein 1 (PB1) of H9N2-IAV and facilitates the autophagic degradation of PB1. Mechanistically, ATG13 targeted the C-terminal domain of PB1 and recruited microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) to promote the autophagolysosomal degradation of PB1. This process counteracts the PB1-mediated degradation of mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS), thereby attenuating the immune evasion capacity of H9N2-IAV and ultimately suppressing viral replication.
title: ATG13 recruits LC3 to target H9N2-IAV PB1 for autophagic-lysosomal degradation and restricts viral replication.

text: Collectively, our findings unveil for the first time a molecular mechanism whereby ATG13 negatively regulates IAV replication by mediating the targeted degradation of PB1 via the autophagolysosomal pathway. This study reveals a novel role of the autophagy pathway in host antiviral defense and provides a potential therapeutic target for anti-influenza agents.
title: ATG13 recruits LC3 to target H9N2-IAV PB1 for autophagic-lysosomal degradation and restricts viral replication.

text: Purpose Cystic echinococcosis (CE) is a cosmopolitan parasitic zoonosis with public health and economic significance. In this study, we report CE in uncommon host, a chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) in the Kuwait Zoo with description of clinical and pathological findings. Methods In September 2025, a 32-year-old adult female common chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) died at the zoo of Kuwait after showing severe symptoms. Post-mortem examination revealed a handball-sized cyst embedded in the hepatic umbilical fissure, causing lesions. The content of the cyst was examined microscopically as well as by sequencing of the mitochondrial nad1 gene from one of the clonal protoscoleces found in the cyst. Results The cyst proved to be Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto, genotype G1. The clinical case of the infection is described in detail.
title: First molecular characterization of Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto genotype G1 from a common chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) in the Kuwait Zoo.

text: DNA sequence was nearly identical to sequences of G1 genotype of E. granulosus available in GenBank. Conclusions This report of CE in a chimpanzee in the zoo highlights the problem related to environmental contamination. The implication of dogs in environmental contamination and other aspects of CE epidemiology in Kuwait is discussed. This is the first report of genetically identified hydatid cyst of E. granulosus sensu stricto in Kuwait and the first genetically confirmed case of the genotype G1 in chimpanzee.
title: First molecular characterization of Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto genotype G1 from a common chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) in the Kuwait Zoo.

text: The high incidence and poor prognosis of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) underscore the urgent need to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying its progression and chemoresistance. Here, we investigated the role of DDRGK domain-containing protein 1 (DDRGK1) in NSCLC and identified a novel regulatory axis governing its protein stability. Clinically, DDRGK1 was markedly upregulated in NSCLC tissues, and elevated DDRGK1 expression correlated with advanced tumor stage, poor overall survival, and chemoresistance. Functionally, DDRGK1 knockout significantly suppressed NSCLC cell growth, an effect reversed by DDRGK1 re-expression. Mechanistically, tripartite motif-containing protein 26 (TRIM26) was identified as the E3 ubiquitin ligase that catalyzed K48-linked polyubiquitination of DDRGK1 at K267, promoting its degradation.
title: TRIM26-Mediated Ubiquitination and Degradation of DDRGK1 Suppress NSCLC Progression by Inhibiting DNA Repair and Promoting Apoptosis.

text: This modification antagonized E3 UFM1-protein ligase 1 (UFL1)-mediated UFMylation at the same residue, thereby fine-tuning DDRGK1 stability. Functional enrichment analysis showed that DDRGK1-interacting proteins and proteins differentially expressed in DDRGK1 -knockout cells were predominantly associated with the DNA damage response and apoptosis. Consistently, DDRGK1 knockout suppressed ATR phosphorylation and augmented cisplatin-induced apoptosis in NSCLC cells. Collectively, these findings define the regulatory mechanism of DDRGK1, establish it as a key regulator of NSCLC progression, and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for overcoming chemoresistance.
title: TRIM26-Mediated Ubiquitination and Degradation of DDRGK1 Suppress NSCLC Progression by Inhibiting DNA Repair and Promoting Apoptosis.

text: Introduction This prospective study aimed to investigate the use of ultrasonography for verifying central venous catheter placement in hospitalized cats and dogs, in comparison with radiographic assessment. Methods The investigation was conducted on client-owned animals. The position of the central venous catheter was checked using both thoracic radiography and ultrasonography. Ultrasonographic examination was performed in three steps: two intercostal scans of the cranial thorax (transverse and longitudinal scans), to visualize the course of the cranial vena cava within the mediastinum, and one right parasternal scan (sub-costal bicaval view), to visualize both the cranial and caudal vena cava entering the right atrium. Results A total of 15 animals (8 dogs and 7 cats) were included in this study.
title: Point-of-care ultrasonography for verification of central venous catheter placement in cats and dogs.

text: Radiographic evaluation confirmed correct device placement within the cranial vena cava in 15/15 animals, with catheter extension into the right atrium observed in 8/15 cases. Ultrasonographic assessment of the mediastinal region demonstrated good agreement with radiographic findings (94%; CI95%: 83%-100%), and the bicaval atrial view showed high reliability in identifying central venous catheter tip location (Kappa = 0.87; CI95%: 65%-100%). Discussion Ultrasound appears to be a reliable, non-invasive method for evaluating central venous catheter position in dogs and cats, with diagnostic accuracy comparable to radiography and the advantage of avoiding ionizing radiation exposure.
title: Point-of-care ultrasonography for verification of central venous catheter placement in cats and dogs.

text: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a prevalent condition in cats and recognized as a leading cause of mortality among cats generally, yet it is difficult to detect by cat caregivers, especially in its early stages. This retrospective study aimed to enhance detection of CKD by cat caregivers through a smart litter box monitor technology that tracks feline elimination behaviors. We established cohorts of cats with CKD and cats with no known conditions and analyzed behavioral features captured by the monitor. A mixed-effects model identified significant differences, which were then integrated into a machine learning framework for predictive modeling. The model achieved a weighted F1-score of 92.7% in training using cross-validation and 89.9% in validation, demonstrating high precision for CKD predictions.
title: Enhancing Detection of Feline Chronic Kidney Disease Through Smart Litter Box Monitoring.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Key findings included a behavioral profile unique to cats with CKD characterized by increased urination frequency, longer elimination durations, and reduced post-elimination covering behavior. These results suggest that the smart litter box monitor can provide valuable, continuous, and non-invasive data for CKD detection and management.
title: Enhancing Detection of Feline Chronic Kidney Disease Through Smart Litter Box Monitoring.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Computational modelling of the electrical fields generated by helical electrodes surrounding the vagus nerve suggested a current of 1.0 mA should depolarise enough axons to give a therapeutic effect in epilepsy. An assumption that fibrous tissue formation would form between the electrodes and the nerve in implantable vagus nerve stimulators (VNS) led to the recommendation that 1.5 mA should be used to account for the increased impedance this would cause. This increase in impedance has not been documented, meaning that the higher current might not be necessary and could produce avoidable adverse effects such as coughing.
title: Impedance changes in chronic vagus nerve stimulator implantation in epileptic dogs.

text: To test the hypotheses that impedance does not always increase following VNS implantation and that more adverse effects might be seen with lower impedance circuits, circuit impedance was measured in dogs with implantable VNS at implantation and compared to impedance at 3-6 months post-implantation and at non-standardised time points thereafter. Dogs were grouped by severity of their coughing and the impedance between groups at 3-6 months was compared. Mean impedance at first implantation (2219Ω, 95% CI 1894-2544) was no different from impedance at 3-6 months post implantation (2257Ω, 95%CI 1944-2570, p = .80). Only 2 of 17 dogs showed a > 50% increase in impedance (one at 3-6 and one at 7-12 months). Coughing severity was not influenced by impedance value despite similar stimulation currents.
title: Impedance changes in chronic vagus nerve stimulator implantation in epileptic dogs.

text: This work shows impedance does not consistently increase post implantation in dogs with VNS, suggesting that currents > 1.0 mA might not be routinely needed to achieve a therapeutic effect.
title: Impedance changes in chronic vagus nerve stimulator implantation in epileptic dogs.

text: The antemortem clinical and clinicopathological diagnosis of feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) remains challenging, particularly when effusions deviate from the classically protein-rich, low-to-moderate-cellularity phenotype. The FIP Effusion Index, defined as the ratio of delta total nucleated cells (ΔTNC) to the albumin-to-globulin (A/G) ratio, was developed and initially evaluated in 50 effusions. Subsequent European Advisory Board on Cat Diseases (ABCD) guidelines recommended evaluation in larger cohorts and in cats with confirmed FIP. This study retrospectively evaluated the prespecified threshold (≥7.54) in 176 independent feline effusion samples analysed on the Sysmex XN-1000V and classified by effusion FCoV RT-qPCR, without independent confirmation of FIP status.
title: Beyond Modified Transudates: Diagnostic Performance of the Feline Infectious Peritonitis Effusion Index on the Sysmex XN-1000V.

text: Relative to this molecular reference, the FIP Effusion Index yielded a sensitivity of 97.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 92.4-99.7%), a specificity of 88.1% (95% CI, 79.2-94.1%) and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.962 (95% CI, 0.928-0.995). Discrimination exceeded that of ΔTNC alone (AUC, 0.947; ΔAUC, 0.014; p = 0.012) and A/G alone (AUC, 0.887; ΔAUC, 0.074; p = 0.012). In exudates, sensitivity remained 100% (95% CI, 80.5-100%) and specificity was 82.8% (95% CI, 64.2-94.2%). Among reference-negative effusions, false-positive classification was more frequent in septic than in non-septic samples (6/19 vs. 4/65; odds ratio, 7.04; 95% CI, 1.74-28.53; p < 0.01).
title: Beyond Modified Transudates: Diagnostic Performance of the Feline Infectious Peritonitis Effusion Index on the Sysmex XN-1000V.

text: These findings demonstrate that the prespecified FIP Effusion Index threshold retained very high sensitivity and strong discrimination for molecular-reference positivity across a broader spectrum of feline effusions. Future studies should evaluate the FIP Effusion Index within a sequential in vivo diagnostic algorithm, using negative results to support rule-out and positive results to prompt confirmation by FCoV antigen detection using immunocytochemistry and/or immunohistochemistry.
title: Beyond Modified Transudates: Diagnostic Performance of the Feline Infectious Peritonitis Effusion Index on the Sysmex XN-1000V.

text: Background: Canine intestinal sensitivity is a multifactorial functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by recurrent soft feces, impaired nutrient utilization, and low-grade intestinal inflammation, and it acts as a major trigger for chronic gastrointestinal discomfort in dogs. Conventional antibiotic therapy causes side effects and drug resistance. Probiotics modulate host physiology, immunity, and metabolism, serving as promising alternatives for improving canine intestinal health. This study aimed to compare the gut microbiota of healthy and sensitive German shepherd dogs, screen and identify candidate probiotics, and verify their efficacy in ameliorating canine intestinal dysfunction and hypersensitivity.
title: <i>Pediococcus acidilactici</i> Long21 Alleviates Intestinal Sensitivity and Improves Gut Health in German Shepherd Dogs by Regulating Intestinal Metabolic Profiles.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Results: Fecal microbiota transplantation from healthy dogs effectively improved these fecal indicators and was associated with enhanced serum antioxidant and anti-inflammatory capacities in intestinal-sensitive dogs ( p Pediococcus acidilactici enriched in healthy dogs and Shigella increased in diarrheic dogs ( p P. acidilactici Long21 intervention, either alone or combined with its fermentation supernatant, significantly improved fecal traits; reduced pathogenic bacterial abundance; increased the apparent digestibility of dry matter, crude fibre, and ether extract; and was associated with normalized antioxidant function and inflammatory indicators in German Shepherd dogs with intestinal sensitivity ( p P.
title: <i>Pediococcus acidilactici</i> Long21 Alleviates Intestinal Sensitivity and Improves Gut Health in German Shepherd Dogs by Regulating Intestinal Metabolic Profiles.

text: acidilactici Long21 supplementation alleviated intestinal sensitivity-associated diarrhea and improved intestinal health, possibly through coordinated changes in gut microbiota, metabolic profiles, and nutrient utilization. These findings provide a theoretical basis and a candidate strain for microecological intervention, although causal mechanisms remain to be confirmed.
title: <i>Pediococcus acidilactici</i> Long21 Alleviates Intestinal Sensitivity and Improves Gut Health in German Shepherd Dogs by Regulating Intestinal Metabolic Profiles.

text: Conservation biological control is central to sustainable pest management; however, its effectiveness depends on providing natural enemies with adequate floral resources and habitat structure. In Florida citrus, living windbreaks offer potential for improvement through floral resource provisioning. We evaluated whether flower-enriched windbreaks increase predator abundance and group richness in citrus orchards in north and central Florida over two years and assessed the role of wildflowers in supporting predator communities. In central Florida, treatment groves supported higher predator abundance and group richness across both sampling methods (vacuum and sticky trap) and both study years, particularly spiders, ants, minute pirate bugs, long-legged flies, and wasps.
title: Do Flower-Rich Windbreak Margins Enhance Predator Communities in Citrus Orchards?

text: In north Florida, floral plantings did not significantly increase overall predator abundance or group richness, although some treatment effects emerged in the second year, suggesting delayed benefits related to plant establishment. Predator-plant interactions were region-specific: blanket flower attracted the highest proportion of predator visitors in both regions, accounting for 66% of visits by ants in central Florida and 62% of visits by syrphid flies in north Florida. Predator abundance was generally higher near windbreak edges in both regions. In central Florida, wasp abundance was significantly negatively associated with Asian citrus psyllid abundance, with each one-unit increase in wasp density associated with an approximately 2.7% decrease in expected psyllid abundance, whereas spider and ant associations were not statistically significant.
title: Do Flower-Rich Windbreak Margins Enhance Predator Communities in Citrus Orchards?

text: Floral enhancements can strengthen predator communities, but outcomes vary across regions and years and depend on regional conditions, plant establishment, predator functional traits, and ecological interactions. Therefore, conservation biological control in citrus requires region-specific plant selection and consideration of ecological context beyond abundance alone.
title: Do Flower-Rich Windbreak Margins Enhance Predator Communities in Citrus Orchards?

text: Bacterial pneumonia treatment faces significant challenges due to uncontrolled inflammation and rising antibiotic resistance. Excessive inflammatory cytokine release and mitochondrial dysfunction exacerbate tissue damage, contributing to the disease's progression. Mitophagy, a process that eliminates dysfunctional mitochondria, helps regulate reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and suppress inflammation. However, efficient bacteria clearance remains critical for effective inflammatory modulation. Traditional antibiotics struggle against resistant bacteria, necessitating alternative approaches. ROS-based nanocatalytic therapies, particularly nanozymes, show potential for overcoming ROS generation limitations through external stimuli like ultrasound and magnetic fields.
title: Magneto-Sono-Enhanced Nanozyme Catalysis Drives ROS-Mediated Pathogen Killing and Mitophagy-Linked Inflammation Control in Bacterial Pneumonia.

text: This study designs a sono-magneto-responsive nanozyme (BN@NF) composed of boron nanosheets (BN) and neodymium-doped iron phosphide (Nd:Fe 2 P, NF), modified to form a Z-scheme heterostructure. Delivered via nebulization, BN@NF generates ROS under combined internal and external stimuli, enabling efficient bacterial killing and biofilm disruption. It also modulates inflammation by inhibiting the NF-κB pathway and promoting mitophagy, reducing pro-inflammatory cytokine release. Additionally, BN@NF enhances macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, aiding tissue repair. This approach provides a promising strategy for treating bacterial pneumonia by combining effective antibacterial action with intelligent anti-inflammatory functions.
title: Magneto-Sono-Enhanced Nanozyme Catalysis Drives ROS-Mediated Pathogen Killing and Mitophagy-Linked Inflammation Control in Bacterial Pneumonia.

text: This study describes postmortem histological changes in skin appendages of domestic dogs in the first seven days after death. The objective was to document the progression of autolytic change in the sweat glands, sebaceous glands, and hair follicles and to compare it between body regions and sides. Skin samples were collected bilaterally from the neck, thorax, abdomen, and thigh of nine dog carcasses (female, non-pedigree, short-haired, 5-10 years old, ~10 kg). The carcasses were kept at 10-12 °C in Karditsa, Greece, and sampled at 0, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, and 168 h postmortem. Sections were stained with Hematoxylin and Eosin and Alcian Blue-PAS. The rate of change varied by structure, body region, and side. In this cohort, autolysis appeared earliest in the abdomen and on the dependent (left) side.
title: Postmortem Changes in Skin Appendages of Domestic Dogs: A Preliminary Comparative Histological Study Between Body Regions, and Possible Forensic Implications.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: The sweat glands and hair follicles reached the most advanced stage recorded by 48 h, whereas the sebaceous glands remained unchanged for 24 h, except in the dependent abdomen. The three structures changed over different periods, giving complementary timelines. These findings provide the first structured reference data on postmortem change in dog skin appendages, a baseline for early postmortem interval estimation and for recognizing antemortem lesions.
title: Postmortem Changes in Skin Appendages of Domestic Dogs: A Preliminary Comparative Histological Study Between Body Regions, and Possible Forensic Implications.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Streptomyces formicae KY5 is a biosynthetically talented strain isolated from the nest of fungus-farming Tetraponera plant ants. S. formicae KY5 is predicted to encode at least 45 biosynthetic gene clusters (BGC), many of which look novel. However, we do not know the products of most of these pathways. One of the BGCs encoded by S. formicae KY5 produces the polyketide antibiotics, the formicamycins. Here we show that in a mutant lacking the formicamycin BGC, a previously cryptic non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) pathway is induced that produces the cyclic depsipeptide, LL-A0341 B (LL-B) and the related metabolite, LL-A0341 A (LL-A). Using genetics and comparative metabolomics, we have characterised the genes present in the LL BGC and re-wired the pathway to generate high-level producing strains. This has allowed for detailed structural characterisation and bioactivity testing.
title: Activation of LL-A0341B biosynthesis: a cryptic cardiolipin targeting metabolite from <i>Streptomyces formicae</i> KY5.

text: We present the first X-ray crystal structure of LL-B which confirms the recently proposed absolute configuration of this natural product, and show it is a potent inhibitor of Gram-positive microorganisms by targeting the membrane phospholipid, cardiolipin. This work shows the importance of continuing to mine the genomes of talented Streptomyces strains, particularly those that are isolated from under-explored environments, as they are a rich source of both new metabolites and new biology.
title: Activation of LL-A0341B biosynthesis: a cryptic cardiolipin targeting metabolite from <i>Streptomyces formicae</i> KY5.

text: Background Globally, the number of people aged 65 years and older is expected to double by 2050. With increasing age, the risk of frailty and the need for palliative care also rise. A shared understanding of how to assess frailty and determine the need for palliative care could support interprofessional collaboration in clinical practice. The transition from a frail condition to palliative care is a dynamic and individualized process. Although frailty and palliative care are distinct concepts, they may overlap. The present study aimed to examine the components of frailty and palliative care in community-dwelling older people. Early recognition by healthcare professionals of the components that contribute to severe frailty can enable the timely initiation of palliative care.
title: Components and classification of frailty and palliative care.

text: Our second aim was to gain insight into whether an individual should be classified as frail or in need of palliative care according to healthcare professionals. Methods We presented fifteen case studies to respondents who were selected based on their specific expertise in the Netherlands and Belgium. Each respondent was asked to identify, for each case study, the components that indicated frailty, palliative care needs, or both. Additionally, they were asked to rate their level of certainty regarding each indication. Wilcoxon tests were employed to assess differences, and regression analyses were conducted to identify the components most strongly associated with frailty and in need of palliative care.
title: Components and classification of frailty and palliative care.

text: Results In most cases, differences were observed between the identification of frailty and palliative care needs, with par-ticipants indicating that a patient could exhibit components of frailty without necessarily having palliative care needs (p-value Conclusions Our study showed that healthcare professionals use different components to classify individuals as frail or in need of palliative care. In addition, these professionals were more certain in identifying frailty than in identifying palliative care needs, and may be less likely to recognize palliative care needs in their patients, who may already be quite frail. Improved understanding of the progression from frailty to the need for palliative care may support patient-centered care and increase enhance the quality of life for individuals requiring support.
title: Components and classification of frailty and palliative care.

text: Background Equine colic emergencies present highly stressful, time-critical scenarios for both clinicians and patients, thus rapid and accurate diagnostic triage is paramount. To support veterinarians under these high-pressure conditions, deep learning tools can be leveraged for automated image recognition to assist in localizing abdominal organs and interpreting FLASH (Fast Localized Abdominal Sonography of Horses) ultrasound windows. Objectives A software tool was developed to identify FLASH-specific ultrasound windows on the equine abdomen and to recognize ultrasonographic organ patterns. Study design Retrospective-prospective comparison of software and clinical examination, model development. Methods A deep learning approach for image classification was used to train software to assign ultrasound images to FLASH windows.
title: Deep learning-based differentiation of FLASH ultrasound windows.

text: Results Strongest software performance was observed for the duodenal window, with all test images correctly classified, corresponding to a recall of 1.00. Nephrosplenic window demonstrated high classification accuracy, but 23% of images were misclassified as gastric window. While 84% of ventral images were correctly classified, 16% were predicted as duodenal window. Most pronounced confusion was observed between ventral and thoracic windows, with only 55% of thoracic images correctly identified. Left and right middle third FLASH windows 4 and 6 were substantially underrepresented and were therefore excluded from further analyses. In addition, these windows exhibited high anatomical similarity, which further complicated their differentiation.
title: Deep learning-based differentiation of FLASH ultrasound windows.

text: Main limitations Sources of selection bias was interpretation of windows and the definition of normal physiological ultrasound images by the examiners. The specific FLASH windows were not homogeneously dispersed in the dataset (e.g., FLASH windows 4 and 6 were underrepresented). Conclusions The developed deep learning tool demonstrates the feasibility of automated recognition of standardized equine FLASH windows and may support ultrasound training as an educational aid for first-day competencies. Future incorporation of organ-level annotations and probe position information may improve discrimination between anatomically similar windows and enhance model performance.
title: Deep learning-based differentiation of FLASH ultrasound windows.

text: The unprecedented expansion of human activity boundaries is turning spillover from a chance event into a foreseeable ecological and epidemiological certainty. Using the 2026 Andes hantavirus cruise ship outbreak as an entry point, this study examines it within a broader driver framework: nearly all emerging infectious disease events in humans in recent decades have originated from wildlife transmission; under climate-change and land-use scenarios, approximately 3139 mammal species are projected to aggregate in new combinations by 2070, causing an estimated 4000 cross-species viral transmission events.
title: Rising spillover risk: Lessons from the Andes hantavirus outbreak.

text: The rapid expansion of tourism into ecologically fragile regions - sub-Antarctic waters, the deep sea, and primary forests - the persistence of habitat fragmentation and animal trade, and the reshaping of wildlife distribution and vector dynamics by extreme climate events together constitute "novel contact amplifiers" that accelerate contact at the human-animal-environment interface. Robotics, artificial intelligence, autonomous driving, and automated logistics are extending human activities into previously inaccessible regions, yet they remain almost entirely absent from current spillover risk assessments. The limitations of cruise ship medical systems - whose core capacity lies in "recognize, isolate, stabilize, and transfer" rather than definitive diagnosis and treatment - were fully exposed in this event.
title: Rising spillover risk: Lessons from the Andes hantavirus outbreak.

text: From a One Health perspective, this paper proposes that responses to spillover risk must shift from passive reaction to proactive interface governance, incorporate technology-driven increases in contact frequency into prevention and control frameworks, and advance cornerstone strategies such as broad-spectrum vaccines and broad-spectrum antiviral drugs at the basic research level.
title: Rising spillover risk: Lessons from the Andes hantavirus outbreak.

text: Background Intrapelvic urethral strictures in male cats are challenging to manage. Standard perineal urethrostomy cannot address lesions within the pelvic canal, and alternative open surgical techniques carry high morbidity. Case description A 5-year-old intact male domestic shorthair cat with concurrent hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and polycystic kidney disease presented with a 7-day history of stranguria. Diagnostic imaging revealed a focal 1-mm stricture in the post-prostatic urethra. Procedure Under fluoroscopic guidance, retrograde internal urethrotomy was performed using a 1.3 × 130 mm urethral microlancet via a dorsal approach. A self-expanding laser-cut nitinol stent (5.0 mm × 50 mm) was deployed across the stricture. A double-lumen balloon catheter was placed through the stent for 14 days to promote mucosal integration and prevent migration.
title: Microlancet-assisted internal urethrotomy with stent placement for feline pelvic urethral stricture: a case report.

text: Results The procedure was completed in 30 min with no complications. Urethral patency was immediately restored. Follow-up cystoscopy at 7 and 14 days demonstrated progressive epithelial ingrowth and near-complete encapsulation of the stent without restenosis. The cat regained normal urination. Conclusion This report describes the first successful use of microlancet internal urethrotomy combined with nitinol stenting for an intrapelvic urethral stricture in a cat. The technique offers a promising minimally invasive alternative to conventional urethrostomy in high-risk cases.
title: Microlancet-assisted internal urethrotomy with stent placement for feline pelvic urethral stricture: a case report.

text: Green mold ( Penicillium spp.) is a major postharvest disease of grapefruit. Optimal concentrations of bamboo vinegar (BV) and Cryptococcus laurentii were screened in vitro, and their individual and combined efficacy evaluated. BV (1%, 121 °C-sterilized) plus 1 × 10 7 CFU mL -1 C. laurentii (BV- C. laurentii ) significantly inhibited spore germination and germ tube elongation in Penicillium spp., disrupted P. digitatum hyphal cell wall and membrane integrity, and increased extracellular chitinase and β-1,3-glucanase activities by 1.05- and 1.22-fold over C. laurentii alone at 48 h while reducing malondialdehyde and reduced glutathione. BV- C.
title: Enhancing grapefruit resistance to green mold through synergistic effects of bamboo vinegar and <i>Cryptococcus laurentii</i>.

text: laurentii also activated fruit innate defense, with phenylalanine ammonia-lyase and polyphenol oxidase activities 1.03-1.44-fold higher than CK and total phenol and flavonoid contents 20.22% and 19.73% higher on day 28, without adversely affecting total soluble solids, titratable acidity, ascorbic acid or reducing sugar. Thus, BV- C. laurentii effectively controls green mold and delays quality deterioration in grapefruit.
title: Enhancing grapefruit resistance to green mold through synergistic effects of bamboo vinegar and <i>Cryptococcus laurentii</i>.

text: Follistatin-like 1 (FSTL1) has been considered a vital adipokine. Several lines of evidence have shown that FSTL1 is essential for white adipose tissue (WAT) adipogenesis, brown adipose tissue involution, and thermogenesis. However, the roles of FSTL1 in WAT browning and its underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. Our data show that FSTL1 overexpression induces WAT browning, enhances energy metabolism, and promotes glucose uptake in male mice at ambient room temperature. Overexpression of FSTL1 specifically in WAT prevents metabolic dysfunction in mice with diet-induced obesity. Mice with FSTL1 deficiency exhibit cold intolerance and are prone to obesity. FSTL1 cannot directly induce adipocyte browning in vitro. FSTL1 promotes sympathetic innervation both in vivo and in vitro.
title: The Adipose-Sympathetic Nerve Crosstalk: FSTL1 as an Adipocyte-Derived Neurotrophic Factor for WAT Browning.

text: Furthermore, sympathetic denervation in adipose tissue abrogates FSTL1-induced browning, enhancement of energy metabolism, and regional glucose uptake. Notably, FSTL1 is endocytosed by sympathetic neurons primarily via tropomyosin-related kinase B (TrkB) in vitro. Blocking TrkB suppresses WAT browning and sympathetic innervation induced by FSTL1 overexpression in adipose tissue. Our findings shed new light on the role of FSTL1 in WAT browning and identify FSTL1 as an adipose-derived 'neurotrophic factor' adipokine.
title: The Adipose-Sympathetic Nerve Crosstalk: FSTL1 as an Adipocyte-Derived Neurotrophic Factor for WAT Browning.

text: Head and neck cancer, particularly head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, remains difficult to treat because of local recurrence, treatment-related morbidity, and the limited efficacy of systemic drug delivery. Biomaterial-based delivery systems have emerged as useful tools to improve local drug retention, control release kinetics, and support combination treatment. Hydrogels, nanoparticles, liposomes, microneedles, and implantable systems have been explored for the delivery of chemotherapeutic agents, radiosensitizers, immunotherapeutics, and nucleic acids in head and neck cancer. This review summarizes recent progress in biomaterial-based drug delivery strategies, with a focus on local delivery and combination therapy.
title: Biomaterial-based Drug delivery strategies for head and neck cancer: Local delivery, combination therapy, and translational challenges.

text: We discuss the major biomaterial platforms, their therapeutic applications, and the practical challenges that affect clinical translation, including tumor heterogeneity, dosing reproducibility, biocompatibility, and manufacturability. Overall, biomaterials represent a promising but still developing approach for improving treatment delivery and multimodal therapy in head and neck cancer.
title: Biomaterial-based Drug delivery strategies for head and neck cancer: Local delivery, combination therapy, and translational challenges.

text: TP53 mutations (TP53mut) are associated with therapeutic resistance in glioblastoma (GBM) patients, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified an association between reduced P53 function and increased expression of the epigenetic regulator TET1 in GBM models. In TP53mut GBM cells, TET1 knockdown influenced genome fragility, including DNA damage, senescence, and telomere shortening. Specifically, our findings are consistent with a model in which TET1 binds to the ROS1 promoter and may help maintain ROS1 expression, likely by keeping the promoter in a hypomethylated state, along with downstream ERK phosphorylation. Conversely, inhibiting TET1 correlates with reduced ROS1 expression, attenuation of ERK signaling, and increased genome fragility.
title: TET1 Inhibition Promotes Therapeutic Sensitivity in TP53-Mutant GBM by Influencing Genome Fragility and Altering TAMs Biology.

text: Furthermore, TET1 depletion in tumor cells was associated with altered tumor-associated macrophages biology both in vitro and in vivo, including increased infiltration, differentiation, M1-like polarization, and phagocytic capacity. Notably, combining the TET1 inhibitor Bobcat339 with cisplatin synergistically inhibited TP53mut GBM growth in vitro and in vivo, improving survival without significant toxicity. Our findings suggest that TET1 may serve as a potential mediator of therapy resistance and a promising therapeutic target in TP53mut GBM.
title: TET1 Inhibition Promotes Therapeutic Sensitivity in TP53-Mutant GBM by Influencing Genome Fragility and Altering TAMs Biology.

text: mRNA vaccines have become a clinically validated vaccine platform, as demonstrated by the success of COVID-19 vaccines such as Comirnaty and Spikevax, owing to their rapid design, manufacturing scalability, and capacity to induce in situ antigen expression. A key factor underlying this success is the lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery system, which protects mRNA from degradation and promotes efficient cellular uptake and cytoplasmic delivery, thereby enabling the full potential of mRNA technology. The continued advancement of mRNA-LNP vaccines requires integrated optimization of mRNA design, LNP composition, and delivery strategies to achieve improved stability, efficient intracellular delivery, and balanced immune responses.
title: mRNA lipid nanoparticle vaccines: current status, challenges and future prospects.

text: Despite remarkable progress, challenges related to formulation stability, long-term storage stability, safety and reactogenicity concerns, and durability of immune protection continue to hinder the broader application of mRNA-LNP vaccine platforms. This review provides an integrated overview of recent advances in mRNA-LNP vaccines, covering mRNA molecular engineering, LNP composition and delivery mechanisms, immune responses, clinical progress, and current developmental challenges. Furthermore, emerging strategies, including thermostable formulations, next-generation LNPs with improved targeting capability, emerging RNA platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted optimization of RNA sequences and lipid materials, are discussed.
title: mRNA lipid nanoparticle vaccines: current status, challenges and future prospects.

text: By summarizing current achievements and future opportunities, this review highlights key principles guiding the rational design of safer, more stable, and more precise mRNA-LNP vaccine platforms and provides insights into accelerating their clinical translation.
title: mRNA lipid nanoparticle vaccines: current status, challenges and future prospects.

text: The one-pot synthesis of apolar-polar block copolymers combining polyolefins with polyesters has been a long-standing challenge in polymer chemistry. Despite broad-reaching applications of apolar-polar block copolymers in drug delivery, compatibilisation of polymer blends and biomedical materials, their synthesis often requires multi-step protocols with multiple catalysts and several isolation and purification steps. This is a particular challenge when combining the polymerisation of non-activated α-olefins with lactones, as these two distinct polymerisation mechanisms are often incompatible. This work reports heterobimetallic Janus catalysts for orthogonal 1-hexene and ε-caprolactone polymerisation. Generated in situ, the active catalysts combine distinct Ti and Al metal centres connected by a Ti-C(H)═C(R)CH 2 O-Al linker (R = Me or Bn).
title: Heterobimetallic Janus Catalysts for the One-Pot Synthesis of Polar-Apolar Block Copolymers.

text: This approach successfully delivered poly(1-hexene)-block-poly(ε-caprolactone) copolymers with well-controlled linear block copolymer architectures, targeted molar compositions and tuneable molar mass (M n values < 67.3 kDa, Ð = 1.47), in a one-pot reaction, an approach that was successfully extended to poly(1-octene)-block-poly(ε-caprolactone) and poly(1-decene)-block-poly(ε-caprolactone) copolymers. Overall, this work is a notable addition to the toolbox for synthesising apolar-polar block copolymers. This work demonstrates for the first time that titanium-alkenyl complexes can efficiently initiate olefin polymerisations and that heterobimetallic complexes can act as efficient bifunctional initiators for distinct polymerisation mechanisms.
title: Heterobimetallic Janus Catalysts for the One-Pot Synthesis of Polar-Apolar Block Copolymers.

text: Human T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain 1 (TIM-1) facilitates infection of re-emerging viruses, including alphaviruses, through its phosphatidylserine (PS) binding domain. Although alphaviruses are transmitted to humans via mosquito bite, it is unclear whether mosquito-derived viruses also use TIM-1 to infect human cells. Since viruses acquire their PS-containing envelope from the host cell and insect cell membranes differ in lipid composition from mammalian membranes, we here investigate the role of TIM-1 at the mosquito-mammalian interface. We show that TIM-1 promotes infection with mosquito cell-derived, replication-competent alphaviruses, including Chikungunya virus, O'nyong'nyong virus (ONNV), and Sindbis virus. The TIM-1 PS-binding domain is essential for enhancing mosquito cell-derived ONNV infection as shown by TIM-1 mutagenesis.
title: TIM-1 promotes infection with mosquito cell-derived alphaviruses through virion-associated phospholipids.

text: According to untargeted lipidomics, mosquito cell-derived ONNV virions contain higher levels of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) and PS compared to mammalian cell-derived ONNV. Notably, TIM-1 engages PE as well as PS, as demonstrated by liposome competition. PS decarboxylase experiments suggest that PS is an important mediator of mosquito-cell derived ONNV entry into mammalian cells. Taken together, our data show that TIM-1 promotes mosquito cell-derived alphavirus infection of mammalian cells. This work provides implications for the understanding of the TIM-1 ligand repertoire and advances our understanding of arbovirus transmission at the mosquito-mammalian interface.
title: TIM-1 promotes infection with mosquito cell-derived alphaviruses through virion-associated phospholipids.

text: This paper examines the sociomaterial dynamics of mental healthcare by following metaphors circulating among voluntary sector providers that they were becoming 'dumping grounds' within a system in crisis. In the United Kingdom, the voluntary sector has long been called upon to deliver flexible, community-based care that reduces pressure on primary and secondary services. Under chronic conditions of austerity, however, providers have been stretched beyond their capacity. Drawing on ethnographic research across three voluntary sector mental health sites in inner-city London, I analyse how providers made and maintained places of care while grappling with expanding and shifting demands.
title: 'No Dumping!' Threshold Work in Voluntary Sector Mental Healthcare in Inner-City London.

text: Taking a sociomaterial approach, I propose the analytic concept of 'threshold work' to complicate the dumping metaphor and to reconceptualise how material thresholds of place and immaterial thresholds of mental health need are co-constituted with care practices. I identify three interrelated modes of threshold work through which providers manage the limits of inclusion, revealing how diagnostic boundaries of need and spatial arrangements of care move together, shaping the terms and conditions of care in the city.
title: 'No Dumping!' Threshold Work in Voluntary Sector Mental Healthcare in Inner-City London.

text: Studying canine behavioral genetics could provide important insights for dog breeding and for understanding both canine and human behavior. To identify genetic determinants of behavior in German Shepherd Dogs, we used a cohort of 373 dogs to search for genome-wide associations with behavioral variables and personality traits measured by the Dog Mentality Assessment (DMA), a standardized dog behavior evaluation widely used in Sweden. Multidimensional scaling using genetic data revealed two clusters identified by merits as working and show sub-populations differing in most of their DMA scores. These behavioral differences were strongly correlated with BOLDNESS-a higher-order trait considered a measure of the shyness-boldness personality continuum in dogs.
title: The Genetic Architecture of Behavior in the German Shepherd Dog.

text: A region with highest allele frequency differences between sub-populations was found on CFA24: 23.5-25.5 Mb containing genes for coat color specification and previously reported candidate regions of selection. The strongest association signals were found for traits/behavioral variables correlating with BOLDNESS as, for example, on CFA1 within a region encompassing the TCF4 gene for which, in humans, multiple associations with neuroticism (a reverse equivalent in humans of BOLDNESS in dogs) were reported. Signals of association were found in regions containing genes with important roles in the nervous system and associations with comparable personality traits, such as neuroticism, in humans.
title: The Genetic Architecture of Behavior in the German Shepherd Dog.

text: Our results indicate that within-breed selection in GSDs has had an effect on the shyness-boldness personality continuum, with working dogs scoring higher in all aspects of BOLDNESS-being more playful, prone to chase after toys, curious, fearless and socially interested in strangers compared with show dogs.
title: The Genetic Architecture of Behavior in the German Shepherd Dog.

text: We report findings from a Phase 1/2a clinical trial (EUCT No. 2024-514590-22-00, STOP-DCI), an interventional, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple ascending-dose, first-in-human trial to determine safety and evaluate clinical outcome for the MEK 1/2 inhibitor EDV2209 in patients with severe spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). In Phase 1b (N = 11), three cohorts received a single intracerebral ventricular (ICV) bolus (8.55 µg, 17-28.5 µg). In Phase 2a (N = 16), two cohorts were given three ICV injections of 28.5 µg EDV2209 or placebo over 18 h, beginning within 8 h of SAH onset.The study found an equal distribution of adverse events between treatment and placebo with no treatment-associated safety concerns. Outcomes and mortality were as expected or better for patients with severe SAH in the patients treated with EDV2209.
title: First-in-Human Phase 1b/2a Trial Shows Safety with MEK 1/2 Inhibitor EDV2209 as A Novel Treatment for Spontaneous Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.

text: Pharmacokinetics were reproducibly stable in the CSF with no detectable levels of EDV2209 in plasma.Treatment with EDV2209 was considered safe and was interpreted to provide potential benefit for improving patient outcome following severe SAH. These results provide a rationale to continue with a Phase 2b / 3 study powered to determine efficacy as well as safety.
title: First-in-Human Phase 1b/2a Trial Shows Safety with MEK 1/2 Inhibitor EDV2209 as A Novel Treatment for Spontaneous Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
