text: Levetiracetam (LEV) is commonly used as an adjunctive antiseizure medication (ASM) in dogs because of its favorable pharmacokinetic profile and limited hepatic metabolism. However, because LEV is predominantly eliminated through renal excretion, prospective clinical evidence regarding its effects on renal function in dogs remains limited. This prospective study evaluated short-term changes in renal biomarkers and urinalysis parameters in 12 client-owned dogs with idiopathic epilepsy (IE) receiving concurrent phenobarbital (PB) and adjunctive LEV. All 12 dogs were evaluated at baseline (day 0), day 14, and day 28. Renal assessment included serum symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA), serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), phosphorus, albumin, and urinalysis; glomerular filtration rate (GFR) was not directly measured.
title: Short-Term Renal Effects of Add-On Levetiracetam in Client-Owned Dogs with Idiopathic Epilepsy Receiving Phenobarbital: A Four-Week Prospective Study.

text: Changes in SDMA over time were analyzed using the Friedman test, whereas serum creatinine, BUN, phosphorus, and albumin were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA with the Geisser-Greenhouse correction. No statistically significant changes were detected in SDMA, serum creatinine, BUN, phosphorus, or albumin during the 4-week study period. Urinalysis showed no consistent progressive abnormalities, including proteinuria, glucosuria, or urinary casts. Sedation was the most frequently observed clinical adverse event, occurring in 83% (10/12) of dogs, although it was generally mild and did not require treatment discontinuation. Overall, no detectable short-term deterioration in the assessed renal biomarkers or urinalysis parameters was identified during the 4-week study period in non-azotemic dogs receiving concurrent PB and adjunctive LEV.
title: Short-Term Renal Effects of Add-On Levetiracetam in Client-Owned Dogs with Idiopathic Epilepsy Receiving Phenobarbital: A Four-Week Prospective Study.

text: However, the absence of statistically significant or clinically detectable changes does not exclude subtle alterations in renal function or subclinical renal injury. Larger controlled studies with longer follow-up periods and direct assessment of GFR are warranted.
title: Short-Term Renal Effects of Add-On Levetiracetam in Client-Owned Dogs with Idiopathic Epilepsy Receiving Phenobarbital: A Four-Week Prospective Study.

text: Glycosylation, glycogen metabolism, and ubiquitination represent three fundamental cellular processes that are traditionally studied as distinct aspects of biology. Glycosylation and glycogen metabolism are unique carbohydrate-based pathways. The process of glycosylation generates structurally diverse glycans that regulate protein folding, cell signaling, and host-pathogen interactions, while glycogen serves as a glucose reserve essential for energy homeostasis. Emerging evidence reveals a deep mechanistic connection between these pathways, particularly in the context of brain biology and inherited metabolic diseases. Here, we present recent research linking glycosylation defects with glycogen metabolism, highlighting how changes in the shared metabolites and enzymatic pathways contribute to human health and disease.
title: Glycogen and Glycosylation: Friends or Foes?

text: We then discuss the overlapping disease symptoms of congenital disorders of glycosylation and glycogen storage diseases, with particular emphasis on polyglucosan body-forming diseases. We also highlight the role of non-canonical ubiquitin ligase complexes such as laforin-malin and LUBAC and present emerging evidence for their potential role in the glycogen quality-control mechanism. Finally, we review current therapeutic strategies for CDGs and GSDs, including monosaccharide supplementation, glycogen synthase modulation, and gene therapy. Together, this review underscores glycogen as more than an energy store-as a key contributor to glycosylation homeostasis and cellular regulation in health and disease.
title: Glycogen and Glycosylation: Friends or Foes?

text: Background/Objectives : In this study, we investigated whether targeting thiamine (vitamin B 1 ) metabolism could be useful in the treatment of glioblastoma. Methods : The study was conducted using LN-229 and T98G glioblastoma cell lines, as well as glioblastoma tissue samples obtained from up to 30 patients. The effects of thiamine and the thiamine antimetabolites oxythiamine and amprolium on cell viability were assessed using the MTT assay. The effects of hypoxia and temozolomide (TMZ), as well as gene expression in tissue samples, were analyzed using qRT-PCR. The expression of SLC19A2 , SLC19A3 , TPK1 , SLC25A19 , SLC35F3 , and SLC44A4 was evaluated. Results : Higher thiamine concentrations increased the MTT metabolic activity of glioblastoma cells.
title: Do Glioblastoma Cancer Cells Need Vitamins? The Role of Vitamin B<sub>1</sub>.

text: Oxythiamine and amprolium reduced MTT metabolic activity, although their inhibitory effects reached a plateau and neither compound enhanced the effect of TMZ. Chronic hypoxia reduces thiamine metabolism. The expression of proteins involved in thiamine metabolism is lower in glioblastoma tissue than in peritumoral tissue. Conclusions : Overall, targeting thiamine metabolism does not appear to improve the efficacy of TMZ-based glioblastoma treatment. However, the observed viability-promoting effect of higher thiamine concentrations indicates that excessive thiamine intake or supplementation in patients with glioblastoma should be approached with caution and requires further clinical investigation.
title: Do Glioblastoma Cancer Cells Need Vitamins? The Role of Vitamin B<sub>1</sub>.

text: Background Spirometric airflow obstruction frequently remains unrecognised in community settings, representing a major diagnostic gap in chronic respiratory disease management. Population-based epidemiological data from Romanian coastal communities-characterised by a highly dynamic population including residents, seasonal workers, and tourists-remain scarce. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of screening-detected pre-bronchodilator airflow obstruction and chronic respiratory diseases, characterise smoking behaviours including novel tobacco product use, identify individuals at elevated risk for sleep apnea, and examine patterns of preventive care and healthcare utilisation across five Black Sea coastal localities.
title: Prevalence of Chronic Respiratory Diseases, Airflow Obstruction, Sleep Apnea Risk, and Novel Tobacco Use in the Coastal Localities of the Mangalia Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study of 979 Adults.

text: Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 979 adults from five coastal localities in Constanța County, Romania, as part of a community-based respiratory screening campaign conducted 11-16 August 2025: Neptun ( n = 147), Olimp ( n = 178), Saturn ( n = 187), Mangalia ( n = 257), and Jupiter ( n = 210). Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering 22 domains, including medical diagnoses, spirometric measurements (FEV1/FVC%), sleep quality, snoring, anthropometric parameters, comorbidities, and healthcare utilisation. Airflow obstruction was defined as an FEV1/FVC ratio Results Among 979 participants (51.4% female; mean age 47.3 ± 13.5 years), 9.3% had at least one CRD: asthma (4.4%), chronic bronchitis (3.0%), COPD (1.7%), and emphysema (0.3%).
title: Prevalence of Chronic Respiratory Diseases, Airflow Obstruction, Sleep Apnea Risk, and Novel Tobacco Use in the Coastal Localities of the Mangalia Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study of 979 Adults.

text: CRD prevalence increased with age, from 6.1% in individuals 1 /FVC n = 107) and was more common among obese participants (19.5% vs. 7.9%; absolute difference 11.6 percentage points; p Conclusions One in six adults without a prior respiratory diagnosis demonstrated spirometric airflow limitation, suggesting that opportunistic spirometry in primary care could substantially improve case detection in Romanian coastal communities. OSA risk, assessed by symptom-based screening proxy, was present in 10.9% of participants, with higher BMI as the strongest independent predictor among the variables assessed. High smoking prevalence (35.2%) and critically low pneumococcal vaccination coverage (3.4%) represent additional modifiable public health targets.
title: Prevalence of Chronic Respiratory Diseases, Airflow Obstruction, Sleep Apnea Risk, and Novel Tobacco Use in the Coastal Localities of the Mangalia Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study of 979 Adults.

text: These findings support a unified community respiratory screening approach incorporating spirometry, sleep apnea risk stratification, and vaccination audit, particularly in primary care settings serving coastal populations with dynamic demographics.
title: Prevalence of Chronic Respiratory Diseases, Airflow Obstruction, Sleep Apnea Risk, and Novel Tobacco Use in the Coastal Localities of the Mangalia Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study of 979 Adults.

text: Feline calicivirus (FCV) and feline herpesvirus 1 (FHV-1) are major pathogens threatening feline health, and prophylactic immunity remains the primary preventive approach. To develop a safe and effective multivalent vaccine against the two viruses, two recombinant rabies virus (RABV) vaccines expressing the FCV VP1 and FHV-1 gB/gD genes were constructed. The exogenous genes showed stable inheritance following serial viral passages, and the recombinant RABVs exhibited growth kinetics comparable to the parental strain, with a delayed peak titer. After verifying the viral pathogenicity, the recombinant RABV vaccines elicited specific IgG antibodies against VP1, gB, and gD, as well as neutralizing antibodies against FCV, FHV-1, and RABV in mice. Immunized mice were also protected against lethal RABV challenge.
title: Immunogenicity evaluation of recombinant rabies virus-vectored multivalent vaccines expressing feline calicivirus VP1 and feline herpesvirus 1 gB/gD genes.

text: In cats, the vaccines induced neutralizing antibodies against the three pathogens, and immunized cats showed milder clinical signs and less severe histopathological lesions following FHV-1 and FCV challenge. Collectively, these findings indicate that the two recombinant vaccines induce robust humoral immune responses against FCV, FHV-1, and RABV in both mice and cats and confer protection against viral challenges.
title: Immunogenicity evaluation of recombinant rabies virus-vectored multivalent vaccines expressing feline calicivirus VP1 and feline herpesvirus 1 gB/gD genes.

text: The classical swine (CS) H1N1 influenza virus, first isolated in 1930, is highly homologous to the 1918 Spanish influenza virus. CS H1N1 virus, which crossed the interspecies barrier to infect humans has become the dominantly prevalent strain in China's pig population, showing a trend of continuous transmission. However, whether subsequent adaptation of CS H1N1 to mammals would increase their pathogenicity toward humans is unknown. To address this, a mouse-adapted (MA) CS H1N1 virus (A/Swine/Guangdong/1/2011[G11-MA]) was generated through serially passaged in mouse lungs, exhibiting increased virulence compared to the wild-type (WT). Further study showed that the G11-MA strain exhibited amino acid mutations in PB2-D740N, PB1-T56I, PA-T97I and HA-K188E, and the combination of PB2-D740N with PA-T97I improved the replication ability in mammalian cells and mice.
title: Identification of the key amino acid mutations in the PB2 and PA proteins of classical swine H1N1 influenza A virus in mammalian adaptation.

text: The G11-MA strain with PB2 and PA (G11/MA PB2PA) group enhanced the viral polymerase activity, with a similar survival rate and weight loss of mice compared to the G11-MA group. Our study demonstrates that the combination of PB2-D740N and PA-T97I plays a key role in the virulence phenotype of CS H1N1 influenza viruses, and provides important information for evaluating the pandemic risk of swine influenza strains.
title: Identification of the key amino acid mutations in the PB2 and PA proteins of classical swine H1N1 influenza A virus in mammalian adaptation.

text: Heavy metal and organic pollutant co-contamination is increasingly being detected in soils and water systems, particularly due to tire wear-derived compounds such as zinc (Zn) and 2-mercaptobenzothiazole (MBT), yet their combined effects on forage grasses remain poorly understood. This hydroponic study investigated the varied responses of 20 Lolium perenne cultivars to elevated zinc, 2-mercaptobenzothiazole, and their combined stress (Zn 20 mg L -1 (Zn treatment group), MBT20 mg L -1 (MBT treatment group), and MBT20 mg L -1 + Zn 20 mg L -1 (MBT-Zn treatment group)). Fifteen physiological and biochemical markers, including biomass, photosynthetic pigments, osmoregulatory chemicals, and antioxidant enzyme activity, were examined. The results demonstrated specific varietal adaptation mechanisms in response to both individual and combined stresses.
title: Effects of combined zinc and 2 mercaptobenzothiazole exposure on growth and physiological characteristics of <i>Lolium perenne</i> cultivars.

text: Most varieties exhibited significant alterations in 13 of 15 traits compared to controls, except for underground biomass and soluble protein content. Across varieties, plant height, aerial/underground biomass, chlorophyll a / b , carotenoids, and root activity decreased under stress. In contrast, the levels of soluble protein, malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and free proline exhibited significant increases. These changes were consistent with altered oxidative regulation and protective physiological responses under contaminant exposure. Combined Zn and MBT exposure produced trait-dependent and cultivar-dependent responses. Although combined exposure generally intensified oxidative responses, its effects on growth and photosynthetic traits were not consistently more severe than those of the individual stressors.
title: Effects of combined zinc and 2 mercaptobenzothiazole exposure on growth and physiological characteristics of <i>Lolium perenne</i> cultivars.

text: Several cultivars showed partial attenuation of specific growth effects under combined exposure, indicating a nonadditive interaction between Zn and MBT rather than uniformly greater or lower toxicity. The findings provide a physiological basis for identifying L. perenne cultivars that maintain growth and protective metabolism under simultaneous Zn and MBT exposure. The identified tolerant cultivars represent candidates for further studies of contaminant uptake, translocation, and removal.
title: Effects of combined zinc and 2 mercaptobenzothiazole exposure on growth and physiological characteristics of <i>Lolium perenne</i> cultivars.

text: Pulmonic stenosis (PS) is one of the most common congenital cardiac diseases in dogs. Although echocardiography and computed tomographic angiography (CTA) provide valuable diagnostic and anatomical information, the hemodynamic consequences of PS remain incompletely characterized. This study describes patient-specific pulmonary artery hemodynamics in dogs with and without PS using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Contrast-enhanced CTA and echocardiographic data from five dogs with PS and five control dogs without PS were used to reconstruct three-dimensional pulmonary artery geometries and generate patient-specific CFD models. Pressure drop (Δp), blood flow velocity, mean wall shear stress (WSS), time-averaged WSS (TAWSS), oscillatory shear index (OSI), relative residence time (RRT), and pulmonary artery resistance were quantified and compared between groups.
title: Patient-Specific Computational Fluid Dynamics of Pulmonary Arterial Hemodynamics in Dogs with and Without Pulmonic Stenosis.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Dogs with PS exhibited markedly increased transvalvular pressure gradients, peak flow velocities, and pulmonary artery resistance, together with high-velocity jets and localized post-stenotic recirculation that were absent in control dogs. Mean WSS and TAWSS tended to be higher in the PS group, whereas OSI values were similar between groups. In contrast, RRT was significantly lower ( p = 0.032) in dogs with PS. These findings demonstrate that patient-specific CFD enables detailed characterization of pulmonary artery hemodynamics in canine PS, providing information that complements conventional imaging. Although its clinical utility in veterinary medicine has yet to be fully established, CFD can provide valuable insight into flow behavior and disease pathophysiology; however, its ability to yield precise, clinically applicable quantitative values remains limited.
title: Patient-Specific Computational Fluid Dynamics of Pulmonary Arterial Hemodynamics in Dogs with and Without Pulmonic Stenosis.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: This approach shows promise for future applications in the clinical evaluation of PS and other cardiovascular diseases, although further studies are warranted to determine its clinical relevance in veterinary medicine.
title: Patient-Specific Computational Fluid Dynamics of Pulmonary Arterial Hemodynamics in Dogs with and Without Pulmonic Stenosis.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Cloacal swabs were collected from 12 Eurasian goshawk chicks during routine veterinary inspections to evaluate the gut-associated virome of goshawks used for falconry. The material was used for metagenomic screening with high-throughput sequencing. Sequences belonging to several viral families ( Poxviridae , Circoviridae , Anelloviridae , Retroviridae , Parvoviridae and Astroviridae ) were detected and their occurrence differed across samples G1-G12. Most of the identified sequences were highly similar to those of viruses that infect poultry, suggesting a probable alimentary transmission route. Two complete genomes of closely related chicken astroviruses, most likely strains belonging to subgroup Biii, were identified. Their ORF2 proteins shared 98.78% amino acid identity.
title: New Parvovirus and Other Swab-Associated Viruses Identified in the Eurasian Goshawk (<i>Astur gentilis</i>).

text: Another complete genome was identified as that of pigeon circovirus with 98.96% nucleotide identity to a strain previously reported from China. A parvovirus genome sequence, distinct from those of known members of the genus Aveparvovirus genus was also identified. This parvovirus genome sequence represents approximately 86% of the average aveparvovirus genome length (5422 bp) and contains three open reading frames. The sequence lacks the 3' region of the capsid gene is missing and the 3' UTR. The NS1 protein sequence of this virus shares 52.42% amino acid identity with that of its closest relative, the nonstructural protein of silver pheasant parvovirus. These findings suggest that parvovirus infection may occur in birds of prey and that the detected virus may represent a novel member of the genus Aveparvovirus.
title: New Parvovirus and Other Swab-Associated Viruses Identified in the Eurasian Goshawk (<i>Astur gentilis</i>).

text: The infected bird showed no clinical symptoms during sampling; thus, the role of this parvovirus in raptor pathology as well as the possibility that it was of dietary origin remains unknown and requires further investigation.
title: New Parvovirus and Other Swab-Associated Viruses Identified in the Eurasian Goshawk (<i>Astur gentilis</i>).

text: Background Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have attracted considerable attention owing to their unexpected cardioprotective benefits in addition to glycemic control. Indeed, these inhibitors have been reported to exert anti-fibrotic effects and ameliorate NACHT, leucine-rich repeat (LRR), and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3)-dependent inflammation. However, whether SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) attenuate post-infarction myocardial fibrosis by suppressing NLRP3-dependent signaling remains unclear. Thus, this study aimed to investigate the mechanisms through which the SGLT2is dapagliflozin (DAPA) mitigates post-infarction myocardial fibrosis, with particular emphasis on the modulation of NLRP3-dependent signaling.
title: Dapagliflozin Attenuates Post-Infarction Myocardial Fibrosis Associated With the Inhibition of NLRP3-Dependent Inflammation.

text: Methods Male Sprague-Dawley rats were used to establish a myocardial infarction (MI) model via left coronary artery ligation and were treated with DAPA (1 mg/kg/day). Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging was performed to evaluate cardiac function and remodeling. Serial 18 F-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-74 ( 18 F-FAPI-74) positron emission tomography (PET) was used to track temporal changes in cardiac fibroblast (CF) activation. Myocardial fibrosis and NLRP3-dependent signaling were assessed ex vivo . The effects of DAPA on NLRP3-dependent signaling, fibroblast proliferation, phenotypic transition, and collagen synthesis were determined in vitro using cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) stimulated with lipopolysaccharide.
title: Dapagliflozin Attenuates Post-Infarction Myocardial Fibrosis Associated With the Inhibition of NLRP3-Dependent Inflammation.

text: Results Compared with untreated MI rats, MI rats treated with DAPA exhibited significantly lower left ventricular (LV) end-systolic volume, LV end-diastolic volume, and LV mass, along with improved LV ejection fraction (57.6 ± 2.4% vs. 54.4 ± 2.1% in the MI group; p = 0.011). LV fibrosis was reduced in DAPA-treated MI rats (20.1 ± 1.9% vs. 31.1 ± 4.0% in the MI group; p = 0.0026), and fibrosis markers were significantly downregulated. In vivo 18 F-FAPI-74 PET revealed that DAPA suppressed CF activation, as demonstrated by significantly reduced 18 F-FAPI-74 uptake in the infarcted region. In infarcted cardiac tissue, DAPA inhibited the expression of the NLRP3 inflammasome, interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), and interleukin-18 (IL-18).
title: Dapagliflozin Attenuates Post-Infarction Myocardial Fibrosis Associated With the Inhibition of NLRP3-Dependent Inflammation.

text: CF experiments performed in vitro showed that DAPA inhibited the nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)/NLRP3 pathway and attenuated CF proliferation, phenotypic transition, and collagen synthesis. Conclusions By suppressing CF activation, DAPA improved myocardial fibrosis, adverse LV remodeling, and cardiac function post-MI, in association with inhibition of the NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway. 18 F-FAPI-74 PET enabled non-invasive visualization of the anti-fibrotic effects of DAPA post-MI and may serve as a tool to monitor anti-fibrotic treatment efficacy after MI.
title: Dapagliflozin Attenuates Post-Infarction Myocardial Fibrosis Associated With the Inhibition of NLRP3-Dependent Inflammation.

text: Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis with a high case-fatality rate and expanding geographic range. Its persistence depends on complex cycles involving ticks and vertebrate animal hosts. A comprehensive understanding of animal roles is critical for predicting spillover risk and developing effective interventions under a One Health framework. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize existing evidence on the roles of domestic animals, wildlife, and companion animals in the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and transmission of SFTSV. Methods A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Multiple databases (MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang) and grey literature sources were searched from January 1, 2011 to October 21, 2025.
title: The role of animals in the epidemiology and pathogenesis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS): a scoping review.

text: Eligible studies involved non-human animals or ticks and confirmed SFTSV infection or exposure. Evidence was narratively synthesized across prespecified themes: animal host roles, clinical manifestations, transmission dynamics, and prevention strategies. We mapped the distribution of evidence across animal species, study designs, geographic regions, diagnostic approaches, and thematic domains. Results The review identified a broad animal host range comprising at least 15 vertebrate species across domestic, wildlife, and companion categories. Domestic ruminants show high seroprevalence and act as primary amplification hosts. Wildlife (e.g., rodents, shrews) contribute to enzootic maintenance. Cats are highly susceptible, develop severe disease with high viral loads, and are a major source of direct non-vector transmission to humans.
title: The role of animals in the epidemiology and pathogenesis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS): a scoping review.

text: Dogs often have mild illness but can shed virus persistently. Transmission primarily occurs via the tick Haemaphysalis longicornis, but direct transmission via contact with blood/secretions of sick animals (especially cats and farmed mink) is significant. Prevention requires integrated tick management, biosecurity in veterinary/farm settings, and public education. Conclusions Animals are central to the ecology of SFTSV. Current evidence underscores the necessity of integrated, multisectoral One Health strategies for surveillance, risk communication, and control. Future research priorities include standardizing host-competence studies, harmonizing diagnostics, elucidating comparative immunopathology, and evaluating the feasibility and impact of intervention bundles, including potential veterinary vaccines.
title: The role of animals in the epidemiology and pathogenesis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS): a scoping review.

text: In recent years, synthetic biology has been widely applied to engineer and program cellular behaviors. Using this approach, bacteria can be designed to express immunotherapeutic agents, improve tumor targeting, and deliver therapeutic payloads directly to tumor sites. To further improve efficacy, strategies such as hypoxia-responsive promoters, bacterial swarming, and extracellular vesicles (EVs) have been investigated, along with the synergistic effects of combining bacterial therapy with other treatments (e.g., photodynamic therapy, chemotherapy, immune checkpoint inhibitors). This review summarizes recent advances in synthetic biology for bacteria-based cancer immunotherapies, focusing on how bacterial agents activate the immune system and the engineering strategies used to achieve tumor targeting.
title: Leveraging the bacteria for enhanced cancer immunotherapy: from a perspective of synthetic biology.

text: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a severe, life-limiting genetic disorder caused by mutations in the CFTR gene, which lead to defective epithelial ion transport, abnormally thick mucus and multi organ dysfunction, predominantly affecting the lungs, pancreas and digestive system. Despite significant advances in patient care, the complex interplay between CFTR dysfunction, chronic infection and persistent inflammation remains a major therapeutic challenge. In this context, animal models are indispensable for elucidating the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying CF pathogenesis and accelerating drug discovery. Here, we review the relevance of the zebrafish (Danio rerio) as a powerful and complementary preclinical model for CF research.
title: Cystic fibrosis: insights from zebrafish models.

text: In particular, we highlight the unique advantages of zebrafish, including its highly conserved innate immune system and optical transparency, which together enable in vivo visualization of host immune responses under CF-like conditions at subcellular resolution. We further summarize how Cftr-deficient zebrafish models have provided key insights into the increased susceptibility to CF-relevant pathogens, disease mechanisms affecting the pancreas and the reproductive system, and the deleterious neutrophil-driven inflammation that characterizes CF. Finally, we discuss the potential of the zebrafish model for the identification and validation of novel therapeutic strategies to treat infectious and inflammatory lung pathology in CF, and outline future directions to expand its translational impact in CF research.
title: Cystic fibrosis: insights from zebrafish models.

text: The serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) is a promising circulating biomarker for canine cognitive dysfunction syndrome (CCDS). This cross-sectional study evaluated serum NfL (sNfL) as a surrogate for cerebrospinal fluid NfL (cNfL) and assessed the effects of physiological factors on its clinical utility. Biofluid NfL was analyzed using the single-molecule array (Simoa) across 126 clinical samples, comprising 44 cNfL and 25 paired cNfL/sNfL samples in geriatric dogs (>8 years) and 16 paired samples from a younger cohort (≤8 years). A moderate monotonic correlation was observed between cNfL and sNfL in geriatric dogs, but this association was not maintained in the younger cohort after adjusting for body weight. In the geriatric cohort, raw sNfL levels differentiated cerebral atrophy from controls but not from other intracranial pathologies.
title: Investigation of Serum Neurofilament Light Chain as a Surrogate for Cerebrospinal Fluid Neurofilament Light Chain in Canine Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Notably, the ability of cNfL to discriminate structural, atrophic, and mixed brain pathologies from controls significantly improved after adjustment for confounding effects of age and body weight. A similar optimization strategy may be applicable to sNfL. Systematically controlling for these physiological covariates in larger cohorts could potentially further improve the diagnostic precision of blood-based NfL screening in primary veterinary practice.
title: Investigation of Serum Neurofilament Light Chain as a Surrogate for Cerebrospinal Fluid Neurofilament Light Chain in Canine Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: In humans, surgical repair is commonly performed for infective endocarditis (IE) associated with mitral valve destruction. However, extensive valve destruction may make repair impossible and require prosthetic valve replacement. In small-breed dogs, appropriately sized prosthetic valves are lacking, and complete surgical mitral valve reconstruction in dogs has not been reported. We encountered a Chihuahua that developed IE after mitral valve repair. During reoperation for progressive mitral regurgitation recurrence, the mitral leaflets were extensively destroyed and torn, and re-repair using native tissue was impossible; the entire valve was therefore reconstructed with fresh autologous pericardium. A graft was harvested and fashioned into a cylindrical valve based on a design previously described in a human study.
title: Complete Mitral Valve Reconstruction Using Fresh Autologous Pericardium in a Chihuahua with Infective Endocarditis: A Case Report.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Intraoperative saline testing and immediate postoperative echocardiography confirmed adequate opening and closure of the reconstructed pericardial valve, with only mild mitral regurgitation and no stenosis. The dog died on the second day after reoperative day of an uncontrolled infection caused by extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli . This case demonstrates that an autologous pericardial valve can provide short-term mechanical function as a mitral valve in a small-breed dog and indicates that infection control is the principal determinant of outcome.
title: Complete Mitral Valve Reconstruction Using Fresh Autologous Pericardium in a Chihuahua with Infective Endocarditis: A Case Report.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Although One Health and biosecurity both aim to protect the health of people, animals, and ecosystems from biological hazards, the two fields remain heavily siloed across distinct policy and research domains. One Health has yet to fully integrate environmental perspectives, especially biological invasions, into its workplan, whereas biosecurity lacks an effective inclusion of the social and health sciences, further hindering collaboration. One Biosecurity offers a vital interdisciplinary framework that bridges human, animal, plant, and ecosystem health sectors, fostering a stronger connection between biosecurity and One Health. This comprehensive approach spans the entire biosecurity continuum, from pre-border intelligence scans to border inspections and post-border incursion management, enabling more effective responses to the threats posed by biological invasions.
title: One Biosecurity is essential to implement One Health.

text: By unifying these efforts, One Biosecurity will engage a broader group of multilateral organizations, bring together diverse stakeholders, and implement balanced strategies that better safeguard human health, agriculture production systems, and the natural environment.
title: One Biosecurity is essential to implement One Health.

text: Background Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) is a fatal multisystem inflammatory disorder of cats that was historically considered untreatable before the emergence of direct-acting antivirals. Objectives The objective of the study was to evaluate early serial changes in serum protein electrophoresis (SPE) patterns in cats treated with remdesivir for FIP, emphasizing gamma-globulin concentrations and percentages. Animals included eighteen client-owned cats diagnosed with FIP based on clinical presentation, standard clinicopathological profiles, and confirmatory RT-PCR. Methods Cats received remdesivir for 4 weeks and were monitored weekly through clinical examinations and laboratory evaluations. Blood samples were collected at baseline (prior to treatment initiation) and weekly for 4 weeks.
title: Early Changes in Serum Protein Electrophoresis and Gamma Globulin during Initial 4 Weeks of Remdesivir Therapy in FIP Cats.

text: The SPE analyzed the blood taken every week for the serum protein fractions, such as albumin and the different globulins, namely α1-, α2-, β1-, β2-, and γ-globulins. The albumin to globulin ratio (A/G ratio) was also determined. Outcomes Gamma globulins were found to be significantly reduced from a median of 3.1 g/dL at week 2 to a median of 2.2 g/dL at the end of week 4 (p Conclusions Serial monitoring of serum protein electrophoresis, particularly longitudinal trends in gamma-globulin percentages and the A/G ratio, provides an objective, practical biomarker strategy to evaluate treatment response and guide the safe timing of antiviral therapy cessation in cats with FIP.
title: Early Changes in Serum Protein Electrophoresis and Gamma Globulin during Initial 4 Weeks of Remdesivir Therapy in FIP Cats.

text: Controlling glycosylation, a critical quality attribute of biopharmaceuticals such as monoclonal antibodies, is essential, as it significantly influences biological activity and therapeutic efficacy. Although numerous studies have examined the impact of process parameters (PP, e.g. temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen) on glycosylation, the lack of standardized reporting makes cross-study comparisons challenging and prevents clear conclusions. Here, we systematically reviewed the literature and applied a normalized quantitative framework, the Glycan Indices approach, as a standardized quantitative criterion to evaluate the impact of process parameters on glycoform distribution in IgG-producing CHO cell systems objectively.
title: Impact of process parameters on IgG glycosylation in CHO systems: a comprehensive quantitative analysis.

text: This methodology enabled the integration and reinterpretation of large, heterogeneous datasets, validating some well-known patterns while providing novel perspectives about process parameters. Our analysis revealed that PP manipulations of pH, dissolved oxygen or CO 2 partial pressure rarely resulted in meaningful shifts in glycosylation, with changes 10%) and fucosylation (1-10%), variations that may have significant biological consequences. To our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive quantitative assessment of process parameters effects on glycosylation, showing that such influences are consistently limited, independent of CHO cell line or culture mode. Based in our observations we strongly recommend reporting both glycan distribution and glycan indices when performing glycan analysis.
title: Impact of process parameters on IgG glycosylation in CHO systems: a comprehensive quantitative analysis.

text: Dual reporting facilitates inter-study comparisons and prevents subtle shifts in sugar moieties from being masked by glycan redistribution.
title: Impact of process parameters on IgG glycosylation in CHO systems: a comprehensive quantitative analysis.

text: This study investigated the roles of the NLRP3 inflammasome in postoperative ileus (POI) pathogenesis. Male BALB/c mice were randomly divided into sham, POI, and MCC950 (NLRP3 inhibitor) groups. Intestinal motility was assessed 24 h postoperatively. RNA-seq was performed. Histopathological changes were evaluated through H&E and immunofluorescence; CAT and POD activities in the intrinsic muscle layer were detected; Western blot was used to detect NLRP3, GSDMD-N, cleaved caspase-1, and p-NF-κB p65 expressions; ELISA was used to detect blood IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-10 levels. RNA-seq analysis showed 152 differential genes in the POI group, including NLRP3. In intestinal tissue of the POI mice, NLRP3 expression and expressions of GSDMD-N, cleaved caspase-1, and p-NF-κB p65 increased. IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-10 levels increased, while CAT, POD, and SOD activities decreased.
title: The role of NLRP3 inflammasome in the development of postoperative ileus and its molecular mechanism in male mice.

text: The postoperative small intestine advancement rate of POI mice was reduced. After MCC950 intervention, the pathological damage to intestinal tissue and the intestinal function were restored, and the small intestine advancement rate was improved. Meanwhile, MCC950 effectively inhibited the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. NLRP3 inflammasome activation drives the pathogenesis of POI and MCC950 can effectively alleviate intestinal injury.
title: The role of NLRP3 inflammasome in the development of postoperative ileus and its molecular mechanism in male mice.

text: Novel goose parvovirus (NGPV) infection in ducklings induces short beak and dwarfism syndrome (SBDS), leading to significant economic losses. Since NGPV predominantly infects ducklings, whether reshaping the intestinal flora of ducklings through fecal microbiota transplantation from adult ducks (FMT-A) can alleviate SBDS is an interesting question. This study aimed to investigate the impact of FMT-A on the susceptibility of ducklings to NGPV infection, to elucidate the potential relationship between gut microbiota and viral pathogenicity. The results showed that ducklings were more susceptible to NGPV than adults, and that adult ducks exhibited higher fecal microbiota richness and diversity. FMT-A treatment attenuated NGPV-induced reductions in body weight, beak and tibia length, and muscle mass.
title: Adult duck fecal microbiota transplantation alleviates short beak and dwarfism syndrome in ducklings by inhibiting Th17 cell differentiation.

text: Furthermore, FMT-A alleviated gut dysbiosis and intestinal tissue damage, increased glycogen in the intestinal mucosa, upregulated ZO-1 expression, expanded the epiphyseal region, and reduced osteoclast numbers in the tibia of ducklings. Moreover, FMT-A suppressed the expression of the Th17 cell-specific transcription factor retinoic acid receptor-related orphan receptor γt in the ileum and bone, and decreased the expression levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in the ileum, bone, and serum. These findings indicate that ducklings are more susceptible to NGPV than adult ducks, with significantly lower diversity and abundance of fecal microbiota. FMT-A can stabilize intestinal flora, mitigate intestinal barrier damage, inhibit Th17 cell differentiation, thereby reducing abnormal bone development, and ultimately alleviate SBDS in ducklings.
title: Adult duck fecal microbiota transplantation alleviates short beak and dwarfism syndrome in ducklings by inhibiting Th17 cell differentiation.

text: These findings provide a theoretical basis for developing novel strategies targeting gut microbiota modulation to prevent and control SBDS in ducklings.
title: Adult duck fecal microbiota transplantation alleviates short beak and dwarfism syndrome in ducklings by inhibiting Th17 cell differentiation.

text: Molecular-targeted therapies require biomarker-driven evaluation to optimize precision oncology strategies; however, translational models integrating clinical outcomes with mechanistic biomarkers are limited. Canine urothelial carcinoma shares molecular features with human muscle-invasive bladder cancer, including activation of VEGFR signaling, providing a valuable comparative oncology platform. Sorafenib is a multi-kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFRs, PDGFRβ, BRAF, and related pathways, but its therapeutic mechanisms and clinical benefit in urothelial carcinoma remain incompletely understood. In this study, 43 dogs with naturally occurring urothelial carcinoma received first-line sorafenib and piroxicam therapy. The overall response rate was 62.8%, with median progression-free and overall survival of 175 (range, 31-665) and 407 (range, 103-1,723) days, respectively.
title: Sorafenib/piroxicam therapy with biomarker-defined survival benefit in canine muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma.

text: The results exceeded outcomes in historical controls treated with piroxicam alone. Treatment was generally well tolerated, with only three grade 3 adverse events and no grade 4-5 toxicities. Biomarker analyses revealed that treatment-induced hypertension and high tumor CX3CL1 mRNA expression were independently associated with improved overall survival, suggesting that effective VEGFR pathway inhibition and modulation of the tumor immune microenvironment contribute to clinical benefit. These findings support sorafenib-based therapy as a promising strategy for canine urothelial carcinoma and highlight the translational potential of biomarker-driven VEGFR-targeted approaches in precision oncology.
title: Sorafenib/piroxicam therapy with biomarker-defined survival benefit in canine muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma.

text: Porcine rotavirus A (PoRVA) is an important cause of diarrhea in neonatal piglets, resulting in significant economic losses in the swine industry. In this study, a PoRVA strain, designated QY, was isolated from diarrheic piglets and systematically characterized. The virus was propagated in MA104 cells and identified by immunofluorescence assay and transmission electron microscopy, showing typical cytopathic effects and spherical particles of approximately 70 nm. Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis revealed that QY was a G4P[13] strain with a genotype constellation of G4-P[13]-I1-C1-M1-R1-A8-N1-T1-E1-H1. Several genome segments showed close phylogenetic relationships with human- or bat-associated RVA strains, a pattern consistent with a possible reassortment history of QY.
title: A G4P[13] Porcine Rotavirus a Strain with Genomic Features Suggestive of Reassortment: Isolation, Genomic Characterization, and Pathogenicity in Piglets.

text: Experimental infection showed that QY caused watery diarrhea, intestinal lesions, and viral shedding in neonatal piglets under the experimental conditions used in this study. High viral loads were detected in small intestinal tissues, accompanied by villous atrophy and epithelial degeneration. These findings provide new insights into the genetic diversity and evolution of PoRVA and further characterize the pathogenicity of the G4P[13] QY strain in neonatal piglets.
title: A G4P[13] Porcine Rotavirus a Strain with Genomic Features Suggestive of Reassortment: Isolation, Genomic Characterization, and Pathogenicity in Piglets.

text: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major threat to global health. The protective efficacy of the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin vaccine is limited because of the absence of multiple virulence-related genomic regions in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB). The surface proteins of MTB are closely associated with bacterial invasiveness and pathogenicity, representing promising targets for novel vaccine development. In the present study, the MTB polymorphic GC-rich sequence proteins (Pro-Glu and Pro-Pro-Glu-Pro-Arg-Gly-Ser) family fusion protein Rv1768-Rv1983 was cloned, expressed and encapsulated into mannosylated chitosan (MCS) to construct MCS-Rv1768Rv1983 nanoparticles. The immunological and protective effects of this nanoformulation were evaluated in vitro and in a mouse model.
title: Targeted inhibition of <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> invasion into macrophages by Rv1768-Rv1983-loaded mannosylated chitosan nanoparticles.

text: Physicochemical characterization revealed that the nanoparticles had a mean particle size of 196.3 nm and a drug loading efficiency of 8.02%. In vitro cell experiments demonstrated that MCS-Rv1768-Rv1983 exhibited no obvious cytotoxicity and stimulated CD4 + T cells to secrete IFN-γ and IL-4, as well as CD8 + T cells, to produce IFN-γ. Animal experiments revealed that immunization with MCS-Rv1768-Rv1983 markedly elevated serum IgG1 and IgG2a titres and that the induced antibodies significantly reduced the invasion of virulent MTB H37Rv into macrophages. After H37Rv challenge, compared with the control group, the MCS-Rv1768-Rv1983 immunization group exhibited significantly lower bacterial loads in mouse lungs and markedly longer survival times.
title: Targeted inhibition of <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> invasion into macrophages by Rv1768-Rv1983-loaded mannosylated chitosan nanoparticles.

text: These results confirm that MCS nanoparticles can increase the immune efficacy of the Rv1768-Rv1983 fusion protein, block MTB invasion into macrophages and may contribute to the early clearance of MTB by macrophages.
title: Targeted inhibition of <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> invasion into macrophages by Rv1768-Rv1983-loaded mannosylated chitosan nanoparticles.

text: Feline panleukopenia virus (FPV) causes feline panleukopenia (FP), a highly contagious and often fatal disease in domestic cats. This study investigated FPV detection, associated epidemiological factors, and partial VP2 genetic characteristics among clinically suspected cats presented in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. Exploratory molecular docking was also performed to compare predicted VP2-transferrin receptor type-1 interactions in feline and canine systems. FPV DNA was detected in 83 of 180 clinically suspected cats (46.11%). Multivariable analysis revealed higher odds of FPV PCR positivity in female cats than in male cats (aOR: 2.65; 95% CI: 1.35-5.21) and lower odds in vaccinated cats than in unvaccinated cats (aOR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.17-0.97).
title: Molecular Epidemiology and Genetic Characterization of Feline Panleukopenia Virus among Clinically Suspected Domestic Cats in Tamil Nadu, India.

text: Compared with summer, higher odds were observed during the southwest monsoon (aOR: 3.59; 95% CI: 1.26-10.20) and northeast monsoon (aOR: 17.11; 95% CI: 3.86-75.80), whereas age group and breed were not significantly associated with PCR positivity. FPV was successfully isolated from four of the ten PCR-positive clinical samples inoculated onto CRFK cells. Partial VP2 sequencing of 13 PCR-positive samples showed 98.1-98.5% nucleotide identity with the vaccine reference strain and identified several nucleotide and amino acid substitutions. Most study sequences clustered with Indian FPV reference strains, whereas one sequence clustered separately within the carnivore parvovirus grouping.
title: Molecular Epidemiology and Genetic Characterization of Feline Panleukopenia Virus among Clinically Suspected Domestic Cats in Tamil Nadu, India.

text: Molecular docking of the (TfR1-VP2 interaction identified differences in the predicted interaction patterns between feline and canine complexes, with the feline complex exhibiting a more favourable ZRANK score. However, these findings represent computational predictions and require experimental validation. Overall, the study highlights the circulation of genetically diverse FPV strains in southern India and underscores the importance of continued surveillance and molecular characterization to support disease monitoring and control strategies.
title: Molecular Epidemiology and Genetic Characterization of Feline Panleukopenia Virus among Clinically Suspected Domestic Cats in Tamil Nadu, India.

text: Glycolic acid (GA) is an important platform chemical with applications in biodegradable polymers, cosmetics, and pharmaceutical synthesis; however, traditional petrochemical routes raise environmental concerns, and current microbial production platforms remain constrained by acid toxicity. In this study, systematic metabolic engineering combined with fermentation optimization was implemented to construct an efficient GA biosynthetic pathway in the acid-tolerant non-conventional yeast Issatchenkia orientalis . To redirect the metabolic flux of the glyoxylate cycle, the Arabidopsis thaliana glyoxylate reductase ( At GLYR), with a catalytic efficiency approximately 74-fold higher than that of the native yeast enzyme, was heterologously expressed, coupled with the overexpression of endogenous isocitrate lyase (ICL) and the knockout of the competing malate synthase (MLS) gene.
title: Xylose-Assisted Glycolic Acid Overproduction in Engineered <i>Issatchenkia orientalis</i>.

text: Furthermore, a heterologous xylose assimilation pathway was integrated into the engineered strain to rescue the growth deficiency caused by mls deletion. Subsequent fermentation optimization via an ethanol-xylose co-feeding strategy and calcium carbonate supplementation effectively further improved GA accumulation. Ultimately, the optimized engineered strain yielded a maximum GA titer of 712.42 mg/L in shake-flask fermentation. This work validates the potential of I . orientalis as a robust chassis microbe for sustainable GA biosynthesis and broadens the product portfolio of metabolic engineering applications for this yeast strain.
title: Xylose-Assisted Glycolic Acid Overproduction in Engineered <i>Issatchenkia orientalis</i>.

text: Giardia duodenalis , a member of the genus Giardia , is a common intestinal protozoan parasite in humans and some farm, companion, and wild animals. Due to the uniform morphology of the parasites sampled from a wide range of hosts, the taxonomy of the genus Giardia has been the subject of debate for more than a century. The confusion generated by this controversy, and the technological limitations to carry out the necessary research to clarify the matter, led to an insufficient understanding of the epidemiology of the infection, mainly in aspects related to host specificity and zoonotic transmission. The results of molecular and epidemiological studies conducted over the last four decades, which are reviewed in this paper, allow us to conclude that zoonotic transmission of Giardia duodenalis infection is possible.
title: Regarding the Zoonotic Transmission of <i>Giardia duodenalis</i> Infection.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Concurrently, these findings suggest that most Giardia infections are host-specific, rendering zoonotic transmission relatively uncommon. Nevertheless, from a public health perspective, such transmission remains a critical concern for vulnerable groups, particularly children and immunocompromised individuals. In these populations, even infrequent zoonotic events can lead to severe clinical outcomes, including chronic diarrhea, malabsorption, and failure to thrive.
title: Regarding the Zoonotic Transmission of <i>Giardia duodenalis</i> Infection.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: This case demonstrates the successful application of a cruciate suture pattern using silk suture for umbilical hernia repair in a ram. A one-year-old local breed ram was presented to the Professor Feseha Gebreab Memorial Veterinary Teaching Hospital, Addis Ababa University, Ethiopia, with a progressively enlarging umbilical swelling. Clinical examination revealed a non-painful, large umbilical hernia, for which the ram was admitted for surgical repair. Herniorrhaphy was conducted after circular infiltration of 2% lidocaine. The hernial sac was opened through a longitudinal incision cranial to the prepuce, and the herniated omentum and intestine were reduced. The hernial ring was closed using a cruciate suture pattern with size 2 silk. Postoperatively, Penicillin-streptomycin and meloxicam were administered for three consecutive days. Recovery was uneventful, with complete healing.
title: Umbilical Hernia in a Ram and Its Successful Surgical Repair.

text: The outcome suggests this technique is a viable and effective suture pattern for hernias of similar size, in addition to timely diagnosis, accurate surgical execution, and diligent postoperative care.
title: Umbilical Hernia in a Ram and Its Successful Surgical Repair.

text: Kaempferol-enriched Sophora Fructus extract is a promising plant-derived antioxidant feed additive. However, its effects on growth performance and antioxidant capacity in weaned piglets remain poorly documented. This study aimed to investigate whether dietary supplementation with kaempferol-enriched Sophora Fructus extract improves growth performance and antioxidant status in weaned piglets, and further to explore the underlying mechanism using PK-15 cell oxidative-stress model. Twelve weaned piglets (5.14 ± 0.24 kg) were randomly assigned to either a control group (basal diet) or a treatment group (basal diet +400 mg/kg kaempferol-enriched Sophora Fructus extract) for a 35-day feeding trial. To clarify whether kaempferol exerts antioxidant function via the Nrf2 signaling pathway, an H 2 O 2 -induced oxidative stress model was established in PK-15 cells.
title: Activation of the Nrf2 Signaling Pathway by Kaempferol Enhances Growth Performance and Antioxidant Capacity in Piglets.

text: Adding 400 mg/kg kaempferol-enriched Sophora Fructus extract to the diet significantly improved growth performance by increasing body weight on Day 35 ( p p p p 2 O 2 -induced oxidative damage in PK-15 cells. It activated the Nrf2 signaling pathway by promoting Nrf2 nuclear translocation and upregulating downstream antioxidant genes, including HO-1 and NAD (PH) quinone dehydrogenase 1 (NQO1). Moreover, such protective effects were abrogated by the Nrf2-specific inhibitor ML385. Collectively, these results indicate dietary supplementation with 400 mg/kg kaempferol-enriched Sophora Fructus extract has the potential to improve growth performance and antioxidant capacity in weaned piglets. In vitro, kaempferol confers protection against H 2 O 2 -induced oxidative stress in PK-15 cells mainly by activating the Nrf2 signaling pathway.
title: Activation of the Nrf2 Signaling Pathway by Kaempferol Enhances Growth Performance and Antioxidant Capacity in Piglets.

text: Agarikon (Laricifomes officinalis syn. Fomitopsis officinalis) is an endangered fungus belonging to a unique lineage in the Polyporales (Basidiomycota) with a growing body of evidence supporting its medicinal value. In this study, we report the hybrid de novo assembly and annotation of the nuclear and mitochondrial genomes of L. officinalis, with a nuclear genome size of 28.76 Mb assembled across 66 contigs (51.96% GC content; BUSCO completeness of 99.4%) and a complete core mitochondrial genome size of 197.67 kb. Structural and functional annotation of the nuclear genome yielded 8,717 predicted genes including 8,604 protein-coding genes, with 287 genes in 27 candidate biosynthetic gene clusters.
title: Genomic characterization of the endangered medicinal polypore agarikon (Laricifomes officinalis syn. Fomitopsis officinalis).

text: We characterized the mating type loci matA and matB, consistent with a tetrapolar mating system, and identified genes encoding key enzymes involved in triterpenoid and polyketide biosynthetic pathways that lead to the production of a diverse array of secondary metabolites. Additionally, we conducted maximum likelihood phylogenomic analysis to confirm the taxonomic position of L. officinalis among other species in the Polyporales using protein sequences for 730 shared BUSCO genes. This high-quality annotated genome of L. officinalis will serve as a foundation for further investigations into its evolutionary history, provide a reference for future population genomic analyses, and elucidate mechanisms underlying the synthesis of the bioactive compounds responsible for agarikon's wide-ranging medicinal benefits.
title: Genomic characterization of the endangered medicinal polypore agarikon (Laricifomes officinalis syn. Fomitopsis officinalis).

text: The use of ionophore coccidiostats-salinomycin (SAL), lasalocid (LAS), monensin (MON), and narasin (NAR)-in animal production raises toxicity concerns in non-target species through feed contamination and because of their narrow safety margins. Cannabidiol (CBD) has antioxidant and cytoprotective properties that may modify the cellular response to ionophore-induced toxicity. This study examined the effect of CBD on the cytotoxicity of SAL, LAS, MON, and NAR in feline (CRFK) and canine (MDCK) kidney cells. Cells were exposed for 72 h to each coccidiostat, alone or in combination with CBD, and assessed using mitochondrial activity (MTT), lysosomal activity (NRU), total protein content (TPC), and membrane integrity (LDH) assays; the interaction was evaluated by isobolographic analysis.
title: Cytotoxic Interactions Between Cannabidiol and Ionophore Coccidiostats in Feline and Canine Kidney Cell Lines-An In Vitro Study.

text: Molecular docking of CBD and the ionophores to human VDAC1 (PDB 6TIQ) was performed in AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, both individually and in simultaneous multi-ligand combinations, with β-NADH, VBIT-4, and SW016789 as reference ligands. All four ionophores induced concentration-dependent cytotoxicity, with distinct, compound- and species-specific profiles between CRFK and MDCK cells. CBD co-exposure produced divergent interactions depending on the drug and cell model, ranging from marked cytoprotection to pronounced synergistic potentiation of toxicity, most notably for SAL and LAS in canine cells. The ionophores occupied the N-terminal helix, and cannabidiol occupied a partially overlapping C-terminal region, from which β-NADH displaced it, suggesting a plausible structural basis for the observed interactions.
title: Cytotoxic Interactions Between Cannabidiol and Ionophore Coccidiostats in Feline and Canine Kidney Cell Lines-An In Vitro Study.

text: These findings indicate that ionophore nephrotoxic potential and its modulation by CBD are both concentration- and species-dependent, warranting further investigation using additional in vitro and in vivo models.
title: Cytotoxic Interactions Between Cannabidiol and Ionophore Coccidiostats in Feline and Canine Kidney Cell Lines-An In Vitro Study.

text: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains highly lethal due to aggressive metastasis and profound immunosuppression by regulatory T cells (Tregs). Here, we present a biomimetic liquid metal (LM)-based photothermal immunotherapeutic nanoplatform exploiting gallium-based LMs to orchestrate cascade amplification of antitumor immunity. The engineered nanoplatform (B-LM-DMX-αCD25) integrates an LM photothermal core with dual immunomodulatory components-anti-CD25 antibody for Treg depletion and stimulator of interferon genes (STING) agonist 5,6-dimethylxanthenone-4-acetic acid (DMX) for innate immune activation-while blood-derived camouflaging enhances immune evasion and tumor accumulation. Quantitative RT-PCR of 13 immune-related genes confirmed STING engagement, robust CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell infiltration, and Treg depletion in treated tumors.
title: Blood Cell-Camouflaged Liquid Metal Nanoconjugates Orchestrate Treg Depletion and STING-Amplified Photothermal Immunity for Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Therapy.

text: This platform operates through three synchronized mechanisms: (1) selective intratumoral Treg depletion dismantling immunosuppression; (2) near-infrared-triggered LM-mediated photothermal therapy (58°C within 5 min) inducing immunogenic cell death and releasing tumor-associated antigens; and (3) STING pathway activation promoting dendritic cell maturation and tumor-specific cytotoxic T-cell responses, collectively transforming immunologically "cold" TNBC into immune-responsive tumors. In orthotopic 4T1 models, the nanoplatform achieves significant tumor regression with enhanced survival, while in metastatic models, it reduces pulmonary metastatic nodules and extends median survival beyond 70 days.
title: Blood Cell-Camouflaged Liquid Metal Nanoconjugates Orchestrate Treg Depletion and STING-Amplified Photothermal Immunity for Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Therapy.

text: This work establishes a paradigm-shifting biomimetic LM-based nanodelivery strategy addressing fundamental immunological barriers in TNBC through coordinated photothermal-immunotherapy, offering a clinically translatable approach for TNBC.
title: Blood Cell-Camouflaged Liquid Metal Nanoconjugates Orchestrate Treg Depletion and STING-Amplified Photothermal Immunity for Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Therapy.

text: Macrorhabdosis is a contagious fungal gastrointestinal disease of birds, that predominantly affecs the proventriculus of budgerigars (Melopsittacus undulatus). Although the pathological features of Macrorhabdus ornithogaster infection have been extensively described, information regarding local inflammatory cytokine responses in naturally infected birds remains limited. In the present study, archival gastrointestinal tissues obtained from 25 budgerigars naturally infected with M. ornithogaster and 5 non-infected controls were evaluated histopathologically and immunohistochemically. Routine histopathology was performed to characterize tissue lesions, while immunohistochemistry was used to evaluate tissue expression of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α).
title: Immunohistochemical localization of tumor necrosis factor-α in gastrointestinal tissues of budgerigars naturally infected with Macrorhabdus ornithogaster.

text: Histological lesions were predominantly localized to the proventriculus and consisted of mucosal erosion, ulceration, epithelial degeneration, and inflammatory cell infiltration associated with abundant fungal organisms. PAS and Gomori methenamine silver staining confirmed the presence and distribution of fungal elements within affected tissues. TNF-α immunoreactivity was detected mainly in epithelial and inflammatory cells within lesion affected areas, whereas control tissues exhibited minimal or no immunostaining. These findings demonstrate localized TNF-α expression in gastrointestinal tissues affected by M. ornithogaster infection and support the presence of an active TNF-α inflammatory response associated with macrorhabdosis.
title: Immunohistochemical localization of tumor necrosis factor-α in gastrointestinal tissues of budgerigars naturally infected with Macrorhabdus ornithogaster.

text: This study provides a descriptive baseline data for future quantitative and functional investigations evaluating cytokine-mediated mechanisms in avian fungal gastrointestinal disease.
title: Immunohistochemical localization of tumor necrosis factor-α in gastrointestinal tissues of budgerigars naturally infected with Macrorhabdus ornithogaster.

text: Background Paroxysmal dyskinesia (PD) is an episodic movement disorder in dogs. Gluten-sensitive etiology has been suggested, but prospective studies in different breeds are lacking. Hypothesis/objectives Investigate whether a gluten-free hydrolyzed diet (GFHD) decreases PD episode frequency and gastrointestinal (GI) signs, and evaluate associations with serum anti-gliadin peptide immunoglobulin G (AGA IgG) and anti-transglutaminase-2 immunoglobulin A (TG-2 IgA) titers. Animals Twenty-three client-owned dogs with PD. Methods Prospective cohort study with 3 time points: baseline (T0), 90 days (T1), and 180 days (T2). Dogs were fed a GFHD. Episode frequency, GI signs and AGA IgG and TG-2 IgA titers were assessed at each time point.
title: Effects of a gluten-free hydrolyzed diet in dogs with paroxysmal dyskinesia: a prospective cohort study.

text: Response to GFHD was classified as excellent (episode disappearance), good (≥50% decrease), fairly good ( Results Median number of episodes decreased from 6 (range, 2-60) at T0 to 2 (range, 0-10) at T2 (P = .0003). At T2, 17/23 dogs were responders (5 excellent, 12 good). Gastrointestinal signs were present in 15/23 dogs at T0 and in 6/23 dogs at T2, with significant decreases in vomiting and diarrhea (P = .01). No significant correlation was found between episode frequency and AGA IgG or TG-2 IgA titers at any time point (P > .1). Antibody results did not significantly change between T0 and T2. Conclusions and clinical importance The GFHD was associated with a significant decrease in PD frequency and GI signs in most dogs. The AGA IgG and TG-2 IgA titers were not predictive of dietary response, suggesting limited value as biomarkers.
title: Effects of a gluten-free hydrolyzed diet in dogs with paroxysmal dyskinesia: a prospective cohort study.

text: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide and is the principal cause of death in low- and middle-income countries. Although cardiovascular outcome trials have established the benefits of Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) in reducing major adverse cardiovascular events, the translation of this evidence into routine clinical practice in Central Asia remains limited and underexplored. Specifically, in Kazakhstan, despite measurable improvements in cardiac infrastructure over the past decade, critical gaps persist in early diagnosis, cardiometabolic risk stratification, and the integration of newer pharmacological strategies into routine practice. In this review, we aim to evaluate the potential role of GLP-1-based therapies within the current cardiovascular prevention landscape in Kazakhstan.
title: GLP-1-Based Therapies for Cardiovascular Risk Reduction in Kazakhstan: Evidence, Affordability, Equity and Implementation Considerations.

text: It also synthesizes current mechanistic evidence and findings from major clinical trials supporting the use of GLP-1RAs as cardiometabolic agents with potential cardiovascular benefits. Furthermore, we examine the practical factors that may influence their adoption within Kazakhstan's health system, including accessibility, affordability, clinician preparedness, prescribing capacity, regulatory considerations, and policy integration. By integrating evidence from cardiovascular outcome trials, clinical studies, and health-system perspectives, this review seeks to provide a balanced assessment of the potential contribution of GLP-1-based therapies to cardiovascular risk reduction in Kazakhstan while identifying priorities for future research, implementation strategies, and health policy development.
title: GLP-1-Based Therapies for Cardiovascular Risk Reduction in Kazakhstan: Evidence, Affordability, Equity and Implementation Considerations.

text: Context Fridericia chica (Bonpl.) L.G. Lohmann is a medicinal plant rich in bioactive 3-deoxyanthocyanidins with reported wound-healing and gastroprotective properties. A 70% tocotrienol-enriched fraction (TRF) from Bixa orellana L. exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities that may complement those of F. chica in gastric mucosal protection. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the gastroprotective and gastric tissue-repair effects of the F. chica -TRF combination. Materials and methods Dry F. chica standardized crude extract alone or combined with TRF at different proportions was tested in vitro in HaCaT keratinocytes and 3T3 fibroblasts to assess cell viability and select a suitable combination ratio for subsequent in vivo investigation. The selected ratio was then investigated in acute and chronic gastric ulcer models in female Wistar rats.
title: <i>Fridericia chica</i> standardized extract combined with tocotrienol-enriched fraction from <i>Bixa orellana</i> promotes gastric mucosal protection: <i>in vitro</i> combination selection and <i>in vivo</i> evaluation.

text: Results Among the proportions tested in vitro , the 90:10 ( F. chica :TRF) ratio showed the most favorable cell-viability profile and was selected for in vivo evaluation. The combination reduced gastric lesions and significantly increased gastric mucus production. In the chronic ulcer model, treatment was associated with reduced TNF- α and IL-1 β levels and increased IL-10 levels. Histopathological and second-harmonic generation analyses qualitatively indicated mucosal preservation, tissue organization, and collagen deposition. Conclusions The F. chica -TRF combination exhibited gastroprotective effects associated with increased mucus production and modulation of inflammatory mediators.
title: <i>Fridericia chica</i> standardized extract combined with tocotrienol-enriched fraction from <i>Bixa orellana</i> promotes gastric mucosal protection: <i>in vitro</i> combination selection and <i>in vivo</i> evaluation.

text: Qualitative morphological findings further indicated preservation of gastric tissue architecture and collagen organization, supporting the potential of this combination as a natural product-based approach to gastric mucosal protection.
title: <i>Fridericia chica</i> standardized extract combined with tocotrienol-enriched fraction from <i>Bixa orellana</i> promotes gastric mucosal protection: <i>in vitro</i> combination selection and <i>in vivo</i> evaluation.

text: Obesity is a major risk factor for insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. Adipocyte stress responses can either promote metabolic dysfunction or preserve insulin action, but the contribution of the p38 MAPK activator MKK3 to adipose tissue physiology remains poorly understood. Here, we show that adipose MKK3 expression increases early during high-fat feeding and is also elevated in human obesity. In human visceral adipose tissue, MKK3 expression was positively associated with body mass index and leptin and inversely associated with HbA1c in unadjusted analyses. Using germline, Fabp4-Cre, and Adipo-Cre Mkk3-deficient mice, together with p38β-deficient mice and primary adipocytes, we found that loss of adipocyte MKK3 impairs insulin responsiveness.
title: An Adipocyte MKK3-p38β Axis Preserves Insulin Responsiveness in Mice and Is Reciprocally Altered in Human Obesity.

text: Adipo-Cre;Mkk3 fl/fl (Adipo Mkk3 ) mice displayed reduced insulin-stimulated glucose uptake selectively in subcutaneous white adipose tissue despite unchanged body composition and basal brown adipose tissue activity. Mechanistically, MKK3 or p38β deficiency increased p70S6K activity and inhibitory IRS1 Ser307 phosphorylation, reduced GLUT4 translocation and Akt activation, and these defects were partially rescued by rapamycin or the selective p70S6K inhibitor PF-4708671. Together, these findings identify an adipocyte MKK3-p38β-p70S6K axis that helps preserve insulin signaling during nutritional stress.
title: An Adipocyte MKK3-p38β Axis Preserves Insulin Responsiveness in Mice and Is Reciprocally Altered in Human Obesity.

text: Background Conventional triage relies on clinician judgment and limited information available at first contact. AI and machine learning (ML) may improve early risk stratification, whereas tele-triage and patient-facing tools primarily support remote assessment, access, and care routing. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic performance of AI- and ML-assisted triage systems and summarize evidence on tele-triage, workflow, implementation, economic, and equity outcomes. Methods Comparative studies published between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025, evaluating AI-, ML-, natural language processing-, telehealth-, or digitally enhanced triage. At first, clinical contacts were included. PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus, preprint servers, trial registries, and conference proceedings were searched.
title: Technological Integration in Triage With AI and Machine Learning Compared With Conventional Triage and Narrative Synthesis of Telehealth for Patient Prioritization in Emergency and Acute Care Settings: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: Screening and data extraction were performed independently in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools. Clinically comparable area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) estimates were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis; heterogeneous diagnostic, operational, implementation, economic, and equity outcomes were summarized narratively. Exploratory scenario modeling projected effects per 10,000 emergency department (ED) visits. Results Twenty-seven studies were included, comprising 13 studies in the quantitative evidence stream and 14 in the narrative synthesis. Four adult ED studies evaluating critical care or deterioration outcomes demonstrated high pooled discrimination for AI-assisted triage (AUC 0.874; 95% CI 0.845-0.898; I ²=94.4%; 95% prediction interval 0.803-0.922).
title: Technological Integration in Triage With AI and Machine Learning Compared With Conventional Triage and Narrative Synthesis of Telehealth for Patient Prioritization in Emergency and Acute Care Settings: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: Four studies reported directly extractable within-study comparisons favoring AI-assisted models (AUC differences of 0.097, 0.120, 0.108, and 0.065), although these could not be pooled because paired variance estimates were unavailable. Admission/disposition studies reported AI-model AUCs ranging from 0.80 to 0.93 and were summarized descriptively because extreme heterogeneity precluded meaningful pooling. Two pediatric studies (AUCs of 0.85-0.99) were summarized descriptively. Prediction-model studies were primarily limited by deficiencies in model analysis, calibration reporting, and external validation.
title: Technological Integration in Triage With AI and Machine Learning Compared With Conventional Triage and Narrative Synthesis of Telehealth for Patient Prioritization in Emergency and Acute Care Settings: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: Narrative evidence suggested improved front-door operational metrics with tele-triage, including reported reductions of 15%-40% in time to clinical assessment and 2-8 percentage points in left-without-being-seen rates, whereas patient-facing symptom checkers generally favored sensitivity over specificity. Exploratory scenario modeling illustrated that, under specified prevalence and threshold assumptions, AI-assisted triage could be associated with 12-38 fewer missed critical illness cases and 45-120 additional false-positive escalations per 10,000 ED visits. Economic and equity findings were assumption-dependent projections rather than observed clinical, cost-effectiveness, or equity outcomes.
title: Technological Integration in Triage With AI and Machine Learning Compared With Conventional Triage and Narrative Synthesis of Telehealth for Patient Prioritization in Emergency and Acute Care Settings: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: Conclusions AI- and ML-assisted triage models demonstrate promising discrimination for adult ED risk stratification; however, AUC-based discrimination does not establish superiority at clinically relevant decision thresholds, improved patient outcomes, or readiness for clinical implementation. Interpretation is limited by substantial heterogeneity, incomplete threshold-level performance and calibration reporting, limited external validation, and sparse pediatric evidence. Prospective multicenter validation, workflow assessment, subgroup calibration and equity auditing, and formal economic evaluation are required before routine implementation.
title: Technological Integration in Triage With AI and Machine Learning Compared With Conventional Triage and Narrative Synthesis of Telehealth for Patient Prioritization in Emergency and Acute Care Settings: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly explored in veterinary neurology for pattern recognition, prediction and clinical decision support, with relevance to comparative and translational neuroscience. Objectives This review examines AI applications in veterinary neurology, compares them with human neurology and evaluates cross-species technology transfer within a One Health framework. Methods A narrative review synthesized evidence across AI domains in veterinary neurology, including neuroimaging and radiomics, electrophysiology and seizure detection or forecasting, gait and pain assessment, morphometric biomarker discovery, prognostic modelling and laboratory diagnostic tools. Human studies were considered to identify translational opportunities, methodological challenges and the value of transfer learning and domain adaptation.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Veterinary Neurology: Comparative Insights From Human Medicine and Cross-Species Technology Transfer.

text: Results Available evidence suggests that AI holds promise for pattern recognition, prediction and decision support in veterinary neurology. Reported applications include canine brain tumour classification, spinal lesion grading, seizure monitoring and quantitative gait analysis, with encouraging performance. However, most applications remain proof-of-concept. The evidence base is dominated by retrospective single-centre studies with small samples, heterogeneous protocols and limited prospective or external validation. Model calibration, uncertainty reporting and clinically relevant error trade-offs are often insufficiently addressed. Transfer learning and domain adaptation may help overcome limited veterinary datasets, while naturally occurring neurological disease in dogs may also support refinement of human AI systems.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Veterinary Neurology: Comparative Insights From Human Medicine and Cross-Species Technology Transfer.

text: Conclusions AI in veterinary neurology is a promising but early field. Future progress will require multi-centre collaboration, standardized data practices, explainable and ethically governed models and stronger One Health partnerships to support safe translation.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Veterinary Neurology: Comparative Insights From Human Medicine and Cross-Species Technology Transfer.

text: The frequency of spontaneous lymphatic contractions is exquisitely sensitive to changes in intraluminal pressure, enabling lymph transport to be matched to the filling state of the lymphatic capillary network. The mechanistic basis of this mechanosensitive response was investigated using ex vivo contraction assays of mouse popliteal collecting vessels.
