Skin physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models mechanistically characterize the percutaneous absorption process, predict local and systemic exposure, and enhance research and development efficiency through virtual clinical trials. This paper first elaborates on the theoretical foundation of skin PBPK modeling based on Fick's second law of diffusion and compares the model assumptions and application scenarios of four well-established and validated modeling platforms: Simcyp, GastroPlus, Skin-CAD, and PK-Sim. The findings indicate that Simcyp provides a refined depiction of skin physiological structure and is widely applied in clinical evaluation and special population prediction.
title: Skin physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling: current research progress, software comparison, and future perspectives.

text: GastroPlus focuses more on the mechanistic description of TDS formulations. Skin-CAD, as a specialized software, is extensively utilized for in vitro-in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) predictions and formulation optimization. PK-Sim, as a freely accessible open-source software, has been used to investigate the physiological ontogeny of skin in pediatric populations. However, existing studies share limitations such as highly inconsistent model structures with varying complexity, challenges in acquiring accurate parameters, and a scarcity of physiological information for special populations. Future research should prioritize optimizing parameter acquisition methods and broadening physiological databases for pediatric, geriatric, and skin-lesion populations.
title: Skin physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling: current research progress, software comparison, and future perspectives.

text: Additionally, integrating non-invasive imaging technologies to construct high-precision 'digital twin' skin models represents a critical future direction. These advancements will drive the transition of PBPK models from descriptive tools to supportive instruments for individualized dosing and regulatory decision-making.
title: Skin physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling: current research progress, software comparison, and future perspectives.

text: Partial bladder outlet obstruction (pBOO) is a fibroproliferative disorder that results in poorly compliant, high-pressure bladders due to lower urinary tract occlusion. The mechanisms governing pBOO-induced bladder remodeling remain poorly understood. The goals of the present study were to profile global and region-specific transcriptomes of porcine bladders in response to pBOO using RNA sequencing and to identify genes and pathways differentially affected in the bladder dome and trigone by obstructive injury. Nine adult female Yucatan mini-swine were randomized and divided into either nonsurgical controls (n = 5) or those subjected to pBOO for 4 weeks (n = 4). Post-pBOO swine demonstrated bladder smooth muscle hypertrophy as well as significant declines in bladder capacity (35% ± 7% of baseline) and compliance (38% ± 10% of baseline).
title: Characterization of global and region-specific transcriptomic alterations in the bladder following acute partial bladder outlet obstruction in female mini-swine.

text: The global transcriptome of obstructed bladders revealed enrichment of processes related to loss of urothelial barrier function, immune activation, cell cycle regulation, extracellular matrix organization, and signal transduction similar to human and rodent evaluations of pBOO. Moreover, our data also showed that adaptive responses to pBOO are regionally dependent rather than globally uniform, with zonal-specific divergence observed across hypoxic, fibrotic, metabolic, and neuronal pathways between the obstructed dome and trigone. These results highlight the regional heterogeneity of bladder responses to obstructive urologic disease.
title: Characterization of global and region-specific transcriptomic alterations in the bladder following acute partial bladder outlet obstruction in female mini-swine.

text: In December 2025, an H6N2 avian influenza virus (A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025, NL04) was isolated from a chicken outbreak in Henan, China with 15% field mortality and severe respiratory disease. Genome sequencing confirmed it is a novel reassortant possessing a waterfowl‑origin H6‑derived HA, H9N2‑derived NA, and the complete internal‑gene cassette of the H9N2 G57 genotype. Although NL04 caused only mild clinical disease and 100% survival in experimentally infected specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens, prominent respiratory‑tract histopathological damage was observed, revealing a marked phenotypic discrepancy between laboratory outcomes and severe field‑reported mortality that is likely driven by complex commercial‑farm risk factors. Tissue viral loads in SPF chickens peaked in nasal turbinates and the Harderian gland, confirming its predominant respiratory tropism.
title: Characterization and vaccine-induced immunity of a novel H6N2 avian influenza reassortant virus with H9N2-derived NA and internal genes from poultry in Henan, China.

text: In BALB/c mice, NL04 exhibited limited nasal replication, indicating low mammalian‑adaptation potential. We further evaluated an inactivated vaccine candidate based on NL04. The vaccine induced robust humoral immunity, reduced viral shedding after homologous challenge, and elicited cross‑neutralizing antibodies against a heterologous H6N1 isolate. Our findings highlight the veterinary relevance of this unique H6N2 reassortant and stress the value of continuous genomic surveillance among poultry to prevent emerging avian‑influenza threats.
title: Characterization and vaccine-induced immunity of a novel H6N2 avian influenza reassortant virus with H9N2-derived NA and internal genes from poultry in Henan, China.

text: Diabetic foot ulcers are a major complication of diabetes characterized by persistent inflammation and impaired tissue repair, in part driven by aberrant activation of the cGAS-STING innate immune pathway. Precision immunomodulation in the protease-rich wound microenvironment remains challenging because therapeutic efficacy requires both localized retention and responsiveness to pathological cues. Here, we developed an integrated AI-to-biomaterial strategy for diabetic wound repair by coupling generative AI-guided peptide discovery with microenvironment-responsive local delivery. A structure-guided deep-learning pipeline integrating RFDiffusion, ProteinMPNN, and AlphaFold2-multimer identified SCP-1, a conformation-locking peptide designed to stabilize the inactive STING dimer.
title: AI Designed Conformation Locking Peptides Target STING to Restore Diabetic Wound Healing.

text: To enable therapeutic translation, SCP-1 was incorporated into a dual-responsive hydrogel (Gel-SCP-1) that provides in situ gelation and MMP-9-triggered release in the wound bed. Gel-SCP-1 suppressed STING-TBK1-IRF3 signaling, reduced inflammatory and oxidative stress, promoted reparative macrophage polarization, and enhanced angiogenic activity. In a full-thickness excisional wound model in db/db diabetic mice, Gel-SCP-1 significantly accelerated wound closure and improved tissue regeneration, including enhanced re-epithelialization and collagen remodeling. These findings establish an AI-to-biomaterial therapeutic paradigm for precision immunoregenerative therapy in chronic diabetic wounds.
title: AI Designed Conformation Locking Peptides Target STING to Restore Diabetic Wound Healing.

text: Histaglobulin (histamine/immunoglobulin complex) has been used for decades as a non-allergen-specific immunotherapy for allergic diseases including allergic rhinitis, chronic urticaria, and atopic dermatitis. Despite growing clinical interest, no meta-analysis has synthesized the available evidence. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of histaglobulin across allergic diseases, with particular emphasis on implications for allergic rhinitis management. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies evaluating subcutaneous histaglobulin in patients with allergic diseases were included. For chronic urticaria studies reporting Urticaria Activity Score (UAS) as mean ± standard deviation, a random-effects meta-analysis was performed using the standardized mean difference (Hedges' g).
title: Efficacy of Histaglobulin in Allergic Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Implications for Allergic Rhinitis.

text: Allergic rhinitis studies were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Quality Assessment Tools. The protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO). Fourteen studies (N = 754) met the inclusion criteria: six chronic urticaria studies with quantitative data (N = 190), three allergic rhinitis studies (N = 165), two atopic dermatitis/chronic spontaneous urticaria case series (N = 8), and three chronic urticaria studies with incomplete data. Meta-analysis of six chronic urticaria studies, all of which used an uncontrolled before-after design, demonstrated a large pooled within-group effect size (Hedges' g = 2.82; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.75-3.88; p 2 = 98.2%). UAS reduction ranged from 44% to 89% across studies. Complete remission rates ranged from 30% to 89%.
title: Efficacy of Histaglobulin in Allergic Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Implications for Allergic Rhinitis.

text: Sensitivity analysis excluding one study with reporting concerns yielded consistent results (g = 2.34; 95% CI 1.83-2.85; I 2 = 90.2%). All three allergic rhinitis studies reported significant symptom improvement (response rates 57-90%) with normalization of serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) and eosinophil counts. No serious adverse events were identified within the available literature; however, the cumulative sample size (N = 754) remains insufficient to exclude rare or long-term adverse effects. Available evidence suggests that histaglobulin may reduce disease activity in chronic urticaria; because the pooled estimate derives predominantly from uncontrolled before-after studies with substantial heterogeneity, it reflects within-group improvement following treatment rather than a controlled estimate of treatment efficacy, and confidence in the effect remains limited.
title: Efficacy of Histaglobulin in Allergic Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Implications for Allergic Rhinitis.

text: Preliminary evidence suggests that histaglobulin may also provide benefit in patients with allergic rhinitis; however, the available data are limited and heterogeneous, and larger, well-designed controlled studies are needed to confirm its effectiveness. Well-designed randomized controlled trials are needed, particularly for allergic rhinitis, to establish histaglobulin's role in evidence-based otorhinolaryngology practice.
title: Efficacy of Histaglobulin in Allergic Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Implications for Allergic Rhinitis.

text: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses continue to expand their geographic and host range, raising concerns about zoonotic transmission and pandemic preparedness. Immunocompromised individuals often develop severe and prolonged disease, yet evidence guiding antiviral therapy remains limited. Here, we characterized the pathogenesis and assessed direct-contact transmission of an influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 virus recently isolated from a human case in British Columbia, Canada, in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters, with normal hamsters included for comparison of infection outcomes and viral shedding kinetics.
title: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters.

text: We also evaluated the antiviral efficacy of oseltamivir (20 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days), baloxavir (50 mg/kg, 2 doses), and molnupiravir (50 or 200 mg/kg twice daily) as monotherapies or in combination (oseltamivir with low-dose molnupiravir) in immunosuppressed hamsters. While normal hamsters showed no mortality and achieved viral clearance, infection in immunosuppressed hamsters caused severe disease characterized by prolonged viral replication, neuroinvasion, and 75% mortality, with no direct-contact transmission detected. In the antiviral efficacy experiment, placebo-treated hamsters exhibited 50% mortality. Baloxavir resulted in 100% survival, shortened viral shedding, reduced viral replication and pulmonary inflammatory responses, and prevented neuroinvasion. High-dose molnupiravir also prevented mortality and achieved viral clearance in lung and brain tissues.
title: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters.

text: Combination therapy resulted in 75% survival and similarly achieved viral clearance in both tissues, with reduced morbidity compared with oseltamivir and low-dose molnupiravir monotherapies. Oseltamivir resulted in 75% survival but failed to prevent severe clinical signs or reduce tissue viral titers, whereas low-dose molnupiravir showed outcomes comparable to placebo. These findings demonstrate the high pathogenicity of a human A(H5N1) isolate in immunosuppressed hamsters, support baloxavir as an effective therapeutic option, and identify molnupiravir-based regimens as promising strategies for severe influenza A(H5N1) infection.
title: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters.

text: Focused ultrasound (FUS) enables non-invasive, spatially precise modulation of biological tissues. This protocol describes assembly, calibration, and implementation of a diagnostic ultrasound-guided FUS (dUS-FUS) platform for real-time targeting of superficial and deep tissues in small-animal models. We demonstrate reversible sciatic nerve modulation in a rat acute pain model and assess sensory and motor functions using behavioral tests. The platform provides a reproducible workflow for image-guided tissue modulation and can be adapted to diverse preclinical applications. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Sangwan et al. 1 , 2 .
title: Image-guided focused ultrasound for non-invasive modulation of superficial and deep tissues.

text: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most devastating malignancies with high lethality despite the current therapeutic interventions. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) play important roles in many biological processes and disease development. However, the underlying mechanism remains largely unexplored. To identify novel druggable targets, we aimed to elucidate the mechanisms contributing to the critical roles of circRNAs in PDAC. We performed a genome-wide and multi-omics investigation on the circFOXK2-DNA interaction in PDAC progression. Single-cell ATAC-sequencing analysis using the publicly available dataset revealed the importance of the circFOXK2-DNA interaction network in intratumoral heterogeneity. Through circRNA-DNA interaction by complementary base pairing, circFOXK2 recognizes targets at different genomic locations: enhancer, promoter, and intragenic region.
title: Genome-Wide and Multi-Omics Analysis Identified DNA-Interacting Circular RNA circFOXK2 as MLL1 Regulator for Histone H3K4 Methylation in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.

text: CircFOXK2 forms a docking pocket by intramolecular base pairing for the N-terminal RNA-recognition motif of PPIE, disrupting the PPIE-MLL1 interaction. This removes the PPIE inhibitory effects on MLL1 for gene-activating H3K4 methylation. Specifically, circFOXK2 promotes TMSB15B and BCAS1 expressions by enhancing H3K4me3 at the promoter. At the gene body, circFOXK2 facilitates transcription elongation of TRIO and LAMA4 by intragenic H3K4me3. At the distal intergenic enhancer, circFOXK2 promotes H3K4me1 of CYP26A1 and TCP11 for gene activation. These results highlight the importance and therapeutic potential of circRNA-DNA interaction in gene regulation.
title: Genome-Wide and Multi-Omics Analysis Identified DNA-Interacting Circular RNA circFOXK2 as MLL1 Regulator for Histone H3K4 Methylation in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.

text: Previous studies suggest that genetic risk factors for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in Dobermann dogs may differ between populations, complicating the use of genetic tests across subpopulations. Variants in pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 (PDK4) and titin (TTN) have been associated with DCM in North American Dobermanns, whereas two loci on chromosome 5 involving Protein Kinase AMP-Activated Catalytic Subunit Alpha 2 (PRKAA2) and Ring Finger Protein 207 (RNF207) have been implicated in European populations. To assess the consistency of these signals across populations of Dobermanns, we harmonized and imputed genotype data from a Discovery cohort (n = 444) and a Replication cohort (n = 1771), and supplemented these with allele frequency data from a large diversity cohort (n = 3226) for cross-platform analyses.
title: A Large-Scale Cross-Population Evaluation of Genetic Risk Variants for Dilated Cardiomyopathy in Dobermanns.

text: We detected a shared association signal near RNF207 in affected dogs in both Europe and North America. In contrast, SNPs located in and near PDK4 and TTN variants showed no association with DCM in either population. These findings indicate that the RNF207 variant represents a shared genetic risk factor for DCM in Dobermanns across populations, and support the dog, particularly the Dobermann, as a relevant spontaneous model for RNF207-driven DCM. The previously reported associations between PDK4 and TTN variants and DCM were not replicated in the North American Dobermann population, nor in the European Dobermann populations. Also, these results highlight the need for population-specific validation and functional validation of identified variants where possible, before implementation of variants in genetic testing strategies.
title: A Large-Scale Cross-Population Evaluation of Genetic Risk Variants for Dilated Cardiomyopathy in Dobermanns.

text: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases have been widely exploited as targets for antiparasitic and antifungal inhibitors; however, they have received little attention as targets in multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria. Here we describe the biochemical characterisation of Prolyl-tRNA synthetase from Klebsiella pneumoniae (KpProRS), highlighting its ligase and proofreading activities. Distinct classes of ProRS inhibitors were evaluated against KpProRS but only halofuginone (HF) strongly modulated KpProRS activity. A new HF analog (Cpd-6) was developed and exhibited superior inhibitory activity against KpProRS relative to HF but low efficacy against MDR K. pneumoniae , despite good antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Further studies revealed that Cpd-6 resistance in K.
title: Inhibition of prolyl-tRNA synthetase and efflux pumps as a dual-targeting strategy against multidrug-resistant bacteria.
journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry

text: pneumonia is mainly mediated by AcrAB efflux pump activity, which could be counteracted by efflux pump inhibitors. These findings therefore reinforce KpProRS as a target for antimicrobial development and highlight the therapeutic potential of combining HF analogues with efflux pump inhibitors to fight Gram-negative MDR pathogens.
title: Inhibition of prolyl-tRNA synthetase and efflux pumps as a dual-targeting strategy against multidrug-resistant bacteria.
journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry

text: Emerging infectious diseases, driven by climate change, urbanization, and global wildlife trade, pose significant threats to public health, ecosystems, and biodiversity. The One Health (OH) approach, which emphasizes the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health, is critical to address these challenges. In this context, animal organoids have emerged as innovative in vitro models that can advance OH goals. Organoids are 3-dimensional (3D) structures that closely resemble the cellular composition, organization, and function of the organ they mimic. This review outlines the steps to establish organoid systems and provides an overview of the different animal organoid types developed to date and their contribution to OH.
title: Animal organoids as models for integrated One Health research.

text: We further explore the applications of these new approach methodologies in the context of OH in studying cross-species diseases, zoonotic infections, environmental pollutant, chemical biocides toxicity, antimicrobial resistance, animal breeding, and pandemic preparedness.
title: Animal organoids as models for integrated One Health research.

text: Persistent symptoms following the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection have emerged as an increasing health problem. The pathogenesis for the development of post-COVID Condition (PCC) is still elusive. Herein we included serum samples from non-hospitalized (n = 189) and hospitalized (n = 52) COVID-19 patients, representing approximately 90% of all patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in the municipality of Bergen, Norway between 28 February and 4 April 2020. The patients were followed clinically with systematic interviews for up to 18 months. Accompanying serum samples were analyzed by un-targeted proteomics and enzyme immunoassay (EIA). Our major findings were: (i) In a subpopulation of the total cohort (n = 69) proteome analyses identified 28 proteins that were dysregulated in individuals with mild and moderate PCC.
title: Serum proteomic profiling identifies transforming growth factor β receptor as a marker of persistent symptoms up to 18 months after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection.

text: Pathway analyses suggested the involvement of cell adhesion, extracellular matrix remodeling and immunity. (ii) The most significant finding were elevated serum levels of transforming growth factor β receptor 2 (TGFBR2) that were significantly higher in those with moderate as compared with those with mild and those without any PCC symptoms. (iii) This finding was conformed in the total cohort as assessed by EIA. (iv) The strongest association for TGFBR2 was found for impaired cognition that was seen at both 6, 12 and 18 months after infection. (v) In contrast to the home-isolated patients, no association of TGFBR2 to PCC symptoms were seen for those that were hospitalized during the acute infection. Our finding may indicate the involvement of TGFBR2 related pathways in the pathogenesis of PCC, in particular in those with cognitive symptoms.
title: Serum proteomic profiling identifies transforming growth factor β receptor as a marker of persistent symptoms up to 18 months after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection.

text: Lumpy skin disease (LSD) is a severe transboundary disease of cattle caused by lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV), which is highly transmissible and responsible for substantial economic losses worldwide. Although cellular immune responses are critical for controlling poxvirus infections, the viral strategies used by LSDV to evade cytotoxic T-cell immunity remain poorly understood. In this study, we demonstrate that LSDV infection markedly downregulates major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) surface expression in host cells. Screening of LSDV-encoded proteins identified LSDV003 as a key viral factor responsible for MHC-I downregulation. Mechanistically, LSDV003 interacts with both the MHC-I heavy chain and β2-microglobulin and mediates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) retention of MHC-I via a C-terminal HNEL motif, thereby preventing its transport to the cell surface.
title: The lumpy skin disease virus protein LSDV003 regulates MHC-I trafficking and surface expression.

text: Mutational analyses demonstrated that disruption of the HNEL motif impaired the ability of LSDV003 to alter MHC-I localization and surface expression. Furthermore, an LSDV003-deficient virus exhibited a markedly reduced capacity to suppress MHC-I surface expression. Collectively, these findings identify LSDV003 as a viral regulator of MHC-I trafficking and reveal a mechanism by which LSDV modulates host immune recognition.IMPORTANCELumpy skin disease is a highly contagious viral disease of cattle that has spread rapidly across Afro-Eurasia and causes major economic losses. However, the mechanisms used by lumpy skin disease virus to evade host immune defenses remain incompletely understood.
title: The lumpy skin disease virus protein LSDV003 regulates MHC-I trafficking and surface expression.

text: In this study, we identify a previously unrecognized lumpy skin disease virus protein, LSDV003, that reduces the surface expression of major histocompatibility complex class I molecules in infected cells. We found that LSDV003 prevents these molecules from leaving the endoplasmic reticulum by using a C-terminal retention motif, thereby altering their normal intracellular trafficking. An LSDV003-deficient virus showed a reduced ability to suppress major histocompatibility complex class I surface expression during infection. These findings reveal an important immune evasion strategy used by lumpy skin disease virus and highlight LSDV003 as a potential target for improved vaccines and antiviral approaches to control this economically important disease.
title: The lumpy skin disease virus protein LSDV003 regulates MHC-I trafficking and surface expression.

text: Canine pyometra is associated with systemic inflammation, but erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) has been less extensively evaluated alongside cytokines, C-reactive protein (CRP), and routine hematologic variables. This case-control study compared inflammatory and hematologic measurements in 15 dogs with closed pyometra and 15 clinically healthy controls. Interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), CRP, ESR, white blood cell (WBC) count, packed cell volume (PCV), and serum creatinine were assessed. Group differences were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests, with Welch correction when variance heterogeneity was detected. Mean differences were reported with 95% confidence intervals and Hedges' g effect sizes. Dogs with closed pyometra had higher IL-6, TNF-α, CRP, ESR, and WBC counts and lower PCV and serum creatinine than controls (all p ≤ 0.005).
title: Evaluation of serological changes of ESR, CRP, IL-6 and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-a) and hematologic parameters in pet dogs with pyometra.

text: The largest standardized differences were observed for ESR (g = 2.39), PCV (g = -2.29), and serum creatinine (g = -1.94). Within the pyometra group, IL-6, TNF-α, and CRP were strongly correlated (r = 0.974-0.978; p < 0.001). These findings demonstrate a pronounced systemic inflammatory and hematologic phenotype in closed canine pyometra and identify ESR as a potentially informative component of multimarker inflammatory assessment. Prospective studies incorporating longitudinal measurements and clinical outcomes are required to determine diagnostic or prognostic utility.
title: Evaluation of serological changes of ESR, CRP, IL-6 and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-a) and hematologic parameters in pet dogs with pyometra.

text: Objective To evaluate intraoperative cholangiography (IOC) during open cholecystectomy in dogs with benign gallbladder disease, including cases with preoperative common bile duct (CBD) obstruction, and to describe the short-term outcomes. Study design Retrospective case series. Animals A total of 73 client-owned dogs. Methods Medical records (2014-2022) were reviewed. All dogs underwent open cholecystectomy, bile duct flushing (BDF) with saline, and IOC under subtraction fluoroscopy. Cholangiograms were assessed for complete CBD obstruction (no duodenal passage), partial obstruction (CBD filling defects indicating retained debris), and filling defects in hepatic ducts. Perioperative mortality (≤14 days) and post-discharge findings during 3 months of follow-up were recorded. Results IOC was evaluable in 72 of 73 dogs; assessment was precluded by catheter perforation in one dog.
title: Intraoperative cholangiography during open cholecystectomy in 73 dogs with benign gallbladder disease.

text: Complete CBD obstruction was identified in 12.5% (9/72). Partial obstruction with retained debris occurred in 20.8% (15/72); debris migrated to transiently obstruct the distal CBD during contrast injection in four of 15. Among the 66 dogs in which IOC opacified the right and left hepatic ducts, seven (10.6%) had filling defects in the hepatic ducts. One dog developed suspected contrast-associated shock that resolved with treatment. Perioperative mortality was 6.8% (5/73) in the total cohort; 0% (0/29) in dogs without jaundice, and 11.4% (5/44) in dogs with jaundice. Among 61 dogs with follow-up, no deaths occurred within 3 months. Conclusion During open cholecystectomy, IOC frequently identified retained debris and other biliary abnormalities. Clinical significance IOC may be a useful adjunct to BDF when CBD or hepatic duct obstruction or retained debris is suspected.
title: Intraoperative cholangiography during open cholecystectomy in 73 dogs with benign gallbladder disease.

text: Routine IOC may improve surgical outcomes, particularly in dogs with preoperative CBD obstruction.
title: Intraoperative cholangiography during open cholecystectomy in 73 dogs with benign gallbladder disease.

text: African swine fever virus (ASFV) can be transmitted through direct contact and, in specific ecological settings, by Ornithodoros spp. soft ticks. However, the cellular mechanisms that support ASFV replication in both porcine host and tick vector remain poorly understood. Iron is essential for cellular metabolism and viral replication, but excessive labile iron can induce oxidative stress and ferroptosis-like morphological changes in mitochondria. Whether and how ASFV exploits intracellular Fe3+ homeostasis to sustain its replication has not been fully defined. In this study, proteomic analysis of ASFV-infected PAM (pig) and OME/CTVM24 (derived from Ornithodoros moubata) cells revealed a marked reduction in ferritin/FTH1 abundance, suggesting that ASFV infection alters intracellular iron storage and availability.
title: Modulation of Fe3+ homeostasis by African Swine Fever virus facilitates its efficient replication in Ornithodoros lahorensis and pigs.

text: Further analyses showed that ASFV dynamically regulated labile Fe3+ levels during infection. At the early stage, ASFV promoted NCOA4-associated ferritin turnover, increased labile Fe3+ release, enhanced mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact, and induced ferroptosis-like changes in mitochondrial morphology. At later stages, ASFV restrained excessive iron-associated damage, thereby maintaining an intracellular environment compatible with continued viral replication. Pharmacological depletion of labile iron with deferoxamine mesylate markedly suppressed ASFV replication in both porcine and tick-derived cells, indicating that controlled Fe3+ availability is required for efficient viral propagation. Mechanistically, the ASFV-encoded protein pA151R interacted with NCOA4 and promoted autophagic degradation of FTH1 in a manner dependent on its intact LC3-interacting region motif.
title: Modulation of Fe3+ homeostasis by African Swine Fever virus facilitates its efficient replication in Ornithodoros lahorensis and pigs.

text: pA151R also impaired mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and disrupted MDA5-MAVS/VISA signaling. Deletion of A151R impaired the ability of ASFV to modulate Fe3+ homeostasis and significantly reduced viral replication. ASFV infection increased serum iron levels in pigs and caused abnormal iron redistribution and depletion in splenic tissues in vivo. Similar iron depletion and transient ferroptosis-like morphological changes in mitochondria were observed in the salivary glands of ASFV-infected O. lahorensis. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that ASFV exploits Fe3+ homeostasis through a pA151R-NCOA4-FTH1-dependent mechanism to support replication in host and vector cells.
title: Modulation of Fe3+ homeostasis by African Swine Fever virus facilitates its efficient replication in Ornithodoros lahorensis and pigs.

text: This study provides new insights into ASFV metabolic regulation and identifies iron homeostasis and pA151R-mediated ferritinophagy as potential targets for strategies aimed at limiting ASFV replication and tick-associated transmission.
title: Modulation of Fe3+ homeostasis by African Swine Fever virus facilitates its efficient replication in Ornithodoros lahorensis and pigs.

text: Background Serial measurements of acute-phase proteins help monitor the development of and recovery from sepsis in people and dogs. To date, the kinetics of regenerating protein (REG) 3E, a novel biomarker for inflammation in dogs, are unknown. Objectives The goal of our study was to assess changes in the concentrations of REG3E and compare these to C-reactive protein (CRP) concentrations over 48-72 h in different cohorts of dogs. Methods Plasma REG3E concentrations were measured using an ELISA on 3-4 consecutive days from 43 dogs, including 12 healthy controls, 17 undergoing tibial plateau leveling osteotomy (TPLO), and 14 with sepsis. Canine CRP was measured using a turbidimetric immunoassay. Results REG3E concentrations were low in control and TPLO dogs throughout all time points. In the TPLO group, there was a mild but significant increase in CRP over time.
title: Kinetics of Regenerating Protein 3E and C-Reactive Protein in Healthy Dogs, Dogs Undergoing Tibial Plateau Leveling Osteotomy, and Dogs With Sepsis.

text: REG3E and CRP concentrations were higher in septic dogs at admission compared to the other groups and progressively decreased after initiation of treatment to 14% and 28% of initial levels, respectively, within 72 h. REG3E, but not CRP concentrations, stayed high in two dogs, one of which developed recurrent sepsis. There was a significant moderate correlation between both acute-phase proteins among all groups and within the sepsis group, but not within the TPLO group. Conclusions In conclusion, based on this cohort of dogs, CRP appears to be more sensitive to detect minor postsurgical inflammation, but the potential of REG3E to predict developing or recurrent sepsis deserves further investigation.
title: Kinetics of Regenerating Protein 3E and C-Reactive Protein in Healthy Dogs, Dogs Undergoing Tibial Plateau Leveling Osteotomy, and Dogs With Sepsis.

text: Feeding behavior, which is crucial for all mammals, is regulated by a delicate equilibrium between the orexigenic and anorexigenic activities of hypothalamic neurons. This exquisite control of the neuropeptides that govern the feeding behavior could be a focal point in the pathogenesis of obesity. We reported that inactivation of C-terminal binding protein 2 (CtBP2), a transcriptional corepressor with metabolite-sensing capabilities, contributes to the pathogenesis of obesity in liver tissues and pancreatic β-cells. Here, we describe a transcriptional system regulated by CtBP2 in the hypothalamus. Our global mapping of CtBP2 binding sites using ChIP-seq combined with functional analyses revealed that CtBP2 functions as a corepressor for orexigenic neuropeptide promoters.
title: Obesity Disrupts CtBP2-Mediated Maintenance of Transcriptional Equilibrium in Hypothalamic Feeding Circuitry.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

text: In response to the metabolic abnormalities associated with obesity, CtBP2 undergoes allosteric inactivation and dissociates from these promoters, thereby resulting in the derepression of orexigenic neuropeptide expression. Consistently, the loss of CtBP2 in hypothalamic neurons in mice increases the expression of orexigenic neuropeptides, thus leading to increased feeding behavior. These findings highlight how obesity disrupts homeostatic mechanisms that normally maintain body weight within a healthy range.
title: Obesity Disrupts CtBP2-Mediated Maintenance of Transcriptional Equilibrium in Hypothalamic Feeding Circuitry.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

text: This study evaluated the nutritional adequacy of dog diets formulated by four widely used Artificial Intelligence models (Manus, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Gemini) against the recommendations of the European Pet Food Industry Federation. This was a theoretical, in silico study, no animals were fed or clinically evaluated. Using a standardized prompt, complete and balanced diets (beef and chicken) for an 8 kg adult dog were requested. Eleven formulations were analyzed using SuperCracPet® software based on United States Department of Agriculture data. Overall, 61.3% of nutrients were below the minimum recommended levels.
title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in obtaining canine diets: nutritional inadequacy and the need for technical knowledge.

text: Nutrient levels below FEDIAF minimum requirements were identified across multiple categories: energy supply was insufficient in 81% of diets, calcium levels were below recommendations in 91% of formulations, calcium-to-phosphorus ratios were outside the recommended range in 63% of diets, chlorine was absent in all formulations, vitamin D levels were below requirements in 63.7% of diets, choline in 81.8%, and linoleic acid in 72%. Only 18% of the formulations included supplementation, which was provided in insufficient quantity. If implemented chronically, these nutritional inadequacies may pose risks to bone, dermatological, immune, and metabolic health. It is concluded that, in their current form, the evaluated language models are insufficient for the autonomous formulation of canine diets, as the generated prescriptions presented multiple nutritional inadequacies.
title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in obtaining canine diets: nutritional inadequacy and the need for technical knowledge.

text: Safe application requires hybrid systems with mandatory supervision by animal scientists and veterinarians, as well as regulation to prevent avoidable risks to animal health.
title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in obtaining canine diets: nutritional inadequacy and the need for technical knowledge.

text: The capacity of an antibody to recognize and bind an antigen with high specificity and strength (i.e., its binding affinity) is a key determinant in the design and optimization of neutralizing antibodies against pathogenic targets. Here we introduce Ab-Affinity, a fine-tuned protein language model (PLM) that predicts the binding affinity of an antibody against a target peptide within the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Cross-validation results shows that Ab-Affinity outperforms other PLM-based affinity predictors when evaluated on a held-out validation and independent test sets. When integrated with a genetic algorithm and simulated annealing for sequence diversification and fitness optimization, Ab-Affinity enables the generation of candidate antibodies exhibiting over 100-fold improvement in predicted binding affinity relative to their parental (natural) antibody.
title: An antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for antibody design.

text: More broadly, antibodies designed with Ab-Affinity attain higher predicted binding affinities than those produced by alternative mutational strategies, yielding synthetic antibodies with favorable predicted biophysical characteristics. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations for the strongest synthetic candidates indicate enhanced interactions and increased stability with the target peptide epitope within the spike protein. Experimental validation in vitro for a top-ranked candidate reveals an apparent increase in binding relative to its parental antibody. All model weights, source code, and analysis pipelines are publicly released to allow full reproducibility.
title: An antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for antibody design.

text: Iron overload associated with transfusion-dependent disorders promotes oxidative stress, mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction, and ferroptotic cell death. Although iron chelation therapy remains the cornerstone of management, the mechanistic links between iron burden, subcellular injury, and emerging biomarkers have not been comprehensively integrated within a clinically relevant framework. This systematic review aimed to synthesize clinical and preclinical evidence on the effects of iron chelation therapy on systemic iron burden, mitochondrial bioenergetics, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and biomarker-guided management. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published from January 2000 to June 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The database search yielded 465 records.
title: Iron Chelation Therapy in Iron Overload Disorders: A Systematic Review with Narrative Synthesis of Bioenergetic Dysfunction, Oxidative Stress, and Biomarker-Guided Management.

text: After removing 120 duplicates, 345 unique records were screened by title and abstract, of which 210 did not satisfy the predefined eligibility criteria. The remaining 135 articles underwent full-text assessment; 45 were excluded because of inappropriate study design (n = 20), lack of relevant outcomes (n = 15), or unavailable full texts (n = 10). Of the 90 remaining articles, 29 studies (7 randomized controlled trials, 6 observational studies, 3 systematic reviews or guidelines, 6 experimental animal studies and 7 in vitro or cellular mechanistic studies) were included for qualitative narrative synthesis. An additional 61 review articles, guidelines, and epidemiological reports were retained for background context. Methodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and SYRCLE tools.
title: Iron Chelation Therapy in Iron Overload Disorders: A Systematic Review with Narrative Synthesis of Bioenergetic Dysfunction, Oxidative Stress, and Biomarker-Guided Management.

text: Clinical evidence indicated that deferoxamine, deferiprone, and deferasirox consistently reduce systemic iron burden, reflected by improvements in serum ferritin, liver iron concentration, and cardiac T2* magnetic resonance imaging. Circulating iron-related biomarkers, including non-transferrin-bound iron and labile plasma iron, provided additional information on redox-active iron exposure. Preclinical evidence further suggested that iron chelation may attenuate mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and ferroptotic signaling. However, mechanistic biomarkers of mitochondrial bioenergetics, oxidative injury, and ferroptosis remain insufficiently validated in prospective clinical populations.
title: Iron Chelation Therapy in Iron Overload Disorders: A Systematic Review with Narrative Synthesis of Bioenergetic Dysfunction, Oxidative Stress, and Biomarker-Guided Management.

text: Considerable heterogeneity in study populations, interventions, biomarker methodologies, and clinical and mechanistic outcomes limited direct quantitative comparison and supported a narrative synthesis approach. Current evidence supports iron chelation as an effective strategy for reducing systemic iron burden, while emerging bioenergetic, redox, and ferroptosis-related biomarkers provide promising mechanistic insights into iron-mediated cellular injury. Nevertheless, their clinical utility remains uncertain because of limited prospective validation, methodological heterogeneity, and insufficient standardization. Future translational studies should integrate conventional iron indices with validated mitochondrial and redox biomarkers and determine whether biomarker-guided chelation strategies can improve clinically meaningful outcomes beyond conventional iron-burden monitoring.
title: Iron Chelation Therapy in Iron Overload Disorders: A Systematic Review with Narrative Synthesis of Bioenergetic Dysfunction, Oxidative Stress, and Biomarker-Guided Management.

text: Our understanding of a protective humoral immune response to dengue virus (DENV) remains limited. The envelope (E) protein is the main antibody (Ab) target. While anti-fusion loop (FL) epitope monoclonal Abs (mAbs) can induce antibody dependent enhancement (ADE) in vitro, some mAbs targeting quaternary epitopes can cross-neutralize different DENV serotypes. However, the contribution of each Ab subset to disease outcome remains poorly characterized. We defined DENV2 E epitope-specific Abs dynamics and assessed their association with disease outcome in a cohort of hospitalized and subclinical dengue patients during post-primary DENV2 infection. We quantified and isolated anti-E epitope-specific Abs and tested their enhancing and neutralizing capacity. During the critical phase, FL-targeting antibodies were increased in hospitalized patients compared to subclinical cases.
title: Dengue virus envelope epitope-specific antibodies are associated with protection from severe dengue.

text: Antibodies targeting quaternary epitopes were reduced in severe dengue compared to classical dengue fever patients. Functionally, quaternary epitope-targeting antibodies showed stronger neutralization and cross-neutralization properties, while FL-binding antibodies displayed stronger in vitro enhancement. These findings show that anti-DENV2 E epitope-specific Ab proportions correlate with disease susceptibility and severity, with important implications for novel vaccine design.
title: Dengue virus envelope epitope-specific antibodies are associated with protection from severe dengue.

text: Importance Electronic patient-reported outcome (PRO) monitoring has shown benefits in advanced cancer, but data specific to metastatic breast cancer (mBC) remain limited. Fatigue is a common, clinically important, and functionally impairing symptom in mBC, making it a patient-centered target for electronic PRO monitoring. Objective To determine whether digital PRO monitoring with alert-based responses reduces fatigue in patients with mBC. Design, setting, and participants This multicenter randomized clinical trial was conducted from May 2021 to February 2024, with 12 months of follow-up, at 52 breast cancer centers in Germany and included women aged 18 years or older with mBC who were receiving systemic therapy at any point in the metastatic disease course, had a life expectancy of longer than 3 months, were able to read German, and had smartphone access.
title: Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome Monitoring With Alert-Based Interventions in Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: Data analysis started in February 2024 and lasted 6 months. Interventions The intervention group completed weekly PRO questionnaires via a smartphone using validated short forms from the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer computerized adaptive testing core item bank. Automated alerts based on predefined PRO deterioration were emailed to trained local nurses or physicians, who contacted patients by telephone within 48 hours. The control group received usual care with quarterly PRO questionnaires and no alerts. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcome was fatigue at 6 months. Secondary outcomes included fatigue, physical functioning, and quality of life over 12 months. PROs were reported as standardized T scores.
title: Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome Monitoring With Alert-Based Interventions in Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: Results Of 2008 patients screened, 924 (46.0%) were randomized, and 909 (45.3%) were included in the primary analysis (median age, 50 years [range, 19-83 years]). Baseline mean (SD) fatigue T scores were 57.6 (9.5) in the intervention group and 60.2 (9.0) in the control group (P Conclusions and relevance This randomized clinical trial found that digital PRO monitoring was associated with clinically meaningful reductions in fatigue and improved physical functioning. These findings support further evaluation of alert-based PRO monitoring in routine oncology care. Trial registration German Clinical Trials Register: DRKS00024015.
title: Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome Monitoring With Alert-Based Interventions in Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: Cytokines may provide information about inflammation in equine colic, but their clinical relevance remains uncertain. This pilot study assessed short-term changes in serum and faecal interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6 and IL-8 in eight horses undergoing colic surgery and compared measurements with six healthy controls. Colic horses were sampled at admission (D0), 24 h (D1) and day 7 (D7); controls provided serum at D0 and faeces at all three time points. Cytokines were assayed using MILLIPLEX and MAGPIX. Admission faeces were unavailable from 3/8 colic horses (37.5%). Serum IL-1β and IL-6 were below detection limits in 29/29 analysed samples (100%) for each cytokine. Serum IL-8 varied markedly without significant temporal change. Thirty-nine faecal extracts were analysed without faecal assay validation.
title: Feasibility of Serum and Faecal Interleukin Assessment in Equine Surgical Colic: A Pilot Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Faecal estimates were generally lower in colic horses, with nominal between-group differences for IL-6 at D1 ( p = 0.045), IL-1β at D7 ( p = 0.033) and IL-8 at D7 ( p = 0.004). No consistent temporal pattern in faecal estimates or significant association between serum and faecal IL-8 was detected. These findings do not establish the usefulness of these cytokines for clinical monitoring and highlight sampling and analytical limitations that should be addressed in larger, clinically diverse cohorts.
title: Feasibility of Serum and Faecal Interleukin Assessment in Equine Surgical Colic: A Pilot Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Highly pathogenic avian influenza H5NX clade 2.3.4.4b viruses continue to circulate globally. Reintroduction of Eurasian lineage viruses into North America and reassortment with endemic low pathogenicity strains have resulted in new genotypes, including D1.2. To assess pathogenicity and cellular tropism, we intranasally inoculated genotype D1.2 virus into pigs. We isolated virus from nasal secretions from most inoculated animals for multiple days. At 5 days postinoculation, PCR and immunohistochemistry detected virus in musculoskeletal, respiratory, digestive, lymphatic, and nervous systems, and virus was isolated from meat juice. At 35 days postinoculation, we detected viral antigen and low levels of RNA in the brain of an animal with lesions consistent with a viral etiology and found viral antigen in the ethmoid of 2 animals.
title: Detection of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Genotype D1.2 Virus in Swine after Experimental Inoculation.

text: Consistent detection in nasal swab specimens, combined with subclinical respiratory infection, suggest that identifying infection in commercial swine without overt respiratory signs could be difficult.
title: Detection of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Genotype D1.2 Virus in Swine after Experimental Inoculation.

text: Background Canine atopic dermatitis (cAD) is a genetically, aetiologically, immunologically and clinically complex disease requiring both individualised immediate and long-term management. Objectives These updated guidelines from the International Committee on Allergic Diseases of Animals (ICADA) aim to substantially revise previous recommendations by organising treatment according to mechanism-of-action and by distinguishing two therapeutic phases: reactive therapy to resolve existing pruritus and skin lesions, followed by proactive therapy to maintain remission and reduce flares. Materials and methods The literature was reviewed and recommendations are based, where possible, on randomised controlled trials and systematic reviews, with evidence graded using the Strength of Recommendation Taxonomy.
title: Treatment of Canine Atopic Dermatitis: Updated Guidelines From the International Committee on Allergic Diseases of Animals (ICADA).

text: The guidelines review skin barrier care, antimicrobial and microbiome-modulating interventions, avoidance of nonallergenic and allergenic flare factors, allergen-specific immunotherapy, and anti-inflammatory, antipruritic and immunomodulatory treatments. Results Rapid-acting broad-spectrum drugs, particularly glucocorticoids, are recommended for reactive treatment. Janus Kinase (JAK) inhibitors and lokivetmab may be effective depending on lesion type, severity and inflammatory complexity. Secondary infections and flare factors must be addressed. Proactive management essential to prevent repeated cycles of inflammation may include skin barrier support, infection control, allergen avoidance, allergen immunotherapy, topical glucocorticoids, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, lokivetmab or JAK inhibitors, selected according to the patient's disease pattern and response.
title: Treatment of Canine Atopic Dermatitis: Updated Guidelines From the International Committee on Allergic Diseases of Animals (ICADA).

text: Conclusions and clinical relevance A number of interventions are suitable for the treatment of cAD. Interventions are neither universally required, interchangeable nor effective in all cases. Treatment selection should take into account efficacy, safety, practicality, cost, the quality-of-life of both dog and owner, and the legal regulations applicable in the country of use.
title: Treatment of Canine Atopic Dermatitis: Updated Guidelines From the International Committee on Allergic Diseases of Animals (ICADA).

text: Canine chronic enteropathy (CE) is a heterogeneous disorder with variable clinical outcomes. We aimed to identify fecal microbiome and metabolomic signatures associated with CE severity and treatment outcomes. Fecal samples from dogs with CE ( n = 56), acute diarrhea ( n = 8), and healthy controls ( n = 126) were analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and GC-MS-based untargeted metabolomics. CE dogs exhibited significantly reduced microbial diversity compared with the other groups, and unsupervised Partitioning Around Medoids clustering identified two microbiome clusters within the CE cohort. Cluster 2 was characterized by dysbiosis, with enrichment of Streptococcus, Enterococcus, and Klebsiella, and depletion of short-chain fatty acid producers, including Fusobacterium and Blautia.
title: Fecal microbiome-based clustering identifies distinct disease subtypes with differing metabolomic profiles and treatment outcomes in canine chronic enteropathy.

text: Among dogs with baseline Canine Chronic Enteropathy Clinical Activity Index (CCECAI) > 3, 10 of 12 Cluster 1 dogs (83.3%) achieved remission (CCECAI ≤ 3) after treatment, compared with 7 of 18 Cluster 2 dogs (38.9%; p = 0.0256). CCECAI scores decreased significantly after treatment in Cluster 1 ( p = 0.0005) but not in Cluster 2 ( p = 0.077). Fecal propanoic acid and kynurenic acid levels also differed between clusters. These findings suggest that gut microbiota and associated metabolites may contribute to differences in CE severity and treatment outcomes.
title: Fecal microbiome-based clustering identifies distinct disease subtypes with differing metabolomic profiles and treatment outcomes in canine chronic enteropathy.

text: Background/Objectives: Invasive species can disrupt native predator-prey interactions, and toxic invasive prey may pose particular threats to native predators. The cane toad ( Rhinella marina ) secretes cardiotonic steroids (CTSs) that can cause lethal poisoning in predators. We reviewed the molecular basis and evolutionary patterns of CTS resistance and evaluated the potential and limitations of genetic screening for assessing wildlife vulnerability on Ishigaki-jima and Iriomote-jima Islands, Japan. Methods: We reviewed experimental, structural, and evolutionary evidence for CTS resistance associated with Na+/K+-ATPase α subunit (NKAα) and screened publicly available NKAα1 sequences from vertebrates occurring on the two islands, focusing on amino acid states previously associated with CTS target-site insensitivity.
title: Molecular Screening for Potential Resistance to Toxic Invasive Prey: Implications for Island Conservation.

text: Results: NKAα1 sequences were available for 96 of 185 native terrestrial vertebrate species. Most retained the putatively ancestral Q111/N122 combination, whereas alternative states at these major resistance-associated sites occurred in only a few species. These included T111/N122 in the black-faced spoonbill ( Platalea minor ), and E111/N122 in the crested serpent-eagle ( Spilornis cheela perplexus ) and grey-faced buzzard ( Butastur indicus ). T111 has shown context-dependent effects on CTS sensitivity in functional assays, whereas E111 has been proposed as a candidate resistance-associated state but lacks direct functional validation. The endangered Iriomote cat ( Prionailurus bengalensis iriomotensis ), an endemic predator that frequently consumes anurans, retained Q111/N122.
title: Molecular Screening for Potential Resistance to Toxic Invasive Prey: Implications for Island Conservation.

text: Conclusions: NKAα1 sequence alone cannot establish whole-animal susceptibility or conservation risk because resistance may depend on sequence background, other NKAα paralogs, physiological mechanisms, and behavior. Molecular screening should therefore be viewed as an initial tool for identifying candidate molecular signatures and prioritizing species and knowledge gaps for subsequent functional, toxicological, and ecological investigation.
title: Molecular Screening for Potential Resistance to Toxic Invasive Prey: Implications for Island Conservation.

text: Bats are important reservoirs of zoonotic pathogens and valuable models for studying antiviral tolerance and neuroinflammation within a One Health framework. However, chiropteran neural 2D- in vitro models remain limited. Here, we established and characterized the first chiropteran primary (CpBCs) and immortalized (CiBCs) cell lines from Hypsugo savii species. To overcome the limited lifespan of CpBCs, immortalization strategies based on human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) and Simian virus 40 large T antigen (SV40) were evaluated. Electroporation-mediated transfection with SV40 successfully generated CiBCs, whereas liposome-mediated and hTERT-based approaches were unsuccessful.
title: Chiropteran (<i>Hypsugo savii</i>) Post-Natal Brain 2D-In Vitro Models: Primary Cell Isolation, Immortalization and Transcriptomic Changes.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: RNA sequencing revealed marked transcriptional changes comparing CiBCs with CpCBs, such as the upregulation of pathways related to cell cycle progression, DNA replication, and proliferation in CiBCs, together with the downregulation of apoptosis, inflammatory signaling, and immune-related pathways. Immortalized cells also exhibited enrichment of neural stem cell-like and cancer-associated signatures, suggesting partial dedifferentiation induced by SV40-mediated immortalization. Overall, this study provides a novel chiropteran brain-derived 2D- in vitro platform for investigating bat neurobiology, host-pathogen interactions, viral tolerance, and neurotropic infectious diseases relevant to emerging zoonoses.
title: Chiropteran (<i>Hypsugo savii</i>) Post-Natal Brain 2D-In Vitro Models: Primary Cell Isolation, Immortalization and Transcriptomic Changes.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Epimedium is a traditional herb that has been investigated for its potential osteogenic and bone-regenerative effects, yet systematic analyses of its multi-component, multi-target mechanisms in bone metabolism and tissue engineering applications are limited. To address this knowledge gap, this narrative review systematically summarizes more than 20 bioactive constituents extracted from various parts of major medicinal Epimedium species. We elaborate on their pivotal roles in modulating osteogenic differentiation, suppressing osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption, regulating inflammatory responses, exerting antioxidant effects, promoting angiogenesis, demonstrating antitumor activity, exerting chondroprotective effects, and exhibiting antibacterial activity during bone defect repair.
title: <i>Epimedium</i>: A Versatile Player in Bone Tissue Engineering.

text: Furthermore, we highlight recent advancements and current trends in applying these bioactive constituents within the field of bone tissue engineering. Additionally, we compared the osteogenic and osteoprotective potentials of three metabolically related flavonoids (icariin, icaritin, and icariside II). Network pharmacology was utilized to elucidate their multi-target mechanisms in modulating bone metabolism, providing insights for future mechanistic studies. Despite the long-standing clinical use and extensive scientific investigation of Epimedium , this review identifies several challenges associated with its application in bone tissue engineering and offers constructive recommendations to overcome these limitations.
title: <i>Epimedium</i>: A Versatile Player in Bone Tissue Engineering.

text: Cadmium (Cd) contamination of agricultural soils disrupts plant signaling networks, impairing nutrient communication, photosynthetic efficiency, and stress responses. Microbial inoculants offer eco-biotechnological solutions by modulating signal perception and transduction under heavy metal stress. This field study investigated the role of Acinetobacter schindleri strain SR-5-1 in influencing pea ( Pisum sativum L.) signaling pathways under Cd toxicity. Plants exposed to environmentally relevant Cd concentrations (250 and 500 µM) exhibited disrupted chlorophyll biosynthesis, elevated oxidative stress markers, and impaired nutrient signaling. Inoculation with SR-5-1 restored chlorophyll levels, enhanced ROS-scavenging enzyme activities, and reduced lipid peroxidation, indicating microbial effects on oxidative signaling cascades.
title: Microbial intervention by <i>Acinetobacter schindleri</i> SR-5-1 alleviates cadmium toxicity in pea cultivation.

text: Importantly, the inoculated plants accumulated less Cd in the roots and leaves, reflecting microbial mediation of ion transporter activity and rhizosphere detoxification. SR-5-1 also improved nitrogen, iron, zinc, potassium, and magnesium acquisition, highlighting its role in nutrient uptake and homeostasis. These findings demonstrate that SR-5-1 functions as a bio-communicator, alleviating xenobiotic stress by modulating ROS and nutrient signaling pathways. The study underscores the ecological relevance of microbial inoculants in supporting integrative plant communication and resilience, positioning SR-5-1 as a promising bioresource for signaling-driven sustainable agriculture in Cd-affected soils.
title: Microbial intervention by <i>Acinetobacter schindleri</i> SR-5-1 alleviates cadmium toxicity in pea cultivation.

text: Bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) orchestrate the early inflammatory response following myocardial infarction (MI), yet the post‑translational mechanisms governing their phenotypic fate remain poorly understood. Although we previously demonstrated that global deletion of tripartite motif-containing 21 (TRIM21) attenuates post-MI inflammation, its macrophage-specific role and downstream targets are still undefined. Using bone marrow transplantation, we demonstrated that TRIM21 deficiency in BMDMs shifted macrophage polarization from pro‑inflammatory to reparative, limiting infarct size and preserving cardiac function post-MI. Mechanistically, ubiquitination proteomics identified macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) as the substrate of TRIM21 in BMDMs, with TRIM21 catalyzing K48-linked polyubiquitination at lysine 27 (K27) to drive MSR1 degradation.
title: TRIM21 Drives MSR1 Degradation via K27 Ubiquitination in Macrophages to Deteriorate Postinfarction Cardiac Dysfunction.

text: Genetic disruption of this modification via the Msr1 K27R knock-in mutation stabilized MSR1, recapitulating the cardioprotective and anti-inflammatory phenotype in vivo. At the molecular level, stabilized MSR1 enhanced fatty acid uptake and promoted a PPARγ-linked fatty acid oxidation program. This metabolic shift was accompanied by enhanced oxidative phosphorylation, effectively halting the transition toward a pro-inflammatory state. Collectively, our findings identify the TRIM21-MSR1 (K27) axis as a previously unrecognized post-translational regulator of BMDM-mediated post-infarction inflammation. Targeting MSR1 ubiquitination at K27 may represent a potential therapeutic target to resolve sterile inflammation and promote cardiac repair after MI.
title: TRIM21 Drives MSR1 Degradation via K27 Ubiquitination in Macrophages to Deteriorate Postinfarction Cardiac Dysfunction.

text: The increasing virulence of field strains of Marek's disease virus (MDV), which can overcome the immunity conferred by the widely used CVI988 vaccine, underscores the need for more effective alternatives. The SC9-1 vaccine strain has demonstrated superior protective efficacy and is being increasingly adopted in China. Importantly, it harbors a unique recombinant REV-LTR insertion junction that is absent from all other MDV strains. Targeting this strain-exclusive genomic locus, this study established an SYBR Green I-based quantitative real-time PCR assay for specific detection and quantification of SC9-1 to support clinical vaccine surveillance. We designed specific primers and systematically optimized the qPCR reaction conditions. The resulting assay demonstrated high specificity, showing no cross-reactivity with other MDV strains or common avian pathogens.
title: The Development and Evaluation of an SYBR Green I-Based qPCR Assay for Detecting the Marek's Disease Virus SC9-1 Vaccine Strain.

text: It achieved a sensitivity of 1.0 × 10 1 copies/μL, and reproducibility was excellent, with both intra- and inter-assay coefficients of variation below 1.0%. Furthermore, the LOD of this assay for commercial SC9-1 vaccine samples was determined to be 1.22 PFU per 200 μL sample. In conclusion, this SYBR Green I-based qPCR assay provides a specific, sensitive, and reproducible tool for the rapid quantification of the SC9-1 vaccine virus. It is fully validated for routine vaccine quality control, while exhibiting promising potential for subsequent field surveillance within MD vaccination programs.
title: The Development and Evaluation of an SYBR Green I-Based qPCR Assay for Detecting the Marek's Disease Virus SC9-1 Vaccine Strain.

text: Computed tomographic (CT) evaluation of medial iliac (MILN), internal iliac (IILN), and sacral (SLN) lymph nodes (LNs) in dogs provides vital staging information in certain neoplastic conditions. This retrospective study aimed to determine minimum transverse diameter (MinTD) and maximum transverse diameter (MaxTD) values for presumed normal iliosacral LNs and assess their utility in evaluating therapeutic response using response evaluation criteria in solid tumors (RECIST) v1.1. LN margins, number, and pre-contrast attenuation were also analyzed. The CT scans of 71 dogs were reviewed by an ACVR-certified veterinary radiologist. The MILNs were identified in 99% of dogs, predominantly bilaterally. The IILNs and SLNs were identified in 79% and 41% of dogs, respectively, with more variability in bilateral versus unilateral presence.
title: Computed tomographic Characteristics of Presumed Normal Canine Iliosacral Lymph Nodes.
journal: Veterinary radiology & ultrasound : the official journal of the American College of Veterinary Radiology and the International Veterinary Radiology Association

text: Median values for MinTD/MaxTD were 4.2/7.4 mm for MILNs, 2.5/4.0 mm for IILNs, and 2.9/4.9 mm for SLNs. MinTD was 8.6 mm had greater diameters for MILNs and IILNs (p ≤ 0.034). Separate MinTD values for IILNs and SLNs are presented herein, whereas prior studies reported them as a combined group.
title: Computed tomographic Characteristics of Presumed Normal Canine Iliosacral Lymph Nodes.
journal: Veterinary radiology & ultrasound : the official journal of the American College of Veterinary Radiology and the International Veterinary Radiology Association

text: Background This study compared four biomaterials after maxillary sinus floor elevation in rabbits, focusing on graft persistence, tissue organization, space maintenance, and Schneiderian membrane response. Methods Thirteen adult New Zealand White rabbits were enrolled, including 12 males and one female replacement animal; 12 animals provided evaluable specimens, with six assigned to each healing interval. Four elevated sinus compartments per evaluable animal were randomly allocated to Bio-Oss ® , mp3 ® , ReproBone ® novo Paste, or Alos Granular. Specimens were collected after 2 or 10 weeks ( n = 6 each). Histomorphometry quantified new bone, residual graft, soft tissue, elevated area, mucosal alterations, and IBN-like tissue, defined as areas in which biomaterial and bone could not be reliably separated. A combined graft and IBN percentage was calculated.
title: Comparative Histological and Histomorphometric Analysis of Xenografts and Synthetic Biomaterials in Rabbit Sinus Floor Elevation.

text: Results At 10 weeks, materials differed in residual graft ( p = 0.0040) and combined graft and IBN percentage ( p = 0.0218); Bio-Oss ® showed higher values than Alos Granular for both outcomes (adjusted p = 0.0024 and 0.0219, respectively). IBN-like tissue was higher in ReproBone ® novo Paste and Alos Granular than in Bio-Oss ® (adjusted p = 0.0219 and 0.0417), whereas only a small proportion occurred in mp3 ® . New bone did not differ among materials at either interval. Bio-Oss ® and mp3 ® showed predominantly conventional osteoconduction. Alos Granular showed extensive degradation, whereas ReproBone ® novo Paste exhibited irregular graft and IBN regions. In the descriptive mucosal assessment, thinning was observed in all groups, whereas perforations were observed only at Bio-Oss ® -treated sites; no inferential comparisons were performed for these outcomes.
title: Comparative Histological and Histomorphometric Analysis of Xenografts and Synthetic Biomaterials in Rabbit Sinus Floor Elevation.

text: Conclusions The materials differed in graft persistence, tissue architecture, dimensional stability, and mucosal response. Sinus graft evaluation should extend beyond new bone formation to include residual graft, IBN-like tissue, space maintenance, and mucosal compatibility.
title: Comparative Histological and Histomorphometric Analysis of Xenografts and Synthetic Biomaterials in Rabbit Sinus Floor Elevation.

text: Prussian blue (PB) has evolved as the most advantageous electrocatalyst for preparing H 2 O 2 biosensors due to its exceptional high sensitivity and specificity, which are vital to minimizing the interferences in complex biological samples. However, the widespread adoption of PB-based bioanalysis has been severely restricted by its inherent instability in neutral and alkaline environments, compromising the measurement accuracy and reliability. This review provides an overview of the strategies used to improve PB stability in bioanalysis, such as integration with carbon nanomaterials, polymer encapsulation (e.g., Nafion and chitosan), and transition metal ion (e.g., Ni, Co)-doping. Furthermore, we comprehensively cover the bioanalytical applications of PB: from traditional oxidase-based biosensors to emerging high-impact applications enabled by the enhanced PB stability.
title: Prussian blue electrocatalyst in bioanalysis: From oxidase biosensors to peroxidase kinetics assays.

text: These includ real-time H 2 O 2 quantification in tumors and brain tissue, electrochemical immunosensing, and kinetics assays for peroxidases and peroxygenases acting on insoluble substrates.
title: Prussian blue electrocatalyst in bioanalysis: From oxidase biosensors to peroxidase kinetics assays.

text: Deoxycytidine (dC) analogues are widely used to treat solid tumours and blood cancers. However, their clinical efficacy is often limited by resistance mediated by cytidine deaminase (CDA), which converts these drugs into inactive metabolites. Existing CDA inhibitors have limited efficacy and off-target effects, highlighting the need for alternative approaches. Here, we show the development of a CDA biodegrader, an intracellular anti-CDA VHH fused to the SPOP E3 ubiquitin ligase, enabling specific CDA degradation. It effectively depletes CDA in pancreatic, lung, and acute myeloid leukaemia cancer cell lines, increasing sensitivity to dC analogues in vitro. Combined with gemcitabine, the CDA biodegrader inhibits pancreatic and lung tumour growth in vivo.
title: A cytidine deaminase biodegrader sensitises multiple cancer types to deoxycytidine analogue-based chemotherapies.

text: Importantly, mRNA encoding the biodegrader delivered using virus-like particles achieves efficient sensitisation to gemcitabine in vitro and in vivo. This proof-of-concept study establishes targeted CDA degradation as a feasible strategy to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of dC analogues.
title: A cytidine deaminase biodegrader sensitises multiple cancer types to deoxycytidine analogue-based chemotherapies.

text: Infants and toddlers were previously considered to be exempt from Clostridioides difficile -associated disease (CDAD). However, recent studies reported that Clostridioides difficile ( C. difficile ) infection can cause severe gastrointestinal symptoms within this age group, yet the influential risk factors related to CDAD in infants remain unknown. Here, we investigated 27 CDAD cases in infants and toddlers under two and found that the amino acid-based formula (AAF) feeding is a notable risk factor closely associated with the development of CDAD in infants. Infants fed with AAF exhibit reduced levels of Bifidobacteria , which were reported to compete with C. difficile , in their fecal microbiomes. Lastly, we found that mice transplanted with feces from AAF-fed infant donors, compared with those from normal formula (NF)-fed donors, were more susceptible to CDAD.
title: Amino acid-based formula feeding is associated with increased risk of <i>Clostridioides difficile</i>-associated disease in children younger than two years.

text: These findings shed light on the understanding of variables influencing infant CDAD and offer valuable insights for its prevention.
title: Amino acid-based formula feeding is associated with increased risk of <i>Clostridioides difficile</i>-associated disease in children younger than two years.

text: Far‑ultraviolet 222 nm (UV 222 ) effectively activates oxidants to degrade organic micropollutants (OMPs) in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), but its synergy and ecotoxicity with bromide (Br - ) are unclear. This study investigates the synergy of peracetic acid (PAA) and Br - by UV 222 (UV 222 -PB) for OMPs degradation. The system's fluence-based rate constant for model pollutants (0.0159 cm 2 ·mJ -1 ) is 3.01 and 15.74 times that of UV 254 -PB and UV 365 -PB. Radical and theoretical analyses show that far‑ultraviolet strengthens the interaction between PAA and Br - , prolongs radical chains, and boosts organic radicals and reactive bromine species, dominating electron‑rich OMPs oxidation. Correlations of ln(k obs ) with vertical ionization potential and highest occupied molecular orbital energy for 10 OMPs confirm selective oxidation.
title: Bromide-mediated enhancement of far-UVC/peracetic acid process for selective micropollutant abatement.

text: UV 222 -PB performs robustly in various water matrices and shows low ecotoxicity in assays such as seed germination and zebrafish embryo. Life cycle assessment confirms its sustainability. These findings offer insights and guidance for UV 222 -based AOPs in brominated water treatment.
title: Bromide-mediated enhancement of far-UVC/peracetic acid process for selective micropollutant abatement.

text: Nipah virus (NiV) and Hendra virus (HeV) are highly pathogenic paramyxoviruses that produce severe, often fatal disease in humans and animals. Zoonotic spillover of these henipaviruses from the Pteropid bat natural reservoir occurs near-annually in Southeast Asia and Oceania. Outbreaks of NiV disease frequently exceed case fatality rates of 75%, and person-to-person transmission makes controlling outbreaks in low-resource environments challenging. HeV is less transmissible between humans; however, the overall mortality rate is 57%. Approaches to human vaccine development have largely focused on NiV given the larger case burden, and immunogen selection has centered on display of the NiV attachment (G) or fusion (F) surface glycoproteins. However, experimental vaccines displaying these NiV antigens have failed to uniformly cross-protect against HeV disease in preclinical models.
title: A single-cycle, recombinant VSV platform Nipah vaccine cross-protects against Hendra virus in nonhuman primates.

text: The HeV (G) antigen was shown to cross-protect against both HeV and NiV when delivered in a protein subunit form; however, attempts to utilize mRNA or canarypox vectors failed to achieve equivalent protection. We previously developed and evaluated a single-cycle recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus-vectored vaccine displaying the (G) glycoprotein of Nipah virus strain Bangladesh (NiV-B). This experimental vaccine (G*rVSV∆G-NiV-G) demonstrated ideal characteristics of rapid and durable protection against NiV-B challenge in nonhuman primates. In the present work, we show that the G*rVSV∆G-NiV-G vaccine cross-protects against lethal HeV challenge, with the protective response driven by a balance of both cell-mediated and humoral compartments.
title: A single-cycle, recombinant VSV platform Nipah vaccine cross-protects against Hendra virus in nonhuman primates.

text: Illegal wildlife trade (IWT) is a major driver of biodiversity loss, and birds are among the most heavily trafficked taxa. Although China has one of the world's largest wildlife markets, the spatial, temporal, and taxonomic structure of its domestic illegal bird trade remains poorly characterized. We retrieved and analyzed 1427 first-instance criminal verdicts issued between 2014 and 2021 from China Judgments Online, using descriptive and trade-network analyses to identify the key traded species, temporal patterns and major trading regions. The trade involved 19 orders, 48 families and 266 species, of which 37 were listed as threatened (CR, EN and VU) on the Red List of China's Vertebrates and 24 were Class I nationally protected. Psittaciformes appeared in the greatest number of verdicts, and the recorded purposes indicate that they were traded mainly to meet experiential demand.
title: Taxonomic Composition, Trade Networks, and Consumer Demand in China's Illegal Bird Trade: Evidence from Court Verdicts (2014-2021).

text: Annual verdict counts rose steadily from 2014 to 2019 and then declined sharply, reaching 40 in 2021.
