Methods and analysis This is a randomised controlled trial across six centres which includes women (≥16 years old) between 20 and 37 weeks of gestation with suspected pre-eclampsia due to one or more identified symptoms.
title: Cost-effectiveness of the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio and telemonitoring in managing suspected pre-eclampsia: protocol for the PREPARE II randomised controlled trial.

text: For power calculation, we assumed that the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio including a telemonitoring strategy leads to a de-escalation of care by cumulatively reducing the frequency of pre-eclampsia-related hospital admissions and/or outpatient visits in the first week from 50% in the control group to 35% in the intervention group. Considering a loss to follow-up of 5%, a sample size of approximately 470 women is required with 235 women per arm (α=5%; power=90%). The intervention is an algorithm based on the urine protein/creatinine ratio (PCr)+sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, along with a telemonitoring strategy. The algorithm incorporates a PCr cut-off of 30 (mg/mmol) and a sFlt-1/PlGF ratio cut-off of 38 for risk classification.
title: Cost-effectiveness of the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio and telemonitoring in managing suspected pre-eclampsia: protocol for the PREPARE II randomised controlled trial.

text: Subsequent clinical follow-up recommendations are stratified based on this classification: low risk entails no additional follow-up, returning to routine antenatal care; intermediate risk includes telemonitoring; high risk necessitates immediate admission. The primary outcome is the occurrence of pre-eclampsia-related healthcare utilisation in the first week after testing. Secondary outcomes are maternal/perinatal adverse events, total healthcare usage, pre-eclampsia diagnosis, quality of life and productivity losses. A cost-effectiveness analysis from a societal perspective will be performed. Ethics and dissemination Ethical approval was obtained from the Medical Ethics Committee of Leiden University Medical Centre (METC LDD) on 21 July 2025 (reference NL-009295). The results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and presentations at international conferences.
title: Cost-effectiveness of the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio and telemonitoring in managing suspected pre-eclampsia: protocol for the PREPARE II randomised controlled trial.

text: Trial registration NL88527.058.24.
title: Cost-effectiveness of the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio and telemonitoring in managing suspected pre-eclampsia: protocol for the PREPARE II randomised controlled trial.

text: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by epithelial barrier disruption, persistent mucosal inflammation, and progressive intestinal fibrosis, for which effective therapeutic options remain limited. Thymosin β4 (Tβ4) is a highly conserved endogenous peptide with established roles in tissue repair and immune regulation, but its contribution to IBD pathogenesis has not been fully elucidated. Here, we found that TMSB4X, the gene encoding Tβ4, was downregulated in colonic tissues of IBD patients. To investigate its functional significance, we generated Tmsb4x-deficient mice and demonstrated that loss of endogenous Tβ4 markedly increased susceptibility to dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis.
title: Recombinant human Thymosin β4 ameliorates experimental colitis and intestinal fibrosis through suppression of mineralocorticoid receptor signaling.

text: Conversely, oral administration of recombinant human Tβ4 (rhTβ4) significantly improved survival, alleviated body weight loss, reduced epithelial injury, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production in both prophylactic and therapeutic colitis models. Furthermore, rhTβ4 attenuated intestinal fibrosis, as evidenced by reduced expression of fibrosis-associated markers and decreased collagen I deposition. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that rhTβ4 partially restored DSS-induced gene dysregulation and suppressed mineralocorticoid receptor (MR, NR3C2) signaling, a pathway further supported by reporter assays and downstream target gene analyses.
title: Recombinant human Thymosin β4 ameliorates experimental colitis and intestinal fibrosis through suppression of mineralocorticoid receptor signaling.

text: Collectively, these findings identify Tβ4 as an endogenous protective factor against intestinal inflammation and fibrosis and suggest that pharmacological restoration of Tβ4 activity may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for IBD through modulation of mineralocorticoid receptor signaling.
title: Recombinant human Thymosin β4 ameliorates experimental colitis and intestinal fibrosis through suppression of mineralocorticoid receptor signaling.

text: Cancer cachexia is a devastating wasting syndrome with no approved therapies. In this study, we identify the tumor-derived glycoprotein ADAMTSL4 as a circulating factor associated with body weight loss in preclinical cachexia models and patients with colorectal and lung cancers. In mice, Adamtsl4 overexpression converted non-cachexia-inducing tumors into cachexia-inducing tumors, whereas its deletion in cachexia-inducing tumors spared fat and muscle, blunted muscle atrophy signatures, and reduced cachexia severity. ADAMTSL4 engages the latency-associated peptide (LAP) of TGFβ1, promoting local activation of TGFβ1 at muscle cell membranes. Genetic blockade of proTGFβ1 or pharmacologic inhibition of TGFβ signaling reduced ADAMTSL4-dependent wasting in adipocytes and muscle cells. Suppression of tumor-derived ADAMTSL4 attenuated skeletal muscle fibrosis in mice.
title: Tumor-Secreted ADAMTSL4 Activates Latent TGFβ1 to Drive Cancer Cachexia.

text: Together, the association between increased circulating ADAMTSL4 levels and TGFβ-driven muscle atrophy and fibrosis gene signatures in patients with cachectic cancer identifies ADAMTSL4 as an upstream regulator of TGFβ1 and a potential therapeutic target in cancer cachexia. Significance Cancer cachexia lacks effective therapies and remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality. We identify tumor-derived ADAMTSL4 as an upstream regulator of latent TGFβ activation via LAP engagement that promotes multiorgan wasting and fibrosis-related remodeling. Targeting ADAMTSL4 may provide a selective therapeutic strategy without systemic TGFβ pathway blockade. See related commentary by Liu and Janowitz, p. 1964.
title: Tumor-Secreted ADAMTSL4 Activates Latent TGFβ1 to Drive Cancer Cachexia.

text: This exploratory cross-sectional study analyzed owner-reported survey data from 5653 cats belonging to current and prospective customers of a UK fresh cat food company to identify factors associated with body condition in companion cats and to compare owner classifications made using a structured body condition score (BCS) tool with those made by unguided judgment. Owners classified fewer cats as ideal using the structured BCS tool than by unguided judgment, with lower agreement for underweight than for overweight cats. Multivariable logistic regression models were developed for overweight, underweight, and ideal body condition.
title: Diet Formats, Feeding Practices, and Environmental Factors Associated with Overweight, Underweight, and Ideal Body Condition in Household Cats.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: A higher proportion of fresh food was associated with greater odds of ideal body condition (OR 1.22, 95% CI: 1.04-1.42), while dry food was associated with overweight (OR 1.83, 95% CI: 1.33-2.51) and wet food with underweight (OR 1.51, 95% CI: 1.06-2.16), though this association was less robust to differing model specifications. Further associations included certain additional calorie sources, feeding practices, treat type, activity, enrichment, household composition, and established demographic factors. These hypothesis-generating findings highlight a gap between structured and unguided owner assessment and identify associations that merit prospective evaluation in a more generally representative population.
title: Diet Formats, Feeding Practices, and Environmental Factors Associated with Overweight, Underweight, and Ideal Body Condition in Household Cats.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Psychological stress is closely associated with intestinal barrier dysfunction, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, using a 14-day restraint stress mouse model and an HT-29 cell model, we demonstrate that stress-induced elevation of serotonin (5-HT) disrupts intestinal mucosal barrier function through the 5-HT/HTR7/PPAR-γ/NLRP6/autophagy axis. Restraint stress significantly increased 5-HT levels in serum and intestinal tissues, accompanied by reduced goblet cell numbers, impaired mucin 2 secretion, and increased intestinal permeability. Mechanistically, 5-HT acts via HTR7 to downregulate PPAR-γ, which transcriptionally controls NLRP6, thereby suppressing NLRP6 inflammasome activity and autophagy.
title: Psychological Stress Disrupts Goblet Cell Function and Intestinal Barrier via 5-HT/HTR7-Mediated NLRP6 and Autophagy Suppression.

text: Pharmacological inhibition of 5-HT synthesis with PCPA or activation of PPAR-γ with rosiglitazone reversed these pathological phenotypes in vivo, and the 5-HT/HTR7/PPAR-γ axis was further validated in vitro. These findings establish a novel downstream mechanism linking psychological stress to NLRP6 inflammasome dysfunction, impaired autophagy, defective goblet cell function, and intestinal mucosal barrier damage.
title: Psychological Stress Disrupts Goblet Cell Function and Intestinal Barrier via 5-HT/HTR7-Mediated NLRP6 and Autophagy Suppression.

text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes the sexually transmitted infection gonorrhea and is an obligate human pathogen, colonizing the mucosal epithelia of the male urethra and the female endo/ectocervix, resulting in urethritis and cervicitis. These manifestations represent uncomplicated gonorrhea and highlight the gonococcus as a primarily mucosal pathogen. However, gonococci can ascend the female reproductive tract to cause pelvic inflammatory disease and may disseminate to distant anatomical sites. The gonococcus expresses a diverse array of virulence factors that mediate transmission, mucosal colonization, immune modulation, and disease progression. In this review, we outline the mechanisms of gonococcal transmission and colonization of the genital tract epithelium, and examine host-pathogen interactions that drive inflammation, immune evasion, and immune suppression.
title: Pathogenicity and virulence of <i>Neisseria gonorrhoeae</i>.

text: We also discuss the mechanisms underlying dissemination and the resulting spectrum of clinical outcomes. Continued investigation of gonococcal biology and host interactions will advance understanding of pathogenesis and support the development of improved treatments and preventative vaccines.
title: Pathogenicity and virulence of <i>Neisseria gonorrhoeae</i>.

text: Drug repurposing has emerged as an attractive strategy in contemporary pharmaceutical research, presenting an opportunity to expedite drug discovery, minimize developmental costs, and mitigate risks associated with developing new pharmaceuticals. In this study, we investigated a novel approach based on deep learning of human transcriptomic mechanisms for systematic identification of additional therapeutic potential in preexisting drugs. We trained a composite feedforward neural network model using gene expression data sourced from the ARCHS4 compilation of the GEO, encompassing extensive human datasets. Subsequently, disease-associated gene expression data were generated from our stem cell-derived in vitro model of cardiac hypertrophy induced by Endothelin-1 stimulation.
title: Leveraging neural network models for drug repurposing: a case study on cardiac hypertrophy.

text: These data were employed to identify latent variables associated with genes showing differential expression due to Endothelin-1 stimulation. By examining the differential expression profiles within the model's latent space, we successfully correlated the disease signal with known drug targets found in pharmaceutical compounds cataloged in DrugBank. The model accurately encoded additional disease-related genes beyond the curated gene set, demonstrating its ability to generalize disease associations. Leveraging the model, we identified potential drug candidates, such as lapatinib and amiodarone showing promise in mitigating proBNP concentration associated with cardiac hypertrophy.
title: Leveraging neural network models for drug repurposing: a case study on cardiac hypertrophy.

text: This study demonstrates the power of deep learning of human transcriptomic mechanisms in swiftly identifying new therapeutic potentials for existing drugs, highlighting the pivotal role of artificial intelligence technologies in accelerating drug development for other complex medical conditions.
title: Leveraging neural network models for drug repurposing: a case study on cardiac hypertrophy.

text: Objectives This case series aims to describe the use of video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for the treatment of pectus excavatum. Materials and methods Six male, intact kittens, with a median age of 3.3 months (range, 2.5 to 4 months) and median weight of 1.75 kg (range, 0.44 to 2 kg), were presented to one of two referral institutions for evaluation of a concave sternal deformity. On presentation the kittens were found to have radiographically moderate (n = 3) to severe (n = 3) pectus excavatum of the caudal sternum with mild to moderate respiratory signs reported at home. Surgical correction included the use of video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery to facilitate external sternal splint placement.
title: Experience with video-assisted thoracoscopic placement of pectus excavatum splints in kittens: six cases.
journal: The Journal of small animal practice

text: Use of video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery allowed for direct visualisation of needle passage to place the circumsternal sutures, potentially reducing the risk of complications given the proximity of intrathoracic vasculature and organs. Results All patients recovered from anaesthesia uneventfully, and post-operative thoracic radiographs revealed reduction in sternal concavity and increase in thoracic height at the level of the original deformities. One cat suffered respiratory arrest 36 hours post-operatively for unknown reasons. Clinical significance Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery-assisted external splint placement for pectus excavatum may help reduce intraoperative risks associated with pectus excavatum repair, though additional research is warranted.
title: Experience with video-assisted thoracoscopic placement of pectus excavatum splints in kittens: six cases.
journal: The Journal of small animal practice

text: Tremorgenic mycotoxicosis is a well-recognized cause of acute neurotoxicosis in dogs, most commonly associated with penitrem A (PTA), which is mainly produced by Penicillium crustosum. However, analytical confirmation of such cases is rare. This study describes five clinical cases of canine tremorgenic mycotoxicosis in Germany, together with comprehensive analytical confirmation. All dogs had been presented at the veterinary clinic of Justus-Liebig-University because of acute-onset generalized tremors. Clinical findings, therapeutic measures and final outcome were documented. Samples of gastric content (induced emesis or gastric lavage) and blood serum (if available) were analyzed for several neurotoxic mycotoxins, penitrems A-F, paxilline (PAX), α-cyclopiazonic acid (CPA), and ergoline alkaloids. Analysis was done by enzyme immunoassay (EIA), and by HPLC-MS/MS.
title: Five cases of tremorgenic mycotoxicosis in dogs - clinical aspects and analytical methods.

text: EIA of gastric content was positive for PTA in all samples, and for PAX, CPA, and ergoline alkaloids in some. HPLC-MS/MS analysis confirmed the presence of penitrems A-F, PAX, and CPA. Trace levels of PTA, PAX and CPA were also detected in serum samples. Penitrem producing P. crustosum was isolated from gastric content of all animals. This is the first full analytical study on acute canine tremorgenic mycotoxicoses in Germany, and presents comprehensive results along the causal chain of tremorgenic mycotoxicosis. In addition to the penitrems, several other neurotoxic mycotoxins (PAX, CPA, ergoline alkaloids) may play a role in canine mycotoxicosis. While immediate stabilisation and symptomatic treatment are paramount, prompt mycotoxin testing can help identify the source of poisoning during differential diagnosis.
title: Five cases of tremorgenic mycotoxicosis in dogs - clinical aspects and analytical methods.

text: Objective To determine the use of resting serum cortisol concentration as a marker of outcome and illness severity as assessed by the Acute Patient Physiologic and Laboratory Evaluation (APPLE) full and fast scores in critically ill dogs with and without systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS). Design Prospective, observational study. Setting University teaching hospital. Animals Client-owned dogs were enrolled into three different groups: SIRS (30 dogs), non-SIRS (25), and healthy controls (19). Dogs with acute critical illness ( Interventions None.
title: Resting Cortisol Concentration as a Predictor of Illness Severity in Critically Ill Dogs With Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome.
journal: Journal of veterinary emergency and critical care (San Antonio, Tex. : 2001)

text: Measurements and results Resting serum cortisol concentrations were higher in the SIRS and non-SIRS groups compared with the control group (p full scores were higher in the SIRS group compared with the non-SIRS (p full scores increased by 1 (95% CI: 0.6-1.4) for every increase of 62.5 nmol/L (2.2 µg/dL) in resting serum cortisol concentration. Resting serum cortisol concentrations were not associated with mortality (p = 0.33). There was moderate evidence that APPLE full scores can predict mortality (p = 0.03). Conclusions Resting serum cortisol concentrations can be used as a marker of illness severity in critically ill patients with SIRS. Further studies enrolling larger numbers of cases may clarify its potential as a marker of outcome.
title: Resting Cortisol Concentration as a Predictor of Illness Severity in Critically Ill Dogs With Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome.
journal: Journal of veterinary emergency and critical care (San Antonio, Tex. : 2001)

text: Prostatitis is one of the most common prostatic disorders in dogs, although its ultrasonographic features remain poorly characterized. The aim of this retrospective study was to describe the ultrasonographic findings of canine prostatitis and prostatic abscessation and to investigate their association with clinical and laboratory abnormalities. Medical records of 35 client-owned dogs with cytologically or histologically confirmed acute prostatitis were reviewed. Clinical, ultrasonographic, laboratory, bacteriological, treatment, and follow-up data were collected. The most common ultrasonographic findings were inhomogeneous parenchymal echotexture, intraparenchymal cystic lesions, capsular edema, periprostatic steatitis, and asymmetry of the prostatic lobes. Prostatic abscesses were detected in 25 dogs and showed marked variability in size and morphology.
title: Ultrasonographic Appearance of Acute Prostatitis and Prostatic Abscesses in Dogs.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Abscess diameter was positively correlated with body weight ( p = 0.001; rho = 0.6) and negatively correlated with the percentage of neutrophils with toxic granulation ( p = 0.02; rho = -0.4). Most dogs recovered following medical or combined medical-surgical treatment. Follow-up examinations demonstrated resolution of the inflammatory changes surrounding the prostate, whereas parenchymal inhomogeneous echotexture frequently persisted. These findings provide a comprehensive ultrasonographic description of canine prostatitis and support the use of ultrasonography as a valuable tool for diagnosis and follow-up.
title: Ultrasonographic Appearance of Acute Prostatitis and Prostatic Abscesses in Dogs.

text: Hemerocallis citrina Baroni, commonly known as daylily or "Huang Hua Cai," is a well-established traditional medicinal and edible plant widely cultivated in East Asia for more than two millennia. Its flower buds, stems, leaves, and roots are rich in flavonoids and phenolic compounds, which constitute the principal bioactive phytochemicals responsible for a wide range of pharmacological effects, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, neuroprotective, antidepressant, and sleep-improving activities. Although several studies have investigated the chemical composition of Hemerocallis citrina Baroni, a comprehensive and up-to-date review specifically focused on the flavonoids and phenolic compounds of this plant remains lacking.
title: <i>Hemerocallis citrina</i> Baroni (Daylily): A Comprehensive Review of Flavonoids and Phenolic Compounds-Extraction, Phytochemistry, Biological Activities, and Food Applications (2000-2026).

text: In this review, we systematically summarize the research progress from 2000 to 2026 on the extraction methods, structural identification, phytochemical profiles, and biological activities of flavonoids and phenolic compounds from H. citrina flower buds, stems, and leaves. Advanced analytical techniques, such as UPLC-PDA/MS, UHPLC-QQQ-MS/MS, and HPLC-Q-TOF-MS, have revealed a diverse array of these compounds, including quercetin, kaempferol, and isorhamnetin glycosides, as well as various caffeoyl- and p -coumaroylquinic acids. The health-promoting effects of these polyphenols, together with current knowledge on their mechanisms of action and potential applications in functional foods and traditional Chinese medicine, are critically discussed.
title: <i>Hemerocallis citrina</i> Baroni (Daylily): A Comprehensive Review of Flavonoids and Phenolic Compounds-Extraction, Phytochemistry, Biological Activities, and Food Applications (2000-2026).

text: By consolidating recent phytochemical and pharmacological findings, this review provides a scientific foundation for the further development and utilization of H. citrina flavonoids and phenolic compounds as valuable resources for functional foods, nutraceuticals, and natural therapeutics.
title: <i>Hemerocallis citrina</i> Baroni (Daylily): A Comprehensive Review of Flavonoids and Phenolic Compounds-Extraction, Phytochemistry, Biological Activities, and Food Applications (2000-2026).

text: Background The European Union is currently facing a demographic, digital, and environmental transition collectively known as the triple transition. Although these trends significantly impact long-term care services, they have typically been studied in isolation, overlooking potential synergies between the adoption of digital tools and environmental practices among informal caregivers of older adults. This study uniquely bridges this gap by applying an integrative social-ecological-infrastructural systems framework to examine how these transitions interact in everyday caregiving contexts. Objective This study examined the relationship between the use of digital tools and eco-friendly practices among informal caregivers of older adults across the European Union and whether the adoption of digital solutions related differently to specific types of eco-friendly behaviors.
title: Use of Digital Tools and Environmental Practices Among Informal Caregivers of Older Adults in the European Union Embracing the Triple Transition: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: Unlike previous research focusing on isolated aspects of each transition, we examined their interconnections, providing empirical evidence for developing integrated policy approaches. Methods Using data from the Survey of Gender Gaps in Unpaid Care, Individual and Social Activities project (n=5761 informal caregivers of adults aged ≥65 years), we analyzed the association between frequency of use of digital tools for caregiving and environmental practices. We used the social-ecological-infrastructural systems conceptual framework and the theory of planned behavior (TPB) to interpret findings. Analyses included descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, and multilevel mixed-effects regression models.
title: Use of Digital Tools and Environmental Practices Among Informal Caregivers of Older Adults in the European Union Embracing the Triple Transition: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: Results A weak positive association was observed between the frequency of use of digital tools and environmentally sustainable behaviors (ρ=0.28; P P =.23) and mindful consumption of natural resources (ρ=-0.02; P >.99). Respondents using digital tools daily had scores of environmentally sustainable behavior (SESBs) 22% higher than nonusers. Demographic patterns revealed higher use of digital tools among younger, more educated, and employed caregivers, indicating that any potential digital-environmental co-occurrence may be unevenly distributed across the caregiver population. Conclusions The use of digital tools may be related to environmental behavior through improved access to information, peer norms, and a greater perceived ability to act, though these mechanisms were not directly tested.
title: Use of Digital Tools and Environmental Practices Among Informal Caregivers of Older Adults in the European Union Embracing the Triple Transition: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: The stronger associations with consumption-related behaviors indicate that digital platforms may be particularly relevant to caregivers' access to eco-friendly products, second-hand goods, fair-trade options, and sustainable local services. By contrast, the lack of statistically significant correlations with recycling and resource conservation suggests that digital solutions alone may be insufficient to address behaviors that depend on structural conditions, physical infrastructure, local service availability, or established household routines. Policies should consider digital inclusion, caregiver support, and green infrastructure as interconnected areas while ensuring that older, less educated, and more burdened caregivers are not excluded from these potential co-benefits.
title: Use of Digital Tools and Environmental Practices Among Informal Caregivers of Older Adults in the European Union Embracing the Triple Transition: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: Giardia duodenalis is a common intestinal protozoan parasite in dogs, but the systemic immune response associated with canine giardiasis remains incompletely characterized. This study aimed to evaluate serum concentrations of immunoglobulin E (IgE), interleukin-4 (IL-4), and interleukin-13 (IL-13) as Th2-associated immune markers in naturally infected dogs. Thirty client-owned dogs with confirmed giardiasis and 10 clinically healthy control dogs were included in the study. Serum IgE, IL-4, and IL-13 concentrations were measured using canine-specific enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Between-group comparisons were performed using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests, with Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons, and effect estimates were calculated using the Hodges-Lehmann method. Spearman's rank correlation was used to assess associations among biomarkers within each group.
title: Serum IgE, IL-4 and IL-13 Concentrations as Th2-Associated Biomarkers in Canine Giardiasis.

text: Serum IL-4 concentrations were significantly higher in dogs with giardiasis than in control dogs (median 38.12 [IQR 32.55-57.97] vs. 23.65 [18.86-27.90] pg/mL; Mann-Whitney U = 238.5, Holm-adjusted p p = 0.125), while IL-13 concentrations did not differ between groups (78.23 [53.05-103.42] vs. 79.05 [65.44-103.68] ng/L; Holm-adjusted p = 0.988). Within the giardiasis group, IgE, IL-4, and IL-13 concentrations were significantly and positively correlated with one another (ρ = 0.644-0.690, p p = 0.048). These findings provide evidence consistent with altered Th2-associated immune activity in canine giardiasis, characterized by a significant elevation of serum IL-4 and coordinated variation among Th2-associated biomarkers.
title: Serum IgE, IL-4 and IL-13 Concentrations as Th2-Associated Biomarkers in Canine Giardiasis.

text: The non-significant findings for serum IgE and IL-13 may reflect a selective pattern of systemic Th2-associated biomarker expression, although limited statistical power prevents exclusion of smaller between-group differences. Further studies incorporating intestinal mucosal measurements and longitudinal assessment are warranted to clarify the relationship between systemic and local immune responses in canine giardiasis.
title: Serum IgE, IL-4 and IL-13 Concentrations as Th2-Associated Biomarkers in Canine Giardiasis.

text: Background The gut-brain axis (GBA) represents a paradigm shift in veterinary neuropharmacology, offering novel approaches for managing neurological and behavioural disorders in companion animals. Objectives This review synthesizes current evidence on the bidirectional communication between the gut microbiome and the central nervous system, examining the neural, endocrine, immune, and metabolic pathways that facilitate this dialogue. We explore the unique aspects of canine and feline microbiomes and their implications for species-specific drug development and critically evaluate emerging pharmacological strategies, including psychobiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics and faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), highlighting their clinical applications in conditions ranging from anxiety and aggression to cognitive dysfunction and epilepsy.
title: Targeting the Gut-Brain Axis: Pharmacological Modulation of the Microbiome for Neurological and Behavioural Disorders in Companion Animals.

text: Methods This narrative review followed established guidelines for evidence synthesis in veterinary medicine. A comprehensive literature search was performed using PubMed, Google Scholar and Scopus databases covering publications from January 2011 to March 2026. Results While promising results have been demonstrated with specific strains, such as Bifidobacterium longum BL999 and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum PS128, significant challenges remain. These include methodological limitations in microbiome research, the predominance of correlative over causal evidence and the need for standardized diagnostic tools. Conclusions Future directions must prioritize large-scale longitudinal studies, robust clinical trials and advanced multi-omics approaches to establish causal mechanisms and develop personalized, microbiome-targeted therapies.
title: Targeting the Gut-Brain Axis: Pharmacological Modulation of the Microbiome for Neurological and Behavioural Disorders in Companion Animals.

text: Realizing this potential requires a shift from correlative data to causal mechanisms, from a one-size-fits-all approach to species-specific therapeutics and from rodent models to rigorous trials in dogs and cats.
title: Targeting the Gut-Brain Axis: Pharmacological Modulation of the Microbiome for Neurological and Behavioural Disorders in Companion Animals.

text: Respiratory disease remains highly prevalent in pig production and constitutes a major health and welfare challenge worldwide. However, most studies assessing pig welfare impairment from respiratory disease rely on isolated animal-based indicators, limiting integration across welfare domains. This study aimed to quantify welfare impairment from respiratory disease in fattening pigs (8-10 weeks of age) using indicators aligned with the Five Domains Model. A survey using adaptive conjoint analysis was conducted with animal welfare researchers (n = 32) and practising swine veterinarians (n = 22). Respondents completed pairwise comparisons of profiles defined by combinations of five welfare indicators-appetite, coughing, respiratory distress, play behaviour, and exploratory behaviour-each expressed at increasing severity levels.
title: Quantifying welfare impairment from respiratory disease in fattening pigs using adaptive conjoint analysis.

text: Based on respondents' choices of which profile represented greater welfare impairment, indicator importance scores and level-specific contributions to pig welfare impairment from respiratory disease were estimated. Across respondent groups, severe respiratory distress was perceived as the largest contributor to pig welfare impairment from respiratory disease, with an estimated contribution of 29.8%, followed by repeated coughing (+ 22.7%) and complete loss of appetite (+ 19.2%). Reductions in play and exploratory behaviour were perceived to contribute comparatively less to welfare impairment from respiratory disease but remained relevant. Agreement between researchers and veterinarians was high, with statistically significant differences limited to occasional coughing and complete loss of play behaviour.
title: Quantifying welfare impairment from respiratory disease in fattening pigs using adaptive conjoint analysis.

text: In addition, profiles representing single-pathogen respiratory infections were constructed based on expert elicitation, providing an illustrative demonstration of how outcomes from adaptive conjoint analysis may be used to assess welfare impairment under different respiratory disease scenarios. The findings of this study may inform refinement of welfare assessment protocols, support the integration of welfare metrics into epidemiological models, and enable comparison of disease scenarios. However, results should be interpreted with caution, as they reflect perceived rather than directly measured welfare impairment and assume independence between biologically interrelated indicators.
title: Quantifying welfare impairment from respiratory disease in fattening pigs using adaptive conjoint analysis.

text: Future work should prioritise the application of welfare impairment estimates to biologically realistic welfare profiles in which interrelated indicators co-occur, while also exploring integration with observational approaches and extension to broader, multifactorial welfare contexts.
title: Quantifying welfare impairment from respiratory disease in fattening pigs using adaptive conjoint analysis.

text: Assessment of oral mucosal colour is widely used in equine clinical and welfare evaluations, but inconsistent terminology limits comparison between clinical observations and research studies. This study evaluates, as an initial proof-of-concept, the Uldahl Standard for systematically describing mucosal colour and saturation. Gingival and lingual mucosae were assessed in clinically normal horses, healthy horses sedated for routine dental procedures, and horses with severe systemic circulatory compromise. Photographic colour samples validated against in vivo observations were classified using Munsell notation, ISCC-NBS terminology and the Uldahl Standard. Three illustrative cases of tongue discolouration were additionally assessed.
title: Assessment of Oral Mucosal Colour in Horses: Initial Application of the Uldahl Standard Across Physiological States.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Descriptive analyses characterised colour and saturation across physiological states, while clinically normal and sedated horses were compared using exact chi-square tests and logistic regression. Overall, 42 unique colour-saturation combinations were identified. Chromatic diversity increased with physiological compromise. Primary colour differed significantly between clinically normal and sedated horses for both gingival ( p = 0.05) and lingual ( p = 0.004) mucosae, whereas secondary colour and saturation did not. Grey was significantly associated with physiological state in both gingival ( p = 0.05) and lingual ( p = 0.03) mucosae. It showed high specificity but low sensitivity, including 100% specificity for lingual grey. Purple occurred only in sedated and systemically compromised horses, while blue occurred only as a secondary colour in systemically compromised horses.
title: Assessment of Oral Mucosal Colour in Horses: Initial Application of the Uldahl Standard Across Physiological States.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: The findings demonstrate the feasibility of applying the Uldahl Standard to equine oral mucosal assessment and suggest that primary colour, particularly grey, may provide greater discriminatory information than secondary colour or saturation. Further studies are required to establish the diagnostic relevance of broader colour-saturation patterns.
title: Assessment of Oral Mucosal Colour in Horses: Initial Application of the Uldahl Standard Across Physiological States.

text: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely due to limitations in early diagnosis and effective treatment. To address these challenges, we developed a multifunctional probiotic nanoplatform, EcNA@Cur-Lip-FA, that integrates real-time diagnosis, targeted therapy, and immune modulation for enhanced CRC treatment. Specifically, this system leverages genetically engineered Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) encoding acoustic reporter genes (ARGs) to produce ultrasound (US)-responsive gas vesicles (GVs), enabling real-time, noninvasive tumor imaging. Simultaneously, folic acid (FA)-modified curcumin-loaded liposomes (Cur-Lip-FA) are co-delivered with EcN, enhancing tumor-specific accumulation and therapeutic precision.
title: Genetically Engineered Probiotic Nanoplatform for Ultrasound-Enhanced Colorectal Cancer Therapy via Targeted Delivery, Immune Modulation, and Anti-Angiogenesis.

text: After being taken up by tumor cells, curcumin is released locally upon exposure to US irradiation, generating reactive oxygen species (ROS), inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD), and activating the cGAS-STING pathway to promote dendritic cells (DCs) maturation and robust CD4 + /CD8 + T-cell responses. Additionally, EcNA@Cur-Lip-FA downregulates angiogenesis-related factors (VEGF, VEGFR1, and ANGPT1), thereby inhibiting tumor neovascularization. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that EcNA@Cur-Lip-FA enables precise tumor localization, dynamic imaging, and effective suppression of both primary CRC and metastatic liver lesions with favorable biocompatibility. This multifunctional platform offers a promising strategy for integrating diagnosis and treatment, paving the way for next-generation CRC theranostics.
title: Genetically Engineered Probiotic Nanoplatform for Ultrasound-Enhanced Colorectal Cancer Therapy via Targeted Delivery, Immune Modulation, and Anti-Angiogenesis.

text: Purpose Evaluate whether adding pan-mucosal irradiation (50 Gy) reduces recurrence or improves survival in head and neck carcinoma of unknown primary. Methods and materials Retrospective 2-center analysis (center 1, 2009-2018, and center 2, 2005-2023). All patients underwent neck dissection with adjuvant irradiation to lymphatic drainage or definitive radiochemotherapy; center 2 additionally received 50 Gy pan-mucosal irradiation to the upper aerodigestive tract. Definitive radiation therapy/chemoradiation therapy was used for advanced nodal disease. Results Of 164 screened, 134 were included (center 1, n = 88, and center 2, n = 46). Median follow-up was 72 months (95% CI, 48-96). Sixty-five patients (42%) died (37 vs 28). Overall survival did not differ between centers (log-rank P = .899).
title: Comparable Outcomes Without Routine Pan-mucosal Irradiation in Head and Neck Carcinoma of Unknown Primary.

text: Combining centers 1 and 2, there were 39 recurrences in 134 patients; 24 out of 88 patients (27.3%) in center 1 and 15 out of 46 patients in center 2 (32.6%), P = .519. There were no differences noted in time-to-event analysis (log-rank P = .724). Mucosal recurrences occurred in 13 patients (9 vs 4; P = .282); all arose more than 36 months after diagnosis and exclusively in persistent smokers. Conclusion In thoroughly staged head and neck carcinoma of unknown primary, adding pan-mucosal irradiation to standard nodal irradiation was not associated with improved survival or lower mucosal recurrence rates compared with nodal-only fields. The late occurrence of mucosal events and their association with persistent smoking suggest second primary tumors rather than missed index lesions.
title: Comparable Outcomes Without Routine Pan-mucosal Irradiation in Head and Neck Carcinoma of Unknown Primary.

text: Given potential toxicity and quality-of-life trade-offs, routine pan-mucosal irradiation may not be warranted, and treatment should be individualized.
title: Comparable Outcomes Without Routine Pan-mucosal Irradiation in Head and Neck Carcinoma of Unknown Primary.

text: Malignant gliomas are the most common primary brain tumors, with dismal outcomes. Pet dogs have been proposed as a valuable model for studying gliomas. Here, we compare spontaneously occurring gliomas from adult and pediatric human and canine patients, focusing on the tumor microenvironment (TME) and the canonical pathways of human glioma dysregulation (RTK/RAS/PI(3)K, p53 and Rb). Transcriptomic, genomic, and methylation data from adult, pediatric, and canine samples were evaluated. Across cohorts, aberrant signaling in the three canonical pathways correlated with increasing tumor grade. Canine high-grade glioma (HGG) showed extensive pathway dysregulation, especially when incorporating differentially expressed genes such as TP53. PDGFRA was a key driver of glioma in purebred brachycephalic ("short-skulled") dogs. IDH1 mutations and hypermethylation were concentrated in adult tumors.
title: The Same, but Different: Shared Hallmarks and Divergent Drivers in Adult, Pediatric and Canine Glioma.

text: Both species exhibited increased neutrophils, M2 macrophages, and regulatory T cells, coupled with depletion of key antitumor effectors. PD-1 and PD-L1 immune checkpoint biology was similarly preserved. Canine glioma seems to occupy a "middle ground" between pediatric and adult. Methylation patterns mirrored pediatric glioma, yet immune infiltration and pathway activation resembled adult HGG. Complex heterogeneity between patients was a major similarity between species. Despite different driver mutations, dogs and humans converge on a similar malignant, immune-suppressed TME.
title: The Same, but Different: Shared Hallmarks and Divergent Drivers in Adult, Pediatric and Canine Glioma.

text: Amyloidosis is a disease characterized by the deposition of abnormally folded proteins as amyloid fibrils in tissues and occurs in various mammals and birds. In some cases, amyloids derived from two different precursor proteins may coexist in the same individual, a condition known as double amyloidosis. Amyloid A (AA) amyloidosis is known to occur frequently in birds; however, little is known about other types of amyloidosis. In the present study, we report a case of amyloidosis in a Humboldt penguin involving two distinct types of amyloids. Histopathological examination, transmission electron microscopy, mass spectrometry-based proteomic analysis, and immunohistochemistry revealed the concurrent occurrence of fibrinogen Aα-chain (FibA) amyloidosis and AA amyloidosis.
title: Concurrent fibrinogen Aα-chain amyloidosis and AA amyloidosis in a Humboldt penguin (Spheniscus humboldti).

text: FibA-derived and AA amyloid deposits exhibited distinct nodular and diffuse morphologies, respectively, suggesting that their deposition patterns may provide a morphological clue for distinguishing between the two types of amyloids. To our knowledge, this is the first case of FibA amyloidosis in a penguin and the first report of the concurrent occurrence of two distinct types of systemic amyloidosis in a bird.
title: Concurrent fibrinogen Aα-chain amyloidosis and AA amyloidosis in a Humboldt penguin (Spheniscus humboldti).

text: The tolerability and efficacy of treatment with allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (aAMSCs) were evaluated in dogs with kidney disease secondary to canine leishmaniosis (CanL). In this non-blinded, single-center, 3-month study, twenty dogs received either conventional treatment (CT; n = 10) or conventional treatment plus an intravenous dose of aAMSCs (CT + aAMSCs; n = 10). Efficacy was assessed at days 0, 30, and 90 using plasma and urinary biomarkers. In both groups (CT, n = 6; CT + aAMSCs, n = 7), glomerular filtration rate was estimated by scintigraphy, and urinary proteomics was performed. No serious adverse events were observed, although two dogs experienced transient gastrointestinal events. No significant between-group differences occurred in renal parameters at time points.
title: Evaluation of the Tolerability and Efficacy of Adjuvant Treatment with Adipose Mesenchymal Stem/Stromal Cells in Dogs with Kidney Disease Secondary to Leishmaniosis.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Intragroup analyses showed significant reductions in uNGAL/c in both groups and UPCR only in CT + aAMSCs. Longitudinal mixed-effects analyses revealed no significant group × time interactions for any of the evaluated variables. Urinary proteomics identified four protein entries with higher abundance in the CT + aAMSCs group at T90, although UMAP showed no separation between groups. A single intravenous aAMSCs dose was well tolerated but provided no renal benefits over conventional treatment. Further studies should evaluate alternative dosing protocols.
title: Evaluation of the Tolerability and Efficacy of Adjuvant Treatment with Adipose Mesenchymal Stem/Stromal Cells in Dogs with Kidney Disease Secondary to Leishmaniosis.

text: Cats frequently develop myocardial remodeling, for example, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, affecting 14.7% of domestic cats compared to 0.2% of humans, with shared genetic features making them relevant to human disease. Yet features distinguishing clinical outcomes such as heart failure and arterial thromboembolism remain poorly characterized. Using artificial-intelligence-based digital pathology and Oxford Nanopore sequencing, we analyzed myocardial tissue from 37 cats grouped by outcome: arterial thromboembolism, congestive heart failure, or no documented cardiac disease. Myocardial fibrosis was significantly higher in cats with arterial thromboembolism, indicating a distinct fibrotic phenotype. Cats with heart failure showed nuclear hypertrophy, while cats with arterial thromboembolism had increased numbers of small, hematoxylin-dense non-myocyte nuclei.
title: Phenotypic patterns in feline heart failure: A natural model for understanding variable disease severity in humans.

text: Higher fibrosis was associated with downregulation of mitochondrial and cardiac conduction genes, and nuclear size correlated with proteostasis and stress-response pathways. This multimodal framework reveals distinct histological and molecular profiles by outcome, with relevance for translational hypertrophic cardiomyopathy research.
title: Phenotypic patterns in feline heart failure: A natural model for understanding variable disease severity in humans.

text: Trypanosoma brucei and Leishmania tarentolae are model kinetoplastids whose mitochondria contain a unique DNA network, kinetoplast DNA (kDNA), and exhibit specialized features, including developmental remodeling and RNA editing. By integrating mass spectrometry-based protein correlation profiling with published datasets, we assembled inventories of 1,666 mitochondrial proteins in T. brucei and 1,594 in L. tarentolae. These include 124 polypeptides not previously recognized as mitochondrial. Despite their phylogenetic distance, trypanosomes and leishmanias maintain highly conserved mitoproteomes, including about 700 components with no detectable homologs in other eukaryotes. Comparison of T.
title: Lineage-specific innovations expand mitochondrial proteomes in kinetoplastids.

text: brucei insect and mammalian stages revealed similar mitoproteome compositions but globally reduced mitochondrial protein abundance in the latter, except for components of calcium homeostasis and the alternative oxidase pathway. We also detected ten kDNA-encoded proteins, including products of pan-edited transcripts. These inventories establish a framework for functional analysis of previously uncharacterized mitochondrial factors and illuminate innovations that have shaped kinetoplastid evolution.
title: Lineage-specific innovations expand mitochondrial proteomes in kinetoplastids.

text: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) are sub epithelial soft tissue neoplasms in the gastrointestinal tract. Extragastrointestinal stromal tumors (E-GISTs) are rare, comprising 5%-7% of GISTs. A case of a 65-year-old female with abdominal bloating, heaviness, and constipation is reported. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a mass in the ischioanal region, initially thought to be a solitary fibrous tumor. The mass was completely excised, and pathological examination confirmed it as a C-Kit Negative E-GIST. This case highlights the rarity and uniqueness of the ischioanal mass detected through pelvic MRI.
title: Extra gastrointestinal stromal tumor (EGIST) of the ischioanal space detected on pelvic MRI.

text: There is growing interest in natural bioactive compounds as potentially safer and more sustainable sources of therapeutic agents. Terpenoids, one of the most structurally diverse and biologically active classes of natural products, are derived from repeating isoprene units and possess a broad range of pharmacological and industrial applications. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in terpenoid biosynthesis, structural classification, and therapeutic applications. It also discusses emerging approaches for enhancing large-scale production, improving functional efficacy, and overcoming pharmacokinetic limitations. Attention is given to terpenoids currently undergoing clinical evaluation, along with their progress toward commercial development.
title: Terpenoids: A Comprehensive Review on Biosynthesis, Applications and Enhancement Strategies for Translational Research.

text: Despite substantial preclinical evidence supporting their therapeutic potential, the clinical translation of many terpenoids remains limited. Key challenges include poor aqueous solubility, low permeability, slow dissolution, and high lipophilicity, which can collectively restrict systemic bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy. Moreover, only a relatively small proportion of biologically active terpenoids have progressed to advanced stages of clinical development, highlighting a considerable gap between experimental findings and clinical application. This review integrates current knowledge of terpenoid biosynthesis, biological activities, production strategies, and translational development while highlighting sustainable and scientifically driven approaches that may facilitate their future therapeutic and commercial utilization.
title: Terpenoids: A Comprehensive Review on Biosynthesis, Applications and Enhancement Strategies for Translational Research.

text: Purpose of review Implementation of falls prevention programs at scale remains challenging due to resource constraints, clinic dependency and inequitable access. We critically review digital health technologies and map these to the World Falls Guidelines (WFG) risk-stratified pathway, from risk screening to intervention delivery, appraising the evidence, clinical readiness and implementation challenges. Recent findings Self-managed digital exercise programs have the strongest evidence base, with three trials demonstrating reductions in falls among community-living older people and economic data supporting cost-effectiveness in those with a history of falls. Other technologies demonstrate feasibility, but none has demonstrated falls reduction in adequately powered trials. Implementation evidence is emerging but concentrated in high-income, digitally literate populations.
title: Digital Health Interventions for Falls Prevention in Older People.

text: Mapped to the WFG pathway, digital exercise programs are ready for routine implementation; realising broader potential requires regulatory frameworks that set evidence standards for digital products, funding models that support digital care and sustained commitment to equitable access across the diversity of older people.
title: Digital Health Interventions for Falls Prevention in Older People.

text: Background Skin NTDs cause mental ill health, primarily through social stigma and discrimination, overburdening services and undermining elimination efforts. A holistic One Health (OH) approach is essential for NTD elimination, but evidence and operational guidance lack. This scoping review documents the current state of integration of mental health and OH-based skin-NTD programmes. It forms part of a series of reviews on the role of OH in skin NTDs, led by the WHO skin NTD working groups. Methodology We searched four peer-reviewed databases for terms related to skin NTDs, OH, mental health and social determinants of health (SDH). Peer-reviewed articles exploring all four concepts were eligible, with no language/geographical/time constraints. Grey literature, conference abstracts and non-peer-reviewed materials were excluded.
title: Mental health, social determinants and One Health in skin neglected tropical diseases (NTDs): A scoping review.

text: Abstract screening and extraction was supported by ASreview and NotebookLM. Outcomes related to mental health, OH/SDH and skin NTDs were analysed and charted, using a descriptive thematic analysis approach. Principal findings Twenty-two papers were included; predominantly quantitative studies in Africa, focused on cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL), with few intervention studies. Mental health was typically explored as a downstream effect (primarily stigma and distress), with limited use of validated instruments. Few studies meaningfully embedded OH approaches, including cross-sectoral collaboration and changes were rarely attributed to climate change. A theoretical framework for the multi-directional and intersectional relationship between mental health, SDH and OH is presented.
title: Mental health, social determinants and One Health in skin neglected tropical diseases (NTDs): A scoping review.

text: Conclusions/significance The underlying mechanisms of mental health remain poorly characterised, with a lack of integrated OH thinking. Exposure to skin NTDs is generally due to lack of agency and choice. Evidence on the role of household economic conditions and climate change in relation to mental health and skin NTDs lacks. Participatory research has a critical role to play in co-designing nuanced OH-informed interventions, but it is critical that we build on identified synergies within existing frameworks, including person-centred care and syndemics.
title: Mental health, social determinants and One Health in skin neglected tropical diseases (NTDs): A scoping review.

text: Background/Objectives : Cardiovascular involvement is among the most consequential sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection. Myocardial injury, arrhythmia, and thromboembolic disease have been characterized in depth, yet the relationship between COVID-19 and valvular heart disease (VHD), and its interplay with heart failure (HF), has received comparatively limited synthesis. This narrative review consolidates current evidence on the mechanisms, diagnosis, differential assessment, and clinical outcomes linking acute and post-acute COVID-19 to valvular dysfunction and to incident or worsening heart failure, with emphasis on practical implications for cardiologists and internists.
title: Valvular Heart Disease and Heart Failure in the Post-COVID-19 Era: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Diagnosis, Differential Assessment, and Clinical Outcomes.

text: Methods : We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2020-January 2026) for studies on valvular dysfunction, heart failure, myocardial injury, and endothelial pathology in SARS-CoV-2 infection, and synthesized findings narratively. Results : Convergent pathways-endothelial injury, systemic hyperinflammation, micro- and macrovascular thrombosis, and pressure-volume overload-contribute to functional and, less frequently, structural valvular changes. Available evidence suggests that clinically relevant post-COVID valvular abnormalities are more often secondary/functional (mitral and tricuspid regurgitation) than primary structural lesions, although dedicated prospective valvular studies remain scarce. Pre-existing severe VHD markedly worsens acute COVID-19 prognosis.
title: Valvular Heart Disease and Heart Failure in the Post-COVID-19 Era: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Diagnosis, Differential Assessment, and Clinical Outcomes.

text: Elevated NT-proBNP, troponin, and interleukin-6 consistently predict decompensation and mortality, and a substantial minority of survivors show persistent fibrotic pulmonary changes and restrictive ventilatory defects on follow-up (pulmonary rather than cardiac findings). Conclusions : Post-COVID valvular dysfunction appears, on currently available but largely indirect evidence, predominantly functional and inflammation-related, and may overlap with HFpEF phenotypes in selected patients when objective diagnostic criteria are fulfilled. Biomarker-guided, multimodality follow-up is reasonable in high-risk survivors, and prospective longitudinal studies with standardized valvular endpoints remain a priority. Dedicated longitudinal evidence on valvular outcomes specifically remains very limited.
title: Valvular Heart Disease and Heart Failure in the Post-COVID-19 Era: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Diagnosis, Differential Assessment, and Clinical Outcomes.

text: Background High-altitude exposure has been linked to an increased risk of Parkinson's disease (PD), potentially through hypoxic neuronal damage, yet the involvement of α-synuclein (α-syn) remains poorly understood. This study integrates population-based surveys, animal experiments, and clinical cross-sectional data to elucidate the role of high-altitude environments in PD pathogenesis. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among middle-aged and elderly high-altitude residents. Additional cohorts (low-altitude PD patients, low-altitude controls, and high-altitude controls) were enrolled for plasma and erythrocytic α-syn measurement, and a subset of PD patients underwent transcranial sonography to assess correlations between erythrocyte indices and substantia nigra echogenicity.
title: High-altitude environments elevate central and peripheral α-synuclein levels and accelerate PD-related pathology.

text: A53T transgenic mice were exposed to high altitude for six months and evaluated by behavioral tests, omics sequencing, α-syn assays, and immunohistochemistry. Erythrocyte-derived extracellular vesicles from PD patients were intravenously injected into wild-type mice to assess brain entry. Results The crude prevalence of PD tended to be higher in high-altitude populations than the national average. A53T mice exposed to high altitude displayed more severe motor deficits, elevated brain α-syn levels, and pronounced dopaminergic neuron loss. Omics analyses revealed enrichment of pathways related to IL-17, sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling, and oxidative stress in brain tissue from high-altitude versus low-altitude A53T mice, suggesting blood-brain barrier disruption and impaired α-syn clearance.
title: High-altitude environments elevate central and peripheral α-synuclein levels and accelerate PD-related pathology.

text: In peripheral blood, both high-altitude mice and humans exhibited elevated α-syn levels compared with their low-altitude counterparts, and erythrocyte indices correlated positively with α-syn levels. After normalization to erythrocyte count and hemoglobin, however, erythrocytic α-syn did not differ between high-altitude and low-altitude controls. In mice, intravenously injected human-derived erythrocytic vesicles entered the brain. Conclusions Chronic high‑altitude exposure is associated with peripheral and central α‑syn accumulation, which may be driven by a hypoxia‑induced erythrocyte pool expansion and increased α-syn burden, potentially aggravating PD‑related neuropathology.
title: High-altitude environments elevate central and peripheral α-synuclein levels and accelerate PD-related pathology.

text: The aim of this systematic review was to critically assess the available evidence regarding risk factors associated with surgical site infections following tibial plateau levelling osteotomy. This study aims to identify clinically relevant determinants of surgical site infection following tibial plateau levelling osteotomy and inform future preventive strategies. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. The review question was structured using the PECOS framework. Searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus without date restrictions, including all studies indexed up to June 2025. The search strategy combined terms related to surgical site infection, tibial plateau levelling osteotomy and dogs. Risk of bias was assessed across predefined methodological domains.
title: Assessment of risk factors for surgical site infection following tibial plateau levelling osteotomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: The Journal of small animal practice

text: The literature search yielded 436 results, and a total of 11 papers met the inclusion criteria. The study designs included two prospective clinical trials, one double-blinded randomised controlled trial and eight retrospective case series. Several risk factors for postoperative surgical site infection were investigated across the studies, with increased body weight being the most frequently identified. Most of the studies presented a high risk of bias in the domains of allocation concealment, blinding of participants and personnel and blinding of outcome assessment. In contrast, incomplete outcome data and selective reporting were generally assessed as low risk of bias.
title: Assessment of risk factors for surgical site infection following tibial plateau levelling osteotomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: The Journal of small animal practice

text: Knowledge of specific risk factors for surgical site infection after tibial plateau levelling osteotomy may support the clinician in tailoring antimicrobial prophylaxis and anticipating potential complications, thereby improving perioperative decision-making and patient outcomes.
title: Assessment of risk factors for surgical site infection following tibial plateau levelling osteotomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: The Journal of small animal practice

text: Cryopreservation techniques and protocols for ram semen, particularly those with a focus on semen extender additives, have gained popularity recently, as many scientists are looking for ways to mitigate cryodamage and improve post-thaw sperm quality. The purpose of this structured narrative review was to examine studies published in 2019-2024 on both synthetic and natural additives, to separate evidence obtained in rams from comparative evidence in other species, and to analyze current trends and potential gaps for future research. Cryopreservation is an indispensable aspect in livestock production and conservation of genes using artificial insemination. Nevertheless, the freezing and thawing processes result in DNA fragmentation, oxidative stress and low sperm motility, which are detrimental to reproductive success.
title: Cryopreservation of Ram Semen: A Review on the Roles of Emerging Synthetic and Natural Additives.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Conventional extenders that contain glycerol or egg yolk have been used extensively to support cell membranes and prevent the formation of ice crystals. Nevertheless, the fertility rates obtained from frozen-thawed ram semen have been poor, which has led to the investigation of other substances. Natural additives like plant polyphenols, vitamins, fatty acids and sugars have shown great potential to decrease free radicals and enhance sperm integrity. Synthetic additives, including Trolox, MitoQ, and Mito-TEMPO, were also found to enhance the antioxidant capacity. Over the past few years, some trends have emerged, including an increased interest in plant-based antioxidants and nanoparticle-based additives.
title: Cryopreservation of Ram Semen: A Review on the Roles of Emerging Synthetic and Natural Additives.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Nevertheless, several research gaps were observed, including the need for further optimization of the additive dose ratios, availability of studies on the stability of these additives when used long-term, and the compatibility of extender formulations across breeds and species. This review synthesizes recent developments in ram semen cryopreservation additives; for most additives, the evidence is presented in a single study with sperm-quality endpoints. Few studies measured in vivo fertility. It emphasizes the necessity of shifting from descriptive additive studies to mechanism-focused protocols validated across breeds to enhance the scalability and reliability of reproductive biotechnologies.
title: Cryopreservation of Ram Semen: A Review on the Roles of Emerging Synthetic and Natural Additives.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Giardiasis, caused by Giardia intestinalis , is a prevalent intestinal protozoan infection worldwide. Clinical manifestations are variable, and many infections remain asymptomatic. Disease pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving brush border enzyme deficiency, apoptosis, dysbiosis and increased intestinal permeability. Advances in genomics, genetic tools, and model systems have substantially improved our understanding of the parasite's virulence mechanisms. Giardia exhibits considerable genetic diversity, with distinct assemblages associated with differences in parasite biology. Attachment is mediated by the ventral disk, while the parasite's eight flagella contribute to motility and intestinal persistence. Antigenic variation of cysteine-rich surface proteins enables immune evasion and promotes chronic infection, but the level of inflammation is low.
title: Pathogenicity and virulence of <i>Giardia intestinalis</i>.

text: The parasite releases a variety of proteins and extracellular vesicles containing proteins and small RNAs that play important roles in host-cell interactions and modulation of the gut microbiome. This review describes areas that need further research to connect pathogenesis to specific virulence mechanisms.
title: Pathogenicity and virulence of <i>Giardia intestinalis</i>.

text: Degenerative joint disease, including osteoarthritis (OA), is frequently diagnosed in working dogs and is a major cause of retirement or euthanasia. Pregabalin is a gabapentinoid used mainly for neuropathic pain, but evidence for pregabalin monotherapy in canine OA-related chronic pain is limited. Of 702 cases screened, this retrospective study included 21 working dogs with radiographically confirmed OA and chronic pain of at least three months' duration that received pregabalin monotherapy (4 mg/kg PO q12h). Handler-completed Liverpool Osteoarthritis in Dogs (LOAD), Canine Brief Pain Inventory (CBPI) pain severity score (PSS), and pain interference score (PIS) at baseline and at 14 ± 3 days were compared using paired t -tests, with predefined responder criteria applied to individual dogs.
title: Pregabalin Monotherapy for Chronic Pain Associated with Osteoarthritis in Working Dogs: A Retrospective Study of 21 Cases.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: LOAD, CBPI-PSS, and CBPI-PIS decreased by 2.33, 0.67, and 1.00 points, respectively (all p < 0.001). However, only 5 of 21 dogs (23.8%) met the LOAD responder criterion and 3 of 21 (14.3%) met the CBPI criterion. No adverse effects were recorded. Although scores decreased significantly at the group level, clinically meaningful improvement was limited, and the uncontrolled design precludes causal inference. Controlled studies are needed to determine whether pregabalin has a role when non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use requires caution.
title: Pregabalin Monotherapy for Chronic Pain Associated with Osteoarthritis in Working Dogs: A Retrospective Study of 21 Cases.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Several species have demonstrated the ability to mentally manipulate quantities in tasks requiring their combination and dissociation, reflecting perceptual memory-based mechanisms that may be the foundation of proto-arithmetic and in some cases more advanced arithmetic abilities. Yet, ungulates remain underrepresented in this line of research. Here, we present the first investigation in giraffes (Giraffa camelopardalis) assessing their ability to combine and dissociate quantities. We tested four captive giraffes in three experimental and two controls tasks. In the experimental tasks, the animals could only see the initial quantities and the items moved, but not the final amounts. Results revealed that giraffes performed above chance in the Combination task (where food was combined to one of two covered quantities).
title: Assessing quantity combination and dissociation in giraffes.

text: However, they performed at chance level in both the Dissociation task (where food was removed from one of two covered quantities) and the Subsequent Events task (where food was transferred from one of the two quantities to the other one). Further analyses suggested that while two subjects might have relied on simpler strategies (e.g., choosing or avoiding the dish manipulated by the experimenter), the other two succeeded even when this strategy could not be used, suggesting the potential use of more complex mental computations.
title: Assessing quantity combination and dissociation in giraffes.

text: Background Propriospinal myoclonus (PSM) is characterized by repetitive, brief jerks of the trunk, hips, and knees in humans and has not been reported in dogs. Hypothesis/objectives To describe phenotype, diagnostic findings, treatment, and outcomes in presumptive PSM in dogs. Animals Twenty-seven dogs with presumptive PSM. Methods Multicenter, retrospective study of dogs with myoclonus affecting the limbs and trunk without head involvement, identified through online calls for suspected cases. Results Median age at onset was 9 months (range, 2-44 months). Propriospinal myoclonus involved pelvic limbs in all dogs, thoracic limbs in 14/27 (52%), and trunk in 9/27 (33%). Pelvic limb myoclonus was extensor in all dogs, whereas thoracic limb involvement was extensor in 12/27 (44%) and flexor in 3/27 (11%) dogs.
title: Phenotypic characterization of presumptive propriospinal myoclonus in young dogs (2013-2025).

text: Episodes were observed in a non-weight-bearing posture in all dogs, mainly lateral (25/27; 93%) and sternal (12/27; 44%) recumbency. Neurological examination was normal in all dogs. Abnormalities were not detected on magnetic resonance imaging of the spinal cord (4/6) or brain (6/6) in 5/6 dogs; in the remaining dog, findings were unrelated to the presumptive PSM. Follow-up information was available for 26/27 (96%) dogs. Sixteen dogs (59%) received no treatment, of which 9/16 (56%) showed spontaneous reduction in PSM frequency. Treatment with various antiseizure medications was started in 11/27 (41%) dogs, of which 5/11 (45%) improved. Conclusions and clinical importance Presumptive PSM affected young dogs and is likely idiopathic. The condition is characterized by extensor myoclonus predominantly affecting pelvic limbs during recumbency, with preserved mentation.
title: Phenotypic characterization of presumptive propriospinal myoclonus in young dogs (2013-2025).

text: Spontaneous improvement seems common. Abstract translated to dutch/flemish Achtergrond: Propriospinale myoclonus (PSM) wordt bij mens gekenmerkt door repetitieve, schokbewegingen van de romp, heupen en knieën. Tot op heden is deze aandoening niet beschreven bij honden.Doelstelling; Het beschrijven van het fenotype, diagnostische bevindingen, behandeling en klinische uitkomst.Dieren: Zevenentwintig honden met vermoedelijke PSM. Methoden-Multicentrische retrospectieve studie bij honden met myoclonus waarbij de ledematen waren betrokken, geïdentificeerd via online meldingen van vermoedelijke gevallen.Resultaten: De mediane leeftijd bij aanvang van de symptomen bedroeg 9 maanden (spreiding: 2-44 maanden). Bij alle honden was PSM aanwezig in de achterpoten, bij 14/27 (52%) in de voorpoten en bij 9/27 (33%) in de romp. De myoclonus van de achterpoten was bij alle honden in extensie.
title: Phenotypic characterization of presumptive propriospinal myoclonus in young dogs (2013-2025).

text: Ter hoogte van de voorpoten was de myoclonus in extensie (12/27 (44%) en in flexie (3/27 (11%). De episoden traden voornamelijk op in zijligging (25/27; 93%) en sternale (12/27; 44%). Neurologisch onderzoek was bij alle honden normaal. Magnetische resonantiebeeldvorming van ruggenmerg (4/6) en hersenen (6/6) was bij 5/6 honden normaal. Follow-upinformatie was beschikbaar voor 26/27 (96%) honden. Zestien honden (59%) kregen geen behandeling, waarvan 9/16 (56%) een spontane afname van de frequentie van de PSM vertoonden. Bij 11/27 (41%) honden werd een behandeling met aanvalswerende medicijnen gestart, waarbij 5/11 (45%) een verbetering vertoonden.Conclusies en klinische relevantie: Vermoedelijke PSM lijkt voornamelijk voor te komen bij jonge honden en is waarschijnlijk idiopathisch.
title: Phenotypic characterization of presumptive propriospinal myoclonus in young dogs (2013-2025).

text: Het klinisch beeld wordt gekenmerkt door een myoclonus in extensie van voornamelijk de achterpoten tijdens het liggen. Een spontane verbetering lijkt vaak voor te komen.
title: Phenotypic characterization of presumptive propriospinal myoclonus in young dogs (2013-2025).

text: The parrots, a highly intelligent avian species, possesses distinctive characteristics including remarkable cognitive abilities, strong mimetic capacity, and significant economic value as companion pets, with the scale of commercial captive breeding expanding considerably over recent decades. Intestinal health is critical for nutrient digestion and absorption, and serves as a primary barrier against pathogen invasion; thus, maintaining optimal gut function is essential for enhancing overall health and breeding performance. However, compared to other poultry species, research on the pivotal role of gut health in the breeding and management of parrots remains limited.
title: A Review on Parrot Gut Health: Insights into the Intestinal Structure, Microbiota Diversity, Influencing Factors, and Nutritional Strategies.

text: This review summarizes the unique anatomical and physiological features of the parrot digestive system, the characteristics of its gut microbiota, and their interrelationship with intestinal health, and further discusses the significance of intestinal health for the overall well-being of parrots. Additionally, this review highlights emerging nutritional regulation strategies, particularly the application of probiotics and other functional additives for improving intestinal health, which will provide new insights into enhancing the health status of parrot populations and formulating management strategies for the parrot breeding industry.
title: A Review on Parrot Gut Health: Insights into the Intestinal Structure, Microbiota Diversity, Influencing Factors, and Nutritional Strategies.

text: Brachycephalic dogs are predisposed to respiratory and thermoregulatory impairment, which may become evident during physical exertion. This study evaluated thermal and pulmonary ultrasonographic responses to standardized submaximal treadmill exercise in 41 clinically healthy brachycephalic dogs. Rectal temperature and infrared thermographic measurements of the ocular and facial regions were obtained before and immediately after exercise. Thoracic ultrasonography was performed at baseline and after a standardized 20-min post-exercise recovery period. The dogs walked on a treadmill at 1.3 m/s, with a 0° incline, for up to 6 min. Rectal temperature increased significantly after exercise ( p p < 0.0001), whereas facial surface temperature did not differ significantly.
title: Ultrasonographic and Thermographic Evaluation in Brachycephalic Dogs Before and After Physical Exercise in the Brazilian Northeast Semi-Arid Region.

text: No pulmonary ultrasonographic abnormalities were detected at baseline; after exercise, abnormalities were identified in 30/41 dogs (73%), including B-lines, pleural irregularity, pleural thickening, and, less frequently, discrete pleural effusion. These findings demonstrate measurable thermal responses and pleuropulmonary ultrasonographic changes following standardized submaximal exercise in brachycephalic dogs. Infrared ocular thermography and thoracic ultrasonography may provide complementary, non-invasive information for monitoring exercise-associated responses; however, the relationship between ocular and core body temperatures and the temporal and clinical significance of the pulmonary findings require further investigation.
title: Ultrasonographic and Thermographic Evaluation in Brachycephalic Dogs Before and After Physical Exercise in the Brazilian Northeast Semi-Arid Region.

text: Communication is an accepted clinical competency in veterinary medicine, taught and increasingly assessed during the veterinarian-client consultation. However, the same encounter is also the profession's most frequent point of contact with antimicrobial stewardship, zoonotic risk, food safety and public trust in science, and the population- and public-facing communication demanded by the One Health role remains comparatively overlooked in veterinary curricula. This narrative review reframes the clinical consultation not as the boundary of veterinary communication but as its gateway. Synthesizing current literature on communication teaching in veterinary education, it argues that provision is heavily weighted towards the dyadic core and comparatively silent on interprofessional, community, public health and digital communication.
title: The Clinical Encounter as a Gateway to One Health: Rethinking Communication Education in Veterinary Curricula.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: On this basis, it proposes an integrated Communication Competency Continuum, in which five transversal competencies (relational, informational, behavior change, risk and audience adaptation) are progressively re-contextualized from the clinical dyad outward to the One Health mandate, anchored in established competency frameworks and made explicitly assessable. Offered as a conceptual contribution rather than a prescription, the continuum is not intended to replace clinical communication training, which should be preserved, but to extend it, so that veterinary communication education matches the breadth of the profession's role.
title: The Clinical Encounter as a Gateway to One Health: Rethinking Communication Education in Veterinary Curricula.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
