text: Within the retrieved literature, stx2 and stx1 were widely reported, and stx2a, stx2c, and stx2d were among the recurrently reported stx2 subtypes. O157 and non-O157 STEC were both represented across the included studies. These findings describe reporting patterns within the retrieved literature and should not be interpreted as frequencies of occurrence among studies specifically testing each characteristic or as prevalence among STEC isolates. The included studies also reported diverse sequence types and additional virulence determinants, including eae and ehxA. Clinical information was available in only a subset of studies and included manifestations ranging from diarrhea and bloody diarrhea to hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS). text: Environmental heat stress disrupts cellular homeostasis through coordinated molecular responses involving protein quality control, oxidative stress regulation, inflammatory signaling, and water homeostasis. Although saliva plays an essential role in maintaining oral homeostasis, the molecular pathways underlying salivary adaptation to heat stress remain insufficiently characterized. We hypothesized that integrating the human salivary proteome with systems biology approaches would identify a reproducible heat-stress-responsive molecular signature. Human salivary proteomic datasets retrieved from the Human Salivary Proteome Wiki were integrated into a non-redundant dataset comprising 15,594 protein accessions corresponding to 2540 distinct proteins.
title: System-Level Identification of Heat Stress-Responsive Pathways in Human Saliva.

text: Following deduplication, functional annotation, and biological curation, proteins associated with heat stress response, oxidative stress regulation, inflammatory signaling, water homeostasis, salivary secretion, and mucosal protection were assembled into a Salivary Climate Stress Panel (SCSP). Protein-protein interaction and functional enrichment analyses were performed, and the biological relevance of the identified proteins was independently evaluated using a human heat stress transcriptomic meta-analysis comprising 322 comparisons and the GEO dataset GDS3004. Functional filtering identified 2050 heat-stress-associated salivary proteins, from which a curated SCSP of 35 proteins was established.
title: System-Level Identification of Heat Stress-Responsive Pathways in Human Saliva.

text: Network analysis identified HSP90AB1, HSP90AA1, and IL1B as the principal hub proteins linking heat stress, oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and water homeostasis pathways, while transcriptomic validation confirmed consistent activation of representative SCSP genes under heat stress conditions. These findings provide a reproducible systems-level framework for investigating heat-stress-responsive molecular pathways in the human salivary proteome and support future studies on salivary biomarkers of environmental heat exposure.
title: System-Level Identification of Heat Stress-Responsive Pathways in Human Saliva.

text: Postoperative ileus (POI) is a common complication after abdominal surgery, driven by inflammation. This study investigated how extracellular-ATP (eATP) and intestinal CD8αβ + intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) contribute to POI. Using an intestinal manipulation mouse model, we found that CD8αβ + IELs were increased and activated during POI, producing elevated granzyme B. Depletion of these T cells or inhibition of granzyme B ameliorated gastrointestinal transit impairment. Damage-induced eATP promoted granzyme B production in CD8αβ + IELs via P2X7R signaling. Mechanistically, granzyme B degraded the tight-junction protein ZO-1, leading to enterochromaffin cell loss, reduced serotonin levels, and subsequent motility dysfunction.
title: P2X7R+CD8αβ<sup>+</sup> T cells exacerbate postoperative ileus by inducing the loss of enterochromaffin cells.

text: These findings reveal a pathway in which eATP activates CD8αβ + IELs through the P2X7 receptor to drive enterochromaffin cell loss via granzyme B-mediated tight-junction degradation, identifying potential therapeutic targets for POI.
title: P2X7R+CD8αβ<sup>+</sup> T cells exacerbate postoperative ileus by inducing the loss of enterochromaffin cells.

text: Motion sickness (MS) is a common response to conflicting motion signals and can cause nausea, dizziness, malaise, and reduced activity. Sound can lessen MS, but how auditory cues influence the brain circuits that generate these symptoms is unclear. Here we show, using a repeated rotation paradigm in male mice, that a brief anticipatory tone reduces MS-like responses. We identify Cerebellin-2-expressing (Cbln2 + ) glutamatergic neurons in the medial vestibular nuclei (MVN), a brainstem center for balance signals, as key drivers of these responses. These neurons act through two separable outputs: a projection to the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray that promotes MS-like behavior, and a projection to the nucleus of the solitary tract that contributes to nausea-related aversion, likely through the parabrachial nucleus.
title: The Neural Mechanism of Motion Sickness Alleviation by Anticipatory Sound.

text: Anticipatory tone cues recruit an inhibitory pathway from the central amygdala to suppress Cbln2 + MVN neurons. These findings reveal how auditory prediction can dampen vestibular circuits that drive MS.
title: The Neural Mechanism of Motion Sickness Alleviation by Anticipatory Sound.

text: Background: Platinum-resistant ovarian cancer with peritoneal metastases remains a therapeutic frontier marked by limited systemic efficacy and a persistent unmet clinical need for effective locoregional strategies. Pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC) has emerged as a novel minimally invasive platform designed to enhance intraperitoneal drug distribution and overcome biological barriers to chemotherapy delivery. Methods: We performed a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating clinical outcomes of PIPAC in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Primary endpoints included histologic regression (PRGS ≤ 2), severe toxicity, and 12-month overall survival, complemented by exploratory analyses of treatment feasibility, disease burden dynamics, and bidirectional therapy strategies.
title: Pressurized Intraperitoneal Aerosol Chemotherapy for Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Outcomes.

text: Results: PIPAC demonstrated a consistent signal of biologic activity, with pooled histologic response rates indicating meaningful tumor regression despite advanced disease. Severe toxicity remained low across studies, supporting the favorable tolerability of repeated intraperitoneal treatment. Survival outcomes were clinically relevant for a heavily pretreated population, while feasibility analyses suggested that PIPAC may facilitate downstream surgical opportunities in selected patients. Exploratory findings further supported the concept of intraperitoneal disease modulation, reflected by reductions in peritoneal cancer index and integration within multimodal treatment pathways. Conclusions: Beyond a purely palliative intervention, PIPAC may represent a biologically active component of personalized treatment strategies for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
title: Pressurized Intraperitoneal Aerosol Chemotherapy for Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Outcomes.

text: These findings redefine the therapeutic narrative from symptom control toward disease modulation and treatment escalation, underscoring the need for prospective trials to refine patient selection and optimize multimodal sequencing.
title: Pressurized Intraperitoneal Aerosol Chemotherapy for Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Outcomes.

text: Mucosal colour assessment is widely used in veterinary medicine as an indicator of physiological states, but current approaches are characterized by inconsistent terminology, variable methodology, and differing levels of validation. This communication introduces the provisional Uldahl Standard, a conceptual framework developed to improve consistency, transparency, and reproducibility in mucosal colour assessment in terrestrial mammals. The framework integrates principles from veterinary medicine, colorimetry, and modern imaging technologies, combining perceptual, computational, and instrument-based approaches to colour analysis. Mucosal colour assessment is defined as a multidimensional process comprising colour category, light saturation level, physiological association, assessment method, and level of validation.
title: A Provisional Conceptual Framework for Mucosal Colour Assessment in Terrestrial Mammals.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Nine principal colour categories and eight standardised saturation modifiers were identified through a literature review and incorporated into the framework. The standard further emphasizes transparent reporting of assessment conditions, validation procedures, artefact evaluation, and analytical pathways, including examples using AI-assisted visual analysis. The framework acknowledges the inherent variability in mucosal colour assessment arising from environmental conditions, limitations of human colour perception, and differences in descriptive methods while providing a structured and comparable terminology, linked to defined levels of validation.
title: A Provisional Conceptual Framework for Mucosal Colour Assessment in Terrestrial Mammals.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: It is anticipated that application of the proposed Uldahl Standard will provide markedly more robust and consistent descriptions of mucosal colours, which, provided they are combined with well validated clinical signs of the underlying physiology and/or pathophysiology, will greatly enhance the diagnostic power of the procedure.
title: A Provisional Conceptual Framework for Mucosal Colour Assessment in Terrestrial Mammals.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Background Glioblastomas (GBMs) are highly invasive and heterogeneous in nature which strongly contributes to poor survival of patients, averaging 15 months after diagnosis. With little treatment options being available in particular for addressing GBM invasiveness, there is a high need for supplementary therapies in addition to classical cytostatics like Temozolomide (TMZ). Methods The aim of this study was to examine promising compounds, the natural indole scaffold RAD114 and three semisynthetic analogs (RAD118, RAD119, RAD120) as well as the aryl sulfonamide AqB011, for their inhibitory potential specifically on tumor cell invasion. For this, GBM xenograft tissue slice tandem co-culture (XTCC) models were employed, closely reflecting the in vivo patient situation.
title: Indole analogs and the aryl sulfonamide AqB011 potently restrain the invasiveness of glioblastoma cells, as determined in ex vivo xenograft tissue slice co-cultures (XTCCs).

text: In particular, these ex vivo tissue slice air-liquid interface (ALI) models also allow for distinguishing between inhibitory effects on bulk tumor growth vs tumor cell invasion into the normal brain tissue. Results Profound anti-invasive effects of the natural indole scaffold RAD114, three semisynthetic analogs (RAD118, RAD119, RAD120), and the aryl sulfonamide AqB011 were observed in XTCC models based on G55T2 and U87-MG GBM xenografts co-cultured with mouse brain slices in ALI tandem co-culture. While effects on bulk tumor growth were rather moderate, profound inhibition or even abolishment of tumor invasion was observed, dependent on the compound, its dosage and the model. At a non-toxic concentration (10 µM), RAD118 and AqB011 showed the highest effectiveness in reducing tumor invasion. Combination effects at sub-optimal compound dosages were observed as well.
title: Indole analogs and the aryl sulfonamide AqB011 potently restrain the invasiveness of glioblastoma cells, as determined in ex vivo xenograft tissue slice co-cultures (XTCCs).

text: Conclusions Both compound classes - the tested semisynthetic indole analogs and the sulfonamide derivative - may be promising lead candidates for drugs useful to specifically address the issue of GBM invasiveness. They strongly restrained GBM cell invasion, alone and in combination. Rather than acting through cytotoxic effects, they specifically inhibit cell migration into native brain tissue.
title: Indole analogs and the aryl sulfonamide AqB011 potently restrain the invasiveness of glioblastoma cells, as determined in ex vivo xenograft tissue slice co-cultures (XTCCs).

text: Hemorrhagic hepatic pseudocysts are uncommon in cats and can present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. This report describes the diagnosis and surgical management of a massive hemorrhagic hepatic pseudocyst in a 1-year-old intact male British Shorthair cat presented for castration with several days of intermittent vomiting. Physical examination revealed marked abdominal distension, while routine hematologic and biochemical testing showed no clinically significant abnormalities. Abdominal radiography revealed a large soft tissue opacity occupying most of the abdominal cavity. Ultrasonography identified a large fluid-filled cystic structure, and computed tomography confirmed a large hepatic cystic lesion with displacement of adjacent organs. Surgical exploration revealed a solitary hepatic cyst containing dark red hemorrhagic fluid.
title: Diagnosis and Surgical Management of a Hemorrhagic Hepatic Pseudocyst in a Young British Shorthair Cat.

text: The cyst-fluid total bilirubin concentration was markedly higher than the serum concentration, although no gross communication with the biliary tract was identified during surgery. The lesion was completely excised while preserving the adjacent hepatic parenchyma. Histopathologic examination revealed a fibrous cyst wall with extensive hemorrhage and multifocal necrosis without an epithelial lining, supporting the diagnosis of a hemorrhagic hepatic pseudocyst. At 26 months after surgery, the owner reported that the cat had remained clinically well, and abdominal radiographs showed no evidence of a recurrent abdominal mass. This case highlights hemorrhagic hepatic pseudocyst as a differential diagnosis for large hepatic cystic lesions in cats and suggests that complete surgical excision may be a treatment option for a resectable hepatic pseudocyst.
title: Diagnosis and Surgical Management of a Hemorrhagic Hepatic Pseudocyst in a Young British Shorthair Cat.

text: Diquat (1,1'-ethylene-2,2'-bipyridinium dibromide) is a nonselective bipyridyl herbicide widely used in agriculture for crop desiccation and weed control. Following the global restriction of paraquat, diquat usage has surged substantially, leading to increased poisoning incidents particularly in agricultural regions of China and other developing countries, where intentional ingestion for self-harm constitutes the predominant exposure route with mortality rates of 16.7-60% depending on ingested dose and treatment timing. At the molecular level, diquat undergoes nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH)-dependent redox cycling generating excessive reactive oxygen species, triggering mitochondrial dysfunction, Nrf2-Keap1 pathway activation, and multiple regulated cell death modalities including apoptosis, necroptosis, and ferroptosis.
title: Diquat Poisoning: Epidemiology, Molecular Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Clinical Management.

text: However, a comprehensive synthesis integrating epidemiological patterns, molecular mechanisms, organ-specific pathophysiology, and evidence-based clinical management remains lacking. This review systematically examines the global epidemiology and demographic characteristics of diquat poisoning, elucidates the interconnected molecular pathways underlying multiorgan toxicity affecting kidneys, liver, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system, evaluates current diagnostic approaches including severity scoring systems and biomarker-guided prognostication, and critically appraises therapeutic strategies from emergency decontamination to investigational cell death pathway inhibitors.
title: Diquat Poisoning: Epidemiology, Molecular Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Clinical Management.

text: This work provides a comprehensive framework for understanding diquat toxicology and identifies critical knowledge gaps to guide future research toward precision medicine approaches and improved clinical outcomes.
title: Diquat Poisoning: Epidemiology, Molecular Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Clinical Management.

text: Influenza H3N8 viruses have been frequently isolated from chicken farms. However, comprehensive characterization of their virological properties, molecular evolution, virulence, and risk of spillover into mammals remains limited. In particular, little attention has been given to the transmission efficiency of H3N8 avian influenza viruses among chickens and their spillover risk. Here, we systematically characterized H3N8 isolates obtained from asymptomatic chickens through multidisciplinary approaches, including genomic surveillance, receptor binding profiling, and in vivo pathogenicity and transmission assays. All strains showed >98% nucleotide homology with human-infecting strains. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that their internal genes were derived from H9N2, while HA and PB2 genes shared high homology (bootstrap support >98%) with the novel H3N3 virus.
title: Virulence and transmission characteristic of H3N8 avian influenza virus circulating in chickens in China.

text: All isolates maintained avian-type receptor-binding motifs (HA-Q226/G228) while exhibiting dual α2,3/α2,6-sialic acid binding and robust replication in mammalian cells (peak MDCK titer: 10 7 · 5 TCID 5 0 /mL). ZJ07 demonstrated exceptional thermostability (HA activity persisting >3 hr at 56°C), while JS13 showed 1.8-fold elevated neuraminidase activity versus controls ( p In vivo , all strains caused subclinical infections with broad tissue tropism in chickens and mice without adaptation, transmitting efficiently among direct-contact poultry. Strikingly, AH12 achieved 100% airborne transmission in chickens. These findings confirm H3N8's capacity for silent poultry circulation and identify key features conducive to cross-species infection, including dual receptor binding, infection in a mammalian model, and high genetic homology with human strains.
title: Virulence and transmission characteristic of H3N8 avian influenza virus circulating in chickens in China.

text: The airborne transmissibility of AH12 underscores a heightened spillover risk, necessitating enhanced surveillance and vaccines targeting avian-human interface strains.
title: Virulence and transmission characteristic of H3N8 avian influenza virus circulating in chickens in China.

text: Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell, playing vital roles in energy production and metabolism. Most mitochondrial proteins are encoded in the nuclear DNA and must be synthesized in the cytosol before being transported into the appropriate mitochondrial compartments. Mitochondrial protein import is not only essential for mitochondrial biogenesis but also a crucial regulatory step in mitochondrial proteostasis surveillance and stress response. Additionally, defects in mitochondrial protein import lead to mislocalization of precursor proteins to the cytosol, disrupting cytosolic proteostasis and contributing to various human diseases. This review summarizes recent findings demonstrating that mitochondrial protein import is a key regulator of cellular proteostasis. This article is part of the Theo Murphy meeting issue 'ProteostaSys: a systems view of proteostasis'.
title: Regulation of cellular proteostasis via mitochondrial protein import.
journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences

text: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) variant strains lead to vaccine failures and significant economic losses in swine farming, highlighting the need for new natural small-molecule antiviral candidates. In this study, we screened a library of 45 small molecules using a cytopathic effect (CPE)-based cytoprotective assay. Saikosaponin B2 (SSB2), a triterpenoid saponin derived from Bupleuri Radix, emerged as the most promising candidate, boasting a selectivity index of 19.77, which surpasses that of most natural compounds. Dose-response tests confirmed SSB2's concentration-dependent anti-PEDV activity, with an inhibitory plateau reached at concentrations above 60 μmol/L (μM). The 50 half-maximal effective concentration (EC 50 ) values differed between CPE reduction and viral titer readouts, a discrepancy commonly due to varying detection sensitivities.
title: In Vitro Assessment of Antiviral Activity of Saikosaponin B2 Against Porcine Epidemic Diarrheal Virus.

text: Mechanistic assays revealed that SSB2 does not possess direct virucidal properties; instead, its antiviral efficacy depends on sustained treatment to inhibit viral adsorption and internalization. Time-of-addition experiments further demonstrated that SSB2 effectively suppresses both early viral entry and mid-stage intracellular genome replication, without affecting viral release. Notably, post-infection treatment resulted in stronger inhibition compared to continuous administration, possibly due to disrupted cellular proliferation homeostasis from prolonged exposure. Additionally, SSB2 maintained strong inhibitory effects against prevalent G2a (JL-06) and G2b (JL-08) field variants, though its efficacy was reduced for both strains and slightly weaker against JL-08 than JL-06.
title: In Vitro Assessment of Antiviral Activity of Saikosaponin B2 Against Porcine Epidemic Diarrheal Virus.

text: Overall, this study systematically characterizes SSB2's dual-stage anti-PEDV profile and its broad-spectrum activity against spike-mutant strains, supporting SSB2 as a promising herbal lead for developing veterinary antivirals targeting variant PEDV.
title: In Vitro Assessment of Antiviral Activity of Saikosaponin B2 Against Porcine Epidemic Diarrheal Virus.

text: Moderately hypofractionated definitive-intent radiotherapy protocols can be used for canine intracranial meningiomas to shorten overall treatment time while maintaining tumour control and limiting normal tissue toxicity. This retrospective study evaluated oncologic outcomes, toxicity, and radiation dose-volume-related prognostic factors in dogs with imaging-based intracranial meningiomas treated with a 10-fraction definitive-intent protocol. Medical records from 2015 to 2025 were reviewed. All dogs received 10 daily fractions of 4 Gy delivered with a homogeneous dose prescription, risk-adapted heterogeneous dose distributions, or an 11% simultaneously integrated boost (SIB) to the gross tumour volume. One hundred and ten dogs were included, with a median follow-up of 498 days.
title: The Definitive-Intent 10-Fraction Radiotherapy Protocol ('The Zurich Protocol') Yields Lasting Tumour Control and Survival in Dogs With Intracranial Meningiomas.

text: Median time to progression was 873 days (95% CI: 552-1195), median overall survival after first radiotherapy was 756 days (95% CI: 474-1039), and median DSS was 1078 days (95% CI: 915-1242). Time to progression differed among treatment subgroups (p = 0.024). Larger volumes of normal brain receiving ≥ 32 Gy (> 11.5 cm 3 ) were associated with shorter overall (p < 0.001) and disease-specific survival (p = 0.002). Use of an SIB was associated with shorter disease-specific survival (HR 2.47; p = 0.012), and post-radiotherapy seizures were associated with reduced time to progression (HR 2.01; p = 0.026). Tumour location was not identified as a prognostic factor. Acute or early delayed neurologic toxicity occurred in 10% of dogs and was generally transient and generally corticosteroid responsive.
title: The Definitive-Intent 10-Fraction Radiotherapy Protocol ('The Zurich Protocol') Yields Lasting Tumour Control and Survival in Dogs With Intracranial Meningiomas.

text: In conclusion, the definitive-intent, moderately hypofractionated 10-fraction radiotherapy protocol achieves long lasting tumour control and survival outcomes in dogs with intracranial meningiomas, provided that evidence-based brain dose-volume constraints are respected.
title: The Definitive-Intent 10-Fraction Radiotherapy Protocol ('The Zurich Protocol') Yields Lasting Tumour Control and Survival in Dogs With Intracranial Meningiomas.

text: Despite the success of suppressive antiretrovirals, infection with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is associated with several comorbidities which include negative consequences to the central nervous system (CNS), where disruption of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a major underlying factor in the resulting chronic inflammation and contribution to the pathogenesis of neuroHIV. Currently, the use of cannabis and cannabinoid derivatives among persons living with HIV (PWH) is common. Despite perceived benefits, we have previously identified context-dependent effects of cannabis use, including its impact on vascular biomarkers.
title: Contrasting Cannabinoid Receptor 2 (CB2R)-Associated Responses in Two Different Cerebrovascular Endothelial Cell Lines in a Blood Brain Barrier Model in the Context of HIV.

text: In this study, we used an in vitro polycellular BBB model with two different human cerebrovascular endothelial cell lines (hCMEC/D3 and HBMEC/ci18) to test the effects of cannabinoids and their receptors on barrier integrity and function in the context of the latent HIV brain environment, mimicked by the addition of conditioned media from HIV latently infected promonocytes. We found that the two brain endothelial cell lines had similar responses to HIV-conditioned media by increasing permeability to dextran and decreased expression of tight junction proteins. However, their response to cannabinoids, particularly via the cannabinoid receptor 2 (CB2R), was markedly different, with hCMEC/D3 cells showing improvement of BBB integrity by all measures, but HBMEC/ci18 cells showing no benefits or aggravation of damage.
title: Contrasting Cannabinoid Receptor 2 (CB2R)-Associated Responses in Two Different Cerebrovascular Endothelial Cell Lines in a Blood Brain Barrier Model in the Context of HIV.

text: While the contrasting effects were not due to differences in cell viability or proliferation, differences CB2R-elicited baseline G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) response thresholds between the two cell lines were significant, revealed by forskolin-induced cAMP levels that were 50-200-fold higher in hCMEC/D3 cells in comparison to HBMEC/ci18. This was correlated to higher baseline CB2R expression in hCMEC/D3, and was not an HIV-induced signaling defect in HBMEC/ci18. The CBD/THC-induced phosphorylation of p38 MAPK was also significantly stronger in hCMEC/D3 compared to HBMEC/ci18, was abrogated by a CB2R inverse agonist/antagonist.
title: Contrasting Cannabinoid Receptor 2 (CB2R)-Associated Responses in Two Different Cerebrovascular Endothelial Cell Lines in a Blood Brain Barrier Model in the Context of HIV.

text: Motivated by the need to identify predictors of positive response to cannabinoids, our study suggests that CB2R levels and GPCR activation thresholds in cerebrovascular endothelium may be important candidate mechanistic biomarkers to be tested in primary cells, animal models, and longitudinal clinical cohorts, with the goal of distinguishing beneficial versus aggravating effects of cannabis to the BBB, particularly in the context of HIV.
title: Contrasting Cannabinoid Receptor 2 (CB2R)-Associated Responses in Two Different Cerebrovascular Endothelial Cell Lines in a Blood Brain Barrier Model in the Context of HIV.

text: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a common complication of canine heartworm disease caused by Dirofilaria immitis and is associated with right-sided cardiac remodelling. This study evaluated the diagnostic value of the Right Vertebral Heart Index (VRHi) for identifying dogs with a high echocardiographic probability of PH and its association with echocardiographic indices of right-sided cardiac remodelling. Fifty-four dogs from Gran Canaria were included: 20 healthy controls and 34 dogs naturally infected with D. immitis , classified according to the presence or absence of a high echocardiographic probability of PH. Thoracic radiographs were obtained without sedation, and the vertebral heart size (VHS) and VRHi were measured using DICOM software. Heartworm infection was confirmed using a commercial antigen detection test.
title: Diagnostic Value of the Vertebral Right Heart Index (VRHi) for Identifying Pulmonary Hypertension in Dogs with Heartworm Disease.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: Echocardiography was performed to assess parasite burden, determine the probability of PH, and evaluate right-sided cardiac remodelling. Dogs with a high echocardiographic probability of PH showed more frequent clinical signs and greater echocardiographic evidence of right-sided cardiac remodelling than dogs without PH. The VRHi values differed significantly among the three study groups and were highest in dogs with a high echocardiographic probability of PH. The VRHi was significantly correlated with echocardiographic indicators of right-sided remodelling. The right lateral projection showed the highest AUC among VRHi measurements (AUC = 0.835), although its AUC did not differ significantly from that of conventional VHS (AUC = 0.764; DeLong p = 0.519).
title: Diagnostic Value of the Vertebral Right Heart Index (VRHi) for Identifying Pulmonary Hypertension in Dogs with Heartworm Disease.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: These findings suggest that VRHi may provide a simple and objective complementary radiographic parameter in dogs with heartworm disease and suspected PH.
title: Diagnostic Value of the Vertebral Right Heart Index (VRHi) for Identifying Pulmonary Hypertension in Dogs with Heartworm Disease.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

text: This study aimed to qualitatively and quantitatively characterize the gene and protein expression of cannabinoid receptors type 1 (CB1) and 2 (CB2), and to describe their cellular distribution in the urinary bladder of cats. Samples were collected post-mortem from 11 cats with no history of lower urinary tract disease and were analyzed using reverse-transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), Western blot, and immunofluorescence. Mean fluorescence intensity was analyzed in the urothelium and detrusor muscle using a paired t -test ( p CNR2 transcripts were detected in both compartments, whereas CNR1 transcripts were not detectable. Western blot detected both CB1 and CB2 bands. CB1R immunoreactivity (CB1R-IR) was sparse within the urothelium, with occasional umbrella and basal cells, and was detected in endothelial cells, intramural neurons, nerve fibers, and detrusor smooth muscle cells.
title: Cellular Distribution and Expression of Cannabinoid Receptors Type 1 and 2 in the Urinary Bladder of Cats (<i>Felis catus</i>).

text: CB1R-IR was significantly higher in the detrusor muscle ( p = 0.0006). CB2R-IR showed marked staining in umbrella cells and faint staining in basal cells; it was also observed in bundles of nerve fibers, intramural neurons, detrusor smooth muscle cells, and vascular structures. CB2R-IR was significantly higher in the urothelium ( p < 0.0001). These findings provide a molecular basis for studies investigating the endocannabinoid system as a potential therapeutic target in feline lower urinary tract disorders.
title: Cellular Distribution and Expression of Cannabinoid Receptors Type 1 and 2 in the Urinary Bladder of Cats (<i>Felis catus</i>).

text: Metabolic remodeling is one of the hallmarks of malignant tumors, and post-translational modifications of proteins, such as succinylation, play an important role in the process of metabolic remodeling by regulating the function of metabolic enzymes. However, the role of succinylation modifications of key mitochondrial metabolic enzymes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. Here, using succinylation proteomics, it is demonstrated that the succinylation level of lysine 409 (K409) on dihydrolipoamide S-succinyltransferase (DLST) is significantly increased in LUAD. Further, DLST K409 succinylation (K409succ), which is catalyzed by carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A), can affect oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and redox homeostasis by regulating enzyme activity, thereby promoting the malignant progression of LUAD.
title: DLST Succinylation-Mediated Mitochondrial Metabolic Remodeling and Cuproptosis Resistance Promote Malignant Progression of Lung Adenocarcinoma.

text: Notably, the succinylation of DLST can enhance the cuproptosis resistance by inhibiting its lipoylation. Subsequently, a small-molecule inhibitor SI409-1 that can specifically target DLST K409 has been developed. In vitro and in vivo experiments show that SI409-1 can inhibit the LUAD growth and enhance the sensitivity to cuproptosis inducers. Collectively, these findings provide a novel predictive target and intervention strategy for the clinical diagnosis and treatment of LUAD.
title: DLST Succinylation-Mediated Mitochondrial Metabolic Remodeling and Cuproptosis Resistance Promote Malignant Progression of Lung Adenocarcinoma.

text: Environmental persistent free radicals (EPFRs) are a class of long-lived, redox-active species that persist on fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) surfaces for days to months. Upon inhalation, EPFRs catalyze the generation of hydroxyl radicals through Fenton-like cycling, driving oxidative stress and inflammation at the site of deposition. Current air filtration technology focuses almost exclusively on physical interception of particulate matter, leaving the surface-bound radical activity of captured PM entirely unaddressed. This review advances a testable hypothesis rather than reporting a validated outcome: that cerium dioxide (CeO 2 )-based materials, whose Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ redox cycling is well-established as a broad-spectrum antioxidant mechanism in biomedical contexts, can be functionally migrated to air filtration to chemically quench EPFRs on captured PM 2.5 .
title: Cerium Dioxide-Based Scavenging of Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals in Fine Particulate Matter: A Prospective Review.

text: We first summarize the formation and health impacts of EPFRs, then introduce the mechanistic basis of CeO 2 radical scavenging, emphasizing its self-regenerating valence cycling. We then examine the existing but functionally distinct use of CeO 2 in air pollution control, including its role as an oxygen storage component in three-way catalysis and as an additive in filter media, and argue that these high-temperature oxidation applications do not constitute a functional precedent for ambient-temperature radical scavenging. The central gap is that no study has systematically tested whether CeO 2 can chemically quench EPFRs on PM 2.5 surfaces under filtration conditions.
title: Cerium Dioxide-Based Scavenging of Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals in Fine Particulate Matter: A Prospective Review.

text: We articulate the key experimental questions that must be resolved-direct EPFR quenching versus ROS interception, the effects of humidity, airflow, and contact time, and the long-term fate of CeO 2 under realistic filtration conditions-and argue that the demonstrated gaseous ROS scavenging of CeO 2 in cigarette smoke, together with its self-recovery capability, provides sufficient mechanistic justification to pursue this direction experimentally.
title: Cerium Dioxide-Based Scavenging of Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals in Fine Particulate Matter: A Prospective Review.

text: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome viruses (PRRSVs) cause significant economic losses to the global swine industry. Current live attenuated vaccines are unable to effectively control PRRSV infection, and strain variability, driven by rapid mutation, complicates the development of improved vaccines. Identification of the targets of broadly neutralizing antibodies is crucial for guiding next-generation vaccine design, yet PRRSV glycoproteins bearing conserved neutralizing epitopes remain poorly defined. To address this, recombinant soluble forms of PRRSV-1 envelope glycoproteins, GP2, GP3 and GP4, were produced using mammalian cells. The screening of serum from hyperimmune pigs demonstrated GP3 as the most highly recognized of the three glycoproteins. Fluorescently tagged GP3-tetramers were utilized to isolate single B cells from a hyperimmune pig via flow cytometry.
title: Evaluation of the contribution of the minor envelope complex glycoprotein 3 ectodomain to the porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus 1 neutralizing antibody response.

text: Immunoglobulin VH and VL regions were amplified by RT-PCR and sequenced. Fifteen unique heavy and light chain pairs were cloned and expressed as recombinant monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). mAbs were evaluated for specificity, cross-reactivity and neutralizing capacity. Antigenic sites targeted by GP3-specific mAbs were mapped to several conserved linear sequences, but mAbs did not exhibit virus neutralizing activity in vitro , suggesting that these may serve as decoy epitopes. An immunogenicity study with recombinant GP3, delivered as a protein subunit or via an RNA vector, also demonstrated a lack of neutralizing antibody response despite high GP3-binding antibody titres. Collectively, these data suggest that antibodies directed against the isolated PRRSV-1 GP3 ectodomain are unlikely to contribute substantially to neutralization.
title: Evaluation of the contribution of the minor envelope complex glycoprotein 3 ectodomain to the porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus 1 neutralizing antibody response.

text: However, the workflow established for isolating porcine mAbs could be utilized in future research to further dissect the neutralizing antibody response to PRRSV.
title: Evaluation of the contribution of the minor envelope complex glycoprotein 3 ectodomain to the porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus 1 neutralizing antibody response.

text: DNA and RNA methylation are key epigenetic and epitranscriptomic modifications involved in gene regulation, genome stability, RNA metabolism, and disease progression. Aberrant methylation patterns in cell-free DNA and RNA have emerged as valuable biomarkers for cancer detection, disease monitoring, and therapeutic stratification. However, conventional methods such as bisulfite sequencing, methylation-specific PCR, MeRIP-seq, SCARLET, and LC-MS/MS often require harsh processing, high sample input, complex instrumentation, or lack site-specific resolution, limiting their clinical and point-of-care applications. CRISPR-based diagnostics provide a promising alternative by combining programmable nucleic acid recognition with collateral cleavage-mediated signal amplification.
title: CRISPR technologies for detecting DNA and RNA methylation: Mechanisms, platforms, and translational opportunities.

text: This review summarizes recent CRISPR strategies for detecting DNA and RNA methylation, including chemical conversion-assisted assays, restriction enzyme-mediated detection, direct amplification-free sensing based on methylation-modulated Cas activity, detection of oxidized cytosine derivatives, reverse transcription-mediated Cas12 detection of m6A, and structure-sensitive Cas13 sensing. We highlight how methylation-dependent sequence conversion, enzyme accessibility, polymerase behavior, and nucleic acid structure can be translated into CRISPR-readable signals. Finally, we discuss current translational challenges and emerging opportunities in point-of-care methylation diagnostics, integrated DNA-RNA profiling, engineered Cas effectors, AI-guided assay design, and CRISPR-compatible methylome analysis.
title: CRISPR technologies for detecting DNA and RNA methylation: Mechanisms, platforms, and translational opportunities.

text: Pancreatic α cells play essential roles in maintaining glucose homeostasis. However, the epigenetic mechanisms governing α-cell proliferation and differentiation remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a systematic screen of a targeted PROTAC library and identified BET proteins as key regulators of α-cell proliferation and function. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that BRD4 promotes the acquisition of an intermediate endocrine progenitor-like state in progenitor cells. In vivo, α-cell-specific deletion of Brd4 markedly reduced α-cell mass and suppressed Men1-driven pathological α-cell proliferation, demonstrating that BRD4 is required for the establishment and/or maintenance of α-cell identity and abundance in vivo.
title: An Intra-BET Epigenetic Mechanism Driven by BRD4 Controls Pancreatic α-Cell Expansion.

text: Mechanistically, we identified the histone methyltransferase KMT5B as a BRD4-interacting protein and demonstrated that BRD4 directly binds to and represses the BRD2 promoter, with this BRD4-BRD2 regulation being modulated by KMT5B. Combined BRD4 overexpression and BRD2 suppression accelerated endocrine differentiation, reduced progenitor identity, enhanced α-cell features, and increased glucagon secretion in human islet organoids. Collectively, our study identifies a previously unrecognized KMT5B-modulated BRD4-BRD2 regulatory mechanism that coordinates pancreatic α-cell proliferation and differentiation, providing new insights into intra-BET epigenetic regulation during α-cell development and functional maturation.
title: An Intra-BET Epigenetic Mechanism Driven by BRD4 Controls Pancreatic α-Cell Expansion.

text: The recent surge in spillover events of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b to humans and mammals in North America has raised urgent pandemic concerns. Human H5N1 vaccines are unavailable in most countries. We synthesized data from ferret challenge trials to evaluate whether widely available seasonal influenza vaccines confer cross-protection against lethal H5N1 infection. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for ferret studies of lethal H5N1 challenge published up to 5 July 2025 (PROSPERO #CRD42024520346). Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to compare vaccine efficacy (VE) of seasonal influenza vaccines and H5N1 vaccines against H5N1-related mortality. Seroprotection was defined as a neutralizing antibody titre of ≥1:40. We identified 35 studies (157 trials).
title: Cross-protection against highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus from seasonal influenza vaccines: a systematic review and meta-analysis of ferret studies.

text: Seasonal influenza vaccines without N1 did not confer significant cross-protection (five trials; VE 14.8%, 95% CI -3.6 to 30.0). In contrast, VE was 73% for N1-containing seasonal influenza vaccines (19 trials; 95% CI 54-84) and 77% for H5N1 vaccines overall (133 trials; 95% CI 72-82) ( p = 0.52). The VE of N1-containing seasonal influenza vaccines was modestly lower than that of H5N1 vaccines with seroprotection (88%; 66 trials; 95% CI 84-91; p = 0.009), but comparable to H5N1 vaccines that did not achieve seroprotection (63%; 67 trials; 95% CI 52-71; p = 0.29). The VE of seasonal influenza vaccines against H5N1 was robust across sensitivity analyses, with no evidence of publication bias ( p = 0.99). Seasonal influenza vaccines significantly reduce H5N1-associated mortality in ferret trials, suggesting the cross-protection potential of currently available vaccines.
title: Cross-protection against highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus from seasonal influenza vaccines: a systematic review and meta-analysis of ferret studies.

text: Human studies are warranted.
title: Cross-protection against highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus from seasonal influenza vaccines: a systematic review and meta-analysis of ferret studies.

text: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, emphasizing the need for new targeted therapies. We recently identified CARM1-expressing HGSOCs as a distinct molecular subset associated with poor prognosis. To uncover therapeutic vulnerabilities in this subgroup, we performed a small-molecule inhibitor screen and identified the molecular chaperone heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) as a selective target in CARM1-high epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) cells. Pharmacological inhibition of HSP70 suppressed the growth of CARM1-expressing cells but not CARM1-knockout or normal epithelial cells, confirming on-target selectivity. Mechanistically, coactivator-associated arginine methyltransferase 1 (CARM1) regulates expression of multiple HSP70 co-chaperone genes from the DNAJ family without affecting total HSP70 expression.
title: CARM1-expressing ovarian cancers are selectively sensitive to HSP70 inhibition.

text: A newly developed HSP70 inhibitor, AP-4-139B, significantly reduced tumor growth in CARM1-high xenografts. Importantly, AP-4-139B was well tolerated with no detectable toxicity. Together, these results identify CARM1 as a key regulator of the HSP70 co-chaperone network and reveal HSP70 inhibition as a selective and well-tolerated therapeutic strategy for CARM1-expressing ovarian cancers.
title: CARM1-expressing ovarian cancers are selectively sensitive to HSP70 inhibition.

text: Background Since the 1990s, the United States has been facing the recurring problem of widespread misuse, addiction and overdoses involving opioid compounds. This phenomenon is known as the opioid crisis or the opioid epidemic. Every day, around 200 Americans die due to opioid use. Nowadays the country is facing the fourth wave, dominated by fentanyl combined with stimulants. The problem of opioid abuse is not confined to the United States alone, but is a global issue. Objective In this paper, we do not focus on fentanyl, but on another painkiller, oxycodone, as it is often overlooked in discussions of the current crisis, whilst its sale and use are becoming increasingly common. In Poland alone, the number of prescriptions increased by 50% between 2019 and 2023, and nearly 200 Poles have died as a result of an opioid use disorder.
title: Oxycodone at the Crossroads of Pain Management, Misuse, and Toxicological Investigation.

text: This narrative review examines oxycodone at the intersection of pain management, non-medical use, and toxicological investigation, with emphasis on its pharmacology, clinical applications, abuse liability, overdose risk, and detection in biological matrices. Methods PubMed and Google Scholar were searched using terms related to oxycodone, toxicology, addiction, the opioid crisis, detection methods, biological matrices, analgesic effects, pharmacokinetics, metabolism, overdose, and hospital treatment. English- and Polish-language publications from January 2020 to July 2026 were prioritised, with the search extended to 2000 where necessary. No formal systematic-review protocol was applied. Results By interacting with opioid receptors, oxycodone relieves moderate to severe pain.
title: Oxycodone at the Crossroads of Pain Management, Misuse, and Toxicological Investigation.

text: It is therefore used as an analgesic for various types of pain-intraoperative, postsurgical or chronic pain, including cancer-related pain. It has good bioavailability following oral administration and accumulates in tissue less than, for example, morphine. A further advantage is the availability of a variety of routes of administration: in addition to oral administration (including through immediate- and extended-release formulations), oxycodone can also be administered, inter alios, intravenously, intranasally, and rectally. On the other hand, oxycodone causes a range of adverse effects-it can lead to respiratory depression and constipation and has high potential of addiction. Its use is associated with a risk of developing tolerance, and discontinuation may trigger withdrawal symptoms. Oxycodone's high utility for medical purposes makes it a widely used drug in hospital settings.
title: Oxycodone at the Crossroads of Pain Management, Misuse, and Toxicological Investigation.

text: At the same time, there is an increasing number of cases of inappropriate oxycodone use. This results in the need for analytical methods to monitor concentrations in hospitalised patients and to investigate concentrations in cases of suspected poisoning. The toxicological methods used for detection of oxycodone include both screening tests, such as immunoenzymatic assays, and confirmatory tests-i.e., liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry. The process of choosing an appropriate method begins at the stage of selecting the diagnostic sample. Both standard samples, such as blood (including dried blood spots-a novelty) and urine, and alternative samples-oral fluid, hair, nails and vitreous humour-are useful, depending on the patient's condition, their availability and the time elapsed since the substance was ingested.
title: Oxycodone at the Crossroads of Pain Management, Misuse, and Toxicological Investigation.

text: Conclusions Oxycodone remains an important analgesic but carries substantial risks of misuse, addiction, and fatal toxicity. Safe prescribing and monitoring, recognition of drug interactions and individual variability, and integrated interpretation of individual case circumstances, appropriate biological samples, and confirmatory mass-spectrometric findings are essential in clinical and forensic practice.
title: Oxycodone at the Crossroads of Pain Management, Misuse, and Toxicological Investigation.

text: Lithium is widely used to treat psychiatric disorders, including bipolar disorder. However, long-term lithium therapy is frequently associated with acquired nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (NDI), a disorder characterized by impaired urinary concentrating ability and excessive water loss. Tamoxifen (TAM), a selective estrogen receptor modulator, has previously been shown to alleviate lithium-induced NDI by restoring AQP2 and AQP3 expression. Here, we investigated whether necroptosis-related signaling, primary cilium remodeling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-like changes contribute to lithium-induced collecting duct alterations and whether TAM modulates these responses.
title: Beyond Aquaporins: Tamoxifen Preserves Collecting Duct Epithelial Homeostasis in Lithium-Induced Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus.

text: Using complementary in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo approaches, we found that lithium significantly reduced the expression of the necroptosis-related proteins receptor-interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) and mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL), whereas TAM prevented their downregulation. Lithium also induced primary cilium elongation and promoted EMT-like changes, characterized by reduced E-cadherin and increased vimentin expression, which were attenuated by TAM. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that lithium profoundly alters collecting duct epithelial homeostasis by modulating the abundance of necroptosis-related proteins, primary cilium morphology, and epithelial phenotype.
title: Beyond Aquaporins: Tamoxifen Preserves Collecting Duct Epithelial Homeostasis in Lithium-Induced Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus.

text: The ability of TAM to counteract these alterations indicates that its protective effects extend beyond aquaporin regulation, supporting its potential as a therapeutic strategy for lithium-induced NDI.
title: Beyond Aquaporins: Tamoxifen Preserves Collecting Duct Epithelial Homeostasis in Lithium-Induced Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus.

text: Background Symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) is a biomarker of renal function derived from arginine methylation, unaffected by muscle mass or diet, and increases after only a 25% reduction in renal function, allowing earlier detection of renal dysfunction compared with serum creatinine. Although serum SDMA is well established in veterinary nephrology, urinary SDMA (uSDMA) remains comparatively underexplored, particularly in dogs with acute kidney injury (AKI). This study evaluated uSDMA concentrations and the uSDMA-to-creatinine (uSDMA/Cr) ratio as biomarkers for AKI, using renal histopathology as the reference standard. Methods Twenty-seven non-azotemic dogs diagnosed with pyometra were evaluated. uSDMA was measured using ELISA, and renal lesions were histopathologically classified as discrete, moderate or severe.
title: Urinary symmetric dimethylarginine: A promising biomarker for acute kidney injury in dogs with pyometra.

text: Results Median uSDMA concentrations were significantly higher in dogs with severe lesions (0.43 µg/mL, interquartile range [IQR] 0.40-0.47) compared with those with moderate lesions (0.31 µg/mL, IQR 0.24-0.38) and discrete lesions (0.26 µg/mL, IQR 0.22-0.30) (p Limitations The main limitations include the absence of a healthy control group and lack of serial biomarker measurements, which may restrict the assessment of dynamic changes. Conclusions These preliminary findings suggest that uSDMA and uSDMA/Cr ratio may serve as biomarkers for assessing AKI severity in dogs, supporting earlier detection and monitoring.
title: Urinary symmetric dimethylarginine: A promising biomarker for acute kidney injury in dogs with pyometra.

text: Rabies remains a major public health threat in the Philippines, particularly in urban areas such as Davao City, where frequent animal bites from domestic reservoirs increase the transmission risk at the human-animal-environment interface. Detailed epidemiological data on animal bites and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) coverage are limited. This One Health-framed retrospective cohort study describes trends in bite incidents, assesses PEP coverage, and identifies gaps in rabies prevention efforts from 2019 to 2023. Surveillance data from the Davao City Animal Bite Treatment Centers captured 98,442 cases. Dogs caused 63.5% of bites, with a significant upward trend ( p = 0.027; τ = 1.0, 95% CI 0.200-1.800); cat bites (36.4%) rose sharply, indicating an emerging reservoir challenge. Children ≤15 years of age showed a significant increase ( p = 0.027).
title: Epidemiology of animal bites and post-exposure vaccination coverage in Davao City, Philippines: A five-year retrospective cohort study, 2019-2023.

text: The 3rd congressional district had the most pronounced rise across demographics and exposure categories. Tissue culture vaccine coverage remained at 100%, equine rabies immunoglobulin rose from 18.5% to 85.9%, whereas human rabies immunoglobulin remained low post-COVID. Despite universal TCV access, immunoglobulin gaps limit its control. Rising cat bites and severe exposures demand integrated One Health strategies, enhanced surveillance, animal vaccination, and supply chain strengthening, to achieve zero human rabies deaths by 2030.
title: Epidemiology of animal bites and post-exposure vaccination coverage in Davao City, Philippines: A five-year retrospective cohort study, 2019-2023.

text: Background/objectives Rapid antimicrobial decision-making in small-animal practice is limited by the turnaround time (≥2 days) of conventional laboratory-based culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST). Existing point-of-care and in-clinic tests can provide faster results, but their performance often depends on user experience. This study evaluated VetBac, a hybrid workflow in which the test is conducted in the clinic, while experts centrally interpret bacterial growth on plates. Methods We analyzed 60 interpretable plates from canine and feline skin, ear, and urine infections. In the clinic, samples were inoculated onto chromogenic Mueller-Hinton agar plates, after which antibiotic discs were applied. Plates were incubated for 16-20 h, photographed, and interpreted centrally by an expert.
title: Clinical Evaluation of a Centralized In-Clinic Direct Culture and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing Workflow for Canine and Feline Skin, Ear, and Urine Infections.

text: For comparison, samples were submitted in parallel to standard microbiology laboratories. Results Identification of primary bacterial populations in clinical samples showed high species-level agreement with laboratory results (83.9%), increasing to 100.0% when staphylococci species were grouped. Secondary bacteria agreement (16.7%) was lower due to unrecognizability and overgrowth by dominant bacteria. Overall AST agreement was 93.6% (262/280), with 91.9% sensitivity for detecting resistance and 94.0% specificity for detecting susceptibility. VetBac-susceptible discrepancies occurred in 5/62 laboratory-resistant comparisons (8.1%), and VetBac-resistant discrepancies occurred in 13/218 laboratory-susceptible comparisons (6.0%).
title: Clinical Evaluation of a Centralized In-Clinic Direct Culture and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing Workflow for Canine and Feline Skin, Ear, and Urine Infections.

text: Conclusions In interpretable skin, ear, and urine samples, the VetBac workflow showed high agreement with laboratory results for primary bacterial identification and AST. These findings support the hybrid in-clinic/centralized model as an adjunctive source of earlier antimicrobial decision support, pending laboratory confirmation. However, the study did not estimate the proportion of all clinical samples suitable for direct culture and AST.
title: Clinical Evaluation of a Centralized In-Clinic Direct Culture and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing Workflow for Canine and Feline Skin, Ear, and Urine Infections.

text: Heat stress, a critical environmental stressor intensified by global warming, increasingly threatens bull semen quality. This review synthesizes the multi-level mechanisms underlying this impairment. Heat-stressed bulls exhibit behavioral changes that serve as early indicators of reproductive dysfunction, alongside pronounced declines in routine semen parameters and alterations in the seminal plasma biochemical microenvironment. At the endocrine level, heat stress disrupts the hypothalamic-pituitary axes, suppressing testosterone synthesis and perturbing the testicular microenvironment to compromise spermatogenesis. At the molecular level, altered expression of heat-stress-related genes and epigenetic reprogramming-involving non-coding RNAs, DNA methylation, and m 6 A methylation-collectively disturb this process.
title: Heat Stress and Bull Semen: From Endocrine and Molecular Dysregulation to Targeted Intervention.

text: Notably, the "gut-testis" axis emerges as a key pathway: heat-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis compromises intestinal barrier integrity, and immune and endocrine signals from translocated microbial metabolites ultimately impair testicular function and semen quality, as evidenced by cross-species studies. At the application level, the above mechanistic evidence, which is largely derived from model animals or non-bovine livestock, still requires direct and systematic validation in bulls. Collectively, this review provides an integrative mechanistic framework for heat stress-induced deterioration of bull semen quality and highlights critical directions for developing targeted mitigation strategies under global climate change.
title: Heat Stress and Bull Semen: From Endocrine and Molecular Dysregulation to Targeted Intervention.

text: Sugarcane smut, caused by S. scitamineum , results in substantial economic losses across global sugarcane growing areas. Elucidating the pathogenic mechanisms of S. scitamineum is therefore crucial for developing effective disease control strategies. Our previous work has shown that the protein phosphatase SsPpe1 regulates mating and pathogenicity in S. scitamineum . In this study, we identified SsRts1 as a novel interacting protein of SsPpe1, which contains a PP2A regulator subunit B56 domain. Deletion of Ssrts1 gene impaired sporidia growth, resulting in pseudohyphal sporidia with multiple nuclei and aberrant chitin distribution. Further analysis revealed elevated phosphorylation levels of the cell cycle-related kinase CDK1 T161 in the Δ Ssrts1 mutants, suggesting that SsRts1 participates in mitosis regulation.
title: The PP2A phosphatase regulatory subunit SsRts1 regulates morphogenesis, mitosis, sexual mating and virulence in <i>Sporisorium scitamineum</i>.

text: Moreover, the Δ Ssrts1 mutants exhibited increased sensitivity to cell wall, oxidative and high osmotic stresses. Mechanistically, SsRts1 negatively regulates the phosphorylation levels of the CWI-MAPK Mps1, implicating that SsRts1 is involved in regulating the cell wall integrity (CWI) pathway. Additionally, deletion of Ssrts1 also led to abnormal accumulation of autophagosome, along with defects in sexual mating, filamentation, and virulence. Global transcriptome profiling indicated that SsRts1 modulates ATPase activity, cell cycle progression, transmembrane transport, and tryptophan metabolism. Notably, exogenous supplementation with tryptophan partially restored the mating and filamentation defects in the Δ Ssrts1 mutants, indicating that SsRts1 modulates these processes partly through the tryptophan catabolism pathway.
title: The PP2A phosphatase regulatory subunit SsRts1 regulates morphogenesis, mitosis, sexual mating and virulence in <i>Sporisorium scitamineum</i>.

text: Collectively, these findings provide insight into the regulatory roles of PP2A regulatory subunit SsRts1 in S. scitamineum , and expand our understanding of PP2A function in plant-pathogenic fungi.
title: The PP2A phosphatase regulatory subunit SsRts1 regulates morphogenesis, mitosis, sexual mating and virulence in <i>Sporisorium scitamineum</i>.

text: Wearable and attachable healthcare devices provide valuable insights across a broad range of applications, from health monitoring and disease diagnosis to the assessment of daily human activities. For these devices, both the formation of high-performance electrodes and mechanical, electrical, and physiological stability at human-device interfaces are critically important. Conductive gels, which combine deformable polymer networks with electrical conductivity, show considerable potential as functional materials for such applications. However, existing reviews have often considered material properties, interfacial behavior, and device reliability separately. This review examines hydrogels, ionogels, and organogels by linking material design, stimulus- and analyte-responsive sensing, biological and device interfaces, and healthcare applications.
title: Conductive Gels for Wearable and Attachable Healthcare Devices: Materials, Sensing Mechanisms, Interfaces and Applications.

text: This integrated perspective emphasizes evaluating conductive gels within complete healthcare devices, where material properties, biological interfaces, and device integration jointly determine practical performance. Such evaluation needs to address signal quality and the stability of the assembled system during deformation, environmental exposure, and prolonged use. Future progress will require reproducible device fabrication and standardized validation tailored to the intended application, with systematic assessment of long-term biosafety and alignment with relevant regulatory requirements. Integration with flexible electronics, intelligent data processing, and feedback control may further enable reliable and responsive healthcare platforms.
title: Conductive Gels for Wearable and Attachable Healthcare Devices: Materials, Sensing Mechanisms, Interfaces and Applications.

text: Climate change poses a growing threat to U.S. healthcare systems, which are uniquely positioned to mitigate its impacts while addressing their own greenhouse gas emissions from energy use, supply chains, clinical operations, and waste. Clinical informaticists can advance mitigation by integrating environmental data into health system operations and decision-making. Tracking emissions across scopes enables data-informed strategies, while frameworks such as I-CLIMATE and One Digital Health can help coordinate disparate data streams and reduce healthcare's environmental impact. Integrated dashboards can support renewable energy adoption, energy efficiency, and operational decision-making, while telehealth can reduce transportation-related emissions.
title: Health systems and climate change mitigation through an applied health informatics and sustainability perspective.

text: Artificial intelligence may also reduce resource use when applied judiciously through narrowly scoped, task-specific models, with frameworks such as SAHAI guiding sustainable implementation. Financial approaches such as New York University's Return on Sustainability Investment framework can quantify the financial value of decarbonization initiatives. Effective governance, including vertical alignment and horizontal integration, is essential to operationalizing these strategies. Emerging opportunities include climate-conscious hardware design and carbon accounting applications. Ultimately, informatics can provide the data, tools, and governance infrastructure needed to translate climate mitigation goals into measurable health system action and establish carbon neutrality as an organizational performance priority.
title: Health systems and climate change mitigation through an applied health informatics and sustainability perspective.

text: Although osteosarcoma is the most common primary bone tumour in dogs, involvement of the pelvic bones is rare. The aim of the present study was to describe clinical presentation, identify possible prognostic factors, and evaluate outcomes in dogs diagnosed with pelvic osteosarcoma. Seventy-four dogs with cytologically or histologically diagnosed pelvic osteosarcoma were included in this multicentre retrospective study (2007-2025). The median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with comparisons performed using log-rank tests. Prognostic factors for PFS and OS were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. Lameness (84%) was the most common presenting clinical sign, and the ilium (57%) was the most frequent intrapelvic tumour location.
title: Clinical Behaviour and Outcome of Pelvic Osteosarcoma in Dogs: A Retrospective Multicentre Analysis of 74 Cases (2007-2025).

text: Thirty-one percent of dogs had metastases at diagnosis, primarily affecting the lungs. The median PFS was 75 days, and the median OS was 79 days. Dogs receiving any treatment had significantly longer PFS (116 vs. 7 days, p < 0.001) and OS (145 vs. 8 days, p < 0.001) than untreated dogs. No factors were significantly associated with PFS. In contrast, dogs with higher body weight and shorter time to diagnosis tended to have more favourable survival, whereas chemotherapy and local progression were associated with poorer outcomes. Despite the overall poor prognosis associated with pelvic osteosarcoma, treatment may extend survival. An individualized, often multimodal approach may provide clinical benefit in selected dogs.
title: Clinical Behaviour and Outcome of Pelvic Osteosarcoma in Dogs: A Retrospective Multicentre Analysis of 74 Cases (2007-2025).

text: Caregiver-mediated interventions are widely used to support social communication development in young autistic children. While many such interventions are evidence-informed, limited information exists about their shared and unique elements, making it challenging for caregivers and clinicians to tailor program selection to individual needs and preferences-an essential part of personalized care in autism. This scoping review with content analysis examined 18 commercially available, caregiver-mediated social communication interventions to identify similarities and differences in child skills targeted and caregiver-coached strategies. Data were extracted from program manuals, fidelity tools, published literature, and program websites for eight developmental social pragmatic (DSP) programs and 10 naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions (NDBIs).
title: Common and Differing Elements Across Caregiver-Mediated Social Communication Programs Supporting Autistic Children: A Scoping Review With Content Analysis.
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice

text: Programs varied in scope, with some supporting a broad range of child skills and others focusing on specific areas. Across all programs, 70 caregiver-coached strategies were identified, and then thematically grouped into eight categories aligned with the developmental skills the strategies aim to support. Although some strategies were common across all programs, some unique strategies were also identified. In addition, there were notable differences in how these strategies were operationalized despite using similar terminology, underscoring the need for more precise, clearly defined fidelity measures to enable accurate assessment of caregiver implementation and meaningful comparisons across programs.
title: Common and Differing Elements Across Caregiver-Mediated Social Communication Programs Supporting Autistic Children: A Scoping Review With Content Analysis.
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice

text: This study lays the groundwork for future research to identify active ingredients of interventions and supports more informed, individualized decision-making in clinical practice.Lay AbstractYoung autistic children may engage with others and communicate in ways that differ from non-autistic peers, and may need support to develop skills to communicate with, and navigate interactions with others. Many programs have been developed for this purpose, with a growing number of programs including caregivers in this process. In programs where caregivers play a primary role, professionals coach them to use certain techniques that can support social communication. Although many such programs exist, we still lack clarity on how these programs are similar or different, making it tough for families to choose among them.
title: Common and Differing Elements Across Caregiver-Mediated Social Communication Programs Supporting Autistic Children: A Scoping Review With Content Analysis.
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice

text: To address this gap, we reviewed 18 well-known caregiver-led programs to compare the skills they aim to support children with, and the specific techniques they teach caregivers. We gathered information from program resource materials, published research, and official program websites. We found that some programs focused on supporting a wide range of skills, whereas others targeted only certain developmental areas. In total, we identified 70 distinct caregiver-coached techniques, which we organized into eight categories. Many techniques were common across all programs, but others were unique to specific programs. Even among the shared techniques, there were differences in the way they were practiced, despite using the same strategy name. For example, a technique like "following the child's lead" could look quite different depending on the program.
title: Common and Differing Elements Across Caregiver-Mediated Social Communication Programs Supporting Autistic Children: A Scoping Review With Content Analysis.
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice

text: These findings show that having descriptions of how techniques should be used is important to understanding and comparing different programs. Overall, these findings provide families with information about program ingredients and can be used to guide clinicians toward programs that match individuals' needs and wants. This work also paves way for future research exploring how these social communication programs work, and evaluating which techniques are most effective for specific groups of children and families.
title: Common and Differing Elements Across Caregiver-Mediated Social Communication Programs Supporting Autistic Children: A Scoping Review With Content Analysis.
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice

text: Ribosome collisions during aberrant translation activate ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) to resolve stalled ribosome complexes and triage incomplete nascent chains. How this co-translational surveillance is coordinated with other ribosome-associated activities remains unclear. Here, we identify the ribosome-associated Hsp40 chaperone DNAJC2 that restrains translational flux and limits RQC engagement during collision-prone translation. Genetic epistasis analysis revealed that DNAJC2 titrates the flux of aberrant translation intermediates through the canonical RQC pathway, from the collision-sensing RQC factor ZNF598 to the downstream NEMF-LTN1 E3 ligase complex for proteasomal degradation. DNAJC2 depletion further sensitized cells to collision-induced ribotoxic stress response (RSR), indicating increased vulnerability to global translation stress.
title: Ribosome-associated chaperone DNAJC2 titrates translation flux to alleviate the burden of co-translational quality control.

text: Mechanistically, loss of DNAJC2 accelerated translation elongation, thereby promoting ribosome collisions and ZNF598-dependent ribosome disassembly. Accordingly, reducing translational flux with the translation inhibitor homoharringtonine or a huntingtin upstream ORF rescued DNAJC2-depletion phenotypes during RQC-sensitive poly(A)-mediated translational stalling. Together, we propose that DNAJC2 acts as a translational rheostat to buffer ribosome collisions, prevent RQC overload, and set the threshold for RSR activation.
title: Ribosome-associated chaperone DNAJC2 titrates translation flux to alleviate the burden of co-translational quality control.

text: Objectives: This paper explores whether deaf Greek-Cypriot (GC) children with cochlear implants (CIs) begin using the various forms of the definite article (DA) of the Greek language similarly to their typically hearing peers in terms of order of appearance and age. Furthermore, it explores if their MLUm growth correlates with that of typically developing peers. Methods: This is a longitudinal study with quantitative and qualitative analyses. The sample comprises four prelingually deaf GC children with CIs and eight typically hearing (TH) children with no developmental delays. Age and hearing status (CIs vs. TH) were used to explain variability in results. The effect of random effects was also examined. Presence of random effects was examined using Mixed Linear Models. Growth trajectories were plotted for in-depth result description and interpretation.
title: A Longitudinal Exploratory Case-Series Comparing Morphological Trajectories in Four Early-Implanted Greek-Cypriot Children and Eight Typically Hearing Peers.

text: Results: Both groups demonstrated a significant linear increase in their accurate usage of definite articles with age, whereas hearing status showed no statistically significant impact on any outcome measure. Individual variance among children accounted for approximately 33% to 50% of the variance in correct article production. Additionally, Mean Length of Utterance in morphemes (MLUm) values between the two groups remained correlated across all age levels. Discussion: While random individual effects influence the rate of correct production, early morphosyntactic trajectories for CI children seem to be similar to those of typically developing controls. Due to the small sample size, studies with bigger samples are needed to replicate, confirm and validate further the results of the current study.
title: A Longitudinal Exploratory Case-Series Comparing Morphological Trajectories in Four Early-Implanted Greek-Cypriot Children and Eight Typically Hearing Peers.

text: Objectives Human Factors (HF) principles are essential for safe and effective clinical decision support (CDS), yet existing guidance is fragmented and rarely evaluated in real world settings. A novel, evidence-based, vendor-agnostic HF-informed guideline was developed to address this gap. This study evaluated its perceived usefulness, usability, and impact on CDS design and optimization. Materials and methods A 2-phase explanatory sequential mixed methods approach was used. Phase 1 involved a survey of guideline users (n = 25) assessing usefulness, ease of use, satisfaction, and influence on decision-making. Phase 2 included semi-structured interviews (n = 10) to explore real-world application experiences. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and qualitative data were analyzed thematically using a general inductive approach. Results Findings were consistently positive.
title: Evaluation of a clinical decision support design guideline.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

text: Participants reported that the guideline was easy to use and supported structured, evidence-based CDS decision-making. It improved confidence in selecting and designing CDS interventions, with particular value placed on its consolidated format and step-by-step approach. Suggested enhancements included adding practical tools, worked examples, and case studies to support broader application across contexts. Discussion This study represents the first real-world evaluation of a consolidated HF-informed CDS guideline, addressing the gap between theory and practice. Results indicate that integrated, accessible HF guidance can strengthen consistency and quality in CDS design, particularly when embedded within routine workflows and governance processes. Conclusion The guideline is a valuable, practical resource for CDS design and optimization.
title: Evaluation of a clinical decision support design guideline.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

text: Future research should assess its impact on post-implementation optimization and include objective measures of usability, safety, and CDS effectiveness to further demonstrate its value.
title: Evaluation of a clinical decision support design guideline.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

text: Degenerative lumbosacral stenosis (DLSS) causes progressive nerve root compression, leading to cauda equina syndrome (CES) and painful gait impairments in dogs. Epidural co-administration of autologous conditioned serum (ACS) and glucocorticoids (GC) is used as a conservative intervention, but objective outcome data remain lacking. This retrospective exploratory study evaluated whether an inertial measurement unit (IMU)-based kinematic system (LupoGait) could detect gait changes following a single epidural injection of ACS and triamcinolone acetonide in 44 dogs with CES. Nominal post-treatment changes were observed in several hindlimb parameters, including stance phase (HL +0.03, 95% CI 0.005-0.05, p = 0.018), maximum gyroscope amplitude (HL +0.32, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.69, p = 0.032), and variance of the differentiated gyroscope signal (HL +0.10, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.23, p = 0.036).
title: Kinematic changes following concurrent epidural injection with autologous conditioned serum (ACS) and glucocorticoids in dogs with cauda equina syndrome.

text: However, no evaluated outcomes remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons.
